# RUITK Builder — Godot parity gaps

**What this is.** A feature-by-feature account of what the Godot leg of the RUITK UI Builder does not yet do, measured against the Unity leg, which is the reference implementation.

**How it was produced, in two passes.**

*Pass one* read sixteen subsystem areas of Unity's 20,970-line builder for BEHAVIOUR rather than for code — what each does, why, the concrete thresholds and orderings, the visual detail, the gestures, the edge cases — yielding **850 catalogued behaviours**. The Godot port's 12,494 lines were audited against that inventory, and every claimed gap was then put to a second agent briefed to REFUTE it by finding the Godot code that already implements it.

*Pass two* ran the three checks pass one could not finish: the **behaviour contract read clause by clause** (`../ruitk-unity/plans/UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md`, 195 clauses, split seven ways so no agent had to emit them all at once), **four completeness critics**, and **adjudication of the 78 leads** pass one had noticed but never verified. Several findings in both passes were confirmed with headless probes against Godot 4.7 rather than by reading alone.

## How to read this register

Four things a reader needs before trusting the numbers. All four come from a critic whose only job was to audit **this document** rather than the port.

- **The critical count was inflated by duplication.** 12 clusters — covering 16 entries — are one defect filed twice or three times, because two areas read the same code. `LANG-##` and `ctx-##` are largely the same subsystem read twice. Duplicates are now **marked, not deleted** — both entries carry evidence worth keeping and it was the count that was wrong. Counts below are of PRIMARY entries only.
- **77 entries carry a correction that supersedes their own headline**, not the 12 the first draft claimed. Where an entry has a "Correction from the adversarial pass" block, that block is the finding and the headline is not. Entries so affected are flagged in "Start here".
- **Two "To build" recipes are wrong and would reintroduce the bug they fix.** `CANVAS-04` prescribes `clip_text` on the header title Label, which is the exact mechanism `CANVAS-03` identifies as a defect; the title sits in an HBox where nothing carries an expand flag, so `clip_text` collapses it to 17px — measured. `CANVAS-07` prescribes a `ScrollContainer` with a `custom_minimum_size` cap, but that property is a floor rather than a cap and a vertically-scrolling ScrollContainer reports ~0 minimum height, so the section vanishes — probed at 61x0. Read `GP-11`'s recipe instead for the second.
- **The canvas-geometry cluster has two contradictory prescriptions.** `CANVAS-01` says make measurement authoritative and the model a fallback; `GP-12` says keep the model authoritative for layout and reconcile only for hit-testing. They produce different code for `edge_source_anchor` and different invariants for the saved layout. This needs deciding before either is built.

## The contract: how much of it is met

All 195 clauses of `UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md`, the portable behaviour contract, audited against the port.

| Status | Clauses |
|---|---:|
| HONOURED | 63 |
| PARTIAL | 91 |
| ABSENT | 34 |
| DELIBERATE-DIVERGENCE | 7 |

Roughly a third of the contract is fully honoured and nearly half is partially honoured. That ratio, not the gap count, is the honest headline for where the port stands.

## Start here

Distinct critical gaps, duplicates folded in. An entry marked *(corrected)* has a superseding correction in its body — read that, not the headline.


**Action ledger: undo/redo, coalescing, history jump, what is recorded and what is not**

- `L-01` Undo and redo have no reachable trigger: the keyboard model needs a focus nothing ever gives it, and the only Undo/Redo menu is dead code *(corrected)*
- `L-02` Source-pane edits are absent from the ledger entirely: typing records nothing, Apply records nothing, and only Revert records
- `L-03` Redoing a creation restores an EMPTY module — the file's whole content is destroyed

**Canvas drawing: LOD bands, card geometry, section stack, edges, anchors, palette, grid, framing**

- `CANVAS-01` The card geometry model is a prediction that nothing validates, and it does not match what the view lays out — every row gesture targets the wrong row *(corrected)* *(also filed as GAP-01, GP-12)*
- `CANVAS-03` Hook chips and the Layer 3 attribute run render one pixel wide — the BODY section is visually empty and the attribute run is invisible

**Canvas input and gestures: pan, zoom, hit-testing, selection, card drag, row drag, drop bands**

- `GAP-02` No drop hint at all: three bands resolve and nothing is ever drawn
- `GAP-03` Pan and card-move state survive Godot's own drag-and-drop: the camera runs away and the next gesture is hijacked

**Create / rename / delete / move flows, save, abort, unsaved-tree placement, journal recovery**

- `G-03` Journal recovery is never offered, and the first Save of any later session destroys the crashed session's only copy
- `G-04` Format-on-save mutates every dirty buffer behind the UI's back: not through the funnel, not in the ledger, no re-projection — so the canvas's row spans are stale and the next canvas edit writes at the wrong offsets

**Document model: workspace, tree, module, specifiers, dirtiness, projection, orphans, read-only, import reconciliation**

- `DM-01` A load replaces the tree with no unsaved-work veto — right-clicking a .guitkx destroys the session *(corrected)* *(also filed as shell.load-tree-veto)*
- `DM-02` Rename does not rename: no export rewrite, no reference rewrite, no folder carry, no ledger entry *(corrected)* *(also filed as G-01, G-02)*

**Folder pane: tree rendering, state column, selection, re-filing by drag, folding**

- `FP-01` A re-file onto a folder that already holds that file name silently creates two modules claiming one path -- and Save overwrites the resident file *(corrected)*
- `FP-02` Re-filing a component that OWNS its folder dissolves the folder instead of carrying it -- the house layout is destroyed on the drag *(corrected)*

**Graph projection: cards, rows, sections, imports, hook chips, markup walk, edges**

- `GP-01` The card's section list is written TWICE and the two copies disagree — the hit-test addresses rows that are not drawn, and Delete removes them

**Language intelligence: completion, diagnostics plumbing, schema cache, element/hook classification**

- `LI-01` The "add attribute" menu offers 139 rows whose NAME is a stringified Dictionary, and picking one writes it into the tag
- `LI-03` Every hook dragged or clicked from the library writes `var _ = <hook>()`, which is a GDScript PARSE ERROR

**Language surface: directive vocabulary, style key surface with value helpers, text/labels, element classification**

- `LANG-01` The style-key menu writes a stringified Dictionary as the key — every "Add entry…" corrupts the module *(corrected)* *(also filed as LI-02)*
- `LANG-02` "Remove <badge>, keep its contents" is offered on every directive row; Unity offers it on exactly one *(corrected)* *(also filed as ctx-01)*
- `LANG-03` Deleting a MIDDLE clause takes the next clause's head with it *(also filed as ctx-02)*
- `LANG-04` The directive header seed and its commit are not inverse — editing a header writes `@if (@if (true))` *(corrected)*

**Library pane: sections, search, drag sources, selection sync, card framing, "+ new"**

- `LIB-01` The library's drag source is unreachable: every row is a Button with the default MOUSE_FILTER_STOP, which stops Godot's drag walk before it reaches the pane
- `LIB-02` Both gates over LIB-01 are green over a dead gesture: the parity sweep greps an identifier and the chrome test asserts `has_method`

**Live preview: compile pipeline, mirroring, scheduling, knobs, state panel, usage notes, failure isolation**

- `PV-01` Applying a source edit produces no ledger entry, no card re-projection and NO preview round — the funnel rejects it as a no-op *(corrected)*

**Searchable menu, name prompt, inline editor overlay, cursor feedback**

- `SM-01` The rename prompt validates the name against a folder the module does not live in, and nothing downstream catches the collision — Save silently overwrites one module with another *(corrected)*

**The defect register as forward-looking risk: which UB-## root causes the Godot port has hit or will hit**

- `ub-risk.path-availability-asks-disk` is_path_available consults the disk about an in-memory tree, and the name prompt asks a different question entirely *(corrected)*
- `ub-risk.move-has-no-destination-guard` No move route checks whether the destination is occupied, so two modules can claim one path and Save silently overwrites one

**The source editing surface: syntax colouring, completion, diagnostics, gutters, scrolling, apply**

- `SRC-01` Typing in edit mode writes the model on every keystroke, and apply then records nothing and re-projects nothing — a source edit is silently absent from undo and the canvas keeps showing the old file
- `SRC-02` Abandoning an edit — switching module, or the module being deleted — leaves the typed text in the model with no snapshot and no ledger entry; Save writes it to disk

**Window shell, layout, toolbar, commands, status, console, help, keyboard model**

- `shell.keyboard-focus-dead` The entire keyboard model is unreachable: nothing ever gives — or gives back — keyboard focus to the window Control *(corrected)*
- `shell.external-change-adoption` External .guitkx edits are never adopted, and Save writes the stale buffer over them
- `shell.no-save-door` Nothing outside the builder knows it is dirty: no quit prompt, no close prompt, and plugin teardown frees the window with unsaved work in it *(corrected)*

## Corrections to this register

Findings from the critic that audited this document rather than the port. Apply these before acting on anything above.

### "Start here" and the 38-critical count double-count ~10 criticals: nine verified pairs are one defect filed twice in two areas

Nine pairs in the triage list are the same code and the same fix, each counted twice in the scoreboard and each listed separately under "Start here": CANVAS-01 + GAP-01 (both critical, both = section_stack is a model nothing measures); LANG-01 + LI-02 (both critical, both = builder_window.gd:1240-1258 `str(key)` on a style-key Dictionary); LANG-03 + ctx-02 (both critical, both = builder_edits.gd delete_clause missing Unity's branch A, both citing BuilderWindow.cs:2155-2205); LANG-02 + ctx-01 (both critical, both = unwrap offered on every directive row); DM-01 + shell.load-tree-veto (both critical, both = load replaces the tree with no unsaved-work veto); DM-02 + G-01 (+G-02) (all critical; DM-02 is literally G-01 ∪ G-02); L-01 + shell.keyboard-focus-dead (both critical, both = nothing grab_focus()es the window Control); FP-01 + SM-01 (both critical, both = no destination-occupied guard, Save overwrites — with G-06 and ub-risk.move-has-no-destination-guard as third and fourth copies); L-02 + SRC-01 + PV-01 (all three critical, all three = the source-pane apply is rejected by the funnel as a no-op, so no ledger entry, no re-projection, no preview round). A planner working "Start here" top-to-bottom opens 38 tickets for ~28 defects, and in four of those cases two different people would write two different fixes for one function. Fix: give each cluster one id, list the co-filed ids under it, and restate the critical count.

*critical* — plans/BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md:43-133 (Start here lists both members of each pair), :244 vs :482 (CANVAS-01/GAP-01), :3452 vs :3222 (LANG-01/LI-02), :3484 vs :2504 (LANG-03/ctx-02 — identical Unity citation BuilderWindow.cs:2155-2205, identical Godot citation builder_edits.gd:635-657), :1740 vs :3002 (DM-01/shell.load-tree-veto), :1756 vs :1426 (DM-02/G-01), :1206 vs :2988 (L-01/shell.keyboard-focus-dead), :2044 vs :946 (FP-01/SM-01), :1222/:2722/:3766 (L-02/SRC-01/PV-01)

### CANVAS-04's "To build" reintroduces CANVAS-03: clip_text on the header title Label collapses it to 17 px — measured

CANVAS-04 prescribes "Give the header title Label `clip_text = true` and `text_overrun_behavior = OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS` like the signature row already has ... with clip_text the Label's minimum width is 0 and the card holds its declared width." That is exactly the mechanism CANVAS-03 identifies as a defect nine entries earlier. The signature Label survives it because it is a direct child of the section VBox and so is stretched to card width; the title Label is one of two-to-three children of an HBoxContainer where nothing carries an expand flag, so its minimum width becomes its size. Probe (Godot 4.7 headless, PanelContainer 300 wide > HBox > badge Label + title Label "ShoppingCartSummaryPanelWide" with clip_text + ellipsis): title size = (17, 29). Adding `size_flags_horizontal = SIZE_EXPAND_FILL` restores it to (193, 29). The recipe as written trades a card that is too wide for a card whose name is an ellipsis — and it would pass the entry's own proposed assertion ("a card with a 40-character title still measures card_width_for(lod) wide"). The recipe needs the expand flag, or a `custom_minimum_size.x`, in the same line.

*high* — plans/BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md:290 (the To build) against :264 (CANVAS-03's own diagnosis of the same mechanism); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/canvas_view.guitkx:138-149 (the HBox, no expand flag on any child) and :143 (the title Label); contrast :176-177 (the signature Label, an only child of the stretched VBox). Measured headless on Godot 4.7.

### CANVAS-07's ScrollContainer recipe collapses every capped section to zero height — and contradicts GP-11's correct recipe for the same fix

CANVAS-07 says "Wrap each section body in a `ScrollContainer` with `custom_minimum_size.y` unset and a max height enforced by the section's own `custom_minimum_size`/`clip_contents`." Both halves are wrong in Godot: `custom_minimum_size` is a floor, not a cap, and `clip_contents` affects painting, not layout. ScrollContainer::get_minimum_size only contributes a child's extent along axes where scrolling is DISABLED, so a vertically-scrolling ScrollContainer reports minimum height ~0 and a VBoxContainer gives it exactly that. Probe: a ScrollContainer holding 40 Labels (inner min 1316 px) inside a VBox reported min (0,0) and laid out at 61x0 — the section vanishes; setting `custom_minimum_size.y = 140` laid it out at 61x140. GP-11, the third copy of this same gap, gets it right ("custom_minimum_size.y = min(content, cap)"), and GAP-12 is a fourth statement that specifies neither. Whoever implements CANVAS-07 first ships a card with no sections. Same entry: "handle it in the host's `_handle_button` by checking `event.ctrl_pressed` before letting the scroller see the wheel" inverts Godot's GUI routing — a descendant ScrollContainer receives the wheel first and the host's `_gui_input` only sees what the descendant did not accept; only the entry's hedged alternative (set the scroller's mouse_filter) is reachable.

*high* — plans/BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md:340 (CANVAS-07's recipe) vs :850 (GP-11's correct one) vs :660 (GAP-12's third); measured headless on Godot 4.7; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_canvas_host.gd:379-384 (_gui_input is the host's only input path)

### The intro says 12 entries carry a superseding correction; 77 do — 65 of them on entries labelled CONFIRMED, and "Start here" quotes the superseded headline

"The result. 286 gaps. 267 confirmed by the adversarial pass, 12 judged overstated and carrying the skeptic's correction (which supersedes the original claim), 7 without a verdict." A cross-tab of the file says otherwise: 202 CONFIRMED with no correction, 65 CONFIRMED **with** a "Correction from the adversarial pass (supersedes the claim above)" block, 12 OVERSTATED with one, 7 UNVERIFIED. So a reader who trusts the framing treats 65 entries' headlines as the finding when the entry itself says they are superseded — and "Start here" reproduces the un-corrected headline verbatim. CANVAS-04 is the clean example: the headline says "a long module name doubles the card", the correction says only a long FILE name does because the signature is already clipped, and "Start here" is not affected only because CANVAS-04 is not critical. Fix: either fold each correction into its claim, or say plainly in the intro that 77 entries carry one and that the correction, not the heading, is the finding.

*high* — plans/BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md:7 (the claim); counts by awk over the file: 202 CONFIRMED/-, 65 CONFIRMED/CORR, 12 OVERSTATED/CORR, 7 UNVERIFIED/-; example at :282-294 (CANVAS-04 heading vs its correction)

Every directive operation is filed twice, once as LANG-## and once as ctx-##, with the same Unity citation and the same Godot citation: LANG-02≡ctx-01 (unwrap offered on every directive row, both critical), LANG-03≡ctx-02 (delete_clause middle clause, both critical), LANG-06≡ctx-03 ("Add @else" on an @if that has one), LANG-08≡ctx-04 (@match has no clause operations), LANG-13≡ctx-10 (an emptied header writes `@if ()`), LANG-15≡ctx-12≡SM-13 (@for seeds range(1) with no collection menu — three copies), LANG-14≡ctx-13≡LI-08 (no directive-drift warning against the 8-entry schema — three copies), and GP-04≡ctx-05 (the row menu is markup-shaped for every section). ### The canvas-geometry cluster is filed three times with two CONTRADICTORY "To build"s

CANVAS-01 (critical), GAP-01 (critical) and GP-12 (medium) are one defect: nothing measures the rendered card, so section_stack drives row_hit, card_at, Drag.resolve and edge_source_anchor. Their prescriptions disagree about the answer. CANVAS-01: add a measurement pass and "have `row_hit`, `card_at`, `on_title_bar`, `Drag.resolve` and `edge_source_anchor` consult `measured_rows` first and `section_stack` only as the pre-layout fallback". GP-12: "Keep the model as the layout/edge answer (it must stay zoom-invariant), but add a measurement reconciliation for hit-testing". Those produce different code for `edge_source_anchor` and different invariants for the saved layout — and GP-12's reservation is the correct one, because the saved layout is keyed on the zoom-invariant estimate (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:219-228 says so in its own comment). Whichever is right, the register must not ship both. A fourth entry (the lead "`edge_source_anchor` does not re-accumulate section tops for the LOD the way `row_hit` does") is the same seam again. Related and separable: CANVAS-02 ≡ GAP-04 exactly (drawn_height returns HEADER_H at Lod.PILL — one line, two high entries, two To builds).

### One missing `double_click` branch is filed four times, and the four entries specify four different signal shapes for it

CANVAS-19, GAP-09, GP-03 and SM-05 are all "there is no double-click on the canvas", and all four fixes are a branch in `_handle_button`'s MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT case. They do not agree on the interface: CANVAS-19 wants `row_activated(card_index, section, row_index)` plus a `card_activated`; GAP-09 wants the double-click to resolve a COMPONENT row and reuse `_on_library_framed`; GP-03 wants a dispatch by section inside the host; SM-05 wants `row_activated(card_index, section, row_index, at)` — with the extra `at` the other three omit and the inline editor needs. Implemented as four tickets this lands two signals with overlapping meaning, which is the exact class of defect GP-01 and CANVAS-05 are about. Merge into one entry that names the signal once. The same shape applies to the drop-hint trio CANVAS-06 (high) + GAP-02 (critical) + LIB-07 (high): one `_can_drop_data` position record and one paint in builder_canvas_edges._draw, three entries, three To builds.

### CANVAS-03's chip alternative ("autowrap_mode = AUTOWRAP_WORD with a MaxWidth of card_width-30") has no Godot analogue and makes the chip worse — measured

The entry offers two options: a `custom_minimum_size.x` (correct) "or `autowrap_mode = AUTOWRAP_WORD` with a `MaxWidth` of card_width-30, which is what Unity does". Godot Control has no max-width property; the only way to bound a Label's wrap width is to give it a width, which in an HFlowContainer means `custom_minimum_size.x` — i.e. the first option, not a second one. Taken literally the alternative is worse than the defect: probe (PanelContainer 340 wide > HFlowContainer > PanelContainer chip > Label "useState -> count, set_count" with AUTOWRAP_WORD and no minimum) gave chip size (29, 109) and label (17, 101) — the text wraps to roughly one character per line and the chip becomes a 109 px vertical string. Delete the alternative, or spell it as "custom_minimum_size.x = card_width - 30 plus autowrap so the pill wraps inside itself", which is what the Unity behaviour actually translates to.

### Dragging a file or a folder onto another folder re-files it.

**Status:** PARTIAL — spec lines 92-93

The gesture itself is wired for both row kinds. Two problems on top of the ones already registered: (1) NOT REGISTERED — re-filing the module you are currently looking at leaves `_focus_path` naming a path that no longer exists, so the source pane blanks, the folder pane deselects, the preview stops following and `Service.project(..., _focus_path)` re-roots the graph off a dead focus (GP-05's fallback). G-16 covers only modules that LEAVE the tree (delete/abort/restore) and explicitly lists `move_folder` as a site that DOES assign `_focus_path`, never noticing that `place_module` — the folder pane's own route — does not; L-09's *remediation* mentions 'the focus re-point' in passing but its finding is about card positions. tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:945-968 re-files `app.style.guitkx`, which is not the focus, so the suite cannot see it. (2) Already registered: dropping onto a FILE row is refused where Unity resolves it to that file's folder (FP-06); the destination is not type/owner-aware (FP-02); no collision guard (FP-01); no drop highlight (FP-07).

*high* — godot builder_folder_pane.gd:89-109 (`_get_drag_data` produces `{source:"module"|"folder", path}` for both row kinds), :112-156 (`_can_drop_data`/`_drop_data`/`_drop_target` accept only a FOLDER row), builder_window.gd:671-674 (`refile_requested` → `move_folder` / `place_module`). place_module: builder_window.gd:1725-1748; move_folder: :1668-1717. THE FOCUS DEFECT: `place_module` never re-points `_focus_path` — compare `move_folder`'s movers branch, which does (builder_window.gd:1708-1709). Downstream after re-filing the focused module: `reproject()` (:1745) rebuilds the pane, whose `rebuild()` restores `previously_selected` = the OLD path (builder_folder_pane.gd:163, 207-208) and `select_path` falls to `deselect_all()` (:286-289); `_source.refresh_from_model()` (:1746) finds no module at `_path` and calls `clear()` (builder_source_pane.gd:159-162); `_preview_pane._path` is never re-pointed; `_refresh_status` prints the dead path's file name (:2458). `move_folder`'s OWNER-delegation branch (:1683-1684) returns through `_move_one` and so drops the focus the same way.

### It adds and removes no imports: dragging X onto Y does not make Y use X, and the old parent keeps its import because its markup still references X.

**Status:** PARTIAL — spec lines 134-136

NOT IN THE REGISTER. The register's GAP-08 ("The kind chip is not a drag handle") reaches the opposite conclusion — it proposes building a canvas drag source that emits exactly this `{source:"module", path}` payload and calls `drop_module` "the ready-made sink" — without noticing that the folder pane already emits that payload and can already reach that sink. Unity cannot do this: its folder pane uses manual pointer capture and resolves the drop against its own rows (BuilderFolderPane.cs:246-316), so a folder-pane drag never leaves the pane, and BuilderDragService's payloads ("element:", "component:", "hook:", "stylemod:", "utilmod:") are produced only by the library. Two smaller consequences of the same over-permissive `_can_drop_data`: a FOLDER row dragged onto the canvas is accepted by the cursor and then silently ignored (`_on_canvas_drop`'s match has no "folder" arm), and a module dropped on empty canvas is refused with the toast "Couldn't move that module there" (:1055) — a message that tells the user the canvas is a move target, which contradicts the clause two lines above this one.

*high* — THE RE-FILE PATH HONOURS IT: builder_workspace.gd:431-462 only replaces existing specifier spans — no insertion, no deletion — and neither `place_module` (builder_window.gd:1725-1748) nor `move_folder` (:1668-1717) calls `Edits.ensure_import` or `Edits.remove_import`. THE DRAG ESCAPES THE PANE: builder_folder_pane.gd:104-109 returns `{source:"module", path}` through Godot's engine-wide drag, and builder_canvas_host.gd:457-458 `_can_drop_data` accepts ANY Dictionary carrying a "source" key; :461-462 forwards it to `dropped`, which builder_window.gd:1041-1055 routes on `"module"` to `drop_module` (:2353-2375) — which writes `style={ Export }` onto the row under the cursor (:2370) and then `Edits.ensure_import(...)` into that card's buffer (:2374) through `apply_edit`. So dragging X out of the folder tree and letting go over Y's card makes Y import X, in one ledger entry, on a file the user was not editing.

### "Colouring comes from language-server semantic tokens (markup structure plus merged C# classification) with a lexical fallback so identifiers, types, members, calls and numbers are always coloured, tokens or not."

**Status:** PARTIAL — spec lines 335-337

NEW, and it directly corrects a re-confirmed 'deliberate divergence'. The semantic-token half being answered lexically is legitimate and listed. But the clause is specific about what the FALLBACK must deliver — identifiers, types, members, calls and numbers — and the Godot tokenizer delivers exactly one of the five (numbers, :145-149) plus keywords, which the clause does not even ask for. Every identifier in an embedded GDScript body or a `{expr}` — every call, every member access, every type name, every local — renders in the default ink. That is precisely the state the Unity owner filed against and Unity fixed by name with ClassifyIdentifier. BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md:228 lists this as a re-confirmed correct divergence, asserting "Contract §8's 'markup structure plus merged C# classification' is answered by the tokenizer's gd_mode recursion" — true for the markup/gd split, false for the fallback clause in the same sentence, which that entry does not test. Fix is local: extend guitkx_tokenizer.gd's identifier branch with the four classifications and add `function`/`type`/`member` keys to the highlighter palette, sourced from EditorSettings `function_color` / `engine_type_color` / `member_variable_color` the way :39-55 already does. Secondary: :67-70 means a user who turned highlighting off for the .guitkx editor silently loses all colour in the builder's source pane, which the clause states unconditionally.

### Non-capability: "`@uss` and `Asset<T>` references added since the last Save resolve only after saving — the asset cache is disk-gated."

**Status:** ABSENT — spec lines 417-418

NEW, and worse than the non-capability it corresponds to. Unity's asset refs are disk-gated: they resolve after Save. Godot has no asset cache at all, so `res://` and `uid://` asset paths resolve immediately from disk — better than the reference. But a `~/`-rooted `@uss`/`@theme` NEVER resolves in the preview, saved or not, because the mirror re-roots it into the scratch tree where no asset was mirrored. MEASURED on Godot 4.7 headless against the real compiler and the real `scratch_root_for`: source `@theme "~/theme.tres"` for res://examples/demos/probe.guitkx compiles in the project and, through the preview's exact call shape, yields `ok=false` with `GUITKX0120 asset not found: res://__ruitk_builder_preview__~/theme.tres`. The module fails to build, and `_restrict_to_focus_closure` means every dependent fails with it — so a component that uses the family-idiomatic root-relative asset form shows nothing in the preview, forever, with a diagnostic naming a path the user never wrote. Fix is one line in `_sync_scratch`: also mirror (or symlink/copy) the asset the compiler will look for, or pass the REAL root for asset resolution while keeping the scratch root for specifiers. The register blesses the mirror design as a deliberate divergence at its line 222 without recording this cost.

### …clicking away commits.

**Status:** ABSENT — spec lines 166-167

DEAD, AND VERIFIED DEAD IN THE ASSEMBLED BUILDER. The commit-on-blur is wired to LineEdit.focus_exited (builder_inline_editor.gd:42 -> :121-124), which is the right hook in UI Toolkit and the wrong one in Godot. Godot's Viewport grabs keyboard focus only for the control a press DIRECTLY hits, and only when that control's focus_mode != FOCUS_NONE; it never walks ancestors and never RELEASES focus when the hit control is unfocusable. RuitkBuilderCanvasHost._init sets `mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` and never sets focus_mode, so it is FOCUS_NONE — meaning a click anywhere on the canvas is delivered to the host (its _gui_input fires, the row selection changes, a pan can start) while the LineEdit keeps focus, focus_exited never fires, and the edit is neither committed nor closed. Probed on Godot 4.7 twice: (a) synthetic hierarchy — a focused LineEdit beside a FOCUS_NONE/STOP full-rect Control, clicking the Control leaves `has_focus=true` and emits no focus_exited; (b) the real thing — RuitkBuilderWindow assembled with a seeded workspace, `inline_editor().open_at(...)` then a real InputEventMouseButton pressed+released into the viewport over the canvas: `canvas.focus_mode=0`, and after the click `editor open=true visible=true has_focus=true committed=[]`. Consequences beyond the lost commit: the editor stays FLOATING over the card while the canvas selects a different row under it, and it keeps its old token — so the deferred commit that eventually fires (from the next open_at, builder_inline_editor.gd:53-54) writes the earlier edit at a moment the user did not choose, into a row reference that ctx-07 already shows can be stale. Right-clicking to open the row menu likewise leaves it open, so a menu-dispatched delete can run while an editor holds a token pointing at the deleted row. Note this is a DIFFERENT defect from SM-06: SM-06 is about nothing ever GIVING focus to the builder Control; this is about the inline editor never LOSING it. The register assumes the blur path works — SM-10 (line 1070) reasons that 'commit() is called identically from text_submitted and from focus_exited … so the editor cannot tell Enter from a blur', which presupposes a blur that never arrives. Coverage: tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:730-800 calls editor.commit() as a method and never drives focus at all, so the suite is green over a dead path; tests/builder_parity.gd has no entry for it.

*high* — godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_inline_editor.gd:42 + :121-124 (focus_exited -> commit); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_canvas_host.gd:89-91 (_init sets mouse_filter = STOP, focus_mode never set — measured 0 at runtime); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:352-353 (editor parented to canvas_layer beside _canvas); unity Builder/Editor/Controls/BuilderInlineEditorOverlay.cs:176-192 (FocusOutEvent -> Close(commitIfChanged: true), which works because UI Toolkit's focus controller blurs on a pointer-down over a non-focusable element)

### "The menu item opens the builder with no tree, on a start screen offering the four module kinds."

**Status:** PARTIAL — spec lines 20-22

MISSED BY THE REGISTER. The Godot menu item does NOT open with no tree: `_open_builder` calls `open_tree(_builder_focus_path())`, and `_builder_focus_path()` returns whatever `.guitkx` the editor's main-screen view is currently showing (any path not under res://addons/). So opening the builder from Reactive UI Toolkit → Builder… while any project `.guitkx` is open in the editor lands on THAT file's whole tree, not on the start screen. The start screen is reached only by accident — when the `.guitkx` view happens to be empty. And because `_open_builder` gates re-opens on `focus_path().is_empty()` and there is no "close tree" / "new tree" command anywhere (MenuId is SAVE, ABORT, UNDO, REDO, FIT_VIEW, REVEAL, HISTORY, TRACE, HELP), once any tree is open the start screen is unreachable for the rest of the session except by aborting a wholly-unsaved tree. A user who wants to start a new UI from the menu cannot get to the four buttons. The choice is deliberate and argued in-file ("'Open the builder' means 'on what I am looking at'"), but it is an undocumented divergence: it is not in CLAUDE.md's divergence list, not in tests/builder_parity.gd's DELIBERATE table, and not in BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md. The four-kinds part of the clause, when the start screen is reached, is honoured (builder_window.gd:492-506 builds all four buttons).

### "The diagnostics console is scrollable" — measured against the builder's substitute console

**Status:** ABSENT — spec lines 342

NEW. `ItemList.auto_height = true` makes the control's minimum height equal its full content, so the list can never scroll — its scrollbar has nothing to scroll — and a VSplitContainer clamps the split to respect that minimum. A twenty-module tree with one broken shared import produces 1 failure + 19 skipped rows; `trace()` on a fifty-module tree produces fifty-plus. In both cases the console grows to full content height and squeezes the canvas, with no cap, no scroll, and no way to shrink it short of hiding the whole pane. This is UB-77's failure mode arriving from the other direction: Unity's console could not show enough, Godot's cannot show less. Fix: drop `auto_height`, give the list a `custom_minimum_size.y` of ~90 and let its own VScrollBar do the work. The register touches this file twice (console.never-hides, toolbar.trace-crashes) and neither notices the growth.

### …hovering one highlights every usage of those names in the markup rows…

**Status:** PARTIAL — spec lines 154-155

THREE DEFECTS THE REGISTER DOES NOT NAME, all in the projection/view layer and all independent of the known reachability problem (CANVAS-01/CANVAS-03). (1) THE HIGHLIGHT IS NOT CARD-SCOPED. canvas_view.guitkx:61 passes `highlight_names` to EVERY CanvasCard unconditionally, while the two lines directly above it (:59-60) gate `sel_section`/`sel_row` on `i == selected` — the gating idiom is present and was not applied. Unity carries `traceOwner` beside `traceStates` and every consumer tests `traceOwner == index` (CanvasView.uitkx:53, :1001-1003, :753). So hovering `useState → sel` on card A lights every markup row on every OTHER card that happens to mention `sel` — a claim about identity that the language does not make, since `sel` in another module is a different variable. (2) THE CODE ISLAND IS NEVER HIGHLIGHTED. The SETUP rows are styled `row_selected() … else row_plain()` with no highlight branch (canvas_view.guitkx:257), where Unity has a third state, CodeIslandTrace, keyed on `RowMatchesTrace(join(node.IslandLines), traceStates)` (CanvasView.uitkx:751-755). The state a hook returns is used in the setup block at least as often as in markup, and that is exactly the half Godot does not warm. (3) THE HIGHLIGHT IS NEVER CLEARED WHEN THE POINTER LEAVES THE CANVAS. `_track_hover` runs only from `_handle_motion` (builder_canvas_host.gd:505), and there is no `mouse_exited` connection and no NOTIFICATION_MOUSE_EXIT branch anywhere in the host (its only `_notification` is at :334). Move off a chip onto the source pane, the library or the toolbar and the rows stay lit indefinitely; `show_graph` does not reset it either, so the stale highlight survives a re-projection. Unity clears on the chip's own onPointerLeave (CanvasView.uitkx:599-605). Coverage: tests/builder_canvas_test.gd:226-256 exercises `_bound_names` and `row_mentions` as pure functions only — never the card scope, never the island, never a leave — and tests/builder_parity.gd:100 maps this whole contract line to the token `func row_mentions`, which is the one piece that is correct.

### Existing markup rows drag to reorder or re-parent, **moving their whole line range with re-indentation**.

**Status:** PARTIAL — spec lines 264-265

NEW — the register has no entry for the re-indentation half and every existing move test in builder_edits_test.gd:242-303 moves a SINGLE-LINE row, so the case is untested. The whole line range does move, but only its FIRST line is re-indented: `markup.strip_edges()` removes the first line's leading indent and the destination indent is prefixed once, while every subsequent line keeps its original indentation verbatim. Verified in Godot 4.7 — moving a two-child `<HBoxContainer>` from depth 1 to depth 3 gives `<HBoxContainer>` at 12 spaces with its `<Button>` at 8 and its `</HBoxContainer>` at 6; moving an `@if`/`@else` construct into a container leaves the `}` / `} @else {` / `}` lines dangling to the LEFT of their own head. Both still compile (guitkx markup is whitespace-insensitive), and format-on-save (workspace.gd:45-57) would eventually normalise it — so this is text mangling the user sees on the card and in the source pane until the next Save, not a compile break. Unity's MoveLineRange re-indents every line, which is why the clause says so.

### "The tree is journalled while work is unsaved…"

**Status:** PARTIAL — spec lines 394

NEW. Godot's journal is TIMER-driven, not change-driven, and has no 'anything changed since the last capture' test. So a dirty tree re-serialises itself to user:// every five seconds for as long as the session lasts, whether or not a single character moved. It keeps going after the user closes the builder, because plugin.gd:435 wires `close_requested` to `hide()` and a hidden Window's children still get `_process` — measured on Godot 4.7 headless (a Control child of a hidden Window ticked 2 times in 2 frames). Leave the builder open with one unsaved edit and Godot writes the whole tree to disk ~720 times an hour, invisibly. The trade is not all bad — timer-driven capture is FRESHER than Unity's (Unity can leave the last burst of edits unjournalled indefinitely once the change stream stops) — so the fix is a guard on 'the tree changed since the last capture', not a change of driver.

*low* — godot chrome/builder_window.gd:936-947 (`_journal_tick`: bail if not `workspace.has_unsaved_changes()`, else write once per `JOURNAL_INTERVAL_MSEC` = 5000), :300-301 (`_process` -> `tick()`), :917 (`tick` -> `_journal_tick`); document/builder_journal.gd:40-54 (capture is guarded on has_unsaved_changes and serialises the WHOLE tree). unity BuilderWindow.cs:6232-6245 drives it from `OnWorkspaceChanged` with the same 5 s throttle — i.e. only when something actually changed.

### "…a session that ended cleanly leaves no journal."

**Status:** PARTIAL — spec lines 396-397

NEW. A save that fails part-way through — a locked file, a read-only file on disk, a refused DirAccess.rename_absolute, a full disk — still clears the crash journal in Godot, so the recovery file is destroyed at exactly the moment recovery becomes most likely to be needed. Godot cannot use Unity's try/catch (no exceptions), but `save_all`'s early return is the signal and it is discarded: `save()` neither inspects it nor distinguishes it from a complete save (which is also why nothing is toasted). Mitigation that keeps this low rather than high: `_journal_tick` re-captures within 5 s if the process survives, so the loss window is bounded unless the failure is what kills the editor. G-03 names the unconditional `Journal.clear()` but for the different failure mode of opening some other tree later; the failed-save case is not covered anywhere.

### "Modules that live in immutable packages open read-only"

**Status:** PARTIAL — spec lines 402-403

NEW, and arguably a deliberate simplification rather than a defect — but it is undocumented either way. Unity carves Embedded and Local packages OUT of read-only precisely so a package the user is developing stays editable. Godot's rule has no such carve-out: `res://addons/` is a blanket immutable zone, so an addon the user is actively authoring — including this repo's own dogfooded `addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/canvas_view.guitkx` — opens read-only in the builder and can never be edited there. The comment at builder_workspace.gd:111-115 asserts the equivalence to "a non-embedded Unity package" without noticing that Unity's rule is specifically about non-embedded ones.

Unity also toasts the resulting folder afterwards for the same reason ("Created X in <folder> - applies on Save"), which the Godot leg omits too (G-13).

## Completeness findings

27 findings from three critics: a sweep of every file under `Builder/Editor/` for behaviour no area claimed, a read of the Unity defect register for portable design traps, and an audit of Godot's own test gates.

### Completeness critic over every file in r

#### The canvas/folder-pane style drop writes the RAW export name, not a disambiguated binding — so applying a style to the component it is named after redeclares the file's own name

Unity's `ApplyStyleModuleToRow` calls `ImportAliasFor(...)` first and applies `style={<alias>.<export>}`, with an entire doc comment about why: "PascalCasing the module name ... walks straight into the component's own name: a style module called someComponent, imported into SomeComponent, produced `SomeComponent.container` — which binds to the COMPONENT and fails. That pairing is legal, and the folder convention positively encourages it, so the ALIAS is what has to give." It also reuses whatever alias an already-imported module was given, so a second element styled from the same module references a name the file actually bound.

The Godot port has TWO doors into the same gesture and only one of them does this. `drop_module_export` (the LIBRARY drag) correctly calls `Edits.bind_export`, which builds a `taken` set from the file's imports AND its own `analyzed_decls` and falls back to `<name>Style`, `<name>2`, … `drop_module` (the FOLDER-PANE drag onto the canvas, reachable via the `{source:"module"}` payload the folder pane arms) does neither: it writes `Edits.set_attribute(text, row, "style", export_name, false)` with the raw export name, then `Edits.ensure_import(...)`, which does no collision aliasing at all (it delegates straight to `_ensure_import_line` with `entries == remotes`). Concrete failure: drag `card.style.guitkx` (exporting `Card`) from the folder pane onto a row of `Card.guitkx` and the buffer gets `style={Card}` plus `import { Card } from "./card.style"` — the module's own declaration name redeclared, and the style attribute pointing at the component. The two paths must share one binding routine; `bind_export` already is it.

*high* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:4180-4246 (ApplyStyleModuleToRow → ImportAliasFor first), :4041-4113 (ImportAliasFor, the `taken` set and the already-imported reuse) | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:2353-2375 (drop_module: :2363 `exports[0]`, :2370 raw `export_name` as the style value, :2374 `ensure_import`) vs :2299-2323 (drop_module_export, which uses `bind_export`); edits/builder_edits.gd:342-350 (ensure_import — no `taken` set) vs :406-443 (bind_export — has one); chrome/builder_folder_pane.gd:104 (the `{source:"module"}` payload) → chrome/builder_window.gd:1053-1055

#### `insert_setup_line` only finds a COMPONENT declaration, so "+ hook", "+ code" and every library hook drop are dead no-ops on hook, util and value cards — and BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md `GP-06` states the opposite mechanism, which invalidates its prescribed fix

Unity's hook drop is `InsertBeforeLastReturn` gated only on `node.Kind == Style` ("Style modules have no hooks."), so a hook module or util module receives the line. Godot routes all three affordances through `Edits.insert_setup_line`, whose anchor `_body_open_of` iterates `Compiler.analyzed_decls(source)["decls"]` and `continue`s on every decl whose kind is not `"component"`, returning -1 otherwise — and the compiler classifies `export use_x() -> Variant {…}` as kind `"hook"` and `export helper(x:int) -> int {…}` as kind `"util"` (guitkx.gd:526-534). Probed headlessly on Godot 4.7: `insert_setup_line` returns the source UNCHANGED for both a hook module and a util module. `_on_card_add` then hits `if after == before: return` with no toast, and `canvas_view.guitkx:198` renders the BODY section (and therefore both chips) for every `card.kind != 2`, i.e. for HOOK, UTIL, VALUE, MODULE and UNKNOWN cards. So on every non-component card both chips are silently dead buttons, and the library's hook drop/click is dead there too.

This also corrects the register: `GP-06` asserts "the line is written into the buffer and neither shown nor editable", and prescribes extending the island projection to hook/util modules as the fix. Nothing is written, so that fix alone would leave both chips dead — `_body_open_of` has to accept non-component declarations in the same change.

#### UB-115 reintroduced: the inline attribute-value editor has no expression/literal flip, so typing `{count}` into a quoted attribute writes the literal string `text="{count}"`

Unity's `OnAttrValueEdited` keeps the wrapper outside the field AND reads the user's own wrapper back: a typed value that starts and ends with `{ }` sets `expr = true` and strips the braces; one wrapped in `" "` sets `expr = false` and strips the quotes. The recorded reason is UB-115 verbatim — "typing an EXPRESSION into a quoted attribute used to nest it — {value} became text=\"{value}\", a literal brace string. A value the user wrapped in braces themselves means 'make this an expression'."

The Godot port implements the first half and not the second. `_search_purpose == "edit_attribute"` opens the inline editor on `spec["value"]` (wrapper stripped) and carries `quoted` from the ORIGINAL spelling, and `_on_inline_committed` passes that same `quoted` straight to `Edits.set_attribute`. There is no branch anywhere that inspects the typed text for a wrapper. Probed on Godot 4.7: `set_attribute(src, row, "text", "{count}", true)` on `<Label text="hi" />` produces `<Label text="{count}" />` — exactly UB-115's output. The reverse (typing `"hello"` into an expression slot) yields `{"hello"}`. The port's own comment at builder_window.gd:1391-1393 claims the wrapper-outside-the-field design makes this impossible, which is true only of double-wrapping, not of the flip. Nothing in the register mentions UB-115.

#### No target-module-kind rules on any drop: Unity refuses a style import onto a non-component, a util import onto a style or util, and a hook onto a style; the Godot port has none of the three and silently writes or silently no-ops

Unity's `OnCanvasRowDrop` gates the sink on the TARGET node's kind before any edit: `stylemod` onto a non-Component → "Style imports go on components."; `utilmod` onto a Style or Util → "Util imports go on components and hook modules."; `hook` onto a Style → "Style modules have no hooks."; plus `AlreadyImports` → "<name> is already imported." These are refusals, not messages — the edit does not happen.

Neither Godot door checks the target's kind. `drop_module` refuses only self-drop and an empty export list; `drop_module_export` refuses only self-drop and a missing source card. So dropping a util module onto a style card writes an import into a style module — which the port's own comment at builder_window.gd:2351 says is GUITKX2304 ("an import added without the use") — i.e. the gesture produces a file that will not compile, from an action Unity refuses outright. The hook-onto-style case is right by accident (`insert_setup_line` finds no component declaration and no-ops) rather than by rule, and reports the generic "Couldn't place <X> there."

The register's `GAP-10` quotes all four of these strings, but frames the whole entry as message quality ("three generic toasts") and its "To build" asks only for a `{ok, reason}` return shape — the semantic gates themselves are never asked for. `ctx-05` and the addendum at :4337 cover the ROW-kind gate; the CARD-kind gate is a different question and is nowhere.

#### `BuilderWorkspace.rescan` is a documented Callable that is never assigned, and `touched_disk` is computed before the write — so a builder Save tells the editor nothing at all, and a content-only Save does not even try

Unity's save path is announced to the host by construction: `EnsureDirectory`/`EnsureAssetFolder` create folders THROUGH the AssetDatabase so they have GUIDs (UB-204), `MoveAsset` re-homes files, and the resulting import fires `BuilderAssetEvents.UitkxImported`, which is what re-runs the source generator and feeds `OnUitkxImported` back into the builder.

The Godot leg models the same handoff as one injected callable: `var rescan := Callable()` at builder_workspace.gd:43, documented at :40 as "Asked to rescan after a batch of writes. The plugin wires this to the editor's …" and called once at :547-548. `grep -rn "rescan\s*=" addons/ tests/` returns NOTHING — the plugin creates the builder at plugin.gd:429-437 and never assigns it. So the one outbound notification the builder has is a dead wire.

Underneath that sits a second bug that would survive the wiring: `touched_disk = touched_disk or not module.is_on_disk()` (:533) is evaluated BEFORE `_write_text`, inside the `if not module.is_on_disk() or module.is_dirty()` branch — so a dirty module that already exists on disk leaves the flag false, and the gate `if touched_disk and rescan.is_valid()` is not even reached for the most common save there is. The port self-heals only because the RUNTIME addon runs its own independent watch-poll sweep (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit/plugin.gd:61,154), which is luck, not design. This is precisely the class `ub-risk.unwired-second-routes` was written to catch, and it is not in the register.

#### Closing the builder window never unmounts the live preview: the user's component keeps rendering, running effects and holding signal connections inside the editor indefinitely

Unity's `OnDisable` disposes the whole preview stack when the window goes away: `_canvasHost?.Unmount(); _previewPane?.Dispose(); _previewCompiler?.Dispose();`.

The Godot builder deliberately HIDES its Window rather than freeing it (plugin.gd:435, so unsaved work survives a close) — but the only call to `preview.teardown()` in the entire addon is `builder_window.gd:145-146 _exit_tree()`, which by that design never runs on a close. The Control stays in the scene tree, so `_process` keeps calling `tick()` (compile rounds, journal ticks), and `_root` — a live `RuitkRoot.create(container, V.fc(script.render, props))` — is never unmounted: the previewed component's effects, timers, `useAnimate`/`useSfx` and signal connections keep running on the editor's shared scheduler for the rest of the editor session, with no window showing them. The scratch mirror under `res://__ruitk_builder_preview__~/` likewise stays populated on disk.

The register's addendum at :4328 notices `teardown()` "runs only from `_exit_tree` … so in normal use it never runs at all between sessions", but files it as cross-tree cache staleness on `open_tree`. The lifecycle consequence — a hidden window keeps a live component mounted — is a different and larger claim, and the fix is a different place: `NOTIFICATION_VISIBILITY_CHANGED` / the Window's `close_requested` should `preview.unmount()` (not `teardown()`, which would also drop the caches the session wants to keep).

#### No save-batch instrumentation and no gate proving an editing session touches zero project files — the VE-06 acceptance numbers have no Godot analogue

`BuilderSaveMetrics.cs` is a permanent `[InitializeOnLoad]` instrument, not a debug aid: it logs every save batch with its file count and HMR state, arms a flag, and logs the reload that follows, "so a validation session produces the acceptance numbers (N edits -> 0 reloads; 1 save -> 1 reload; abort -> 0; HMR-active save -> 0) straight from the console without manual counting."

The Godot translation of that acceptance set is sharper here than in Unity, because the builder writes into `res://` continuously: the preview mirrors the whole tree to `res://__ruitk_builder_preview__~/` on every compile round. The invariant that has to hold is "N builder edits cause zero compiles of real project files; one Save causes one sweep" — and it rests entirely on the double-hiding (`~` for the importer, `.gdignore` for `find_all`) that builder_preview.gd:491-500 documents at length as load-bearing, warning that without it the sweep compiles the mirror, collides every component with the real one (GUITKX2106), and the duplicate-binding remediation DELETES the real generated `.gd`. ### Completeness critic over the Unity defec

#### A continuation clause is a drag source: `@elif`/`@else`/`@case`/`@default` can be dragged out of its construct, and the file stops parsing

`_get_drag_data` (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_canvas_host.gd:466-487) arms a ROW drag for ANY row in `Section.MARKUP`, which after this port's directive model includes every clause head row. `drop_row` (chrome/builder_window.gd:2330-2346) hands it to `Edits.move` (edits/builder_edits.gd:190-211), which cuts `_line_start(row.at) .. _line_end(row.end_at-1)`. For a continuation clause that span is the clause ALONE: `_walk_if` sets `close_at = _body_close_at(source, body_at)` for k>0 and for `@else` (canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:676-678, :686-690), and `_directive_head` (:810-828) states the consequence in its own comment — "A row's span is what a delete removes and what a move carries". So dragging the `@else` of an `@if`/`@else` cuts `@else { ... }` and pastes it as a child of whatever element was under the cursor: an orphan `@else` with no `@if`, and an `@if` whose closing brace no longer has its continuation. `can_place` only ever inspects the TARGET, never the source, so nothing refuses it; `apply_edit` records it as one undoable entry and Save writes it. The port has the fact it needs — `Graph.Line.clause_index` — and reads it in exactly two places, both in the row context menu (chrome/builder_window.gd:1097, :1103); the drag path never asks. The same gap has a second face: nothing stops the ONLY child of a directive body being dragged out, leaving `@if (c) { return ( ) }` — which is ctx-14's shape reached by the drag path ctx-14 explicitly does not cover. Fix: refuse a ROW drag whose source row is `kind == DIRECTIVE and clause_index > 0` in `_get_drag_data` (cheapest, and it also suppresses the ghost), and belt-and-braces refuse it in `Edits.move` the way `set_directive_header` already refuses a non-directive row at builder_edits.gd:321.

*high* — The rule is written down in the reference and was skipped: UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md §8.1 "Move/drag rules" — "A `ClauseIndex == 0` head drags the WHOLE construct … A `ClauseIndex > 0` head is **not draggable** (an `@else` cannot live anywhere else — today it can be dragged into garbage, UB-02)". The port adopted the rest of §8.1 verbatim (clause rows instead of `Attach` badge-stamping, `clause_index`, construct-span-on-head vs clause-span-on-continuation, per-kind badges) and left this one clause out. UB-02 lists it as one of five confirmed consequences of the badge model. Godot: canvas/builder_canvas_host.gd:466-487; chrome/builder_window.gd:2330-2346, :1097, :1103; edits/builder_edits.gd:190-211, :55-70 (`can_place` checks the target only); canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:676-678, :686-690, :810-828. Register: ctx-14 covers only the DELETE path; GAP-05 covers dropping ONTO a continuation clause; no entry covers dragging one AWAY. Gate: tests/builder_parity.gd:79 `["drag sources", "func _get_drag_data"]` is green over the token, and no case in tests/builder_edits_test.gd drives a clause row through `move`.

#### `drop_module` writes the raw export name where `drop_module_export` writes a collision-avoided binding — UB-147 reintroduced on one of the two module-drop routes, and the register endorses it

There are two module-drop implementations. `drop_module_export` (chrome/builder_window.gd:2299-2325), reached from the library pane, calls `Edits.bind_export` (edits/builder_edits.gd:406-440) and writes `style={ binding }` — `bind_export` collects every name the file already means (its own `analyzed_decls` plus every existing import's local and namespace bindings) and picks a non-colliding alias, keeping whatever alias the module already has. `drop_module` (chrome/builder_window.gd:2353-2375), reached from the canvas/folder-pane module drag at :1053-1055, does not: it takes `var export_name := str(source_card.exports[0])` and writes `Edits.set_attribute(text, row, "style", export_name, false)` plus `Edits.ensure_import(..., [export_name])`. Drop `card.style.guitkx` (exporting `Card`) onto an element of `Card.guitkx` and the import binds `Card` into a file that already declares `Card` — the exact redeclaration `bind_export`'s own doc comment describes: "a style module and the component it belongs to are named by two conventions that collapse onto one identifier by construction". `_validate_name` (chrome/builder_window.gd:1783-1786) makes that name pair legal on purpose, which is precisely the sequence Unity walked (UB-145 legalised the pair, UB-147 was its immediate consequence). Two further divergences in the same function: it ignores `source_card.kind` on the import branch, so a HOOK module dropped on a card gets `import { useX }` and no call site; and it takes `exports[0]` blind where Unity asks which export when a module has several (UB-146). Fix: delete `drop_module`'s own body and route it through `drop_module_export`, which already handles style-onto-element, import-onto-card, self-containment refusal and the binding.

*high* — UB-147 (CRITICAL): "a star import's alias was the module name PascalCased … `SomeComponent.container` resolved to the component type … FIX: `ImportAliasFor` chooses a name that cannot collide with something the file already means — the importing component's own name and every binding its existing imports introduce." Godot has that fix in `bind_export` (edits/builder_edits.gd:406-440) and one of two callers uses it. Register audit: BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md:602 (GAP-08 "To build") states "the payload `_on_canvas_drop` ALREADY handles (chrome/builder_window.gd:1053-1055 -> `drop_module`), which already does style-onto-element and import-onto-card and refuses self-containment (:2353-2372). Note `drop_module` already uses `source_card.exports[0]`, matching Unity's CardDragName rule" — the register inspects this exact function, endorses it, and would have GAP-08's fix feed the kind-chip drag into it. No register entry mentions `bind_export` at all except BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md:1434, which cites it as a model to imitate.

#### The preview mirror and the built-script cache are reconciled only inside a round that has a TEXT-dirty module, so any structural change reconciles nothing — and re-opening a tree runs the whole session off the previous one's scripts

`compile_dirty` (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/preview/builder_preview.gd:146-240) computes `dirty` purely by comparing each module's `buffer_text` against `_compiled_from`, and returns at :165-166 (`if dirty.is_empty(): return null`) BEFORE `_ensure_scratch_root()` at :170 and `_sync_scratch(by_path)` at :182. `_sync_scratch` (:424-450) is the only thing that prunes `_mirrored`, `_compiled_from`, `_built` and the mirror files, and its own doc says why it must run — "A stale mirror is worse than none — a deleted module left behind keeps satisfying the import that should have started failing." But a DELETION moves no text, so `dirty` is empty and the sync never runs: the deleted module's `.guitkx` shadow, its generated `.gd`, its `_built` GDScript and its `_compiled_from` entry all survive, and `built_script(deleted_path)` (:288-289) goes on answering. Compounded by the open path: `open_tree` (chrome/builder_window.gd:762) calls the STATIC `Preview.clear_scratch()`, which deletes the mirror FILES, but never `preview.teardown()` (preview/builder_preview.gd:590-599), which is what clears the three caches. Re-open the same tree and `load_tree` restores buffers identical to `_compiled_from`, so `compile_dirty` returns null on every tick, nothing is ever written to the mirror, and `select_module`'s forced round (chrome/builder_window.gd:2170-2171) is skipped because `built_script` is non-null — the session renders entirely from the previous session's in-memory scripts against an empty scratch root. Fix: hoist `_sync_scratch` above the dirty test (it is cheap — it early-continues on unchanged text with the file present), or make the tree's module SET part of the dirty test; and have `open_tree` call `preview.teardown()` rather than the static `clear_scratch()`.

*high* — The invariant this violates is the file's own opening claim (preview/builder_preview.gd:5-17): "THE WHOLE TREE IS MIRRORED … A preview that compiles differently from the build is the one thing a preview must not do", and CLAUDE.md's "Cleared on teardown and on open" — which on open clears the files but not the caches keyed to them. This is UB-159's shape ("nothing owned 'which assembly is the current build' … the pane guessed") plus UB-143/150's ("a module that has never been written fails the existence test") in the port's own terms. Register audit: BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md:222 lists the mirror as a re-confirmed deliberate divergence — "This is the one place the Godot leg is structurally ahead of the reference, and it should stay that way" — citing `:419-450 _sync_scratch` and `:498-508 _ensure_scratch_root` without reaching the guard at :165-166 that decides whether either runs. None of PV-01..PV-18 mentions the dirty gate or the open-path cache survival.

#### `wrap_in_directive` and `wrap_in_match` are LINE-based, in the one file whose class doc claims span-exactness as its advantage over Unity and names the exact failure line granularity causes

`edits/builder_edits.gd:4-15` states the design: "SPAN-EXACT. Each operation is addressed by a row from the graph projection, and every row carries the absolute offsets of what it came from … The Unity leg works in whole LINES, because its parser does not surface positions, and pays for it wherever two things share one: a self-closing tag on the same line as its parent, an attribute beside a directive head." Two operations do not honour it. `wrap_in_match` (:690-716) and `wrap_in_directive` (:847-880) both address by `row.source_line` / `row.end_line` (:695-697, :852-854) and rewrite whole lines; every other operation in the file uses `row.at` / `row.end_at`. So wrapping the `<Label>` in `<HBoxContainer><Label text="a" />` — parent open tag and child sharing one line, which the language allows and the formatter only normalises at Save (document/builder_workspace.gd:44-54, `format_on_save`) — carries the parent's open tag into the directive body while its close tag stays outside it, producing unbalanced markup rather than a wrapped child. Where the parent's whole element fits on the line, the wrap silently changes the meaning instead: the parent becomes conditional, not the row the user pointed at. Neither wrap consults `can_place` or the row kind, so this compounds with ctx-05 (an import row or hook chip reaching the same function). Fix: rewrite both to splice at `row.at` / `row.end_at` like `insert`/`remove`/`move`, computing the indent from `_indent_of(source, row.at)` which is already there.

*medium* — The trap is the root cause of the class UB-02 and UB-116 both sit in — a row addressed at the wrong granularity — and the file names it explicitly as the reason for its own design. `grep -n "source_line\|end_line" edits/builder_edits.gd` returns exactly four hits, all four inside these two functions (:695, :696, :852, :853). Register: BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md discusses `wrap_in_directive` at :2550 (ctx-05, wrong row kind), :2536 and :3564 (ctx-04/LANG-08, `wrap_in_match` seeds one arm), :2666 (ctx-12, `@for` collection binding) — never its addressing granularity, and never the shared-line case.

#### Every `@for`/`@while` the builder seeds trips GUITKX0106, because the wrap gives the body no `key` — and the console only shows errors, so the warning is invisible

`Edits.WRAPS` (edits/builder_edits.gd:675-682) seeds `@for (item in range(1))`, and `wrap_in_directive` (:847-880) copies the wrapped lines verbatim into the new body. The compiler warns on every loop body whose returned root carries no `key`: `guitkx.gd:1732` ("element returned in @for/@while has no `key` -- add key= so reordered children reconcile correctly"), with the fragment and expression variants at :1727 and :1729 and the sibling GUITKX0019 rule at :1736. So the first thing a user does after "Wrap in… @for" is produce a warning they are never shown — LANG-20 establishes that the console reports one first-ERROR line per failed module and never warnings, and the preview still compiles green because GUITKX0106 is a WARNING. The consequence is a real runtime one, not cosmetic: unkeyed loop children mis-reconcile on reorder, which is the whole reason the diagnostic exists. `key` is reachable only as one row in the attribute menu (`Attributes.STRUCTURAL`, edits/builder_attributes.gd:21-25) that nothing points the user at. Fix: when the wrap header is a loop, seed `key={ item }`-shaped guidance on the wrapped row (or, better, seed the key from the collection menu ctx-12 asks for, which is where the binder name is known) and route GUITKX0106/0019 to the console; at minimum, surface warnings for the wrapped module.

*medium* — This is UB-03's second half generalised — "`@if`/`@switch` are node-valued and `@for`/`@foreach`/`@while` are array-valued, and the builder must know which it is inserting and where arrays are legal" — restated for this language, where the array-ness shows up as the per-iteration key requirement rather than UITKX0025. §8.1's capability table encodes the same distinction (`if`/`switch` yield node, `foreach`/`for`/`while` yield array). Godot: addons/reactive_ui_toolkit/guitkx/guitkx.gd:1723-1737; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_edits.gd:675-682, :847-880; edits/builder_attributes.gd:21-25. Register: ctx-12 and LANG-15 cover only the collection-binding half of UB-03 ("`@for` seeds `range(1)` and never asks what to iterate"); `grep -n "GUITKX0106\|keyed\|key=" plans/BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md` finds nothing on this.

#### "Delete this entry" on a style EXPORT HEAD deletes the whole export block, under an entry-shaped label and with no confirmation

The row menu's EXPORTS branch (chrome/builder_window.gd:1083-1090) builds exactly two items — "Add entry..." and "Delete this entry" — for EVERY row the section holds, and DELETE_ROW dispatches `Edits.remove(before, row)` (:1141-1143). But `_fill_export_detail` (canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:897-906) appends an EXPORT HEAD row per declaration whose span is `dm["at"] .. dm["next"]` — the entire declaration, correctly so, since `Edits.remove` is span-exact. So right-clicking `export var Card := {` and picking an item labelled "Delete this entry" removes the whole style block, every entry in it, in one click, silently and with nothing to distinguish it from deleting the single line the label describes. Unity ships these as two differently-labelled operations for exactly this reason, and had to teach its parser to record the head's extent to offer the second one at all. Fix: branch the EXPORTS menu on the row's badge — `Graph.Badge.STYLE_HEADER`/EXPORT head gets "Delete style <name>" (and should confirm, since it is many lines), an entry line gets "Delete entry", and the synthetic "+ entry" row (LANG-17) gets neither.

*medium* — UB-183 (SHIPPED): "Right-click did nothing on style rows … It now offers 'Delete entry' on an entry line and 'Delete style <name>' on the export head, which needed the head to carry its block's EXTENT: `ParseStyleDetail` now records where the export closes, so deleting it is one range rather than a walk each caller repeats." Godot: chrome/builder_window.gd:1083-1090, :1141-1143; canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:897-906. Register: ctx-05's adversarial correction notes only that `_on_row_context` "special-cases only EXPORTS" and never examines what the two items in that branch do; LANG-17 covers the synthetic "+ entry" row's delete ("a synthetic Line at offset 0 — selecting it and pressing Delete removes the file's first line") and nothing else in the section; `grep -n "Delete entry\|export head" plans/BUILDER_PARITY_GAPS.md` returns no match.

#### reproject() slams zoom and re-centres the camera on twelve gestures that are not "opening a tree" — and parity entry :106 is green over it

`reproject()` ends with `if not layout.has_saved_view and not graph.cards.is_empty(): _canvas.zoom = Metrics.DEFAULT_ZOOM; _centre_when_sized()` (builder_window.gd:838-844). `has_saved_view` is set in only two places — `builder_canvas_layout.gd:159` (`save()`) and `:278` (a stored layout was read back) — and `_capture_layout()` has exactly two callers: `_on_card_moved` (builder_window.gd:1033) and `save()` (:1978). Meanwhile `reproject()` re-reads the layout from `user://` every call (`layout = CanvasLayout.for_graph(graph)`, :823 — GP-08's observation), so `has_saved_view` is re-derived as false on every reprojection until the user drags a card or saves. `reproject()` has thirteen call sites: open (:755, :771), create (:1890), rename (:1911), create_module (:1928), folder move (:1714, :1745, :1755), place-the-tree (:2072), abort (:2082), undo/redo replay (:2111), delete (:2435), and :958. So on any freshly opened tree, pan and zoom somewhere, then create/rename/delete/move/undo anything, and the camera jumps back to the graph's centre at DEFAULT_ZOOM 0.75 (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:45). Unity cannot do this: BuilderCanvasHost mount persists the adoption immediately (`if (_config.AdoptUnplaced(_graph)) _config.Save()`), so the saved-view flag is true from the first mount. GP-08 records the POSITION half of this same reset (`seed_positions` re-running over the new node set) and its "To build" fixes only the adoption persistence; the camera/zoom half is unrecorded, and fixing GP-08 as written would not fix it. Parity entry tests/builder_parity.gd:106 ["a tree with no saved layout opens at Layer 2", "func _centre_when_sized"] is green over a function whose prose describes one of thirteen call sites. No suite drives `reproject()` twice and asserts the camera held; builder_canvas_test.gd:444-478 exercises the layout store directly and never through the window.

#### `["FormatDirtyBuffers", "format_on_save"]` answers a window operation with a workspace boolean, and the token is satisfied by a doc comment

The register found exactly one name/answer mismatch in the checklist — `["MoveModuleToFolder", "func drop_module"]` at :33, where `drop_module` is "Drops a MODULE onto an element" and the real answer is `place_module` (register line 2104). There is a second. Unity's `FormatDirtyBuffers` is a BuilderWindow operation: it formats each dirty session's buffer, runs the writes through the ledger and re-projects, which is why G-04 exists ("Format-on-save mutates every dirty buffer behind the UI's back: not through the funnel, not in the ledger, no re-projection"). Parity :107 answers it with `format_on_save` — a plain `bool` member on the workspace (builder_workspace.gd:54). Two consequences. (a) The entry can never notice G-04, because a flag is not an operation: the gate is structurally blind to the exact defect this checklist row covers. (b) The token is not `func`-prefixed and not unique — it matches the doc comment at builder_workspace.gd:47 ("matching the editor's own `format_on_save`") and the declaration at :54 as well as the one consumer at :740, so deleting `_format()` and its call site entirely leaves three hits and a green gate. SM-20's "Godot specifics" notes in passing that "any token that appears in a doc comment also passes — worth checking when picking replacements" but never identifies an entry where that is already true; this is one.

#### `canvas_palette.section_rule()` is defined and never used: card sections have no dividing hairline, and Unity's LastSectionOf has no counterpart

`static func section_rule()` (canvas_palette.gd:243-245) returns `{ "color": Color(0.24,0.24,0.29,0.9), "custom_minimum_size": Vector2(0,1) }` under the doc comment "The hairline between one section of a card and the next." It has no caller anywhere: a grep across builder/ returns only the definition, and `canvas_view.guitkx` contains no separator, rule or 1px divider of any kind. Unity draws a 1px border-bottom on every card section, suppressed on the last one — that is the entire purpose of `LastSectionOf` (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:305-322, whose own doc comment quotes the POC rule `.card-section:last-child { border-bottom: none }`). So the Godot cards have no visual boundary between SIGNATURE, IMPORTS, BODY, RETURN—MARKUP and EXPORTS at all, and the palette carries an unreferenced entry for the thing that is missing. The register cites `LastSectionOf` twice (:298 and :714) but only as evidence that Unity keeps one section definition — it never notices that the rule the function exists to suppress is absent here. This is also a second instance of the pattern the parity gate's own header says it was written to catch ("a mechanism that already existed with nothing wired to it"), and no parity entry covers card chrome.

#### `_append_code_rows` is an orphaned projection helper: the behaviour above it was deliberately abandoned and the function was left behind

`static func _append_code_rows(...)` (builder_graph_service.gd:796-808) is documented as "One PLAIN row per non-blank line of a GDScript segment inside a directive body" and has zero callers anywhere in the repo — a grep over addons/ and tests/ returns only its own definition. The function is the discarded half of that decision, still compiled, still carrying the only production path that would ever set `Graph.LineKind.PLAIN` on a markup row. Two consequences worth acting on: it is a live trap for the next person editing the directive walk (calling it would silently reintroduce the defect the comment describes), and its presence means `LineKind.PLAIN` in the MARKUP section is unreachable while `_row_of` (builder_window.gd:1530-1550) and the row menu still branch as though rows of every kind can appear there. #### BuilderText.cs has no Godot counterpart and no test: the port re-created the four-copy indent scan Unity refactored away

`Lang/BuilderText.cs` exists for one stated reason: "The leading-space scan had four independent copies (two in the window, one in the move-payload re-indent, one inside the graph service's block dedent); a divergence there re-indents an edit differently depending on which path applied it." The Godot port has four again, none shared: `_indent_of_line` (builder_edits.gd:877-881), `_indent_of` (:926-931), `_indent_unit`'s own space loop (:937-948), and `_strip_common_indent` (builder_graph_service.gd:570-575). All four count a tab and a space as one character; Unity's single primitive counts spaces only. The island round trip crosses two of them in opposite directions — `_strip_common_indent` computes the common prefix when the card is projected, `set_island` computes `shallowest` with `_indent_of_line(...).length()` when the edit is written back (builder_edits.gd:743-748) and puts back exactly one `_indent_unit` (:757) — and nothing asserts they are inverse. `unwrap_directive` uses the same char-count a third time (:816-820). I could not construct a failing round trip in the shapes .guitkx actually produces (tab-indented bodies round-trip cleanly, verified headlessly), so this is a missing invariant rather than a confirmed defect — but it is the exact invariant Unity paid for once already, on a language where tabs are mandatory and a mixed paste is the likely input. `BuilderText` has zero mentions in the 4,395-line register, and no suite asserts any two of the four agree.

#### BuilderSaveMetrics.cs is the one Unity builder file with no coverage of any kind — no gap, no parity entry, no divergence note

`Builder/Editor/BuilderSaveMetrics.cs` (38 lines) is VE-06 measurement instrumentation: `RecordSaveBatch(filesWritten, hmrActive)` logs every builder save batch with a timestamp and arms a flag that the next domain reload logs against, so a validation session produces the acceptance numbers (N edits -> 0 reloads; 1 save -> 1 reload; abort -> 0; HMR-active save -> 0) from the console without hand-counting. It is absent from the register entirely — a grep for "BuilderSaveMetrics" returns 0, and it is the only file under Builder/Editor/ for which that is true (Spikes/ aside, which is dev-only). Nothing in the Godot builder logs a save batch, and there is no parity entry and no line in CLAUDE.md's divergence list explaining why. The obvious rebuttal — Godot has no domain reload — is only half the story: a Godot Save writes, moves and trashes .guitkx files that must then be re-scanned and re-compiled by the addon's own compile-on-save sweep, and the register's own appendix finding (line 4304, `workspace.rescan` never assigned) establishes that nobody has ever measured or even wired that cost. The Godot equivalent of the acceptance table is "N edits -> 0 rescans; 1 save -> 1 rescan", and it has neither an instrument nor a test. Fix is either a two-line divergence note in CLAUDE.md and the gate's DELIBERATE table, or a `print_rich` in `save()` paired with the rescan wiring.
