## The canvas: projection, drawing, input and gestures

71 distinct gaps — 6 critical, 22 high, 30 medium, 13 low, plus 3 marked as duplicates.

### Canvas drawing: LOD bands, card geometry, section stack, edges, anchors, palette, grid, framing

### `CANVAS-01` The card geometry model is a prediction that nothing validates, and it does not match what the view lays out — every row gesture targets the wrong row

> Also filed as `GAP-01`, `GP-12` — one defect.

**Unity does:** Unity NEVER trusts an estimate for a row's position. `AnchorOf` (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:745-769) queries the named marker element and reads its real `worldBound`; `CardRect` (:770-782) reads the card element's real `layout.width/height` and only falls back to `CardWidthFor(lod)`/PillH when the element is missing. The section-stack estimate is documented in the source as exactly one thing: 'the named marker elements are measured here; the section-stack estimate is only the pre-layout fallback' (:740-744). When any query falls back it sets `estimated`, and `MaybeRetry` (:1020-1033) schedules up to 12 repaints at 16ms so the measured positions land. Row CLICKS are not hit-tested at all in Unity — each row is a real element with its own pointer handlers (CanvasView.uitkx:1004-1049).

**Godot today:** wrong. `RuitkBuilderCanvasMetrics.section_stack` (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:221-254) is the ONLY answer: `row_hit` (:504-536), `card_at` (builder_canvas_host.gd:554-564), `Drag.resolve` (builder_drag.gd:94-130) and `edge_source_anchor` (:375-397) all read it, and nothing ever compares it to a laid-out Control. I mounted the real host headless at zoom 1.0 on the suite's own fixture and dumped both. Model for the `app` card: SIGNATURE top 38, IMPORTS top 70.4 (lead 34.5, pitch 19.7), BODY top 164, MARKUP top 233.2 (lead 34.5, pitch 22.4), drawn_height 357.3. Actual, card-local: header 10..49, signature 53..69, IMPORTS heading 73..90 with rows at 92/110/128 (pitch 18), BODY heading 148..165 with chips at 167..191, MARKUP heading 195..212 with rows at 214/232/250/268 (pitch 18), card bottom 294. Consequences, all confirmed by a hit sweep down the card: import row 0 (actual 92..108) reports NOT FOUND; clicking import row 1 selects row 0; clicking row 2 selects row 1; clicking the BODY heading selects import row 2. The hook chip (167..191) reports nothing at all, so the hover-usage highlight can never fire on it, while the MARKUP heading and first markup row report BODY row 0. Markup rows 0,1,2 are unreachable and markup row 3 selects row 0. Below the card's real bottom, 294..357 of EMPTY CANVAS still reports markup rows 1..3, so a right-click there opens the card's row menu instead of the canvas 'create module here' menu. Because `_on_row_clicked` (builder_window.gd:1007-1021) sets `_menu_row` and `_source.goto_line(row.source_line)`, this is not merely mis-selection: the source pane jumps to the wrong line and a subsequent Delete removes a line range the user never pointed at. The suite cannot catch it: tests/builder_canvas_test.gd:147-172 sweeps `row_hit` against `drawn_height` — model against model — and passes.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One sharpening: the drift is not a uniform offset. SECTION_OVERHEAD_H (34.5) is roughly double the real heading block (~17.5) and IMPORT_ROW_H/MARKUP_ROW_H (19.7/22.4) are both 18 in the render, so the error accumulates downward and the section origin is wrong too (HEADER_H 38 vs a real first-section top of 53). Recalibrating constants would not survive a palette font change; the measurement pass is the fix.

**To build:** Add a MEASUREMENT pass and make the estimate the fallback, exactly as Unity does. (1) In canvas_view.guitkx, give every row wrapper a stable `name` (`row-{section}-{index}`) and the card frame `card-{index}` — the reconciler's host maps a `name` prop straight onto the Node. (2) In builder_canvas_host.gd, extend the existing settle loop (`_process`/`_fit_cards`, host.gd:293-331, already 8 frames and already walking the whole card subtree) to record each row Control's card-local rect into a per-card `measured_rows` dictionary, and mark the card `estimated` when a row is missing or zero-sized. (3) Have `row_hit`, `card_at`, `on_title_bar`, `Drag.resolve` and `edge_source_anchor` consult `measured_rows` first and `section_stack` only as the pre-layout fallback — the retry is already free because `_render()` re-arms the settle counter. (4) Add the gate this needed from the start: a headless test that mounts the host, walks the rendered tree, and asserts for EVERY row that `row_hit` at the row's own measured centre returns that row's (section, index), and that `card_at` at the card's measured bottom-plus-two returns -1. That test is ~60 lines and would have failed on the first commit. If a full measurement pass is judged too invasive, the minimum honest fix is to recalibrate the constants against the view (SECTION_OVERHEAD_H 34.5 -> ~17.5, IMPORT_ROW_H/MARKUP_ROW_H 19.7/22.4 -> 18, the section origin HEADER_H 38 -> card padding 10 + header 39 + separation 4 = 53) AND ship the same test — but constants recalibrated by hand drift again the moment a font size or a separation changes in the palette, which is precisely why Unity measures.

**Godot specifics:** Measuring is cheap and safe here BECAUSE of how this canvas is built: the reconciler patches rather than rebuilds, cards are `PanelContainer`s in a non-container parent, and the host already runs an 8-frame settle pass (SETTLE_FRAMES, host.gd:288) for `reset_size()` — it is the same schedule Unity's `MaybeRetry` burst provides. The host's comment at :548-553 argues the model must be authoritative because 'the cards are re-created as the graph changes'; that reasoning is the source of this defect and is not true of a reconciler that diffs. Keep `_pass_mouse_through` as-is (rows stay MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE and the host keeps arbitrating the press) — measuring positions does not require handing rows the mouse. All new code stays in `@tool` scripts reached by preload const, so the class-cache hazard is untouched, and a measurement pass over a mounted host is fully headless-testable: Control layout runs in `--headless`, which is how I confirmed every number above.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:740-782 (AnchorOf/CardRect measure; estimate is the fallback), :1020-1033 (MaybeRetry, 12 repaints), :1179-1234 (ImportRowY/MarkupRowY are the fallback only); godot builder_canvas_metrics.gd:221-254 + :504-536 + builder_canvas_host.gd:554-564 + builder_drag.gd:94-130; measured against the rendered tree with tests/builder_canvas_test.gd's own fixture; the model-vs-model gate is tests/builder_canvas_test.gd:147-172

### `CANVAS-03` Hook chips and the Layer 3 attribute run render one pixel wide — the BODY section is visually empty and the attribute run is invisible

**Unity does:** BODY is a wrapping row of pill chips, one per hook line, each carrying its rich text and explicitly sized so it cannot be clipped: 'a chip wider than the card WRAPS inside its own pill and the pill stays whole. A fixed Height plus the default no-wrap sliced the last chip off at the card border — no right cap, no ellipsis' (canvasStyles CardChip, CanvasView.uitkx:523-718; MinHeight 22.7, WhiteSpace Normal, MaxWidth cardWidth-30). The L2 attribute run is four labels per attribute with a per-attribute 6px margin and an explicit MinHeight 0 tuned so the row measures 22.4 rather than 23.4 (CanvasView.uitkx:1152-1226).

**Godot today:** wrong — and it is not a metrics question, it is what the mounted view actually draws. Both labels use `text_overrun_behavior = OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS` inside a parent that does not stretch them, and in Godot 4.7 that makes a Label's minimum width ~0. Measured on the real host: the hook chip's `PanelContainer` is **9x24** with its Label at **1x16** carrying the text 'useState  →  s' (canvas_view.guitkx:203-207 inside the `HFlowContainer` at :199, which hands each child its minimum size); the attribute Label is **1x16** for the text 'style={primary}' at zoom 1.5 (canvas_view.guitkx:307-310, `SIZE_SHRINK_END` beside a tag Label that is `SIZE_EXPAND_FILL` and takes 327 of the 334 available). So the card's 'BODY — HOOKS & STATE' section shows a row of blank 9-pixel pills at every band that draws sections, and 'Layer 3 — Edit' adds an attribute run nobody can read. The rows that DO render correctly (imports, markup, exports) are the ones that are an only child of a stretched PanelContainer, which is why the defect looks selective. This also hollows out a feature the parity gate reports green: hovering a hook chip to highlight its usages (builder_canvas_host.gd:152-165, tests/builder_parity.gd:100) requires pointing at a chip that has no visible extent and, per CANVAS-01, no hit region either.

**To build:** Stop relying on OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS to bound a Label that nothing stretches. For the chip: give the chip Label `custom_minimum_size.x` (or `autowrap_mode = AUTOWRAP_WORD` with a `MaxWidth` of card_width-30, which is what Unity does — the chip wraps inside its own pill and the pill stays whole), and drop `text_overrun_behavior` there. For the attribute run: give the attrs Label a real width — either `SIZE_EXPAND_FILL` with a stretch ratio against the tag label, or `clip_text` plus a `custom_minimum_size.x`, or split it into the per-attribute pieces CANVAS-08 asks for. Then gate it: extend tests/builder_canvas_test.gd's mounted-host section to assert that every Label with non-empty text has `size.x > 8` after the settle frames — a five-line walk that catches this whole class.

**Godot specifics:** This is a pure engine-translation defect: the Unity leg's problem was UI Toolkit having no line-height and an auto flex minimum that was too TALL, so the port carried over ellipsis-everywhere as the counter-measure, and in Godot ellipsis removes the minimum entirely in the opposite direction. `HFlowContainer` (canvas_view.guitkx:199) sizes children to their combined minimum, so a 0-width minimum is a 0-width chip; `PanelContainer` propagates that plus its 4px content margins, which is exactly the 9px measured. Because the whole card layer is `.guitkx`, the fix is three attribute changes in canvas_view.guitkx plus a rebuild of the committed canvas_view.gd (gated by tests/builder_view_build.gd).

*critical · visual · CONFIRMED* — unity CanvasView.uitkx:523-718 (chips: MinHeight 22.7, WhiteSpace Normal, MaxWidth cardWidth-30) and :1152-1226 (attribute run, MinHeight 0 tuned to 22.4); godot canvas_view.guitkx:199-208 (chip) and :300-311 (attrs), canvas_palette.gd:95-100 (chip/chip_text), :115-116 (attrs); measured on the mounted host at zoom 1.0 and 1.5

### `CANVAS-02` A pill's clickable rectangle is 38 units of a card that draws 73 — half of every Layer 1 card is dead to the mouse

**Unity does:** At L0 the card is a 300x~72.7 pill and its whole face is live: the pill wrapper carries the press that arms a card move and selects (CanvasView.uitkx:307-316), and `CardRect` measures the element's real height (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:770-782) with PillH (72.7, :31-35) as the fallback. Unity even records the constant's derivation: 1.5 frame + 16 pad + 37.7 title box + 16 + 1.5.

**Godot today:** wrong, and it is one line. `drawn_height` returns `HEADER_H` (38.0) for `Lod.PILL` (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:196-197) while `PILL_H` (72.7) sits unused two hundred lines above at :60. Measured: the pill renders 300x73 — PILL_H is the correct number. `card_at` (builder_canvas_host.gd:562) and `on_title_bar` (metrics.gd:447) both build their rect from `drawn_height`, so the bottom 35 of 73 units of every pill selects nothing and drags the canvas instead of the card. Layer 1 — Architecture is the layer you browse and rearrange a tree in, so this is the layer where card dragging matters most.

**To build:** `drawn_height` should return `PILL_H` for `Lod.PILL` (or, once CANVAS-01 lands, the card's measured height). Add an assertion to tests/builder_canvas_test.gd's `_test_anchors_land_on_the_drawn_card` that the pill's drawn height equals the mounted card's real height at zoom 0.30 — the existing test at :831-850 only checks that the pill is shorter than a full card, which 38 satisfies as happily as 72.7.

**Godot specifics:** The pill's height comes from `pill_title()` font_size 26 plus the header band's content_margin 8 and the card's content_margin 10 (canvas_palette.gd:79-80, :234-240, :46-53) — so it is a function of the palette, which is the argument for measuring rather than for a second hand-tuned constant. Note that `is_near_viewport` and `content_bounds` (metrics.gd:318-338) use `card_height` (the full-stack estimate, 357) rather than `drawn_height`, so at the pill band the cull and the fit reserve five times the card's real height.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:31-35 (PillH) + :770-782 (CardRect measures) + CanvasView.uitkx:301-316; godot builder_canvas_metrics.gd:60 (PILL_H, unused by drawn_height), :193-204 (drawn_height), :440-448 (on_title_bar), builder_canvas_host.gd:554-564

### `CANVAS-04` Card width is treated as a constant but is only a minimum — a long module name doubles the card and takes the hit rect, the anchors and the seeded layout with it

**Unity does:** `Width = Px(cardWidth)` is set on the card wrapper (CanvasView.uitkx:218) and UI Toolkit's Width is border-box, so 300/340/430 is what the card IS, not a floor. A long pill title is allowed to run PAST the box instead of growing it — `Overflow = lod == 0 ? Visible : Hidden` — and the comment says so: 'Neither ".card" nor ".pill" sets overflow:hidden in the POC'. Even so, `CardRect` measures the real element rather than assuming (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:770-782), so anything that did grow is still hit correctly.

**Godot today:** wrong. canvas_view.guitkx:92-93 sets `custom_minimum_size = Vector2(card_w, 0)` — a FLOOR — and the header title Label (:143) has neither `clip_text` nor a `text_overrun_behavior`, so its minimum width is the full text width and the card grows to fit. Measured: renaming the fixture's card to 'ShoppingCartSummaryPanelWide' makes the pill **594** world units wide where `card_width_for(PILL)` says 300. Everything keyed on the constant then misses: `card_at` (builder_canvas_host.gd:559-562) only hits the left 300, so half the card is unselectable; `on_title_bar` rejects x > 300; `edge_source_anchor` puts every dot at card.x+300, i.e. 294 units INSIDE the card, so the curve leaves from the middle of the card's own content — the exact failure UB-103 take 2 was written to kill; `is_near_viewport` and `content_bounds` under-measure so a fit clips the card; and the seeded layout's column pitch is `CARD_WIDTH_FULL + LAYOUT_GAP` (builder_graph_service.gd:1044,1050), so the wide card overlaps its sibling on the same row. `clip_contents = true` (canvas_view.guitkx:94) clips the PAINT but not the LAYOUT, so it hides the symptom's cause rather than preventing it.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The card's TITLE is the module name derived from the file name, not the declaration name — a 44-character signature does not grow the card, because the signature Label already carries `clip_text` (canvas_view.guitkx:176). So the trigger is a long FILE name, and the fix is precisely to give the title Label the treatment the signature already has.

**To build:** Make the width a real constraint. Give the header title Label `clip_text = true` and `text_overrun_behavior = OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS` like the signature row already has (canvas_view.guitkx:176-177) — with clip_text the Label's minimum width is 0 and the card holds its declared width. Belt and braces: after CANVAS-01's measurement pass exists, take the card's rect from the measured Control the way `CardRect` does, so any future unclipped child cannot silently break the anchors again. Add an assertion that a card with a 40-character title still measures `card_width_for(lod)` wide when mounted.

**Godot specifics:** `custom_minimum_size` is a floor by definition; `size` set on a Control in a non-container parent is overwritten by `reset_size()` in the host's `_fit_cards` (builder_canvas_host.gd:318-331), which sets size to `get_combined_minimum_size()` — so the host actively enforces the grown width every settle frame. A Label only stops reporting its text width as its minimum when `clip_text` is true or autowrap is on; `text_overrun_behavior` alone is why the import rows behave (they are stretched by their VBox) and the title does not.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity CanvasView.uitkx:218 (Width = Px(cardWidth)), BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:770-782 (CardRect measures anyway), :202-207 (CardWidthFor); godot canvas_view.guitkx:92-94 (custom_minimum_size/clip_contents) and :143 (unclipped title), builder_canvas_metrics.gd:90-97, builder_canvas_host.gd:554-564, builder_graph_service.gd:1044-1050; measured 594px pill on the mounted host

### `CANVAS-05` The view and the metrics disagree about when a card has a BODY section — the one thing this file exists to prevent

**Unity does:** BODY presence has ONE rule: `lodFull && (Body.Count > 0 || Kind is Component/Hook)`, and for non-component/hook kinds the same section's heading flips to 'EXPORTS' (CanvasView.uitkx:523-530). `LastSectionOf` (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:305-322) restates the same condition so the section stack and the drawn card cannot disagree about how many sections exist.

**Godot today:** wrong, and it is the defect builder_canvas_metrics.gd:127-140 was written to warn about. The model says a BODY section exists when `not card.body.is_empty() or has_body`, where `has_body := card.kind == COMPONENT or card.kind == HOOK` (metrics.gd:228, :239). The view says a BODY section exists when `card.kind != 2` (canvas_view.guitkx:196) — i.e. util (3), value (4) and module (5) cards get a BODY section with '+ hook' and '+ code' chips that the model does not know about. On any util/value/module card with an empty body the drawn card has one whole section (heading + chip row, ~43 units measured) that the section stack omits, so every section below it — the EXPORTS detail rows, which on a util card are the only editable thing — is hit-tested one section too high, on top of the general drift in CANVAS-01. The signature has the mirror problem: the view draws it only for `card.kind != 2` (canvas_view.guitkx:174) while `section_stack` adds it whenever `signature` is non-empty regardless of kind (metrics.gd:231).

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The stated consequence understates it. For util/value/module kinds the EXPORTS section is not merely hit-tested one section too high — it is never drawn at any zoom, because the view's EXPORTS gate is `draws_exports and card.kind == 2` (canvas_view.guitkx:231) while `_fill_export_detail` populates `export_detail` for every non-component kind (builder_graph_service.gd:897-906, 'Everything else lists its declarations with their signatures'). See the separate MISSED entry.

**To build:** Move both predicates into builder_canvas_metrics.gd beside `draws_section` — `has_body_section(card)` and `has_signature_section(card)` — and have canvas_view.guitkx call them instead of testing `card.kind` inline, the same way it already calls `M.draws_section` for MARKUP/EXPORTS/ISLAND (canvas_view.guitkx:168-170). Decide which rule is right while you are there: Unity's is 'component/hook always, others only when non-empty', and a util card offering '+ hook' is offering something a util module cannot have. Add a test that for every `Module.Kind`, the number of sections `section_stack` reports equals the number of section VBoxes the mounted card contains.

**Godot specifics:** `card.kind != 2` is a magic literal for `Module.Kind.STYLE` in a file that otherwise imports the enum (canvas_view.guitkx uses `M.Section` and `M.Lod` by name), so the drift is invisible to a reader and to grep. Because the view is `.guitkx` and the metrics are a preloaded const, the predicate is reachable from the markup with no class-cache exposure — the existing `M.draws_section` calls prove the pattern works.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity CanvasView.uitkx:523-530 + BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:305-322; godot canvas_view.guitkx:174 and :196 vs builder_canvas_metrics.gd:228,231,239 — and metrics.gd:127-140, the comment describing this exact failure mode as already fixed

### `CANVAS-06` A drop shows no hint — nothing on screen says which row, or which side of it, the element will land on

**Unity does:** `PaintDropHint` (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:920-1004) paints into the same overlay as the edges, from the drag machine's live hit-tested target. A middle-band (INSIDE) target gets a filled accent rectangle with a 2px stroke over the whole row; a before/after target gets 'an unmistakable caret — a thick dashed rule with end caps at the exact line the element will land on', 3px, dash 7/gap 4, with 5px end caps. The source records why the caret had to be that loud: 'the owner tried repeatedly to drop BETWEEN two elements, could not tell it had worked, and concluded it had failed'. The hint is clamped to the section viewport with the same clamp the anchor dots use, so it never bleeds over occluding rows.

**Godot today:** absent. `Drag.resolve` computes `band` and `placement` correctly and live (builder_drag.gd:94-130, :137-150), and the three-band rule including the first-child case is implemented — but nothing draws it. `builder_canvas_edges.gd:_draw` (:78-95) paints anchors and edges and nothing else; the host's `_can_drop_data` (builder_canvas_host.gd:457-458) returns true without recording the position, so no repaint is even requested during a drag. The user gets Godot's generic drag ghost (a Label of the row text, host.gd:479-481) and no target feedback of any kind, which is UB-30's symptom for the target end.

**To build:** Have `_can_drop_data` record `at_position` and `queue_redraw()` on the edge overlay (it is a sibling Control, already full-rect and MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE), then paint the hint in `builder_canvas_edges._draw` after the edges: resolve through `Drag.resolve(graph, at, camera, zoom)`, convert the row's rect with `Metrics.world_to_screen`, and draw either a filled `draw_rect` with a stroked outline (band 1) or a dashed caret with end caps at the row's top or bottom edge (bands 0 and 2) — `_draw_dashed` already exists at edges.gd:169-180. Clear the recorded position in `_drop_data` and on `NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END`. Note this cannot be right until CANVAS-01 is fixed: a hint drawn from today's `row_hit` would confidently point at the wrong row, which is worse than no hint.

**Godot specifics:** Godot calls `_can_drop_data` continuously on the Control under the pointer during a drag, which is the natural hook and gives the live position UB-31 warned about capturing at press time — this leg is already immune to the staleness half. `NOTIFICATION_DRAG_BEGIN`/`NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END` on the host are the reliable way to clear the hint when a drag is aborted with Escape. Drawing into the existing `_draw` costs nothing: the overlay already redraws on every camera change.

### `CANVAS-17` The parity gate is green over three canvas features that do not work, including the one it names 'one definition of what a layer draws'

**Unity does:** n/a — this is a judgement of the Godot gate against the behaviours above.

**Godot today:** tests/builder_parity.gd greps for identifiers, and three of its canvas entries are answered by code whose behaviour is wrong. (1) Line 82, 'one definition of what a layer draws' -> `func draws_section`: the function exists, but the VIEW does not ask it for SIGNATURE or BODY (canvas_view.guitkx:174, :196 test `card.kind` inline) and disagrees with the model for util/value/module cards — the entry's own claim is false while the token is present (CANVAS-05). (2) Line 100, 'hovering a hook chip highlights its usages' -> `func row_mentions`: `row_mentions` is correct and unit-tested, but the chip you must hover renders 9px wide with a 1px label (CANVAS-03) and is not in `row_hit`'s reported band for its own position (CANVAS-01), so the feature cannot be triggered by a human. (3) Line 81, 'card dragging, by the TITLE BAR' -> `func on_title_bar`: it exists and returns the wrong rectangle at the pill band (CANVAS-02) and for any card with a long title (CANVAS-04). Beyond the false greens, the gate has NO entry at all for: the drop hint, section height caps, anchor dot colour, the card shadow, the dot grid, directive badges, the attribute run, LOD card widths, or the zoom clamp — nine of the behaviours in this inventory are not on the checklist in any form.

**To build:** Two things, in this order. (1) Replace the three hollow entries with assertions in tests/builder_canvas_test.gd that a token cannot satisfy: for `draws_section`, assert the mounted card's section count equals `section_stack(card).size()` for every `Module.Kind`; for `row_mentions`, assert `row_hit` at a mounted chip's measured centre returns (BODY, that index) and that the chip Label's `size.x > 8`; for `on_title_bar`, assert it is true at the mounted header's measured centre and false one pixel below the measured header. (2) Add the nine missing checklist entries so the sweep stops 'reading as a complete account' while omitting a third of the canvas. The gate's own header (tests/builder_parity.gd:9-15) says it exists because 'most of it was a mechanism that already existed with nothing wired to it' — a grep gate cannot catch the next instance of exactly that, which is what these three entries are.

**Godot specifics:** Everything needed for the real assertions is already headless: `builder_canvas_test.gd` mounts the host and reads live `Control`s (its `_test_host_renders_each_lod`, `_test_cards_do_not_eat_the_mouse`), so measured-vs-model assertions need no window. Note `ASSERTION_FLOOR` (tests/builder_canvas_test.gd:34-38) must be raised in the same commit or the suite's truncated-run guard stops guarding.

### `CANVAS-07` No section is height-capped and nothing scrolls — a component with a long markup body grows a card without limit

**Unity does:** UB-23 (UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:572-582): 'No card section is height-capped … A component with a long markup body grows a card until it overlaps its neighbours — which is what PRODUCES UB-22 in the first place'. §8.2 (:789-817) capped each section and gave it its own scroller: IMPORTS 140, BODY 260, EXPORTS 280, MARKUP 340, the L2 code island 220 (CanvasView.uitkx:445-447, 533-535, 757-767, 791-793, 985-987), each a ScrollView named `ruitk-section-scroll`. The consequence §8.2 had to solve first is the anchor clamp: 'a dot scrolled out of its section still reports a worldBound, so the curve would attach to a point outside the visible region' — hence the clamp in AnchorOf and the `verticalScroller.valueChanged -> MarkDirtyRepaint` wire (BuilderCanvasHost.cs:730-742), and hence Ctrl+wheel zooming when the plain wheel is scrolling a section.

**Godot today:** absent. There is no `ScrollView`/`ScrollContainer` anywhere in canvas_view.guitkx — every section is a plain `VBoxContainer` that grows with its content (canvas_view.guitkx:182-265). A 60-row component card is 60 rows tall. Because the layout is ADOPTED and never recomputed (builder_canvas_layout.gd:12-15), a card that grows after an edit overlaps whatever was placed below it, and the seeded row pitch was computed from the old height (builder_graph_service.gd:1052-1054). The knock-on behaviours are correspondingly moot rather than wrong: `canvas-draw.anchor-scroll-clamp` has nothing to clamp against, and the Ctrl+wheel arbitration has no scroller to arbitrate with.

**To build:** Wrap each section body in a `ScrollContainer` with `custom_minimum_size.y` unset and a max height enforced by the section's own `custom_minimum_size`/`clip_contents`, at Unity's caps (140/260/280/340, island 220). Then port the two consequences or the cap is a regression: clamp an anchor whose row is scrolled out to the section viewport's edge inside `edge_source_anchor`, and connect the scroll bar's `value_changed` to `_edges.queue_redraw()` so dots track the scroll live rather than lagging. Ctrl+wheel-to-zoom-over-a-scroller then becomes necessary: handle it in the host's `_handle_button` by checking `event.ctrl_pressed` before letting the scroller see the wheel, or set the ScrollContainer's `mouse_filter` so the host arbitrates.

**Godot specifics:** A `ScrollContainer` defaults to `MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` and will swallow presses that the host's `_gui_input` needs — `_pass_mouse_through` (builder_canvas_host.gd:241-245) forces every non-Button Control to IGNORE on every render, so a scroller added naively will be silently disabled and a scroller exempted from that walk will silently break row clicks. That interaction has to be designed, not discovered. Godot's scroll bars are themed from the editor theme, so Unity's whole `RestyleScrollers` pass has no analogue — that part is free.

### `CANVAS-08` Attributes appear at a FOURTH zoom threshold nobody names, and the run is one flat label instead of editable pieces

**Unity does:** The band table is the contract: 'Layer 3 — Edit, zoom >= 0.80: Adds per-row attributes, code islands, directive badges and style entry lines — and this is the layer at which those become clickable to edit' (UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:59-63). The run is four Labels per attribute — name, '=', opening delimiter, value, closing delimiter — with zero spacing between the pieces and a 6px margin per attribute, wrapping onto further lines; hovering a value rules a dotted underline under it (DrawDottedUnderline, BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:701-727); clicking a value opens the editor on that one attribute, and an empty value removes it (CanvasView.uitkx:1152-1226).

**Godot today:** partial and divergent. `shows_attributes(zoom)` (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:115-120) tests `zoom >= ATTRIBUTE_ZOOM` where `ATTRIBUTE_ZOOM := 1.2` (:120) — a fourth threshold that is not `lod_of` and not in the spec. In the whole window [0.80, 1.20) the toolbar reads 'Layer 3 — Edit' and the cards carry no attributes, which is the same class of contradiction between the drawn card and the named layer that this file's own header condemns in the Unity leg; it is only invisible from the dropdown because the Layer 3 preset (1.25) happens to clear 1.2. The run itself is a single `Label` of `row.attrs_text` (canvas_view.guitkx:305-311) with no per-attribute split, no hover underline, no click-to-edit — and per CANVAS-03 it is one pixel wide. Attribute editing exists only through the row context menu (`RowMenuId.EDIT_ATTRIBUTE`, builder_window.gd:76).

**To build:** Either delete `ATTRIBUTE_ZOOM` and gate the run on `shows_detail(lod)` like every other Layer 3 element, or amend UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md — the contract says every capability change is recorded in the same commit, and this one was not. Then build the run as an `HFlowContainer` of per-attribute `HBoxContainer`s (name / '=' / value) with a real width, each value a Button-like Control whose press emits `attribute_clicked(card_index, row_index, attr_index)` into the existing inline-editor path; `attr_pairs` is already projected on every Line (builder_graph.gd:71-72), so the data is there. The hover underline is a `draw_line` in a small `_draw` override or a `Label` with an underlined theme font — either is cheaper than Unity's mesh walk.

**Godot specifics:** Note the ordering trap already present: `shows_attributes` reads `ATTRIBUTE_ZOOM` five lines before the const is declared (metrics.gd:116 vs :120) — legal for a const, and a reason a reader misses that a fourth threshold exists at all. Per-attribute click targets are the one place on a card that genuinely needs the mouse, so they must be `BaseButton`s: `_pass_mouse_through` (builder_canvas_host.gd:241-245) exempts `BaseButton` and forces everything else to IGNORE, which is exactly why the '+ hook' chips are the only card control that works today.

### `CANVAS-09` Directive badges are projected onto every row and never drawn — a contract clause of Layer 3 is unmet

**Unity does:** §8.1 made a directive clause a ROW OF ITS OWN so a badge no longer rides the clause's first element row, and the badge is a real element on that row: 10px bold, `BadgeColor`/`BadgeBg` by directive kind, radius 7, padding 6/6/0/0, Height 14.5, MarginRight 6, drawn whenever `BadgeKind > 0` (CanvasView.uitkx:1004-1049; BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:378-395). Pressing the badge opens the directive editor seeded with `DirectiveText`; right-clicking it opens the row menu. The capability contract lists 'directive badges' as one of the four things Layer 3 adds (UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:63).

**Godot today:** absent from the drawing layer while fully present in the model. `Graph.Line` carries `badge`, `badge_text`, `directive_text`, `directive_line`, `close_line` and `clause_index` (builder_graph.gd:87-106), the projection fills them (builder_graph_service.gd:670, :822), and the row MENU reads `badge_text` in five places (builder_window.gd:1097-1105, 1152-1155, 1501). The canvas never renders it: `CanvasMarkupRow` draws `"    ".repeat(row.depth) + row.text` and the attrs label, nothing else (canvas_view.guitkx:300-312), so a directive row is distinguishable only by its purple text colour and the literal '@if (level > 1)' in its text. The `Badge` enum's IF/ELIF/ELSE/FOR/WHILE/MATCH/CASE/DEFAULT members (builder_graph.gd:44-47) are read by no drawing code at all.

**To build:** In `CanvasMarkupRow`, prepend a `PanelContainer`+`Label` badge when `row.badge_text != ""`, styled from a new `canvas_palette.directive_badge(badge)` that maps the `Badge` enum to a tint the way `kind_tint` maps `Module.Kind` (canvas_palette.gd:133-148 is the pattern). Gate it on `M.shows_detail(lod)` to match the contract. If the badge is to be pressable (Unity's badge press opens the directive editor), it must be a `BaseButton` for the reason in CANVAS-08.

**Godot specifics:** Adding a leading child to the markup row's `HBoxContainer` changes the row's minimum height, which every hit-test constant is calibrated against — so this must land after or with CANVAS-01, or it silently shifts every markup row's target by the badge's height difference. Palette data must stay in the hand-written `@tool` canvas_palette.gd for the static-var reason recorded in its header (canvas_palette.gd:1-17).

### `CANVAS-10` Anchor dots are one flat colour, and their row index is compacted past asset imports so the dots drift up a row

**Unity does:** Each dot's colour is its import's kind: `DotColor(kind)` maps 6 -> HookEdge, 7 -> StyleEdge, anything else -> UsageEdge, with a halo ring at 25% alpha of the same colour (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:1005-1018, 1035-1042) — so a hook import, a style import and a component usage are three visibly different dots in one column. And the row indexing is deliberately NOT compacted: the dot loop skips `BadgeKind == NamespaceImportBadge` but the INDEX keeps counting, 'so anchor names stay 1:1 with row indices' (:890-915).

**Godot today:** partial/wrong. Every dot is `ANCHOR_COLOR` (builder_canvas_edges.gd:47, used at :108 and :117) regardless of `target_kind`, even though the curve it terminates IS coloured by kind (`Palette.edge_style()` / `edge_component()`, edges.gd:148) — so the line says 'style module' and the dot it grows out of says nothing. Separately, `_append_edges_for` increments `import_index` only for rows it emits an edge for, skipping `Badge.IMPORT_ASSET` rows with `continue` before the increment (builder_graph_service.gd:110-128) — but the card DRAWS every import row including asset ones (canvas_view.guitkx:183-192). So on a card with an `@uss`/`@theme` row above a real import, every dot below it is one row (19.7 units) too high and its curve leaves from beside the wrong line. This is precisely the compaction Unity's comment says it refused to do.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The arrival dots are already kind-coloured in practice — `_draw` runs all anchors first (edges.gd:85-86) and `_draw_edge` then overdraws the same point with `draw_circle(to, ANCHOR_RADIUS, color)` (:166). So only the right-border SOURCE dots (:117) are flat, and they also miss the `DIMMED_ALPHA` fade the curves get (:153-154), so with a card selected an unrelated card's source dots stay bright over dimmed lines.

**To build:** Colour the dot from the edge: pass `edge.target_kind` into `_draw_anchors` and pick `Palette.edge_style()` / `edge_component()` / a hook tint, with a halo at ~25% alpha as Unity does — the two-colour palette is already there (canvas_palette.gd:154-163), and a third for hook edges would also fix the legend, which currently names only 'usage edge' (builder_window.gd:629-632). For the index: increment `import_index` for EVERY import row and skip only the edge emission, so the edge's `from_row` indexes the drawn list. Add a test with a card carrying an asset import above a module import that asserts the second dot's Y equals the second drawn row's Y.

**Godot specifics:** `Badge.IMPORT_ASSET` is emitted at builder_graph_service.gd:312 and is a real case (`@uss`/`@theme`), not hypothetical. The dot is drawn in screen space with a fixed 3.5px radius (edges.gd:27) rather than Unity's world-space 4px — that divergence is correct and deliberate here, since the whole overlay is screen-space so stroke weight survives the pill band; do not 'fix' it back.

### `CANVAS-11` The signature row is uncoloured and clipped mid-word — both defects Unity fixed by name

**Unity does:** UB-78 (UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:1060-1078): 'the parameter list used to be emitted RAW, so every type and parameter name in it inherited the section's flat grey while the islands beside it were fully coloured'. The fix colours the whole line once through the code lexer and breaks the bold run at the paren, deliberately not splitting first because that 'would have robbed the name of the paren that classifies it as a call' (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:236-246). And the row WRAPS by design: CardSignature is MinHeight 17.4 with WhiteSpace Normal because 'A pinned Height cut the tail of every long signature mid-word'.

**Godot today:** wrong on both counts. `canvas_palette.signature()` is a flat `#96969F` at font_size 11 with the mono face and no colouring at all (canvas_palette.gd:83-84), and the view renders it with `clip_text = true` + `OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS` (canvas_view.guitkx:174-178) — so a long signature is cut exactly as Unity's comment describes, just with an ellipsis instead of mid-word. The model even predicts wrapping that never happens: `section_stack` computes `wrap_lines(card.signature.length(), inner, MONO_ADVANCE)` and reserves that many 17.4-unit lines (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:232-234), so on any signature longer than one line the model reserves height the card does not draw and every section below it is hit-tested low.

**To build:** Set `autowrap_mode = AUTOWRAP_WORD` on the signature Label and drop `clip_text` — the model already accounts for the wrapped height, so this makes the two agree in the direction that matches the reference. For the colouring, the editor addon already owns a `.guitkx` tokenizer/highlighter (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/, used by guitkx_code_edit.gd); a `RichTextLabel` with BBCode driven by that tokenizer gives the same result as Unity's `BuildLineRichText` without a second lexer. Same treatment applies to the code-island rows and import rows, which are equally flat.

**Godot specifics:** `RichTextLabel` in a `.guitkx` markup tree is a normal tag (any instantiable ClassDB Node class is a valid tag), so this needs no new host support; set `fit_content = true` and `mouse_filter = IGNORE` so `_pass_mouse_through` has nothing to correct. Reusing the addon's own tokenizer keeps the class-cache rule intact if it is reached by preload const like everything else in builder/.

### `CANVAS-12` Cards have no drop shadow — the depth cue both other legs judged load-bearing, and Godot gets it for free

**Unity does:** Every card sits on an 18px Gaussian falloff offset 6px down: `DrawCardShadow` (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:589-632) composites 16 rings whose alphas are solved so N composited rings equal a target `0.35 * NormalCdf(d/9)` at every depth, because 'UITK has no box-shadow, and four stacked opaque rects read as four flat plateaus with visible steps between them' — probed against the reference render, which shows '24 monotone rows below the card, no two the same'. The Unreal leg reached the identical conclusion independently (SRuitkUiBuilderCanvas.cpp:255-292), which is the evidence that the behaviour is portable rather than a Unity taste.

**Godot today:** absent. `canvas_palette.card_box()` sets bg, radius, border and content margin and no shadow keys at all (canvas_palette.gd:46-53); `card_box_selected` and `card_placeholder` likewise (:56-72). Nothing anywhere in builder/canvas/ draws or declares a shadow. Cards therefore sit flat on the ground with only a 1px hairline separating them, which is most of why an overlapping pair reads as one shape.

**To build:** Add `shadow_size`, `shadow_color` and `shadow_offset` to `card_box()` and `card_box_selected()` — StyleBoxFlat has all three natively, and the runtime's style bridge passes any StyleBoxFlat property straight through (documented at addons/reactive_ui_toolkit/core/style.gd:26, which names `shadow_size` as an example). Unity's numbers translate directly: size 18, offset Vector2(0, 6), colour Color(0,0,0,0.35). This is a three-line change that closes a behaviour both other legs spent forty-plus lines on.

**Godot specifics:** This is the clearest case in the area where the engine hands Godot for free what the other two legs had to build by hand — worth taking precisely because it costs nothing. One caveat: the card `PanelContainer` sets `clip_contents = true` (canvas_view.guitkx:94), which clips the panel's own children but not the StyleBox's shadow, so no wrapper element is needed; Unity's whole 'the host element's insets ARE the blur reach' contract has no analogue here and should not be ported.

### `CANVAS-13` The dot grid disappears below zoom 0.219, so Layer 1 — the layer you pan in — has no ground reference

**Unity does:** The lattice is screen-space, 26px pitch, drawn as raw mesh quads with a hard stop, capped at 16000 dots (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:512-558). It is zoom-invariant by construction and therefore always present. The Unreal leg deliberately diverged to a GRAPH-space lattice — the correct call, since a screen-fixed grid gives a pan no reference at all — and paid for it by DOUBLING the tile whenever `tile*zoom < 12`, so the lattice never crowds into a wash and never vanishes (SRuitkUiBuilderCanvas.cpp:192-228).

**Godot today:** partial. builder_canvas_host.gd:353-368 draws a world-space lattice: 64-unit spacing, offset by the camera, alpha ramped down as the screen spacing approaches 14px, and `return`ing entirely when `spacing < GRID_MIN_SCREEN_SPACING`. That means the grid is gone below zoom 0.219 and already faint at the Layer 1 preset of 0.30 (spacing 19.2, alpha 0.37). Godot took Unreal's world-space choice — right — without Unreal's tile doubling, so the one band where the user is panning across a whole tree is the band with no ground reference at all. The comment at :371-372 describes the constant as 'the screen spacing below which it stops being drawn', so this is intentional as written; the point is that the intent leaves Layer 1 blank.

**To build:** Port Unreal's doubling: while `spacing * zoom < GRID_MIN_SCREEN_SPACING`, multiply the world spacing by 2 and re-test, then draw at the doubled tile with the same alpha ramp — the grid coarsens instead of disappearing. Cap the loop (Unreal caps its quad count at 8000; here the `while` loops in host.gd:363-368 are already bounded by the viewport, but a doubling loop needs its own bound).

**Godot specifics:** `_draw` on the host runs before its children, which is why the ground and grid live there rather than on the overlay (host.gd:343-352) — that placement is correct and should be kept. `draw_rect` per dot at the current pitch is a few hundred calls at worst; if the doubled tile ever makes it thousands, `draw_multimesh` or a single `draw_primitive` run is the Godot answer to Unity's mesh-quad reasoning, but it is not needed at 64 units.

### `CANVAS-16` A style module's exports vanish entirely at Layer 2, where Unity keeps the heads, the braces and the add rows

**Unity does:** `detailVisible` is deliberately graded: a row shows at L1 when it is an export head, a closing brace, or a '+ style'/'+ export' affordance, and ENTRIES alone wait for L2 (CanvasView.uitkx:795-825). So at the Cards layer a style module still reads as a card with named exports you can add to; only the individual entry lines are held back.

**Godot today:** partial. `draws_section(EXPORTS, lod)` returns `shows_detail(lod)` (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:144-145), so the whole EXPORTS section — heads, braces, entries, the per-export '+ entry' rows and the card-level '+ style' chip — is hidden below Layer 3 (canvas_view.guitkx:231-250). A style card at Layer 2 is a header and nothing else, and since a style module has no signature, no imports section by default and no markup, that is a card with no content at all at the layer a tree opens in. Confirmed on the mounted host: the fixture's `app.style` card renders header-only until zoom crosses 0.80.

**To build:** Split the predicate the way Unity does: draw the EXPORTS section at SECTIONS with only its `Badge.STYLE_HEADER` rows, `}` rows and the `Badge.ADD_STYLE`/`ADD_EXPORT` affordances, and gate entry rows (and `Badge.ADD_ENTRY`) on `shows_detail`. The badges to filter on already exist (builder_graph.gd:52-55) and the projection already sets them. The section stack must be split the same way or the hit-test drifts again (CANVAS-01/05).

**Godot specifics:** `draws_section` takes only (section, lod), so a per-ROW visibility rule needs either a second predicate (`draws_export_row(badge, lod)`) beside it or a row count that varies by lod inside `section_stack` — the latter is the one the height model and the hit-test both already read, so it is the cheaper place to put it.

### `CANVAS-19` The canvas has no double-click at all — open a file, navigate to a component, edit a chip or an island, copy an import alias are all unreachable from the card

**Unity does:** Double-click is a first-class canvas gesture in four places: on the card body or pill it OPENS the module's file (the press handler arms a drag only for `ClickCount < 2`, CanvasView.uitkx:307-316, 379-386); on a markup row whose tag is a Component it NAVIGATES to that component's file; on a hook chip it opens the inline editor seeded with the chip's `SourceText`; on a code island it opens the island editor seeded with the lines joined by newline; on an import row it copies the import's binding alias (UB-123). The tooltips advertise them ('double-click to edit', '<text> - double-click copies the name').

**Godot today:** absent. `_handle_button` (builder_canvas_host.gd:386-449) never inspects `event.double_click`; the only `double_click` test anywhere under builder/ is in the library pane (builder_library_pane.gd:319). So on the canvas a single click selects a row and jumps the source pane (builder_window.gd:1007-1021) and everything else goes through the right-click row menu. Chip and island editing exist (the inline editor and `set_island` are wired) but only via the menu, which is two gestures where the reference has one, on the surface the builder is FOR.

**To build:** Add a `double_click` branch to `_handle_button`'s MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT case, before the press/drag arming: resolve the card and row as the single-click path does, then emit a new `row_activated(card_index, section, row_index)` (and `card_activated(index)` when no row is hit). Wire it in builder_window.gd to the handlers that already exist — `select_module` + open for a card, the component's file for a `LineKind.COMPONENT` markup row, the inline editor for a BODY chip or an ISLAND row, and `DisplayServer.clipboard_set` for an import row's `attr_pairs`. Every destination is already implemented; only the gesture is missing.

**Godot specifics:** Godot delivers a double-click as a separate `InputEventMouseButton` with `double_click == true` AFTER the first press/release pair, so the first click's selection has already run — which is what you want here (Unity's `ClickCount < 2` guard exists to suppress the drag arm, and the equivalent here is to not arm `_press_on_title` on the double-click event). The 4px DRAG_THRESHOLD (host.gd:534) already prevents a double-click from being read as a micro-drag.

*medium · gesture · CONFIRMED* — unity CanvasView.uitkx:307-316, 379-386 (ClickCount<2 guard / open on double-click), :719-782 (island 'double-click to edit'), :437-522 (import row: 'double-click copies the name', UB-123); godot builder_canvas_host.gd:386-449 (no double_click branch anywhere), builder_library_pane.gd:319 (the only double_click in builder/)

### `CANVAS-14` A persisted zoom is loaded without the clamp, which is the third clamp site UB-79 exists to name

**Unity does:** UB-79 (UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:1079-1091) records that the range had been 'THREE duplicated literal pairs (the canvas wheel handler, the host ctrl-wheel handler, the persisted-layout clamp) that had to agree'. The load site clamps explicitly — `_config.Zoom <= 0 ? 1 : Clamp(...)` (BuilderCanvasHost.cs:180-183) — with the comment 'A layout persisted under a different range loads outside the live one and inverts the first zoom gesture'.

**Godot today:** partial. The constants and `clamp_zoom` are correctly singular (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:22-23, 100-101) and every in-app path clamps. The load path does not: `from_dict` takes `float(d.get("zoom", 1.0))` raw (builder_canvas_layout.gd:264), and `reproject` assigns `_canvas.zoom = layout.zoom` directly (builder_window.gd:828-830), bypassing `set_camera` — which is the only place `clamp_zoom` would have been applied. A layout file written under a wider range, or hand-edited, loads out of range; the first wheel notch then clamps to the boundary, which for a stored zoom above 2.2 means scrolling UP zooms OUT. That is UB-79's named symptom, reachable the moment ZOOM_MAX ever moves — which is exactly the change UB-79 was filed about.

**To build:** Clamp in `from_dict` (`layout.zoom = Metrics.clamp_zoom(float(d.get("zoom", DEFAULT_ZOOM)))`) or, better, route the restore through `_canvas.set_camera(layout.camera, layout.zoom)` in builder_window.gd:828-830 so the one clamp site covers it — that also fixes the restore path silently skipping the `camera_changed` emission the layer selector listens to, so a restored layout currently leaves the dropdown showing the previous band until something else moves the camera.

**Godot specifics:** builder_canvas_layout.gd cannot preload the metrics without a cycle risk; the metrics file preloads Graph and Module only, so a `const Metrics = preload(...)` in the layout is safe, but doing it in builder_window.gd (which already preloads Metrics at :48) is cheaper and fixes the missing signal at the same time.

*low · risk · CONFIRMED* — unity UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:1079-1091 (UB-79) + BuilderCanvasHost.cs:178-183; godot builder_canvas_layout.gd:264 (raw float) and builder_window.gd:828-830 (direct field assignment, bypassing set_camera at builder_canvas_host.gd:123-132)

### `CANVAS-15` The grid constants exist twice — once live, once dead — which is the duplication UB-79 was filed about

**Unity does:** UB-79's root cause is not the range's value, it is that the range lived in three duplicated literal pairs 'that had to agree' (UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:1079-1091); the fix consolidated them onto `BuilderCanvasDrawing.ZoomMin/ZoomMax` (:50-59).

**Godot today:** wrong, harmlessly today. `GRID_SPACING`, `GRID_MIN_SCREEN_SPACING`, `GRID_DOT` and `GRID_COLOR` are declared in builder_canvas_edges.gd:39-42 with a doc comment describing the grid, and nothing in that file uses any of them — the grid is drawn by builder_canvas_host.gd:353-368 from its OWN identical four constants at :373-376. `EDGE_COLOR` (:44) and `EDGE_COLOR_SELECTED` (:45) are likewise dead: `_draw_edge` colours from the palette (:148). So a maintainer who tunes the grid in the file whose comment describes the grid changes nothing at all, and greps for GRID_SPACING find two answers.

**To build:** Delete the dead constants from builder_canvas_edges.gd (or, if they belong anywhere, move the single copy into builder_canvas_metrics.gd, which is the file whose stated job is 'every number the canvas measures with, in ONE place'). Same for EDGE_COLOR/EDGE_COLOR_SELECTED, whose live equivalents are canvas_palette.edge_component/edge_style.

**Godot specifics:** Both files are preloaded consts, so moving a constant between them is a mechanical change with no class-cache exposure; the metrics file is already the declared home for exactly this kind of number (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:4-14).

*low · risk · CONFIRMED* — unity UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:1079-1091 (UB-79, the duplication is the defect); godot builder_canvas_edges.gd:39-45 (dead) vs builder_canvas_host.gd:356-368, 373-376 (live), and builder_canvas_edges.gd:148 (palette wins over EDGE_COLOR)

### `CANVAS-18` A culled card's placeholder is 20% taller than the card it stands in for, so the canvas breathes as you pan

**Unity does:** The culled card keeps the same wrapper and the same estimated box so nothing shifts as it comes into range; the placeholder's geometry comes from the same `CardRect` path the real card uses (CanvasView.uitkx:238-250, BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:770-782).

**Godot today:** partial. The far branch sizes the placeholder from `M.card_height(card)` — the tallest-layout estimate (canvas_view.guitkx:113-114) — while the near branch lets the card size to its content. Measured: the estimate is 357.3 and the drawn card is 294, so a card pops 63 units shorter the moment it crosses into range and 63 taller when it leaves. Since cards are absolutely positioned nothing reflows, so the comment at :110-111 is technically satisfied, but the visible effect is the opposite of what it promises. Below Layer 3 the gap is wider still, because `card_height` ignores the band while the drawn card does not.

**To build:** Size the placeholder from `M.drawn_height(card, lod)` rather than `M.card_height(card)` — `drawn_height` is the band-aware answer and already exists two functions away (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:193-204). Keep `card_height` for the cull and the seeded layout, which genuinely want the tallest-layout number.

**Godot specifics:** Once CANVAS-01's measurement pass exists, the placeholder should reuse the last MEASURED height for that card, which is strictly better than either estimate and is what Unity's `CardRect` fallback ordering amounts to.

### Canvas input and gestures: pan, zoom, hit-testing, selection, card drag, row drag, drop bands

### `GAP-01` The row hit-test names the wrong row: the metric model and the drawn card disagree by 35-60 px at every layer

> **Duplicate of `CANVAS-01`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** HitTest picks the real element under the panel point, walks up to the first `row-{card}-{row}` name, and computes the band from THAT ELEMENT'S `worldBound`: `rel = (panelPos.y - bound.yMin) / bound.height` (BuilderCanvasHost.cs:242-311, :285-291). The geometry it measures is the geometry on screen, so it cannot drift. Unreal does the same from Slate geometry: `Geometry.AbsoluteToLocal(Event.GetScreenSpacePosition()).Y` over `Geometry.GetLocalSize().Y` (SRuitkUiBuilderInteractiveRow.cpp:22-27).

**Godot today:** wrong. `Metrics.row_hit` walks `section_stack`, a table of hand-written constants (HEADER_H 38.0, SECTION_OVERHEAD_H 34.5, IMPORT_ROW_H 19.7, MARKUP_ROW_H 22.4, CHIP_ROW_H 34.7, SIGNATURE_LINE_H 17.4), and NOTHING reconciles that table with the Controls the reconciler commits. Measured on real Godot 4.7 headless, a 5-markup-row component at zoom 0.75 (Layer 2, the layer a tree opens at): the card Control is 340x237 while `drawn_height` says 286.1. Feeding each drawn row's own card-local centre back into `row_hit`: the drawn `<VBoxContainer>` -> MISS, the first drawn `<Label>` -> MISS, the second `<Label>` (markup[2]) -> markup[0], the third (markup[3]) -> markup[1], the fourth (markup[4]) -> markup[2]. Every row click, row menu and drop is off by two rows, and markup[3]/markup[4] cannot be named by any point on the card. `card_at` additionally claims 49 px of card below its visible bottom edge, so a drop in the gap under a card lands on it -- the exact defect builder_drag.gd:111-115 says it fixed.

**To build:** Stop modelling and start measuring. Give each row Control a stable name in canvas_view.guitkx (`row-{section}-{index}`, mirroring Unity's `row-{card}-{row}`) or a `set_meta("row", [section, index])`, and have the host resolve a screen point by walking `_cards` for the deepest named Control whose `get_global_rect()` contains it, taking the band from that Control's own rect. Keep `card_at` model-based if desired (it is cheap and stable), but the ROW answer must come from geometry. If the model is kept for headless provability, then gate it: add a suite that renders a fixture card, walks every drawn row Control, and asserts `row_hit` returns that row's own index -- the assertion the current suite is missing.

**Godot specifics:** The row Controls are PanelContainers built by the reconciler and set to MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE by `_pass_mouse_through` (builder_canvas_host.gd:241-245), so `get_global_rect()` is readable but they will never be hit by Godot's own picking -- walk them yourself rather than reaching for a picking API. The cards are drawn with `scale = Vector2(zoom, zoom)` (canvas_view.guitkx:96), so a global rect is already in screen pixels; do NOT divide by zoom twice. `_fit_cards` (:318-331) calls `reset_size()` for several frames after each render, so measure after `_settle_frames` has run or accept a one-frame lag. Crucially, the constants can never be right for all cases anyway: they are theme-dependent, and the builder runs under the EDITOR theme while every test runs under the default one -- the 35-60 px error I measured is itself theme-specific.

**Risk:** This is the builder's primary editing gesture landing on a different element from the one under the cursor, with no visual to contradict it (see GAP-02). A drop 'into' the row you can see nests into an element two rows above it, and the two bottom rows of every card are unclickable. It is silent, it survives undo (the edit is correct for the row the code chose), and every existing test passes over it.

### `GAP-02` No drop hint at all: three bands resolve and nothing is ever drawn

**Unity does:** During a drag past the threshold, `PaintDropHint` (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:924-1003) paints the resolved target into the edge overlay every pointer move: the INSIDE band gets an accent fill at alpha 30/255 plus a 2 px accent outline over the whole row or card; a SIBLING band gets a 3 px dashed caret (7 on / 4 off, all divided by CurrentZoom so the weight is constant at every LOD) along the row's top or bottom edge, with 2 px end caps. UB-109 is the reason it is a caret and not a thin rule: 'the owner tried repeatedly to drop BETWEEN two elements, could not tell it had worked, and concluded it had failed'. The capability contract states it as a promise: 'a drop lands exactly where the hint is drawn' (UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:254-263). Unreal paints the same three states per row (SRuitkUiBuilderInteractiveRow.cpp:118-152: an outlined box for Inside, a 2 px rule at y=0 or y=Size.Y-2 for Before/After) and clears it on OnDragLeave because 'a caret left behind on a row the pointer has left is worse than no caret at all'.

**Godot today:** absent. `_can_drop_data` returns `true` for any dictionary carrying a `source` key, at any position, and draws nothing (builder_canvas_host.gd:457-458). The edge overlay's `_draw` paints anchors and curves only -- there is no hint branch anywhere in builder_canvas_edges.gd. A repo-wide grep for hint/caret/DropIndicator under builder/ returns only prose in comments. The user gets Godot's default drag cursor and the set_drag_preview label, and no indication whatsoever of which of the three bands they are in, which row is targeted, or whether the target is legal.

**To build:** Give the drag machine a live target and paint it. On `_can_drop_data(at, data)` (which Godot calls on every drag-over motion -- verified: `can_drop at=(49.0,17.5)`, `can_drop at=(63.0,25.5)` interleaved with the motion stream), call `Drag.resolve(graph, at, camera, zoom)`, store `{card_index, section, index, band, placement}` on the host, `queue_redraw()` the edge overlay when it changes, and return the answer of `Edits.can_place` so an illegal target reads as forbidden instead of accepting. In `RuitkBuilderCanvasEdges._draw`, add a hint pass after the edges: INSIDE -> `draw_rect` fill at ~0.12 alpha of `Palette.accent()` plus a 2 px `draw_rect(..., filled=false)`; BEFORE/AFTER -> a dashed 3 px `draw_line` run along the row's top/bottom edge with 2 px end caps, dash and cap lengths in SCREEN pixels (the overlay is already screen-space, so unlike Unity nothing needs dividing by zoom). Clear the target in `_notification(NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END)` -- the same hook GAP-03 needs.

**Godot specifics:** `_can_drop_data` is the only per-motion callback a Godot drop target gets; there is no OnDragOver/OnDragLeave pair, so DRAG_END is the only reliable clear (a drag that leaves the canvas entirely never calls `_can_drop_data` again). The overlay is already `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE` and full-rect (builder_canvas_edges.gd:63-65), so painting there cannot steal the drop. Do not paint the hint from canvas_view.guitkx: a per-row hint prop would re-render the whole card tree on every mouse move and would go through the reconciler's bailout, which is exactly the wrong place for a 60 Hz overlay. Note the hint geometry must come from the same source as GAP-01's fix, or the caret will point at a row the drop will not use.

**Risk:** The contract clause 'a drop lands exactly where the hint is drawn' is unmeetable when nothing is drawn. A markup row is 22.4 world units -- about 17 screen px at Layer 2 -- so each band is roughly 5 px of blind target. UB-109 records what this feels like: a correct drop reads as a failed one, and the user retries until something visibly moves.

### `GAP-03` Pan and card-move state survive Godot's own drag-and-drop: the camera runs away and the next gesture is hijacked

**Unity does:** One machine owns the gesture from press to release. BuilderDragService.Begin takes CapturePointer, so the pointer stream is guaranteed to arrive and PointerUp/CancelInternal always run (BuilderDragService.cs:76-90, :121-161). Panning and card-drag are mutually exclusive by construction: the pan arms only when `dragCard.Current < 0` and a press on any row calls e.StopPropagation() so the root handler never sees it (CanvasView.uitkx:117-130, :303). Unreal makes the same rule explicit -- capture on the CANVAS, and pan on right/middle only so a left row drag and a pan can never be the same event (SRuitkUiBuilderCanvas.cpp:577-590).

**Godot today:** wrong, and demonstrably. `_handle_motion` latches `_panning = true` at its own DRAG_THRESHOLD of 4 px (builder_canvas_host.gd:518-529) while Godot's native DnD arms at ~10 px of accumulated relative motion -- so every row drag starts with the pan already on. Godot then clears `gui.mouse_focus` and the BUTTON RELEASE IS NEVER DELIVERED to `_gui_input`; `_handle_motion` has no button-mask guard on either the `_panning` (:507-513) or the `_moving` (:496-503) branch, and `_notification` handles only NOTIFICATION_RESIZED (:334-338). Probed on Godot 4.7 headless against the real host: after one row drag, `NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END (_panning=true)` fires unhandled and `_panning` stays true forever. The NEXT press -- on the card's TITLE BAR -- does not move the card at all; it pans, and the first motion applies `position - _pan_from` against the stale origin, jumping the camera by (19.5, -145.8) in one frame. Motions continue to reach `_gui_input` during the drag (`motion (49.0,17.5) mask=1` interleaved with `can_drop`), so the canvas also pans UNDER its own row drag, and the drop then resolves at a camera that moved mid-gesture. `_press_index`/`_press_on_title` are likewise left stale.

**To build:** Three changes in builder_canvas_host.gd. (1) Add `func _notification(what)` handling NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END (and DRAG_BEGIN) to reset `_panning`, `_moving`, `_press_index`, `_press_on_title` and the GAP-02 hint target -- Godot delivers it to every Control precisely because the release is not routed. (2) Guard both motion branches with `if not (motion.button_mask & MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_LEFT): _panning = false; _moving = -1; return` so a stale latch cannot survive one buttonless frame. (3) Do not arm a pan on a press that could become a native drag: raise the host's own threshold above Godot's, or -- better, and what Unreal chose -- only arm the left-drag pan when `card_at(_pressed_at) < 0` (a press on empty canvas can never produce drag data, since `_get_drag_data` returns null there), leaving presses on cards to the DnD system alone.

**Godot specifics:** Verified behaviour of Godot 4.7's Viewport GUI: on a successful `_get_drag_data`, `gui.mouse_focus` is cleared, so no button-up reaches `_gui_input`; `NOTIFICATION_DRAG_BEGIN`/`NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END` are broadcast to all Controls and are the intended hook. `_get_drag_data` is handed the drag ORIGIN (`mpos - drag_accum`), not the current pointer -- so the row picked up is the pressed row, which is good, but it is resolved against the CAMERA AS IT IS THEN, and the runaway pan moves that camera between press and threshold. The drag threshold is accumulated `InputEventMouseMotion.relative`, so it is reached by any wiggle, not by net displacement. None of this is reachable from `_gui_input`-driven tests -- tests/builder_canvas_test.gd:722-739 calls `_gui_input` directly, and addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd:213-247 calls `_get_drag_data`/`_can_drop_data`/`_drop_data` directly, which is why neither has ever seen it.

**Risk:** After the first row drag of a session the canvas is stuck to the mouse and cards can no longer be moved; the fix a user finds by accident is to click once on empty canvas. Worse, the drop that ended that drag was resolved against a camera that slid ~146 px during the gesture, so the row moves somewhere nobody aimed -- a wrong edit produced by an input bug, with no hint on screen to contradict it.

### `GAP-04` A pill's clickable rectangle is half its drawn height: drawn_height returns HEADER_H where PILL_H is what is drawn

**Unity does:** L0 renders CardPill with 16 px vertical padding, a 27.75 px kind-badge line box and a 37.7 px title line box (CanvasView.uitkx:307-370), and the whole pill is the drag handle and the click target -- BuilderCanvasDrawing.BeginCardDrag arms from the pill body, and HitTest resolves the card from the picked element's own bounds, so the rectangle and the pixels are the same thing by construction.

**Godot today:** wrong. `drawn_height(card, Lod.PILL)` returns HEADER_H = 38.0 (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:196-197) while `PILL_H = 72.7` sits in the same file (:60) used only as a null-card fallback (:180, :195, :271). Measured at zoom 0.30 on Godot 4.7: the drawn card Control is 300 x 73, the model says 300 x 38. `card_at` (builder_canvas_host.gd:562) and `on_title_bar` (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:446-448, which at PILL asks `drawn_height`) both use the short rect, so the bottom 48% of every pill is dead: a click there selects nothing, a right-click opens the canvas menu instead of the card menu, and a drop over it is refused. Layer 1 is where the whole tree is on screen at once, so this is the band in which a user is most often clicking pills.

**To build:** Make `drawn_height(card, Lod.PILL)` return PILL_H, and once GAP-01's measured hit-test is in, derive it from the drawn header Control instead of a constant. Add the missing assertion to tests/builder_canvas_test.gd's `_test_hit_test_matches_what_is_drawn`: at PILL the existing loop is vacuous (no rows are ever reported, so `outside == 0` and `undrawn == 0` pass trivially) -- it needs a check that the card's own rectangle covers the drawn card.

**Godot specifics:** The pill's height comes from the editor theme's font metrics via `P.pill_badge_text()` / `P.pill_title()` (canvas_view.guitkx:137-146, canvas_palette.gd:249-256), so a fixed constant will be wrong again the moment the editor's font size changes -- the durable fix is measurement, and PILL_H is only the stopgap that makes today's error small. Note the palette is the hand-written @tool script for the documented static-var reason, so these sizes ARE readable from editor code; the metrics file just does not ask.

**Risk:** Half of every card at the architecture layer does not answer the mouse, and the failure is positional -- it works at the top of a pill and not at the bottom, which reads as 'the canvas is flaky' rather than as a bug with a cause.

### `GAP-05` The two band coercions are missing: the root row and continuation clauses refuse drops instead of accepting them as 'inside'

**Unity does:** Both the hit-test and the drop sink COERCE the band to 1 (inside) in two cases, belt and braces: when `rowIdx == FirstElementRow(node)` -- the return root, which can never take a sibling because a component returns exactly one element -- and when `row.Kind == Directive && row.ClauseIndex > 0`, a continuation clause (@else/@elif/@case/@default) which is 'structurally bound'. So the whole height of those rows is a valid inside target and the drop always works (BuilderCanvasHost.cs:285-291; BuilderWindow.cs:2613-2619, applied twice because 'the sink can be reached by a path that did not go through the hit-test').

**Godot today:** absent as a coercion, present only as a refusal. `Metrics.row_hit` returns the raw band with no coercion (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:528-535) and `Drag._placement_of` maps it straight to BEFORE/AFTER (edits/builder_drag.gd:143-153). The rule is instead enforced downstream by `Edits.can_place`, which returns ok=false with 'a component returns exactly one root element -- wrap them in a fragment' for any BEFORE/AFTER on a depth-0 row, and a similar message when the parent is a directive (edits/builder_edits.gd:56-71). Net effect: on a component whose root has no children yet -- the state every new component is in -- the top third of the root row refuses, and the bottom third refuses too (band 2 only becomes FIRST_CHILD when the next listed row is deeper, edits/builder_drag.gd:157-162). Two thirds of the first row a user aims at is a dead zone that answers with a lecture about fragments. `Graph.Line.clause_index` exists (canvas/builder_graph.gd:106) and is read only by the row context menu (chrome/builder_window.gd:1097, :1103) -- never by the drop path.

**To build:** Coerce in `Metrics.row_hit`, where Unity coerces: after computing the band, force it to 1 when the row is the first non-directive markup row of the card (add a `first_element_row(card)` helper mirroring BuilderCanvasDrawing.FirstElementRow -- note it must key on the first NON-directive row, not literal index 0, because a directive can wrap the root) or when `row.kind == DIRECTIVE and row.clause_index > 0`. Re-apply the same coercion in `Drag.resolve` so a caller that bypasses `row_hit` gets it too. Keep `can_place` as the backstop; it should then only fire for genuine second-root cases the coercion cannot reach. As a bonus this makes the row-drag arm rule match Unity's: a coerced root row can no longer produce a sibling move.

**Godot specifics:** `row_hit` is a static pure function on Metrics and already receives the card, so the coercion is headlessly testable as a pure assertion -- add it to builder_canvas_test.gd next to the existing band cases. `clause_index` is already projected by builder_graph_service.gd, so no new analysis is needed. The Godot-specific twist is GUITKX0303 (a directive body cannot be empty), which is the listed deliberate divergence: coercing an empty clause to 'inside' must go through the seeded-placeholder path rather than writing an empty body.

**Risk:** The first drop a new user attempts -- a Label onto the root of a fresh component -- fails two times in three, with a message about fragments that does not describe what they did. Combined with GAP-02 (no hint) there is nothing on screen that distinguishes the third that works from the two thirds that do not.

### `GAP-06` A drop with no row under the cursor is refused, where Unity appends to the root's children

**Unity does:** A card-level target (RowIdx = -1, Band = 1) is a first-class outcome, not a miss. For an insert: `InsertChildTag` on `node.Markup[FirstElementRow(node)]` -- 'POC: a drop with no row under the cursor, and every inside band, appends to the target's children' (BuilderWindow.cs:2634-2640). For a MOVE: the row is retargeted to the root with `appendToRoot = true` and relocates to the end of the root's children, and the toast says so: 'Released between rows - moved to the end of <root tag>', because 'the alternative is the user concluding the gesture is broken' (BuilderWindow.cs:2745-2760, :2830-2834). The hint painter draws the whole card outlined for this case (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:940-968).

**Godot today:** absent. `drop_library_entry` returns false the moment `hit["row"]` is null (chrome/builder_window.gd:2258-2261) and `drop_row` returns false when the target row is null (:2340-2343); both reach a generic toast. So releasing on a card's header, on a section heading, in the padding below the last row, or anywhere on a pill at Layer 1 (where `row_at` deliberately returns not-found, builder_canvas_host.gd:541-542) does nothing at all. `Drag.resolve` already returns a valid card-level hit with `row = null` and `placement = INSIDE` (edits/builder_drag.gd:118-131), so the information is there and both consumers throw it away.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Two specific paths are missing the card-level fallback, not the feature as a whole: (1) the ELEMENT/COMPONENT tag insert, `if row == null or row.kind == IMPORT: return false` at builder_window.gd:2257-2259, which should retarget to the root's first non-directive markup row with Placement.INSIDE; and (2) `drop_row`'s `if target == null: return false` at :2340-2342, which should retarget to the root and toast 'moved to the end of <root>'. Drop the claims that 'most of a card's surface silently rejects drops' and 'at Layer 1 the entire canvas does' -- at Layer 1 element drops are the only ones that fail, and they fail because `row_at` is deliberately not-found there, which is the same one fix.

**To build:** In `drop_library_entry`, when `hit.found` and `hit.row == null`, resolve the target to the card's first non-directive markup row and insert with Placement.INSIDE (append as last child) -- reusing the `first_element_row` helper GAP-05 needs. In `drop_row`, do the same and toast the outcome ('moved to the end of <root>'). Both already have the card in hand.

**Godot specifics:** At Lod.PILL `row_at` returns not-found by design, so the card-level path is the ONLY way a drop can ever land at Layer 1 -- without it, Layer 1 is a read-only view even though `_can_drop_data` accepts every payload there and shows an accepting cursor. Pure model work, fully testable in tests/builder_edits_test.gd as a before/after string.

**Risk:** Most of a card's surface silently rejects drops. At Layer 1 the entire canvas does, while the cursor says the drop is accepted.

### `GAP-16` Nothing in the suites or the gesture rig drives Godot's real input routing, which is why GAP-01 and GAP-03 were never seen

**Unity does:** n/a -- this is about the Godot verification loop.

**Godot today:** wrong in two specific ways. (1) `tests/builder_canvas_test.gd:722-739` drives gestures by calling `host._gui_input(event)` directly. The suite's own comment already names this limitation for mouse_filter ('the one path that cannot reproduce a filter problem'), but the same blind spot hides Godot's DnD interaction entirely: a directly-called `_gui_input` never triggers `_get_drag_data`, never clears mouse focus, never withholds the release -- so `_panning` always clears and GAP-03 is unreachable. Even `addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd`, the rig built specifically to push real input, calls `lib0._get_drag_data(grab)` / `canvas._can_drop_data(...)` / `canvas._drop_data(...)` by hand (:213-247) and prints OK. (2) `_test_hit_test_matches_what_is_drawn` (:140-176) compares `Metrics.row_hit` to `Metrics.drawn_height` -- both computed from `Metrics.section_stack`. It is the model checked against itself, which is why it passes while every row click on a real card is off by two rows. At Lod.PILL the loop is vacuous: no rows are ever reported there, so both of its assertions hold trivially over a rectangle that is half the drawn size.

**To build:** Two tests. (a) A ROUTING test: push `InputEventMouseButton`/`InputEventMouseMotion` through `Input.parse_input_event` with a non-zero `relative` (Godot accumulates `relative`, not position, for its drag threshold) at a host sized larger than the headless 64x64 root, then assert after the drop that `_panning == false`, `_moving == -1`, and that the camera did not move during a row drag. This works headlessly -- I ran exactly this shape against the real host and it reproduced the latch, the (19.5, -145.8) camera jump and the unhandled `NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END`. (b) A MEASURED-GEOMETRY test: render a fixture card, walk the committed row Controls, and for each assert that `Metrics.row_hit` (or its replacement) returns that row's own index, and that the card Control's size matches `drawn_height`. That test is what turns GAP-01 from invisible into a red line.

**Godot specifics:** Headless Godot 4.7 routes `Input.parse_input_event` through the real Viewport GUI stack, including `_get_drag_data`/`_can_drop_data`/`_drop_data` and the DRAG_BEGIN/END notifications -- so this is CI-runnable, no window required. Two gotchas found the hard way: the headless root Window is 64x64, so give the host an explicit `size` and PRESET_TOP_LEFT rather than PRESET_FULL_RECT; and set `InputEventMouseMotion.relative` or the drag never arms. For (b), measure after `SETTLE_FRAMES` -- `_fit_cards` reshapes cards for several frames after each render.

**Risk:** This is the gap that let the other gaps ship. Three of the four criticals in this report are trivially reproducible headlessly, and every existing test passes over them because each one asks the code the same question the code asks itself.
