### `GAP-07` A restored layout's zoom is never clamped and bypasses set_camera, so the toolbar can name the wrong layer

**Unity does:** Mount normalises the stored view before anything reads it: `_zoom = _config.Zoom <= 0f ? 1f : Mathf.Clamp(_config.Zoom, ZoomMin, ZoomMax)`, commented 'A layout persisted under a different range loads outside the live one and inverts the first zoom gesture; clamp on load so the stored camera is always inside it' (BuilderCanvasHost.cs:178-183). ZoomMin/ZoomMax are one pair of constants consumed by the wheel, the ctrl-wheel, the loader and the fit (UB-79).

**Godot today:** partial. The constants ARE single-sourced (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:22-23, consumed by `clamp_zoom` at :101 and by the wheel, `fit_to_view` and `frame_card`) -- UB-79 is honoured. But the restore path writes the fields directly: `_canvas.camera = layout.camera; _canvas.zoom = layout.zoom` (chrome/builder_window.gd:828-830), bypassing `set_camera`, which is the only thing that calls `clamp_zoom` (builder_canvas_host.gd:123-132). The loader does not clamp either -- `layout.zoom = float(d.get("zoom", 1.0))` (canvas/builder_canvas_layout.gd:264). A hand-edited or older layout file with zoom 0 or 5.0 loads as-is; at zoom 0 every card collapses onto the camera point and `world_to_screen` degenerates. Bypassing `set_camera` also skips the `camera_changed` emit, and `_sync_layer_selector` is wired to nothing else (chrome/builder_window.gd:699-700), so on restore the layer dropdown keeps whatever index it had.

**To build:** Clamp on load in `CanvasLayout.load` (`layout.zoom = Metrics.clamp_zoom(z)` with the `<= 0 -> DEFAULT_ZOOM` sentinel Unity uses), and change the restore in `reproject` to call `_canvas.set_camera(layout.camera, layout.zoom)` so the clamp, the redraw and the `camera_changed` emit that syncs the dropdown all happen on the one path.

**Godot specifics:** `set_camera` also calls `queue_redraw()` and `_render()`; during `reproject` the direct writes are followed by `show_graph`, so the render happens either way -- the only thing lost is the clamp and the signal. Cheap to gate: builder_canvas_test.gd already exercises Layout save/load round-trips.

**Risk:** A stored view outside the range inverts the first zoom gesture (Unity's stated symptom) and a zoom of 0 renders an empty canvas that looks like a load failure. The stale dropdown is a smaller, permanent lie about which layer you are in.

### `GAP-08` The kind chip is not a drag handle

**Unity does:** The 'component'/'hook'/'styles'/'utils' badge on a card is a SECOND drag source: dragging it and dropping on another card wires that module in, using the same payload and the same drop rules as dragging it out of the library, self-containment refusal included. UB-182: 'the chip is just a second handle, next to the thing itself rather than in a list of everything'. The payload uses the module's FIRST EXPORT, not its title, because 'a module's EXPORT is what an importer writes'. The arm returns a bool so that when it declines the press bubbles to the header and moves the card instead -- 'the two gestures share one press and only one of them may have it'. UB-186 is the follow-up: the handler must be on BOTH chips (the L0 pill badge and the L1/L2 header badge), or the gesture is missing at exactly the layer the owner works at. Tooltip: 'drag onto another card to use this module'.

**Godot today:** absent. `_get_drag_data` resolves a row and then only accepts MARKUP rows -- `var rows: Array = card.markup if int(hit["section"]) == int(Metrics.Section.MARKUP) else []` (builder_canvas_host.gd:466-487) -- so a press on the badge produces no drag data; the badge is a Label inside the header, set to MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE by `_pass_mouse_through`, so the press falls through to the host and becomes a card move (which is the correct FALLBACK, just with nothing in front of it). Nothing in the builder carries a tooltip about dragging a chip.

**To build:** Recognise the header/pill badge as a drag source. Because the hit-test is model-based, the cleanest route is a `Metrics.on_kind_badge(card, world, card_width, lod)` band predicate alongside `on_title_bar`, checked in `_get_drag_data` before the markup-row branch, returning `{ source: "module", path: card.file_path }` -- the payload `_on_canvas_drop` ALREADY handles (chrome/builder_window.gd:1053-1055 -> `drop_module`), which already does style-onto-element and import-onto-card and refuses self-containment (:2353-2372). Note `drop_module` already uses `source_card.exports[0]`, matching Unity's CardDragName rule. So this is one predicate plus four lines; the whole drop side exists.

**Godot specifics:** Do it at both bands: at Lod.PILL the badge is inside the region `on_title_bar` returns true for, so the badge test must come FIRST or the pill will keep starting a card move -- this is UB-186 in Godot form, and the mirror image of Unity's bool-return bubbling rule. Add a `tooltip_text` on the badge Label in canvas_view.guitkx; a Label with MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE shows no tooltip, so either set MOUSE_FILTER_PASS on that one Label (and teach `_pass_mouse_through` to leave it alone, the way it already exempts BaseButton) or put the tooltip on the card.

**Risk:** The only way to wire one module into another is to find it in the library pane by name. On a tree where both cards are already on screen that is a detour through a list, which is the exact complaint UB-182 was raised about.

### `GAP-09` No double-click gestures on the canvas: neither card-opens-file nor component-row-navigates

**Unity does:** Two double-click routes. On a CARD: `if (e.ClickCount >= 2) { onOpenFile(node.FilePath); e.StopPropagation(); return; }`, checked before the select branch, and the drag handles guard against it (`e.Button == 0 && e.ClickCount < 2` on the header and pill, and BeginCardDrag refuses on ClickCount >= 2). On a markup ROW whose kind is Component: `onRowNavigate(row.Text.Trim('<','>'))` -- jump to that component's own file. UB-80 states the consistency rule: 'canvas rows already double-click to navigate to a component's file - keep the two gestures consistent' (which is why the library's double-click frames a card).

**Godot today:** absent on the canvas. A grep for `double_click` under builder/ hits only chrome/builder_library_pane.gd:319 and the folder pane; builder_canvas_host.gd's `_handle_button` never reads `event.double_click` (:408-432) and the row path emits `row_clicked` unconditionally. The half of UB-80 that the library implements (`entry_framed` -> `frame_card`) is present and correct; the canvas half it was meant to be consistent WITH is missing. There is also no drag guard against a double-click: the first click of a pair records `_pressed_at`/`_press_on_title`, so a double-click on a title bar can still leave a card-move armed.

**To build:** In `_handle_button`'s MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT pressed branch, check `event.double_click` first: with a row hit whose `kind == Graph.LineKind.COMPONENT`, resolve the tag to a card via `graph` and call the same route `_on_library_framed` uses (`select_module` + `frame_card`); with no row hit but a card hit, `select_module(card.file_path)`. Guard the drag arm with `not event.double_click` so the second click of a pair cannot leave `_press_on_title` set.

**Godot specifics:** Godot sets `InputEventMouseButton.double_click` on the second PRESS (there is no ClickCount ladder), so the ordering is simpler than Unity's: test it before the select/drag arming, and remember that the first click of the pair has already selected -- which is the behaviour Unity has too. Everything needed is already on the host: `card_at`, `row_at`, and the graph.

**Risk:** Navigating from a usage to a definition -- the thing a graph view is for -- has no gesture on the canvas; the user has to find the card by eye or go through the library. Low blast radius, high friction.

### `GAP-10` Every drop outcome collapses into three generic toasts

**Unity does:** No drop outcome is ever silent OR vague. The service toasts 'No drop target - release over a card or row.' for a release over nothing, and the sink names the actual rule for every refusal: 'A component can't contain itself.', 'Style modules have no hooks.', 'Style imports go on components.', '<name> is already imported.', 'Read-only file', 'Lost track of the dragged row - press it again.', 'That row is no longer there - try the drag again.', 'Dropped on itself - nothing moved.', "Can't move an element into its own subtree.", 'This clause is empty - drop a new element into it first.', 'Drop into a specific @case arm, not the @switch head.' -- and successes report too ('Moved <row> before|after|into <target>', 'Released between rows - moved to the end of <root>'), because a correct drop that reads as a failure is UB-109's whole lesson.

**Godot today:** partial. Nothing is silent -- `apply_edit` returns false on an unchanged buffer (chrome/builder_window.gd:866-867), so a refused `Edits.move` does surface -- but `_on_canvas_drop` has exactly three messages: 'Couldn't place <X> there.', 'Couldn't move that row there.', 'Couldn't move that module there.' (:1041-1055). The rich reasons that DO exist -- `Edits.can_place`'s two fragment messages (edits/builder_edits.gd:56-71) -- are toasted only on the library-insert path (:2263-2269) and not on the move path, which routes through `Edits.move`'s silent `return source`. Self-subtree (edits/builder_edits.gd:196-197), dropped-on-itself (:2341-2343), cross-file (:2336-2339) and stale-row (edits/builder_drag.gd:192-202) all reach the same one sentence. No successful drop or move is reported at all.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: State it as: the MOVE path has no reason at all. `Edits.move` (builder_edits.gd:190-211) silently `return source`s for a failed `can_place`, a self-subtree target (:203) and a null row, so `drop_row` (builder_window.gd:2330-2350) can only answer with `apply_edit`'s unchanged-buffer false -> 'Couldn't move that row there.' Cross-file (:2338) and dropped-on-itself (:2341) are DETECTED and then discarded into the same sentence. `drop_module`'s three refusals (:2359-2364) likewise. And no drop of any kind reports success, which is the half UB-109 is actually about. The fix is a `{ok, reason}` return on `Edits.move` plus success toasts -- not a wholesale replacement of a message system that already works on the insert path.

**To build:** Give `Edits.move` a `{ text, ok, reason }` return shape mirroring `can_place`, and have `drop_row`/`drop_library_entry` return that reason to the toast instead of a boolean. Add success reporting on the move path ('Moved <row> into <target>'), which is what makes a correct-but-surprising outcome legible. Add the specific refusals for cross-file and dropped-on-itself where they are already detected.

**Godot specifics:** `toast()` already exists and is the ported Toast (chrome/builder_window.gd:196-213). All of this is pure model work assertable in tests/builder_edits_test.gd, which already drives every structural edit as a before/after string -- the reason strings are the natural thing to assert alongside them.

**Risk:** Every failure looks the same, so the user cannot tell a structural refusal from a mis-aimed drop. With no hint (GAP-02) and a mis-registered hit-test (GAP-01) already in play, the message is the only feedback there is.

### `GAP-11` Pan and zoom re-render every card through the reconciler, because the camera is baked into each card's position prop

**Unity does:** The camera is ONE transform on ONE element: the world layer carries `Translate(Px(camX), Px(camY))` and `Scale(zoom, zoom)` (CanvasView.uitkx:189-196), so a pan changes one node's style and every card's props are unchanged -- the fiber bails out on all of them. The dot grid is deliberately outside that transform and painted in screen space (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:512-514).

**Godot today:** divergent-defect (performance). `CanvasView` computes `var pos = M.world_to_screen(Vector2(c.x, c.y), camera, zoom)` per card and passes it as the `at` prop, plus `zoom` as the scale (canvas/canvas_view.guitkx:52-64, :93-96). So every pan motion event and every wheel notch changes a prop on EVERY card, defeating the bailout entirely, and `_handle_motion`'s pan branch calls `_render()` per motion (builder_canvas_host.gd:511), followed by `_pass_mouse_through` walking the whole committed subtree for the next 8 frames (:288-309). On a twenty-card tree that is a full reconcile plus a full tree walk at mouse-event rate. The grid IS correctly screen-space (:353-368), matching the reference.

**To build:** Move the camera onto the container: set `_cards.position = camera` and `_cards.scale = Vector2(zoom, zoom)` on the host, drop `camera`/`zoom` from the card position props, and have the view lay cards out in WORLD coordinates. Then a pan is two property writes and no reconcile; a zoom still needs a re-render only because the LOD band and the cull change, and both change rarely. Keep `viewport`/cull props keyed on the camera but recompute them on a debounce rather than per event.

**Godot specifics:** A Control's `scale` is a render/transform property that does not re-run layout on children, so scaling `_cards` behaves like Unity's world container -- the cards keep measuring in card-local units and text does not re-wrap as you zoom, which is exactly the property canvas_view.guitkx:56-58 says it wants. `_edges` must stay a sibling of `_cards` (not a child) so it keeps painting in screen space, which is already the arrangement (:94-102). Note this also makes GAP-01's measured hit-test cheaper: `get_global_rect()` on a row already accounts for the parent transform.

**Risk:** Not a correctness bug, but it is the canvas's busiest path and the one the dogfooding argument rests on: a pan that costs a full reconcile per mouse event is the worst possible advertisement for the reconciler the builder is a builder for.

### `GAP-12` Card sections have no height cap, so one long module can own the canvas

**Unity does:** Every card section is capped and scrolls on its own: IMPORTS 140 px, BODY 260 px, EXPORTS 280 px, RETURN-MARKUP 340 px, code island 220 px (CanvasView.uitkx:424, 531, 787, 979, 764). Those scrollers are restyled to the window chrome, given 6 px scrollbars, wired to repaint the edge layer on scroll so clamped anchors track live, and given the Ctrl+wheel escape hatch so the canvas can still be zoomed over them (BuilderCanvasHost.cs:704-757). PaintDropHint clamps a hint to the visible slice of its section so it never bleeds over the rows that occlude it (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:936-938).

**Godot today:** absent. No ScrollContainer and no maximum height appears anywhere in canvas_view.guitkx; a card is a PanelContainer over a VBoxContainer that grows to its content, and `_fit_cards` `reset_size()`s it to exactly that (builder_canvas_host.gd:318-331). `Metrics.section_stack` likewise reserves `rows * row_height` with no cap (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:228-252). A 300-line component therefore draws a card thousands of units tall, which at Layer 2 dominates the viewport, pushes every other card's seeded slot apart, and makes the markup rows of a real file unreachable without panning through it.

**To build:** Cap the section heights in `section_stack` (the height model) and in the view together -- they must agree, which is the file's own stated rule -- and give the capped sections a ScrollContainer in canvas_view.guitkx. Then the Ctrl+wheel escape becomes necessary and should be added at the same time: in `_handle_button`'s wheel branch, zoom regardless when `event.ctrl_pressed`, and set the section ScrollContainers' `mouse_filter` so a plain wheel scrolls them.

**Godot specifics:** A ScrollContainer inside a card is the one place `_pass_mouse_through` must NOT blanket-IGNORE, or the section will never scroll -- extend the BaseButton exemption at builder_canvas_host.gd:242-244 to ScrollContainer/ScrollBar. Because the reconciler rebuilds these on every render, the exemption has to live in that walk rather than being set once, exactly as the existing comment argues (:236-240). And a scrolled section breaks the card-local hit-test: the row offsets inside it shift by the scroll value, which is another reason GAP-01's fix must measure rather than model.

**Risk:** The canvas stops being a graph view for any tree containing one real file. It is also the precondition that makes the ctrl+wheel behaviour 'not applicable' -- so that N/A is borrowed against this gap, not earned.

### `GAP-15` The parity gate is green over this whole subsystem and asks nothing about it

**Unity does:** n/a -- this is about the Godot gate, judged against the behaviours the Unity inventory lists.

**Godot today:** wrong. Of the 73 entries, six touch this area and one of them is hollow: `["drop target", "func _can_drop_data"]` is answered by a function that returns `data is Dictionary and data.has("source")` -- true for every payload at every position, drawing nothing and rejecting nothing (builder_canvas_host.gd:457-458). It answers the token and none of the behaviour Unity's HitTest carries. The larger problem is what has no entry at all: no entry for the drop HINT (the contract's 'a drop lands exactly where the hint is drawn'), none for cursor-anchored zoom, none for panning, none for the two band coercions, none for the clamp-on-load, none for the card-level append-to-root, none for the kind-chip drag, none for the canvas double-click routes, none for per-outcome drop reporting. Nine of the sixteen gaps in this report are invisible to the gate by construction.

**To build:** Add entries with tokens that can only be satisfied by the real thing: `["PaintDropHint", "func _draw_drop_hint"]`, `["band coercion: the root row and continuation clauses are always INSIDE", "func first_element_row"]`, `["card-level drop appends to the root's children", "appends to the root"]` (or a named function), `["clamp the stored zoom on load", "clamp_zoom(layout"]`, `["BeginCardDrag from the kind chip", "func on_kind_badge"]`, `["WheelZoom anchored on the cursor", "func zoom_about"]`, `["gesture state is cleared when Godot's DnD ends", "NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END"]`. And replace the `_can_drop_data` entry with one naming the resolver it should consult.

**Godot specifics:** The gate greps the source text under builder/, so a token must be an identifier that only the working implementation would contain -- prefer new function names over strings, since the gate's own preamble warns that prose 'rots into a test of its own comments'. Every one of the suggested tokens is cheap to satisfy honestly and impossible to satisfy accidentally.

**Risk:** A green gate over a subsystem with three critical defects. The gate's own preamble says it exists because 'a drop handler with no drag' shipped once; the current shape would not catch a hint that is never drawn, a coercion that never runs, or a clamp that is never applied.

### `GAP-13` No cursor affordances: nothing on the canvas says it can be grabbed or dragged

**Unity does:** Three cursors, each quoted from the POC: `#canvasWrap { cursor: grab }` -> MouseCursor.Pan on the canvas pane (BuilderWindow.cs:396-398); `.card-title { cursor: move }` / `body.lod0 .pill { cursor: move }` -> MouseCursor.MoveArrow set on the header and pill at AttachToPanel, 'so the card's drag handle says so on hover, distinct from the grab every card would otherwise inherit from the pane' (BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:326-335); `.lib-item { cursor: grab }` -> MouseCursor.Pan on library rows, plus an accent border on hover (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:731-740).

**Godot today:** absent. A grep for `cursor` under builder/ finds only prose in comments and the ledger's undo cursor -- `mouse_default_cursor_shape` is never set anywhere, on the host, on the cards, or on the library rows. Nothing distinguishes the 38-unit title bar (the only drag handle) from the rest of the card, which matters more here than in Unity because on_title_bar is a narrow band and missing it silently pans instead (see GAP-03).

**To build:** Set `mouse_default_cursor_shape = Control.CURSOR_DRAG` on the canvas host. For the title bar the model-based hit-test means there is no Control to hang a cursor on, so set it dynamically in `_handle_motion`: `mouse_default_cursor_shape = CURSOR_MOVE if Metrics.on_title_bar(...) else CURSOR_DRAG`, which `_track_hover` already computes the inputs for. Set CURSOR_DRAG on the library entry Buttons in `_entry_row`.

**Godot specifics:** `mouse_default_cursor_shape` is only consulted for a Control that is not MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE, so per-card cursors are impossible while `_pass_mouse_through` blankets the subtree -- the host-level dynamic shape is the only route, and it is cheap because the hover walk already runs. CURSOR_DRAG is Godot's grab-hand; CURSOR_MOVE is the four-arrow.

**Risk:** Polish, but it is the affordance that teaches the title-bar rule. Without it a user learns 'sometimes dragging a card moves it and sometimes the whole canvas jumps' and concludes the canvas is unreliable.

### `GAP-14` Drop band edges are thirds, not Unity's 0.3 / 0.7

**Unity does:** `band = rel < 0.3f ? 0 : rel > 0.7f ? 2 : 1` -- the middle band is 40% of the row and the sibling bands 30% each, quoted from the POC's 6.6 band math (BuilderCanvasHost.cs:285-291, BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:274-277). Unreal uses the same split via FRuitkUiBuilderDrop::BandFor.

**Godot today:** partial/divergent. `const BAND_EDGE := 1.0 / 3.0`, giving 33.3 / 33.3 / 33.3 (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:493, :531-534). The in-file comment claims the middle is 'the widest target, because it is the commonest intent', which is true in Unity's numbers and not in these -- the three bands are equal here. The difference is small in isolation, but it makes the sibling bands 11% larger than the reference at exactly the rows where the sibling placement is the illegal one (GAP-05), and it is undocumented.

**To build:** Either change BAND_EDGE to 0.3 (a one-constant edit, single-sourced already, with the 1-0.3 upper edge falling out) and fix the comment, or record the deviation in CLAUDE.md as deliberate with its reason. Do not leave a comment describing Unity's proportions over a constant that does not produce them.

**Godot specifics:** BAND_EDGE is already the single source read by `row_hit`; nothing else computes a band, so this is genuinely one line plus a test. Assertable purely in builder_canvas_test.gd.

**Risk:** Minor on its own; it matters as an unrecorded drift between a constant and the comment above it, which is the pattern the parity gate exists to catch and cannot.

### Graph projection: cards, rows, sections, imports, hook chips, markup walk, edges

### `GP-01` The card's section list is written TWICE and the two copies disagree — the hit-test addresses rows that are not drawn, and Delete removes them

**Unity does:** Unity has one card layout and it is MEASURED, not modelled: `CanvasView.uitkx` renders the sections (signature only when `lod >= 1 && Signature.Length > 0`; BODY when `Body.Count > 0 || Kind == Component || Kind == Hook`, headed "BODY — HOOKS & STATE" or "EXPORTS"; EXPORTS-detail when `ExportDetail.Count > 0`), and the edge/anchor painter then reads the REAL element geometry back out (`AnchorOf` queries the named marker element, `CardRect` reads the measured `card-{index}` layout). Row targeting is therefore whatever was actually laid out; `LastSectionOf` exists only to suppress one border. There is no second, independent model of where a row sits.

**Godot today:** wrong. `canvas_view.guitkx` gates sections on `card.kind` while `builder_canvas_metrics.gd:section_stack` gates them on content and a different kind test, and the metrics stack is the ONLY thing `row_hit`, `drawn_height`, `card_at` and every edge anchor consult. Three concrete disagreements, all confirmed by running the projection headlessly: (1) STYLE card — view line 174 hides the signature for `card.kind == 2`, metrics line 231 includes it whenever `signature != ""`, and a style module's binding decl always yields one (probe: `thing.style.guitkx` sig='panel', stack = SIGNATURE top=38 h=32.4, EXPORTS top=70.4). Every export/entry row on every style card is therefore hit-tested 32.4px below where it is drawn, i.e. ~1.5 rows off. (2) UTIL/VALUE/MODULE/UNKNOWN card — view line 196 draws the whole BODY section (chips + "+ hook" + "+ code") for any `kind != 2`, metrics line 239 omits it unless kind is COMPONENT or HOOK (probe: `util.guitkx` stack = SIGNATURE + EXPORTS only). The drawn body band is invisible to the model, so a click on it reports the section BELOW it. (3) HOOK / UTIL / unparseable-COMPONENT card — `_fill_export_detail` populates `export_detail` (probe: hook and broken-component cards both have export_detail=1), metrics line 247 adds an EXPORTS section for it, view line 231 refuses to draw it unless `kind == 2`. Probe: hook card `drawn_height(FULL)=196.5` against ~139.6 of drawn content, so `card_at` claims the card ~57px below its visible bottom and `row_at` reports a phantom EXPORTS row there. The consequence is not cosmetic: `builder_window.gd:_on_row_clicked` sets `_menu_row = _row_of(card, section, index)` and `_delete_selection` calls `Edits.remove(buffer, _menu_row)` on it — an EXPORTS row's span is `[decl.at, decl.next]`, the whole exported declaration. So a click on a util card's chip band followed by Delete removes the module's entire declaration, and the user's pointer was over a hook chip.

**To build:** Make `section_stack` the single gate and have the view ask it, exactly as `draws_section` is already asked. Concretely: move the three predicates into metrics (`has_signature(card) = not card.signature.is_empty() and card.kind != STYLE`, `has_body(card) = kind in [COMPONENT, HOOK]` or `card.body` non-empty, `has_exports(card) = not card.export_detail.is_empty()`), have `section_stack` use them, and have `canvas_view.guitkx` render a section only when the stack contains it — the view already receives the card, so it can call `M.section_stack(card)` or a `M.draws(card, section, lod)` helper in each `@if`. Then decide the EXPORTS question deliberately (see GP-12) rather than by two files' accident.

**Godot specifics:** The card layer is `.guitkx` and the hit model is a hand-written `.gd`, which is exactly why they drifted: the reconciler's `@if` gates live in the compiled view, the metrics live in a preload const, and nothing forces them through one expression. The fix has to stay preload-const (`M` is already an inline `preload` inside each component body — a top-level decl would lower to a `static var` whose initialiser has not run on the first editor render). Note also that `canvas_view.guitkx`'s generated `.gd` is COMMITTED and gated by `tests/builder_view_build.gd`, so the view change must be rebuilt and committed with it.

### `GP-02` Clicking a code-island line selects the component's FIRST MARKUP ROW, and Delete then removes the root element

**Unity does:** An island click selects the island: `onLineSelect(path, IslandStartLine, IslandEndLine, "code island")`, and a double-click opens the multiline island editor seeded with the joined lines. The island is a first-class selectable thing with its own recorded source range.

**Godot today:** wrong. `_row_of` maps `Metrics.Section.ISLAND` to `return card.markup[0] if not card.markup.is_empty() else null` — the first markup row, not the island. `_on_row_clicked` then sets `_menu_row` to that markup row, jumps the source pane to the ROOT ELEMENT's line, and `_delete_selection` calls `Edits.remove(buffer, markup[0])`. So at Layer 3, clicking any SETUP line and pressing Delete deletes the component's whole returned tree. The comment above it ("The SETUP block is edited whole, not row by row") explains why a per-line answer is wrong but does not explain why the answer is a markup row.

**To build:** Return a row that represents the island: either a synthetic `Graph.Line` built from `card.island_start_line`/`island_end_line` (kind PLAIN, `at`/`end_at` from the island's real span so `Edits.remove` is span-exact), or `null` plus a dedicated island branch in `_on_row_clicked`/`_on_row_context` that selects the island and offers "Edit setup…" (see GP-04). Add the island's absolute offsets to `Graph.Card` while you are there — it currently carries only 1-based lines, so any island edit has to go through `set_island`'s line arithmetic.

**Godot specifics:** `Graph.Line` is a RefCounted with spans (`at`/`end_at`) — the machinery for a span-exact island row already exists; only the row is missing. Headlessly testable: `builder_edits_test.gd` already drives `_row_of`-shaped rows through `Edits.remove`.

### `GP-03` No double-click anywhere on the canvas: hook chips, code islands and style entries cannot be edited in place

**Unity does:** Capability §5: "Editable in place: attribute values, directive headers, hook chips, style entry lines, code islands (multiline), and element rows." A hook chip's own tooltip says so — `<SourceText> (double-click to edit)` — and the island's is "double-click to edit". Double-clicking an IMPORT row instead copies the binding via `onCopyImportAlias` (UB-123: "we cannot copy the name of the variable in the import"). One floating editor serves all of them.

**Godot today:** absent. `builder_canvas_host.gd:_handle_button` never reads `event.double_click`; grepping the whole builder for `double_click` finds exactly one hit, in `builder_library_pane.gd:319`. `_inline.open_at` has four call sites and all four are menu- or seed-driven: the directive "Edit header…" item, the attribute-value flow, the seeded wrap header, and the line just seeded by "+ hook"/"+ code". So an EXISTING hook chip, an EXISTING island and an EXISTING style entry line have no edit gesture at all — the inline editor can only ever edit something the builder itself just created. There is also no clipboard path for an import binding.

**To build:** In `_handle_button`'s MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT/pressed branch, when `event.double_click`, resolve `row_at` and dispatch by section: BODY → open the inline editor with `{kind: "body", row}` seeded from `row.source_text` (the token `_on_inline_committed` already handles); ISLAND → open the multiline editor with `{kind: "island", from: island_start_line, to: island_end_line}` seeded from `\n`.join(island_lines) (also already handled); EXPORTS on a style card → the entry editor; MARKUP/element → the attribute or row editor; IMPORTS → `DisplayServer.clipboard_set(row.attr_pairs[0])` plus a toast. Emit it as a `row_activated(card, section, row)` signal so the window owns the dispatch, matching the existing `row_clicked` spine.

**Godot specifics:** Godot delivers the double-click as a second `InputEventMouseButton` with `double_click == true`, and it arrives AFTER the single click that already ran `select_card`/`row_clicked` — so the handler must be additive, not exclusive. `_pass_mouse_through` already forces every non-Button card Control to MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE, so the event reaches `_gui_input` on the host; nothing new is needed there. The inline editor's rect can come from `_body_row_rect`, which already walks `section_stack` — but see GP-01: that walk is the drifted one.

### `GP-04` The row context menu is markup-shaped for every section — an import row and a hook chip are offered "Add child element…" and "Wrap in…"

> Also filed as `ctx-05` — one defect.

**Unity does:** "Rows, cards, import rows and the empty canvas each have their own menu" (capability §5). An import row's right-click opens the IMPORT menu (after `RememberMenuPointer`, so it opens at the click); right-click on a hook chip is IGNORED ("Right click is ignored on the chip itself"); the element menu — add attribute / add child / wrap / delete — belongs to markup rows.

**Godot today:** wrong. `_on_row_context` branches on exactly two things: `section == EXPORTS` (style-entry menu) and `row.kind == DIRECTIVE`. Everything else — an IMPORT row, a hook chip in BODY, an island line (which arrives as `markup[0]`, see GP-02) — falls into the `else` and is served "Add attribute…", "Add child element…", "Apply style from a module…", "Wrap in…" and "Delete element". Those operations compute their insertion points from `row.at`/`row.end_at`/`row.self_closing`; on an import line or a hook call those offsets point into the preamble or the setup block, so accepting one writes markup into GDScript. There is also no import-row menu at all (no "copy the name this binds", no "remove this import", no "go to the module").

**To build:** Branch `_on_row_context` on `section` first: IMPORTS → an import menu (copy binding, remove import, reveal/select the target module when `edges_from` has a resolved edge for that row); BODY → chip menu (edit this line, delete this hook) or nothing, per the reference; ISLAND → edit setup / delete these lines; MARKUP → today's element menu; EXPORTS → today's entry menu. The Edits layer already has `remove` (span-exact) for the delete arms.

**Godot specifics:** The menu is a `PopupMenu` positioned at `_canvas.get_screen_position() + at`, so the "open AT the click" lesson is already answered; only the vocabulary is wrong. Keep the section constants coming from `Metrics.Section` (preload const) rather than magic ints so a new section cannot silently land in the element branch.

### `GP-05` The tree's root is elected from the FOCUS when no module owns the root folder — UB-185's mechanism, one fallback short

**Unity does:** `ResolveRootModule` walks the folder, then among the modules whose folder IS that folder: the first with `OwnsFolder` wins; otherwise `best` = the ordinally-smallest full path in that folder; fallbacks in order best → the first entry of the sorted inventory → the focus. The point is spelled out in the doc comment: the root used to be a property of the FOCUS, "so creating a style module made that module its own root. The saved layout is keyed on the root, so the key changed, every stored position missed, and the whole tree re-laid itself out (UB-185)" — the owner's settings held 35 layout files, "one phantom tree per style module ever created".

**Godot today:** partial, and the missing half is the one UB-185 is about. `_resolve_root` does the folder walk and the `owns_folder` pass faithfully, then: `return focus if not focus.is_empty() else ordered[0].file_path()`. Both of Unity's intermediate fallbacks are gone. Confirmed by running the projection: two modules `res://ui/Alpha.guitkx` + `res://ui/Beta.guitkx` in a folder nobody owns give `root_path = res://ui/Alpha.guitkx` when Alpha is focused and `res://ui/Beta.guitkx` when Beta is; Unity returns Alpha both times. Since `Layout.file_for(root) = sha1(root)` and `_rel_key` is relative to `root_path.get_base_dir()`, the consequences are: a second layout file per focused module (nothing retires the first), and — when the focus sits in a deeper folder — a different KEY SET too. Probe, same two-module tree with a nested child: focus=Alpha → root=res://ui/Alpha.guitkx, keys `["alpha.guitkx", "sub/child.guitkx"]`; focus=res://ui/sub/Child.guitkx → root=Child, keys `["res://ui/alpha.guitkx", "child.guitkx"]`. `load_for_members` finds the old file by overlap (UB-221 is answered), but `apply_to` re-keys against the NEW root and misses every stored key, so every card falls back to its seeded slot. And `reproject()` re-runs with whatever `_focus_path` currently is — which `select_module` changes on every card click — so selecting a nested card and then creating a module re-roots the tree and re-lays it out mid-session.

**To build:** Add the two fallbacks to `_resolve_root`, in Unity's order: after the `owns_folder` pass, take the ordinally-smallest `file_path()` among `ordered` whose `folder` equals `root_folder`; if that is empty, take `ordered[0].file_path()` (the list is already path-sorted, so that IS the sorted-inventory answer); only then the focus. Add a suite case: the same module list projected with two different focus paths must produce the same `root_path` (Unity keeps this invariant in `Builder~/ModelTests/Program.cs:143-155`).

**Godot specifics:** `BuilderTree.resolve_root_from` is already a faithful port of `ResolveRootCore` including the `components/` caveat — the gap is entirely in the module-election step above it. Both are pure and preload-const, so this is directly testable in `builder_graph_test.gd` with no editor: `tests/builder_graph_test.gd:238` already asserts the owns-folder case and stops there.

### `GP-06` Hook modules get no code island, so their non-hook setup is invisible — and "+ code" on one writes a line the card never shows

**Unity does:** `ExtractIslandLines` runs for Component OR Hook (`if (node.Kind != Component && node.Kind != Hook) return;`), so a hook module's setup statements — everything between its declaration head and its return that is not another hook call — appear on the card at L2 with a `[IslandStartLine, IslandEndLine]` write-back range. Unreal's leg states the argument: hiding it "means the card lies about what the component does".

**Godot today:** absent for hooks. `populate_card` calls `_fill_island` only inside `if card.kind == Module.Kind.COMPONENT and not binding.is_empty()`. Probe: a hook module whose body is `var state = Hooks.use_state(start)` / `var doubled = state[0] * 2` / `var label = str(doubled)` projects to body=1 chip, island=0 — the two plain lines are nowhere on the card. Same for UTIL/VALUE/MODULE cards. This also breaks an affordance the view offers on those very cards: `canvas_view.guitkx:211` renders "+ code" for any `kind != 2`, and `_seed_body` then looks the seeded line up in `fresh.island_lines` to open the inline editor over it — on a hook or util card that list is always empty, so the line is written into the buffer and neither shown nor editable.

**To build:** Extend the island to hook (and util) modules. `Compiler.decl_structure(source, binding)` is component-shaped today; the cheapest faithful route is to reuse the binding decl's `body_open`..`next` span (already in `analyzed_decls`) to slice the setup lines for a non-component declaration, filter out the lines that produced chips exactly as `_fill_island` does, and record the range. Then either gate "+ code" to the kinds that can show it or let the island carry it.

**Godot specifics:** `decl_structure` is the compiler's own component-splitter (setup vs markup return); asking it about a hook declaration is a compiler-side change, so prefer slicing from `analyzed_decls`' `body_open`/`next` in the builder rather than widening a compiler API the whole toolchain depends on. Everything here is pure and headless.

### `GP-19` The gates are green over this whole area: parity lists none of it, and the hit-test suite checks the model against itself

**Unity does:** n/a — this is about the Godot gates that are supposed to catch the above.

**Godot today:** `tests/builder_parity.gd`'s 73 entries contain not one line for graph projection: no LoadTree, no PopulateCardDetail, no RefreshEdgesFor, no ResolveRootModule, no SeedDefaultPositions, no unresolved-import warning, no anchor/edge behaviour. **To build:** (a) Add parity entries for this area, each pointing at an identifier that would have to change if the behaviour were lost: ResolveRootModule → `func _resolve_root`, RefreshEdgesFor → `func refresh_edges_for`, SeedDefaultPositions → `func seed_positions`, the unresolved-import report, the per-kind edge tint, the double-click dispatch. (b) Add a suite case that projects one card of EVERY kind (component, style, hook, util, unparseable component) and asserts, for each, that the set of sections in `section_stack` equals the set the view renders — drive it off one shared predicate so it cannot be satisfied by two copies agreeing today. (c) Have the shots rig derive its click point from the RENDERED Control tree (walk `_cards` for the row's Label) and compare it against `row_hit`, rather than reading both from `section_stack`.

**Godot specifics:** The view/metrics agreement test is possible headlessly: `canvas_view.gd` is a compiled `.guitkx` module and `RuitkRoot.create` mounts into an offscreen Control under `--headless` (the canvas suite already does this at :565-600), so the rendered section headings can be read back out of the node tree and compared with `section_stack`. Remember the reconciler's bailout when writing it — the host bumps `revision` on every `show_graph` for exactly this reason — and that a sliced update commits several frames later, so the assertion has to run after the settle loop.

### `GP-07` An unresolved import is never explained — no console line, no diagnostic, no path that was looked for

**Unity does:** UB-144, added "because the failure was invisible": every import that resolves to nothing logs one warning naming the file, the specifier and the mapped path — `[RUITK Builder] unresolved import in <file>: "<spec>" looked for <path|<no mappable path>>` — and the edge is still recorded with ToIndex = -1. Unity deliberately paints NOTHING for a target-less edge ("The red stub this used to paint had no counterpart in the POC") and lets the console carry the why.

**Godot today:** partial. The edge is recorded broken (`to_index = -1`) and the overlay paints a red dashed stub with an unsatisfied dot — visually louder than Unity's answer, and defensible since Godot's stub leaves the ROW anchor rather than the card centre. What is missing is the explanation: grepping the whole builder for "unresolved" finds one comment and no `push_warning`, no console entry, no diagnostic. The user sees a red stub and is told nothing about which path was tried. The preview round raises the compiler's own GUITKX23xx for a module inside the focus closure, but a module outside it never compiles, so most broken imports produce nothing at all.

**To build:** In `_append_edges_for`, when `edge.to_index < 0`, feed one entry to the diagnostics console (the console already takes `{code, severity, line, message}` per file — `builder_window.gd:1968-1972` does exactly this for blank modules) naming `card.file_path`, `row.source_line`, the specifier and `Specifiers.map(...)`'s answer or "<no mappable path>". Console rather than `push_warning`, because the builder has its own copyable console and the Godot Errors dock is append-only and already noisy.

**Godot specifics:** `_append_edges_for` is a static pure function used by tests; pushing a console dependency into it would break that. Return the unresolved list from `project`/`refresh_edges_for` (or hang it on `Graph`) and let `builder_window.reproject`/`_after_model_change` report it — that keeps the projection headless and testable.

### `GP-08` A seeded slot is never written down, and the layout object is thrown away on every reprojection

**Unity does:** UB-180: "A layout that is never recorded is RECOMPUTED on every mount, and the default layout is a breadth-first walk over the whole graph — so its answer depends on the node SET. Adding one module therefore moved every card the user had never dragged, which is not a layout, it is a reshuffle. A slot is decided once and then remembered." Mount does `config.ApplyTo(graph); if (_config.AdoptUnplaced(_graph)) _config.Save();` — the adoption is persisted immediately, at mount, before the user does anything.

**Godot today:** partial. `adopt_unplaced` exists and is correct, but `reproject()` calls it as a statement and discards the bool, and never saves; worse, the line above it is `layout = CanvasLayout.for_graph(graph)`, which re-reads the layout from `user://` on EVERY reprojection — so the in-memory adoption from the previous reprojection is discarded too. `_capture_layout()` (which does save everything) is only reached from a card drag and from Save. So between opening a tree and the first drag-or-save, every reprojection — create, delete, rename, folder move, undo replay, all of which call `reproject()` — re-runs `seed_positions` over the new node set and moves every card whose slot was never persisted. The seed is also root-dependent (`seed_positions(graph, graph.index_of(graph.root_path))`), which compounds GP-05.

**To build:** `if layout.adopt_unplaced(graph): layout.save(Time.get_datetime_string_from_system(true))` in `reproject`, and keep the loaded `layout` object across reprojections instead of re-reading it (re-read only when the tree identity changes — on `open_tree`), so the adoption survives to the save. Add a suite case: project a tree, add a module, re-project, and assert that no previously-seeded card moved.

**Godot specifics:** `user://ruitk_builder/layouts` is outside the project so writing there costs no import cycle and is safe from a `@tool` script. `tests/builder_canvas_test.gd:445-478` already exercises adopt/apply against the store — the gap is purely the call site in the window, which no suite drives.

### `GP-09` Edge colour and anchor-dot colour carry two kinds where the reference carries three — a hook import is drawn as a component import

**Unity does:** Colour and dash come from the TARGET's kind: `TargetKind == Hook ? HookEdge : TargetKind == Style ? StyleEdge : UsageEdge`, dashed when Style or Hook. The anchor dot mirrors it from the import row's badge (`.style` → 7/StyleEdge, `.hooks` → 6/HookEdge, else 5/UsageEdge), so "the column of dots on a card's border reads as a legend of what that card depends on". Dashes are walked by ARC LENGTH so the 6-on/4-off period is uniform through the bend, and the terminal dot is painted at FULL alpha against the stroke's 0.85 ("Reusing the stroke colour washed every endpoint out").

**Godot today:** partial. `canvas_palette.gd` defines exactly two edge tints, `edge_component()` and `edge_style()`; `_draw_edge` picks between them on `to_card.kind == STYLE` alone, so an import of a `.hooks` module is indistinguishable from an import of a component. `Graph.Badge` HAS `IMPORT_HOOKS` and `_import_badge` sets it, and `Edge.target_kind` is computed — both are then unused by the painter. Anchor dots are one flat `ANCHOR_COLOR` for every kind and every row, so the border column carries no information at all. The dash walk itself is correct (`_draw_dashed_path` carries phase across the polyline = arc length). The terminal dot reuses the possibly-dimmed stroke colour (`draw_circle(to, ANCHOR_RADIUS, color)`), which is the washed-out endpoint Unity called out. The toolbar legend names only "usage edge", so the purple style edge that IS drawn has no key.

**To build:** Add `edge_hook()` to the palette; select in `_draw_edge` on `to_card.kind` across STYLE/HOOK/else and dash for both STYLE and HOOK; colour each source dot in `_draw_anchors` from the edge's own row badge (`card.imports[edge.from_row].badge` for import edges, usage tint for `is_usage`); paint the terminal dot at `Color(color, 1.0)`. Extend the toolbar legend to name all three edge kinds.

**Godot specifics:** `canvas_palette.gd` is the hand-written `@tool` script by deliberate divergence — adding `edge_hook()` there is exactly the right place and needs no `.style.guitkx`. `_draw_anchors` already has the edge in hand (`for edge in graph.edges_from(index)`), so the badge lookup is `graph.cards[index].imports[edge.from_row].badge` guarded on `from_section == IMPORTS`. All of it is `_draw`-only, so `tests/builder_canvas_capture.gd` (windowed, run by hand) is the only visual gate — a headless test can still assert the colour-selection function.

### `GP-10` A util or hook module's exported surface is projected and then never drawn

**Unity does:** Capability §2: "Sections, top to bottom: title bar, signature, IMPORTS, BODY (hooks & state), RETURN (markup rows), and FOR STYLE/UTIL MODULES, per-export detail entries." `PopulateCardDetail` calls `ParseStyleDetail` for Style and `ParseUtilDetail` for Util ("value exports as-is; function exports as sig + body lines (L2) + }"), and the view's EXPORTS section renders whenever `ExportDetail.Count > 0`. For a non-component the BODY header is even relabelled "EXPORTS".

**Godot today:** partial. `_fill_export_detail` runs for every non-component card and for any component whose markup will not parse, and fills `card.export_detail` with a header row per declaration (probe: util card export_detail=1, hook card export_detail=1) — but `canvas_view.guitkx:231` renders the section only when `draws_exports and card.kind == 2`, i.e. style modules only. So a util module's card shows a signature and an empty BODY band, and the declarations it exports appear nowhere; a hook module the same; and a component that is mid-edit gets the fallback detail the projection deliberately computed for exactly that moment and shows none of it. There is also no util-style body listing (Unity's `ParseUtilDetail` shows the function's own body lines at L2) — `_fill_export_detail` emits only the signature header for non-style kinds.

**To build:** Render EXPORTS whenever `card.export_detail` is non-empty (and fix the height model with it — GP-01), label the section "EXPORTS", and keep the `+ style` affordance to style cards. If a util card should show its body, feed `_fill_export_detail` the declaration's body lines the way GP-06's island slice would.

**Godot specifics:** Purely a view gate plus the metrics gate beside it; the projection already produces the rows and `tests/builder_graph_test.gd:548` already asserts "a non-style module lists its declarations" — a model test that is green while nothing renders it, which is the shape of gap this area keeps producing.

### `GP-11` No section height caps and no scrolling — a tall card grows without bound, and the scrolled-out anchor clamp has nothing to clamp to

**Unity does:** Each card section is a `ScrollView` named `ruitk-section-scroll` with a max height — IMPORTS 140, BODY 260, EXPORTS 280, MARKUP 340 — which is the §8.2/UB-23 fix for the unbounded card height that caused UB-22's overlap. Because a scrolled-out row still reports a worldBound, `AnchorOf` clamps the anchor's Y into the section viewport, so hidden rows' curves bundle at the section's top or bottom edge ("the clamp edge also tells you which way to scroll"), and each section scroller's `valueChanged` marks the edge layer dirty so edges track the scroll live.

**Godot today:** absent. `canvas_view.guitkx` builds each section as a plain `VBoxContainer` inside `CanvasCardSection` with no `ScrollContainer` and no max height; `section_stack` has no caps (`height = lead + rows * row_height`, unbounded); and `builder_canvas_host._fit_cards` calls `reset_size()` so the card grows to its full content height every frame. A component with sixty markup rows is a ~1400px card. Godot avoids UB-22's overlap differently — `seed_positions` advances each row by the tallest measured card — which is a legitimate answer to the overlap, but it is not an answer to "one card is taller than the canvas", and it leaves the whole clamp behaviour with nothing to attach to.

**To build:** Cap each section in `section_stack` (the same four numbers, or numbers chosen here and written down once) and render the section body inside a `ScrollContainer` with `custom_minimum_size.y = min(content, cap)`. Then clamp `edge_source_anchor`'s Y into `[section.top + lead, section.top + capped_height]` so a curve from a scrolled-out row terminates at the section edge, and connect the scroller's `value_changed` to `_edges.queue_redraw()`.

**Godot specifics:** A `ScrollContainer` inside a card is a mouse-filter hazard: `_pass_mouse_through` sets every non-BaseButton Control to MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE on every render, which will kill the scroller's own wheel handling — so the walk needs an explicit exception, and the canvas's own wheel-zoom must keep winning outside it (capability §2 says Ctrl+wheel zooms over a self-scrolling section). Cap the height in the METRICS first: if only the view caps, GP-01 gets a fourth instance.

### `GP-12` The row hit-test and the edge anchors are a hand-written estimate with no measurement path, and the estimate is known-incomplete

> **Duplicate of `CANVAS-01`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** The estimates (`ImportRowY`, `MarkupRowY`, `EstimateCardHeight`) exist only to bridge the frames before layout: `AnchorOf` queries the real marker element and `CardRect` reads the measured `card-{index}` layout, and when either is unmeasured the painter sets an `estimated` flag and schedules up to 12 repaints 16 ms apart until the measured positions land (UB-81 ties the culled-card placeholder to this: dropping the element would restart the burst on every zoom step). So a wrong estimate costs one frame, never a wrong click.

**Godot today:** divergent by necessity, and load-bearing in a way Unity's is not. `edge_source_anchor` and `row_hit` both read `section_stack`, which is pure arithmetic over hand-tuned constants (HEADER_H 38, SECTION_OVERHEAD_H 34.5, IMPORT_ROW_H 19.7, MARKUP_ROW_H 22.4, CHIP_ROW_H 34.7, MONO_ADVANCE 7.2). Nothing ever measures the rendered Controls, so any drift between the constants and what Godot's editor theme actually lays out is a permanent click error, not a one-frame one. Two known inaccuracies are already in the file: `_chip_rows` charges 71.0 for the "+ hook" chip and NOTHING for the "+ code" chip beside it (Unity has the same under-count, but there it only affects layout, not hit-testing), and the chip wrap is computed against `CARD_WIDTH_SECTIONS - CARD_PADDING` = 316 while a Layer-3 card is drawn at `CARD_WIDTH_FULL` = 360 — deliberate for layout stability, wrong for the hit-test that shares it. The editor's UI scale and font size, which the constants do not model at all, move every one of these numbers.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One qualifier on the 'what to build': hit-testing the MODEL rather than the Control tree is a documented deliberate choice with a stated reason (builder_canvas_host.gd:548-553 -- the reconciler re-creates cards, so a Control walk asks a tree that has already moved on). The fix should add a measured reconciliation alongside it, not replace it. Also, the largest measurement error in this file is neither of the two listed: see the missed gap on the BODY chip flow, where `rows` is a wrapped-LINE count that `_row_of` then uses as a chip INDEX.

**To build:** Keep the model as the layout/edge answer (it must stay zoom-invariant), but add a measurement reconciliation for hit-testing: after `_fit_cards` settles, walk the rendered card subtree once per card and record the real per-section tops/row heights onto the `Card` (the view can tag rows with `name = "row-%d-%d"` the way Unity names its markers), and have `row_hit` prefer measured values when present. Failing that, at minimum charge the "+ code" chip, compute chip wrap against the LOD's own width, and add a windowed gate to `tests/builder_canvas_capture.gd` that asserts the measured section tops match `section_stack` within a pixel or two at 100% editor scale.

**Godot specifics:** The cards are built by the reconciler and re-created as the graph changes, which is exactly why `card_at` hit-tests the model — that reasoning is sound. But a MEASURED read taken after the commit settles is not the same as hit-testing a stale tree: `_process`/`SETTLE_FRAMES` already re-walks `_cards` for the mouse-filter pass, so the measurement can ride along on the same walk. Also note the sliced-render hazard the host documents: an update render commits several frames after `set_root`, so any measurement must be taken in the settle loop, not straight after.

### `GP-13` An island edit deletes the blank lines the island never showed (and the hook lines interleaved with it)

**Unity does:** `ExtractIslandLines` keeps interior blank lines verbatim — blanks are held in `pendingBlanks` and flushed when the next kept line proves they are interior, "POC '.code-island { white-space: pre }' keeps the block verbatim, blank separator lines included — but never a leading or trailing run" — and the doc is explicit that "the displayed text and the [IslandStartLine, IslandEndLine] write-back range are the same block, so a cap here would delete the lines it hid".

**Godot today:** divergent-defect on the blanks. `_fill_island` does `if raw.strip_edges().is_empty(): continue` for EVERY blank line, interior included, while `island_start_line`/`island_end_line` still span them — and `Edits.set_island` replaces that inclusive line range with the island text. So committing an island edit silently removes the user's blank separator lines. The interleaved-hook case (a hook call between two island lines is excluded from the display but inside the range, so the edit deletes it) is a hazard Unity SHARES — report it as a risk in both legs, not as a Godot regression — but Godot makes it likelier because it also strips the blanks that would otherwise sit around the hooks.

**To build:** Port the pendingBlanks rule: hold blanks and flush them when the next kept line arrives, so interior blanks survive display and write-back. For the shared hook hazard, the honest fix is to make `set_island` splice around the excluded lines rather than replace the range wholesale — the projection already knows every excluded line's number (`card.body[i].source_line`), so carry them on the Card and have `set_island` re-interleave them.

**Godot specifics:** Pure string work in two preload-const files; fully headless. `tests/builder_edits_test.gd` already renders structural edits as before/after strings, which is the right shape for a case with a hook call sitting between two island lines.

**Unity does:** Capability §2's LOD table is the contract: Layer 3 — Edit applies at zoom >= 0.80 and "Adds per-row attributes, code islands, directive badges and style entry lines — and this is the layer at which those become clickable to edit." One threshold, one band, one set of content.

Do not leave the toolbar naming a band whose content is absent.

**Godot specifics:** `shows_attributes` takes a raw zoom while every other predicate takes a `Lod` — that asymmetry is the tell. Row heights do not change with attributes (the Label clips), so this is visual only and safe to change without touching `section_stack`.

### `GP-17` Module kind: the file suffix no longer wins, so a `.style.guitkx` holding a function is badged "utils"

**Unity does:** `ClassifyByPathAndExports` tests the FILENAME first — `.style.uitkx` → Style, `.hooks.uitkx` → Hook, both OrdinalIgnoreCase — and only then reads declaration heads. A companion is what its name says it is, whatever its contents currently say.

**Godot today:** divergent by design (the compiler surfaces declaration kinds, so classifying from the declaration is legitimately better than Unity's regexes) but the suffix has been demoted from FIRST to LAST: `classify` reads the binding declaration and falls back to `Module.kind_of(file_path)` only when there is no declaration at all, with one presentational refinement (a `value` decl in a `.style.guitkx` is STYLE). So a `.style.guitkx` whose export is a function classifies UTIL and a `.hooks.guitkx` whose export is not `use_`-prefixed classifies UTIL — while the document layer's `Module.kind` (suffix-derived, used for the file name, the folder pane and the drag payload) still says STYLE/HOOK. **Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Worth flagging that this divergence IS argued in source (builder_graph_service.gd:216-224) and pinned by tests/builder_graph_test.gd:245-251 ('kinds come from the DECLARATION'), so it is a decision to revisit deliberately, not an oversight -- but it is NOT in CLAUDE.md's recorded deliberate list, which is where a divergence with this reach belongs either way.

**To build:** Test the suffix first for STYLE and HOOK, exactly as the document layer's `Module.split_file_name` already does, and keep the declaration read for everything else. That removes the divergence AND makes `card.kind` and `module.kind` agree by construction.

**Godot specifics:** Pure and headless; `tests/builder_graph_test.gd:245` asserts the current declaration-first behaviour, so that case has to be revised deliberately rather than left to fail.

### `GP-18` The "+ entry" affordance is a Label, so left-clicking it does nothing

**Unity does:** Every add affordance is a chip that fires on click (`onAddHook`/`onAddCode`, and the style-entry affordance in the EXPORTS section), and Unity notes the one gesture rule: right click (Button == 1) returns without acting, left/middle fires.

**Godot today:** partial. "+ hook", "+ code" and "+ style" are real `CanvasAddChip` Buttons and work (they are also the only card elements `_pass_mouse_through` deliberately leaves alone). But the per-export "+ entry" row is emitted by the PROJECTION as an `export_detail` `Line` with `badge = ADD_ENTRY` and rendered as a plain Label like any other export row, so a left click on it just selects a row (`_menu_row` = an add row whose span is 0..0) and nothing happens; the only way to add an entry is right-click → "Add entry…".

**To build:** Render an `export_detail` row whose badge is `ADD_ENTRY` as a `CanvasAddChip` carrying the export name, and route it through `card_add_requested(index, "entry")` — the host signal already documents "entry" as one of its four values and nothing ever emits it.

**Godot specifics:** `_pass_mouse_through` leaves `BaseButton` alone, which is why the existing chips work — a Label-shaped affordance can never receive the press. Also note the synthetic row has `at`/`end_at` = 0, so it is currently a valid target for `Edits.remove`, which is a second reason to make it a Button rather than a row.

### Searchable menu, name prompt, inline editor overlay, cursor feedback

### `SM-01` The rename prompt validates the name against a folder the module does not live in, and nothing downstream catches the collision — Save silently overwrites one module with another

**Unity does:** ShowRenamePrompt passes its own validator. ValidateNewName's file-freedom clause asks whether THE FILE THE NAME WOULD PRODUCE is already taken — i.e. the module's real destination path — and rename adds a first clause before it: a name equal to the current one returns 'that is the current name'. A rejected name writes into the inline error line and the prompt stays open.

**Godot today:** wrong. `_on_card_menu` (RENAME) reuses `_validate_name(current.kind, name)`, which is the CREATE validator: it computes the destination with `_create_folder(kind, name)` (builder_window.gd:1861-1875), whose whole job is 'where would a NEW module of this kind be born relative to the card I right-clicked'. For a component being renamed it answers `<parent.folder>/components/<NewName>/` — a folder that does not exist — so `workspace.try_get(...)` is null and no collision is reported (components are saved only by the separate whole-tree name check at :1804-1807). For a STYLE / HOOK / UTIL module `_create_folder` hits `if parent == null or parent.kind != Module.Kind.COMPONENT: return tree_root()` (:1866-1867), because `_menu_target` IS the companion being renamed — so it checks `<tree root>/<name>.style.guitkx` while the module actually lives in, say, `res://ui/card/`. Renaming `res://ui/card/card.style.guitkx` to `panel` while `res://ui/card/panel.style.guitkx` exists passes validation. `_rename_to` then calls `workspace.move_to` → `Tree.move_to` (builder_tree.gd:111-139), which sets `module.folder`/`module.name` with NO collision check and calls `_reindex()`; `_reindex` (:209-221) writes both modules into `_by_path` under the same key, so the earlier one is silently dropped from the index while still living in `_modules` and still being projected at Save. `Tree.validate()` (:230-256) knows how to report exactly this ('two modules claim %s') and NOTHING IN THE RUNNING BUILDER EVER CALLS IT — the only callers are tests/builder_model_test.gd:474-511, 727. There is also no 'that is the current name' clause: renaming a component to its own name reports '<name> already exists in this tree'.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One refinement: the flat case the gap describes as broken can accidentally pass. When the companion happens to sit AT the tree root, `tree_root()` equals its own folder and the check is correct by coincidence — I saw 'panel already exists' in that arrangement. The defect needs the module to live below the shallowest folder in the tree, which is the ordinary `<root>/components/<Name>/` shape.

**To build:** Split the validator. Add `_validate_rename(module, name)` in builder_window.gd that (a) returns 'that is the current name' when `name == module.name`, (b) applies the same shape regexes by kind, and (c) checks `workspace.try_get(module.folder.path_join(name + Module.suffix_for(module.kind)))` — the module's OWN folder, not `_create_folder`'s create-site. Wire `CardMenuId.RENAME` (builder_window.gd:2221-2227) to it. Independently, make `Tree.move_to` refuse a move whose destination path is already claimed by a different module (return false / leave the tree untouched) so the model cannot enter the two-modules-one-path state even if a caller forgets to validate; and call `Tree.validate()` from `Workspace` after every structural operation in debug, pushing the problems to the console rather than only asserting in tests.

**Godot specifics:** `Paths.key()` case-folds, so on Windows a case-only rename also collides. The whole document layer is `FileAccess`-only and headlessly testable, so this is directly coverable in tests/builder_model_test.gd and tests/builder_save_test.gd — assert that a rename onto an occupied sibling path is refused and that `Tree.validate()` stays empty across the operation. Builder files reference each other through preload consts, so the new validator must live in builder_window.gd or a preloaded helper, never behind a global class_name.

**Risk:** Two modules project to one file at Save; the second write wins and the first module's buffer is gone with no diagnostic. The condition is reachable from the ordinary 'Rename x.style.guitkx' gesture on any tree that keeps two style modules in one folder.

### `SM-02` The searchable menu has no keyboard navigation at all — UB-122 and UB-126 reintroduced in the one menu shape where Godot's engine does not answer them

**Unity does:** Down/Up move a highlight through the PICKABLE rows only (headers and separators skipped), the highlight is drawn as an Accent-at-14% band, the ScrollView scrolls it into view, Enter takes the highlighted row (-1 meaning 'the first pickable row' so Enter-without-arrows keeps its old behaviour), the highlight CLAMPS rather than wraps, and Rebuild() resets it to -1 because the previous index means nothing against a new row set. UB-126 then moved the implementation off the search field so both menu shapes share one copy: 'shared by the searchable and the non-searchable menu so neither can drift from the other'. The capabilities spec makes it a contract clause: menus 'are fully keyboard-drivable: up/down moves … Escape backs out', and long-vocabulary menus 'open with a search field instead' — the search field replaces the flat list, not the keyboard.

**Godot today:** absent. builder_search_menu.gd has no highlight index, no arrow handling and no scroll-to. `_input` (:214-220) handles only KEY_ESCAPE (itself redundant — `Popup` already consumes `ui_cancel`). `_submit` (:196-211) walks `_list.get_children()` and fires the FIRST Button it finds, so Enter is permanently 'take the top match' and there is no way to reach the second one from the keyboard. Because focus starts on the `_search` LineEdit (:102, :121) and LineEdit consumes `ui_text_caret_down`/`ui_text_caret_up` (Down moves the caret to the end of the text), the arrows never escape the field. Rows ARE `Button`s (:179-186) with Godot's default FOCUS_ALL, so a Tab would move focus into the list and Godot's own neighbour navigation would then work — but at that point typing no longer filters, which is the opposite of what the search field is for. Godot's `PopupMenu`, used for every PLAIN builder menu (builder_window.gd:429-465, 1080-1124), is fully keyboard-driven natively, so the contract is met exactly everywhere EXCEPT the one shape that had to be hand-written.

**To build:** Port Unity's model verbatim into builder_search_menu.gd: a `_highlight := -1` index over the pickable rows, a `_pickable_rows()` helper that returns only the `Button` children, `_move_highlight(delta)` that clamps and repaints (`add_theme_stylebox_override("normal", ...)` with a flat Accent-at-14% StyleBoxFlat on the highlighted row, cleared on the rest), `_ensure_visible(row)` against the ScrollContainer (`ensure_control_visible`), and `_rebuild()` resetting `_highlight = -1`. Drive it from `_search.gui_input` (not `_input`) so the keys are seen before LineEdit's caret handling, calling `accept_event()` on Up/Down/Enter. Keep `_submit`'s 'no highlight ⇒ first row' fallback so Enter-without-arrows is unchanged.

**Godot specifics:** Use `_search.gui_input` rather than the node's `_input`: `Control._call_gui_input` runs the script hook before the C++ `LineEdit::gui_input`, so `accept_event()` there is what stops Down from moving the caret. Row highlight must be a stylebox override, not `modulate` — the rows are flat `Button`s and the editor theme already paints `hover`, so an unstyled highlight is invisible under the pointer. `ScrollContainer.ensure_control_visible()` is the Godot equivalent of `ScrollView.ScrollTo`. The third leg proves this is portable: SRuitkUiBuilderMenu.cpp:71-73, :198-220 implements exactly this highlight/NextSelectable/Up/Down/Enter model in Slate.

**Risk:** The one menu the builder uses for its longest vocabularies (140-property attribute lists, 55 tags, every style key) is mouse-or-first-match only.

**Unity does:** BuilderInlineEditorOverlay hosts a fragment-mode CodeField. The point, stated in UB-76 and in the class doc, is that ONE editor gives every editable surface 'the same colouring, Ctrl+Space completion (at a position the OWNER maps into the real file) and the coloured-edit overlay — implemented once'. The owner rejected deferring it: 'we have many tests that should all be intellisensed/colored'. The capabilities spec states it as contract: 'A single floating editor serves every surface. **Godot today:** absent. `builder_inline_editor.gd:2` is `extends LineEdit`. There is no colouring, no completion provider, no diagnostics channel, and no equivalent of Unity's `completionProvider` parameter or its `closed` callback (whose purpose is to re-sync the LSP buffer after completion pushed synthesized text). Keep the existing `committed`/`cancelled(token, undo_seeding)` contract — it is correct and tested; only the widget underneath changes.

Keep the editor a preload const, not a global class_name, for the class-cache hazard. The overlay must stay `mouse_filter = STOP` (builder_inline_editor.gd:40) or a click starts a canvas pan.

### `SM-04` No multiline island editor — a code island cannot be edited on the canvas at all

**Unity does:** Show(anchor, seed, multiline: true, …) opens a multiline CodeField sized to REPLACE the island: width Clamp(bound.width, 260, 900), height Clamp(bound.height, 90, 520), topOffset 0, no row widening, no compact chrome, no font scaling. UB-101 is the fix: 'the body code input doesnt match the size (as if its outside island) - maybe we should replace in place the display mode to edit mode same size and everything.' The gesture is a double-click on the component code island (lod == 2) or on a style/util export island; the capabilities spec lists 'code islands (multiline)' among the surfaces editable in place.

**Godot today:** absent. The editor is a `LineEdit`, which has no multiline mode. The `"island"` token kind exists in `_on_inline_committed` (builder_window.gd:1502-1504) and `Edits.set_island` correctly replaces an inclusive line range — but the only call site that ever opens an island editor is the `+ code` seed path (builder_window.gd:1620-1624), where `from == to`, i.e. exactly one line. There is no gesture anywhere that opens the editor over a multi-line island: `builder_canvas_host.gd` never reads `event.double_click`, and `_row_of` for `Metrics.Section.ISLAND` (builder_window.gd:1544-1548) returns the first markup row rather than an island range. So the whole setup block of a component is editable only through the source pane.

**To build:** Give the overlay a `multiline: bool` mode. Behind `guitkx_code_edit.gd` (see SM-03) that is a size/behaviour switch rather than a second widget; as an interim, swap the `LineEdit` for a `TextEdit`-derived control with a one-line layout for the single-line case. Size it Unity's way: `clampf(rect.size.x, 260, 900)` × `clampf(rect.size.y, 90, 520)`, no lift. Add the gesture: detect `event.double_click` in `builder_canvas_host.gd::_handle_button` and emit `row_activated(card_index, section, row_index)`; in `builder_window.gd`, on an ISLAND-section activation open `{kind:"island", from: card.island_start_line, to: card.island_start_line + card.island_lines.size() - 1}` seeded with the joined lines.

**Godot specifics:** `InputEventMouseButton.double_click` is set by Godot's own click-tracking, so the double-click gesture costs one field read in `_handle_button` — no timer. The canvas hit-tests against the MODEL (`card_at`/`row_at`, builder_canvas_host.gd:534-564), not against Controls, so the island's screen rect is pure `Metrics` arithmetic and needs no wait-for-layout retry. The third leg has a real multiline inline editor (SRuitkUiBuilderInlineEditor.cpp:44-51, SMultiLineEditableTextBox), which is evidence the behaviour ports.

### `SM-05` None of the direct inline-edit gestures exist: an existing hook chip, a style entry line and an element row cannot be edited on the canvas at all, and an attribute value takes three steps instead of one click

**Unity does:** CanvasView.uitkx wires the gestures directly: single click (Button != 1) on an attribute VALUE label → onEditAttrValue; single click on a directive badge → onEditDirective; single click on a style entry line → onEditLine; DOUBLE click on a body/hook chip (ClickCount >= 2 && SourceLine > 0) → onEditLine; double click on a component code island or a style/util export island → onEditIsland. Single click on a chip or island selects instead, because those are also selection targets (UB-94/UB-102). Tooltips advertise the gesture ('click to edit; empty value removes', 'double-click to edit'). The capabilities spec lists the editable-in-place set: 'attribute values, directive headers, hook chips, style entry lines, code islands (multiline), and element rows'.

**Godot today:** partial, and the partial half is the wrong shape. `builder_canvas_host.gd` emits `row_clicked` on left press (:420-422) and `row_context_requested` on right press (:432-448). `_on_row_clicked` (builder_window.gd:1005-1019) selects the row and jumps the source pane — it never opens the editor. The ONLY routes into the inline editor are (a) right-click → 'Edit attribute...' → the searchable attribute-value menu → pick → editor (builder_window.gd:1190-1192 then :1394-1399), (b) right-click → 'Edit header...' (:1204-1208), and (c) the builder's own seeded opens after `+ hook` / `+ code` / a wrap (:1611-1624, :1445-1450). Consequences: an EXISTING hook chip has no edit gesture at all (the `"body"` token is only ever produced at :1616, immediately after the chip was seeded); a STYLE ENTRY line has none — the EXPORTS-section row menu offers only 'Add entry...' and 'Delete this entry' (:1083-1090); an ELEMENT ROW has none. An attribute value is three clicks and a menu where Unity is one click.

**To build:** Add `row_activated(card_index, section, row_index, at)` to `builder_canvas_host.gd`, emitted from `_handle_button` when `event.double_click` on a BODY or ISLAND row, and add a left-press branch that opens the editor directly for the surfaces Unity edits on a single click. Because the Godot canvas hit-tests arithmetically rather than per-Control, `Metrics.row_hit` must additionally report WHICH SPAN within the row was hit (the attribute-value sub-rect vs the tag) so a single click can distinguish 'edit this value' from 'select this row' — that is the one piece of new work; `Graph.Line.attr_pairs` already carries the spelling. Wire BODY double-click to `{kind:"body", row}` (the commit path at builder_window.gd:1505-1510 already exists and is correct), EXPORTS single-click to `{kind:"body"}` over the entry's own line, and ISLAND double-click per SM-04.

**Godot specifics:** The cards are rendered by the reconciler from canvas_view.guitkx and then flattened to `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE` by `_pass_mouse_through` (builder_canvas_host.gd:224-243), so per-element pointer callbacks are NOT available the way UITK gives them — the sub-row target must come from `Metrics`, in the same place `row_hit` already lives. That keeps the hit-test headlessly testable (builder_canvas_test.gd drives Metrics directly), which per-Control callbacks would not be. Note the reconciler bailout hazard already handled at builder_canvas_host.gd:110-120 (`_revision`) applies to any new prop the view needs for a hover/target affordance.
