### `SM-06` Nothing ever hands keyboard focus back to the builder — UB-92's CloseAndRestoreFocus, ReclaimKeyboard and RestoreHostFocus have no counterpart, and the builder opened from its own menu entry never has focus in the first place

**Unity does:** Three separate mechanisms, all pointing the same way. (1) CloseAndRestoreFocus: a pick closes the popup, focuses the INVOKING window, and only THEN runs the action — 'the action a pick triggers often opens the inline editor, and that editor was then focusing a field inside a window Unity did not consider focused, so keystrokes went somewhere else entirely: Enter reached the Project window, which runs OpenAsset, which opens VS2022' (UB-92). (2) ReclaimKeyboard(4): after a create prompt closes, window+root focus is re-asserted up to four times over ~120ms, because 'focusing the WINDOW is not enough for shortcuts: a KeyDownEvent is dispatched to the focused ELEMENT, and closing an inline editor leaves none'. (3) RestoreHostFocus, called from every inline-editor exit path: 'closing the editor destroys the focused element, and Unity does not hand the keyboard back to anything … so the next Ctrl+Z ran UNITY's undo instead of the builder's'.

**Godot today:** absent. `grab_focus` appears exactly four times under builder/ — twice on the search menu's own LineEdit (builder_search_menu.gd:102, :121), once on the inline editor's own LineEdit (builder_inline_editor.gd:73), once on the source pane's editor (builder_source_pane.gd:222). Nothing ever focuses the builder Control. `_pick` (builder_search_menu.gd:189-191) hides and emits with no focus restore; `_close` (builder_inline_editor.gd:103-109) hides with no focus restore. The builder's whole keyboard model lives in `RuitkBuilderWindow._gui_input` (builder_window.gd:222-252 — Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z/Y, Delete, Escape), and a Godot `Control` only receives key events while it is its viewport's `gui.key_focus`. The Control sets `focus_mode = FOCUS_ALL` (:138) but nothing grabs it, and the plugin's menu entry ends at `popup_centered()` (plugin.gd:446) — only the FileSystem-dock entry point calls `_builder.grab_focus()` (plugin.gd:455). Every visible pixel of the builder is covered by child containers/panes whose own `focus_mode` is NONE, and Godot's viewport only grabs focus for the control DIRECTLY hit, never an ancestor — so clicking the canvas, a pane or the toolbar does not focus the builder either. Opened from Reactive UI Toolkit → Builder…, Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Z / Delete / Escape are dead, and after any menu pick or prompt they stay dead.

**To build:** Add `reclaim_keyboard()` to builder_window.gd: `grab_focus()` on the window Control, guarded by `_typing_focused()` so it never steals from an open editor, and call it (a) at the end of `_open_builder` in plugin.gd after `popup_centered()`, (b) from `_search_menu.picked`/`submitted` BEFORE dispatching the action (mirroring Unity's close-restore-then-act order), (c) from `_inline._close()` via a `closed` signal the window listens to, and (d) after `_create_named`. Also give `CanvasHost` `focus_mode = FOCUS_ALL` and forward its key events, or simpler: set the builder Control's `focus_mode` and have `CanvasHost._gui_input` call `owner-window.grab_focus()` on any press, so a click anywhere on the canvas restores the keyboard model.

**Godot specifics:** Godot's `Viewport::_gui_input_event` grabs focus only for the control the press directly hit and only when its `focus_mode != FOCUS_NONE`; it does not walk ancestors. So a full-rect Control with FOCUS_ALL under STOP children never receives focus by clicking. Unity's UB-209 FocusInvoker has NO Godot analogue and is correctly absent — a Godot `Popup` opens from an unfocused parent — but UB-92's focus RESTORE is not the same problem and is unaddressed. Because the search menu is a real `PopupPanel` (its own Window/Viewport), keyboard focus genuinely leaves the builder's viewport when it opens, which is exactly the condition UB-92 describes.

**Risk:** The tests drive `_gui_input` directly (tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:763, :926 call it as a method), so the suite is green over a keyboard model that in the real editor never receives a key.

### `SM-07` The inline editor is a fixed 260x24 box regardless of the row it covers, the card it sits in, or the zoom — UB-99 and UB-127 both reintroduced

**Unity does:** Three sizing rules, each a fixed bug. Row widening (owner 2026-08-17): a single-line editor is widened to the full width of the canvas ROW it belongs to whenever that is wider than the clicked element, because 'a field narrower than the highlighted item it is editing reads as misaligned chrome'. Section widening (UB-127): when the badge is small but the LINE is long, the editor takes the card's width minus an 18px inset — 'a hook chip is only as wide as its summary text … but the LINE it edits is the full declaration, so the field clipped mid-word'; effective width band [260, 720]. Zoom scaling (UB-99): 'the overlay is unscaled window chrome positioned over a SCALED canvas row … the selected wrap is big and the input is ugly' — font = Clamp(rowHeight * 0.55, 11, 26), height = Max(font * 1.65 + 8, rowHeight), and the ORDER is load-bearing (glyphs from the row, then the box from the glyphs plus the compact chrome). The capabilities spec states it: 'a single-line editor matches its row's height and glyph size at any zoom'.

**Godot today:** absent for three of the four call sites. `open_at` takes a rect and does `size = Vector2(maxf(rect.size.x, 60), maxf(rect.size.y, 22))` with no widening, no clamping and no font change (builder_inline_editor.gd:69-70). The directive-header editor (builder_window.gd:1207), the attribute-value editor (:1397) and the seeded-wrap editor (:1449) all pass a hard-coded `Vector2(260, 24)`. Only `_body_row_rect` (:1630-1644) scales the BOX (`Metrics.card_width_for(lod) * zoom - 16`, `row_height * zoom`) — and even there the FONT is never scaled, so at Layer 3 the box grows and the glyphs stay 12px, which is the UB-99 symptom the other way round.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The TITLE overstates what the body correctly says. One of the four call sites (`_body_row_rect`, feeding :1615 and :1623) does scale the box with zoom and with `Metrics.card_width_for(lod)` — it is the FONT that is never scaled there, which is the same UB-99 symptom inverted. Also, the real box is not 260x24: LineEdit's own minimum size wins, and I measured 260x31.

**To build:** Move the sizing into `open_at`. Take the row rect from `Metrics` (the canvas already computes exact row spans — `Metrics.row_hit`/`section_stack` give both the row's height and the card's drawn width at the current lod), then: width = `clampf(maxf(row_width, 260.0), 260.0, 720.0)`; font = `clampf(row_height * 0.55, 11.0, 26.0)` applied via `add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", font)`; height = `maxf(font * 1.65 + 8.0, row_height)`. Have `builder_window.gd` build one `_row_screen_rect(card_index, section, row_index)` helper (the correct-space version — see SM-08) and use it at ALL FOUR call sites instead of three literals and one bespoke function.

**Godot specifics:** Godot has no per-Control font scale, so the glyph size is `add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", n)` on the editor — cheap and instant, but it must be re-applied on every `open_at` because the override persists. Unity's `SectionWidthOf` walks named UITK ancestors; here there is nothing to walk (the cards are IGNORE-filtered and hit-tested arithmetically), so the width comes from `Metrics.card_width_for(lod) * zoom`, which is the same number the card is drawn at and is headlessly testable in tests/builder_canvas_test.gd.

### `SM-08` Three call sites hand `open_at` coordinates in three different spaces — the seeded `+ hook` / `+ code` editor opens hundreds of pixels away from the chip it is editing

**Unity does:** Every anchor is converted once: `local = _root.WorldToLocal(bound.min)`, and the panel is positioned in the WINDOW ROOT's coordinates, then clamped 4px inside it. One space, one conversion, everywhere.

**Godot today:** wrong. `RuitkBuilderInlineEditor` is a `Control` parented to `canvas_layer` (builder_window.gd:352-353), so `open_at` sets `position = rect.position` in CANVAS_LAYER-LOCAL coordinates (builder_inline_editor.gd:69). Three call sites disagree about what they pass: (1) `Rect2(_menu_at, …)` at :1207, :1397, :1449 — `_menu_at` is the canvas host's LOCAL pointer position (set from `event.position` in `_gui_input`, builder_canvas_host.gd:445 → builder_window.gd:1079), and since `_canvas` is anchored full-rect at (0,0) inside `canvas_layer` this space happens to be correct; (2) `_body_row_rect` at :1639 returns `_canvas.get_global_rect().position + …`, i.e. VIEWPORT-GLOBAL, so the editor is offset by the whole left-pane + toolbar inset — typically 300+px right and 40+px down from the chip; (3) `_body_row_rect`'s fallback at :1644 returns `_menu_screen_at()` = `_canvas.get_screen_position() + _menu_at`, i.e. OS-SCREEN coordinates, which additionally adds the builder window's own screen origin. `_menu_screen_at()` is correct for the `PopupPanel` (a Window takes screen coordinates) and wrong the moment it is fed to a Control's `position`.

**To build:** Give `builder_window.gd` two clearly named helpers and delete the ambiguity: `_row_screen_rect(...)` (for the search menu / PopupMenu, screen space) and `_row_editor_rect(...)` (for the inline editor, canvas_layer-local — i.e. `Metrics.world_to_screen(...)` with NO `get_global_rect()` or `get_screen_position()` added). Point all four `open_at` call sites at the second. Add the missing containment while you are there: clamp `position` so the editor stays inside `canvas_layer` (`clampf(x, 4, maxf(4, parent_size.x - size.x - 4))` on both axes) and lift a single-line editor 3px, matching Unity.

**Godot specifics:** `Control.position` is parent-relative; `get_global_rect()` is viewport-relative; `get_screen_position()` adds the OS window origin. Three different things, and GDScript's `Vector2` gives no type help distinguishing them — naming the helpers is the only guard. `canvas_layer` is a plain `Control` with `clip_contents` unset, so an overflowing editor is not clipped: it currently draws over the source pane rather than being visibly wrong, which is why this survived. tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:917-918 asserts the editor is open and holds the seeded text and never asserts a position — that is the hole to close.

### `SM-09` The freeform row on the style-key menu produces a payload the handler cannot read: `payload as Dictionary` on a String

**Unity does:** The freeform provider is a FACTORY — `Func<string, Item>` — so each menu builds a fully-formed Item, with whatever OnPick closure it needs, from the trimmed filter text; it may also return null to decline. The four freeform menus each construct a payload of their own shape ('add "x" (untyped)', 'loop over "x"', 'use key "x"', 'use "x"').

**Godot today:** wrong. `open_menu`'s freeform is a FORMAT STRING (`freeform_label := ""`), and `_rebuild` always emits `_pick(typed)` — a raw `String` payload — regardless of what shape the menu's real items use (builder_search_menu.gd:91-95, :158-161). `_on_search_picked`'s `"attribute"` branch defends against this (`if payload is Dictionary … else …`, builder_window.gd:1378-1387), and `"child"` works because a tag IS a string. `"style_entry"` does not: it goes straight to `var pick := payload as Dictionary` then `str(pick["export"])` (:1408-1412) on the String the freeform row handed it. GDScript's `as` on a builtin target compiles to a cast that cannot convert String→Dictionary, so the pick aborts with an invalid-cast error and the entry is never added — the row exists, is orange, is clickable, and does nothing.

**To build:** Change `open_menu`'s freeform parameter from a format string to a `Callable` that takes the trimmed text and returns either an item dictionary or `{}` to decline — matching Unity's factory and letting each menu construct its own payload shape. Then `_style_key_items`' freeform returns `{"export": owner, "key": typed, "value": _style_seed(typed)}`, `"attribute"` returns `{"name": typed, "type": ""}`, and `_on_search_picked` needs no `payload is Dictionary` special-casing at all. Add a test in tests/builder_chrome_test.gd that drives every freeform row through `_on_search_picked` and asserts the buffer changed.

**Godot specifics:** GDScript's `as` on a builtin type emits OPCODE_CAST_TO_BUILTIN, which calls `Variant::construct` and raises a runtime error on a failed conversion rather than yielding null (null-on-failure is Object-type behaviour only). In the editor that surfaces as a red line in the Output dock and a half-executed function, not a crash — which is exactly why an untested menu row can be dead for a long time. A `Callable` freeform is also the shape the reconciler-free chrome layer already uses elsewhere, and it stays headlessly testable.

### `SM-10` No advance-run on a style entry: Enter does not open the next entry, and there is no armed '+ entry' — the parity gate is green over behaviour that does not exist

**Unity does:** AdvanceStyleEntry. Committing a style entry with ENTER opens the editor on the NEXT entry, so writing a style export is one keyboard run: 'Writing a style is a RUN of entries, and committing each by hand - click, type, Enter, click - made the keyboard useless for the one task on this card that is nothing but typing.' On the last entry there is nothing to advance to, so the '+ entry' row is ARMED and lights up; an unmodified Enter at window level then opens its key menu, and anything else disarms — 'Deliberately two presses, not one - a menu that opened by itself after every entry would be a trap.' The mechanism that makes it possible is Close(commitIfChanged, applied): `applied` is true ONLY for Enter, so a blur or a click elsewhere finishes the edit without advancing.

**Godot today:** absent, and the gate says otherwise. tests/builder_parity.gd:76 maps Unity's `AdvanceStyleEntry` to the token `RowMenuId.ADD_STYLE_ENTRY` — which is an enum member for a row-menu item that opens the style-key menu (builder_window.gd:75, :1085, :1180-1184). There is no advance, no arm, no disarm and no next-entry open anywhere under builder/. The enabling distinction is missing too: `RuitkBuilderInlineEditor.commit()` is called identically from `text_submitted` and from `focus_exited` (builder_inline_editor.gd:41-42), so the editor cannot tell Enter from a blur, and `committed(token, text)` carries no `applied` flag. Grepping for an identifier that happens to exist is exactly the failure mode the gate's own header warns about.

**To build:** Add `applied: bool` to the inline editor's commit path: `text_submitted` → `commit(true)`, `focus_exited` → `commit(false)`, and widen the signal to `committed(token, text, applied)`. Then add `_advance_style_entry(path, source_line)` in builder_window.gd: find the export-detail row at that line, look at the next detail row, and either open the editor on it or arm '+ entry' (a bool the canvas renders as a lit row — one more prop through `show_graph`, so remember the `_revision` bailout guard). Fix the gate entry to name the real identifier (`func _advance_style_entry`), and add a second entry for the arm.

**Godot specifics:** `LineEdit.text_submitted` fires on Enter only, so the Enter/blur distinction costs one boolean. The armed state has to reach the card layer through `show_graph` props — and canvas_view.guitkx is a `.guitkx` module whose generated `.gd` is COMMITTED and gated by tests/builder_view_build.gd, so adding the prop means recompiling and committing that `.gd` in the same change.

### `SM-11` Zero cursor feedback anywhere in the builder — BuilderCursor has no counterpart

**Unity does:** BuilderCursor.Set(element, cursor) reproduces the POC's pointer affordances: `#canvasWrap { cursor: grab }`, `.lib-item { cursor: grab }`, `.card-title { cursor: move }`, `.jsx-row { cursor: pointer }`, `.code-island { cursor: text }`. Applied at fifteen call sites: every searchable-menu row and context-menu row (Link), the canvas pane (Pan), a card being dragged (MoveArrow), the fold headers and the library's '+ new' (Link), library and folder rows (Pan), and the splitter anchors (ResizeVertical / ResizeHorizontal).

**Godot today:** absent. `mouse_default_cursor_shape` and `_get_cursor_shape` appear NOWHERE under addons/ — zero hits across the whole repository. Every surface in the Godot builder draws the OS arrow: a menu row you can click, a card title bar you can drag, empty canvas you can pan, an import row, a library entry, the panel splitters. This is the one item in this area with no partial implementation at all, and it is the cheapest to fix.

**To build:** Two mechanisms. (1) Static: `mouse_default_cursor_shape = Control.CURSOR_POINTING_HAND` on the search-menu row Buttons (builder_search_menu.gd:179-186), on library/folder pane rows, and on the toolbar buttons. (2) Dynamic on the canvas: override `func _get_cursor_shape(at_position: Vector2) -> int` on `RuitkBuilderCanvasHost` and answer from the model the host already hit-tests — `CURSOR_MOVE` when `Metrics.on_title_bar(...)` (the same call `_handle_button` already makes at :414-419), `CURSOR_POINTING_HAND` when `row_at()` reports found, `CURSOR_IBEAM` over an ISLAND-section row, `CURSOR_DRAG` while `_panning` or `_moving >= 0`, `CURSOR_ARROW` otherwise.

**Godot specifics:** `_get_cursor_shape` is a first-class `Control` virtual in Godot — no reflection needed, unlike Unity's private-member probe, so this is the one place the Godot port is structurally SIMPLER than the reference. It must live on `CanvasHost` rather than on the card Controls: `_pass_mouse_through` (builder_canvas_host.gd:224-243) sets every non-Button card Control to `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE`, so a per-row `mouse_default_cursor_shape` would never be consulted. `_get_cursor_shape` is called on the control that owns the mouse, so the host is exactly the right owner. Headless-testable: the override is a pure function of the model + camera + zoom, so builder_canvas_test.gd can assert it directly.

### `SM-12` No style-value menu: a style entry's value is seeded once and then unreachable from the canvas

**Unity does:** ShowStyleValueMenu — one of the eight searchable menus: title '<key> — values & helpers', placeholder 'value or helper…', offering the key's value TEMPLATES plus a freeform 'use "x"' row. It is what makes picking a style key a complete gesture: key, then value, both from a searchable vocabulary.

**Godot today:** absent. Picking a key from the style-key menu goes straight to `Edits.insert_style_entry(before, export, key, _style_seed(key))` (builder_window.gd:1406-1412), where `_style_seed` (:1253-1258) guesses from the key's spelling: `*_color` → `Color(0.2, 0.2, 0.24)`, anything with width/radius/margin/separation → `8`, everything else → `null`. There is no second menu, and — because a style entry line has no inline-edit gesture either (SM-05) — the seeded value cannot be changed anywhere except the source pane. A user who adds `font_size` gets `8`; a user who adds `anti_aliasing` gets the literal `null`, which is a compile-time wrong value with no in-builder route to fix it.

**To build:** After a style-key pick, open a second `open_menu` titled '<key> — values & helpers' from a `Schema`-driven template table (the LSP schema already carries property types and enum hint strings — `Schema.property_info` is used by builder_attributes.gd:69-72), with the existing `_style_seed` answer first and a freeform 'use "%s"' row. This is one more `_search_purpose` branch and one table; the chaining works because `_pick` hides before emitting, so opening a second menu from the handler is already the pattern `"edit_attribute"` uses.

**Godot specifics:** The style-key vocabulary already comes from `Schema.style_keys()` (builder_window.gd:1245), so the value templates belong beside it in addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/lsp/guitkx_schema.gd — a pure static table, headlessly testable, and not subject to the @tool static-var hazard because it is read through static funcs. Do NOT put it in a `.style.guitkx` module.

### `SM-13` No in-scope-collection menu for `@for`: wrapping seeds a fixed `range(1)` header with no vocabulary behind it

> **Duplicate of `LANG-15`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** ShowForeachWrapMenu — title '@foreach — collection', placeholder 'in-scope enumerable…'. It offers the in-scope enumerable PROPS (types containing List/[]/IEnumerable/Collection/Dictionary/Set) labelled 'expr — origin', plus hook-state locals parsed out of the body's `var (a, b) =` / `var x =` lines labelled 'hook state', de-duplicated by expression, plus a freeform 'loop over "x"'. Picking one seeds the header with that collection and then opens the header editor.

**Godot today:** absent. `Edits.WRAPS` (builder_edits.gd:675-682) is a fixed three-entry list — `@if (true)`, `@for (item in range(1))`, `@while (false)` — plus `@match` appended at builder_window.gd:1161. The wrap menu offers those four and nothing else; picking `@for` writes `range(1)` and opens the header editor on it (:1443-1450). The seeded-header-then-edit half of Unity's flow IS present and correct; the vocabulary half is not, so the user retypes the collection name from memory in every wrap.

**To build:** When the wrap pick is `@for`, chain a second `open_menu` before applying: in-scope props from `Attributes.props_of_component(card)` (already written, builder_attributes.gd:32-59) filtered to Array/Dictionary/PackedArray types, plus hook-state locals scraped from `card.body` rows with a `^\s*var\s+(\w+)` RegEx, deduplicated, plus a freeform 'loop over "%s"'. Substitute the pick into the seeded header (`@for (item in %s)`) and then open the header editor as it already does.

**Godot specifics:** The prop scrape already exists and is pure (builder_attributes.gd:32-59 parses the card's own signature), and `card.body` rows carry `source_text`, so the whole menu is a pure function of the projected card — directly testable in tests/builder_edits_test.gd with no editor. Unity's version is `async void` because it waits on an LSP round trip; here the schema is local, so this one is synchronous — a legitimate simplification, not a divergence.

### `SM-14` The name prompt's error line is never cleared while you type, and toggling its visibility reflows the prompt

**Unity does:** The value-changed callback branches on the mode: `if (_nameValidate == null) Rebuild(); else if (_errorLabel != null) _errorLabel.text = ""` — in prompt mode every keystroke wipes the message, so the correction and the complaint are never on screen together. The label is CREATED for every name prompt and simply carries an empty string, so 'showing an error does not reflow the rows'.

**Godot today:** wrong on both counts. `_search.text_changed` is wired unconditionally to `_rebuild()` (builder_search_menu.gd:53), and `_rebuild` in prompt mode clears the list, adds the 'Create' row and RETURNS without touching `_error` (:130-132). So a rejected name's message stays on screen, in red, while the user types the fixed name — and only disappears on the next successful submit. Separately, `_error.visible` is toggled (`false` at :99/:118, `true` at :203), so the first error inserts a label into the `VBoxContainer` and pushes the 'Create' row down; in a fixed-height `PopupPanel` that is a visible jump under the cursor.

**To build:** In `_rebuild`'s prompt branch, clear the message: `_error.text = ""` before adding the Create row (or, more faithfully, split the `text_changed` handler so prompt mode clears the error and menu mode rebuilds). Replace the `visible` toggle with a permanently-present label whose text is empty — `_error.visible = true` once in `_init`, `custom_minimum_size.y` set to one line height — so the layout never moves.

**Godot specifics:** Setting `LineEdit.text` from code does NOT emit `text_changed` in Godot, so `open_name_prompt`'s `_search.text = initial` (:116) correctly avoids a spurious rebuild — which is also why the error is not cleared on open by accident. A `Label` with empty text still contributes its font height to a `VBoxContainer`, so making it permanently visible is enough; no spacer needed.

### `SM-15` `_menu_at` is never invalidated, so the create prompt opened from the library pane's '+ new' lands wherever the last canvas right-click was

**Unity does:** Unity records the panel-space point at each gesture that opens a menu (RememberPointer), and its own source flags the failure mode when a gesture forgets to: 'this one did not [record], so the popup landed wherever the previous menu gesture had been'. BuilderLibraryPane fixes it for the one non-canvas case by calling RememberPointer on the '+ new' button's PointerDown before calling onNewFile().

**Godot today:** partial, with the same wart. `_menu_at` is assigned in exactly one place — `_on_row_context` (builder_window.gd:1079) — and is never cleared. `prompt_create` positions itself with `_menu_screen_at() if _menu_at != Vector2.ZERO else get_screen_position() + size * 0.3` (:1776), and `_on_library_create` (:551-553) clears `_menu_target` but NOT `_menu_at`. So after any canvas row right-click, pressing '+ new' in the library pane opens the name prompt over the canvas at that old point — on the opposite side of the window from the button that was pressed. The card-menu create path is fine because it goes through a right-click that did set `_menu_at`.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The gap UNDERSTATES its own scope. 'The card-menu create path is fine because it goes through a right-click that did set _menu_at' is wrong: `card_context_requested` (:701-704) records `_menu_world` and calls `_open_card_menu(..., get_global_mouse_position())` — neither it nor `_open_card_menu` (:2194-2211) ever sets `_menu_at`. The same is true of `canvas_context_requested` (:706-711). So the card menu's 'New ...' prompt AND the rename prompt (:2225-2227, which passes `_menu_screen_at()`) both land at the last ROW right-click point, or at the canvas origin when no row was ever right-clicked.

**To build:** Give the library pane the equivalent of RememberPointer: have `create_requested` carry the button's screen position (the pane already computes one for its own PopupMenu at builder_library_pane.gd:353), and have `prompt_create` take an explicit `at: Vector2` rather than reading `_menu_at`. That also removes the `_menu_at != Vector2.ZERO` sentinel, which is itself wrong — (0,0) is a legal canvas-local point.

**Godot specifics:** A `PopupPanel` takes SCREEN coordinates in `popup(Rect2i)`, so `get_screen_position()` on the source Control is the right conversion — unlike the inline editor, which needs parent-local (SM-08). Godot's `Popup` clamps the rect to the usable parent screen automatically (`Popup::_popup_adjust_rect`), so an at-cursor prompt near a screen edge already slides back on-screen with no port of Unity's ScreenBoundsAround.

### `SM-16` The inline editor's close has no `closed` and no `applied` channel, so nothing can distinguish 'done, next' from 'done'

**Unity does:** Close(commitIfChanged, applied) fires at most one of commit/cancelled, then ALWAYS fires `closed` exactly once ('the owner re-syncs the LSP buffer there because completion requests push synthesized text'), then fires `advance` only when the exit was Enter. Enter on UNCHANGED text fires neither commit nor cancelled but still fires closed AND advance — which is precisely how the style-entry run keeps moving through entries the user did not edit.

**Godot today:** partial. `commit()` fires `committed` only when the text changed (builder_inline_editor.gd:79-91 — correct, and correctly captures `_initial` before `_close()` clears it). `cancel()` always fires `cancelled` (:94-100 — correct). But there is no `closed` signal and no `applied` flag: Enter and blur both land on the same `commit()` (:41-42), and an Enter on unchanged text emits nothing at all, so no caller can act on 'the user finished this edit'.

**To build:** Add `signal closed(token)` emitted from `_close()` on every path, and widen `committed` to `committed(token, text, applied)` with `applied` true only from `text_submitted`. `closed` is what the window will need for the LSP buffer re-sync once SM-03 lands, and `applied` is the prerequisite for SM-10.

**Godot specifics:** Widening `committed` breaks its existing connections at builder_window.gd:687 and tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:738; both are one-line changes. Keep the current ordering — `_close()` before `emit` — it is right, and its comment (builder_inline_editor.gd:88-89) records why: a handler that reopens the editor must not be closed by the tail of this call.

Override `font_hover_color`/`font_pressed_color`/`font_focus_color` alongside `font_color` so the freeform tint survives hover, and add a flat Accent-at-14% `hover` stylebox to match Unity's band (and to share with the keyboard highlight from SM-02). Add `+ Vector2(0, 8)` to the popup anchor.

**Godot specifics:** Godot `Button` theme colours are per-STATE overrides — `font_color`, `font_hover_color`, `font_pressed_color`, `font_focus_color`, `font_hover_pressed_color`. Overriding only the first is the standard way a tinted flat Button loses its tint under the pointer. Note the palette must stay in the hand-written `@tool` builder_chrome_parts.gd for the reason its own doc gives (a generated `.gd` is not `@tool`, so a `.style.guitkx` module read from editor code comes back empty).

## The document model: workspace, tree, ledger, save and recovery

55 distinct gaps — 7 critical, 17 high, 19 medium, 12 low, plus 2 marked as duplicates.

### Action ledger: undo/redo, coalescing, history jump, what is recorded and what is not

### `L-01` Undo and redo have no reachable trigger: the keyboard model needs a focus nothing ever gives it, and the only Undo/Redo menu is dead code

**Unity does:** Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y drive the ledger from ANYWHERE in the builder window, including from inside the source pane's text field: OnKeyDown is registered on rootVisualElement with TrickleDown, and the modified branch deliberately sits OUTSIDE the `if (TypingTargetFocused()) return;` guard (BuilderWindow.cs:5480-5487 vs :5522-5545). UB-82 is exactly this problem already solved once: 'a KeyDownEvent goes to the FOCUSED element and nothing in the canvas was focusable', fixed by making rootVisualElement focusable and adding a TrickleDown PointerDown handler that focuses the root whenever the click target is not a typing surface (BuilderWindow.cs:450-476).

**Godot today:** wrong, and the feature is unreachable. `_gui_input` (builder_window.gd:226-253) implements the whole chord set, but (a) Godot delivers InputEventKey only to the exact `gui.key_focus` control — it does NOT bubble to ancestors' _gui_input; (b) nothing ever focuses the BuilderWindow: `focus_mode = FOCUS_ALL` is set at :139 and `grab_focus()` is called nowhere in builder/ or in the hosting plugin.gd:422-446; (c) canvas/builder_canvas_host.gd:91 is MOUSE_FILTER_STOP with the default FOCUS_NONE, so Godot's focus-grab walk breaks at it and a canvas click moves focus nowhere; (d) the guard at :232 `if _typing_focused(): return` sits BEFORE the ctrl branch, the opposite of Unity, so even a focused source pane cannot reach the ledger. MEASURED (headless probe, InputEventKey pushed at the viewport after an apply_edit): no focus owner -> Ctrl+Z leaves cursor at 1; window explicitly grab_focus()'d -> cursor 0 (works); CodeEdit focused -> cursor unchanged; toolbar OptionButton focused -> cursor unchanged; folder Tree focused -> cursor unchanged; a left click at the canvas centre left focus on the CodeEdit. The mouse fallback does not exist either: the toolbar (:596-618) has History/Trace/Help/Save/Abort and NO Undo or Redo button, `_refresh_status` (:2460-2467) loops looking for MenuId.UNDO/REDO metadata that no button carries, and `_history_menu` — the only Undo/Redo UI, built at :462-465 — is popped only from MenuId._HISTORY_OLD (:976-980), which nothing raises. The single working undo trigger in the whole builder is Escape on a seeded inline editor (:689-699), because the LineEdit holds focus itself.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One sentence of the evidence is factually wrong: `grab_focus()` IS called — plugin.gd:455, inside `open_builder_on`, the FileSystem-dock context route. So there is exactly one entry point that leaves the window focused, and Ctrl+Z works from it until the first click on the folder Tree, library, source pane or the Layers OptionButton takes focus away and nothing gives it back. The main-menu route (plugin.gd:234 -> `_open_builder` :422-446) never grabs focus. The finding stands; the phrase 'called nowhere in the hosting plugin' should read 'called only on the FileSystem-dock route, never on the menu route, and never again after focus moves'.

**To build:** 1. Move the chord handling off `_gui_input` onto `_shortcut_input(event)` (or `_unhandled_key_input`) on RuitkBuilderWindow: those run for the whole viewport regardless of focus and after the focused Control has declined, which is the Godot equivalent of TrickleDown-plus-consume. Keep `accept_event()`/`set_input_as_handled()`. 2. Reorder to match Unity: handle the ctrl/meta branch BEFORE the `_typing_focused()` guard, and keep the guard only for bare Delete/Escape — the source pane's CodeEdit must lose Ctrl+Z to the ledger, since the ledger is where its edits will live once L-02 is fixed. 3. Add Undo/Redo buttons to the toolbar next to Save/Abort with `set_meta("command", MenuId.UNDO/REDO)` so the existing enable/disable loop at :2464-2467 stops being inert, and either wire MenuId._HISTORY_OLD to something or delete it and `_history_menu`. 4. Give canvas/builder_canvas_host.gd `focus_mode = FOCUS_ALL` and `grab_focus()` on a press, so the window has a keyboard home after a canvas click.

**Godot specifics:** Godot 4 routes InputEventKey to `gui.key_focus` alone; `_gui_call_input`'s ancestor walk is for mouse events. `_shortcut_input` and `_unhandled_key_input` propagate through the viewport's tree regardless of focus and are the idiomatic home for window-level chords. The builder lives in its own `Window` (plugin.gd:429-437), which is its own Viewport, so consuming there cannot leak to EditorNode's global Ctrl+Z — Unity's UB-89 hazard does not exist here and no ConsumeKey equivalent is needed. Control.mouse_filter matters twice: MOUSE_FILTER_STOP + FOCUS_NONE on the canvas host halts Godot's focus-grab walk, and MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE on card children (:244) means the walk starts at the host. All of this is headlessly testable — push InputEventKey at `root.get_viewport()` and assert `ledger.cursor()`; no suite does.

**Risk:** Everything else in this area is downstream of this. The ledger is a complete, correct, well-tested data structure that a user cannot reach: no key works until something focuses the root Control, and no menu or button offers undo at all. A reviewer reading builder_window.gd sees a full keyboard model and a green parity row for it.

### `L-02` Source-pane edits are absent from the ledger entirely: typing records nothing, Apply records nothing, and only Revert records

**Unity does:** OnCodeEdited applies the keystroke to the session and calls `_ledger.RecordTyping(_focusFile, before, bufferLf)` (BuilderWindow.cs:1709), which coalesces the burst into ONE entry described 'type in <file>' (BuilderActionLedger.cs:132-180). Every keystroke in the source pane is therefore in the history, one row per burst, and Ctrl+Z walks back the whole burst. UB-161 records this as the finding that decided the design.

**Godot today:** wrong. Two independent faults compose into a total loss of source-pane history. (1) builder_source_pane.gd:174-190 `_on_text_changed` writes EVERY keystroke straight into the model via `workspace.apply_edit(_path, after)` and then emits `buffer_edited`; the window's handler `_on_buffer_edited` (builder_window.gd:903-909) returns immediately when `_source.is_editing()`, and `_on_text_changed` can only fire while editing (the editor is `editable = false` otherwise, and setting `.text` from code does not emit `text_changed`). So `ledger.record_typing` — a correct, fully tested 25-line implementation — has NO reachable caller. (2) Because the buffer was already written per keystroke, when Apply fires `edit_applied` -> `apply_edit(path, text, "Edit <file>")` (builder_window.gd:723-724) the funnel hits `if before == after: return false` at :867 and records nothing, and skips `_after_model_change` too. MEASURED (headless probe, message queue flushed between keystrokes): buffer written per keystroke = true; ledger entries after typing = 0; ledger entries after Apply = 0, can_undo = false. The ONE source-pane action that does reach the ledger is Revert (:725-726), which records an entry whose undo REAPPLIES the text the user just threw away.

**To build:** Decide which contract the source pane keeps and make one of them true. Either (a) Unity's: drop the `is_editing()` short-circuit at builder_window.gd:904-905 so `record_typing` runs per keystroke, and keep the card re-parse (call `_after_model_change` or at least `Service.populate_card`) while leaving `preview.request_refresh()` for Apply — this is what the ledger was written for and it needs no new code; or (b) keep the edit->apply cycle and stop writing the model per keystroke: make `_on_text_changed` a pure notification while editing (do not call `workspace.apply_edit`), snapshot at `_set_editing(true)`, and let Apply be the single `apply_edit` that records one entry. (b) is the smaller behavioural change and matches the pane's own documented intent, but it must also fix `cancel_edit` so a revert restores without a ledger entry. Either way add a chrome-suite assertion that a source-pane edit produces exactly one entry and that `w.undo()` restores the pre-edit text.

**Godot specifics:** TextEdit's `text_changed` is DEFERRED through the MessageQueue, so a naive test that inserts and asserts in the same frame sees an unchanged buffer — the probe only found this after `await process_frame`. Any new suite must flush a frame between `insert_text_at_caret` and the assertion. `TextEdit.set_text` genuinely does not emit `text_changed` (the `setting_text` guard), so builder_source_pane.gd:174-178's comment is right and `refresh_from_model` is safe to keep. CodeEdit carries its own undo stack; once Ctrl+Z is routed to the ledger (L-01) the two must not both be live on the same buffer.

**Risk:** The source pane is one of the builder's two authoring surfaces and NONE of its work is undoable. A user who types for ten minutes and presses Ctrl+Z gets the last canvas gesture reverted instead — silent, wrong-target undo. It also means UB-161's whole design (compile on action boundary, not on keystroke) is moot here, and that the capabilities-spec clause 'a cross-file change undoes as a single step from whichever file is in focus' is unmet for the file actually in focus.

### `L-03` Redoing a creation restores an EMPTY module — the file's whole content is destroyed

**Unity does:** RecordCreation stores only the path; the text is captured LAZILY at undo time — `var pending = _workspace.TryGet(change.FilePath); if (pending != null) change.After = pending.BufferText;` then Delete — and redo re-creates from it: `_workspace.CreateNew(change.FilePath, change.After ?? "")` (BuilderWindow.cs:1374-1390). Unity's own note: 'The text rides along so redo can re-open the session with exactly what the user had' (BuilderActionLedger.cs:252-253); redo restores the LATEST text, including everything typed after the creation.

**Godot today:** wrong. builder_window.gd:2123-2127: undo does `workspace.delete(path)` with NO capture of `module.buffer_text` into `change.after`, and redo does `workspace.create_new(change.file_path, "")` — a hard-coded empty string. `record_creation` (builder_ledger.gd:254-262) leaves before/after as "" and nothing ever fills them. MEASURED: create a component (template text, 75 chars, present), undo past the creation, redo the creation -> module present, buffer_len = 0. The template the module was born with is gone, and so is every edit that lived in the same entry.

**To build:** In builder_window.gd:2123-2127, mirror Unity: on reverse, resolve the module first and write `change.after = module.buffer_text` before `workspace.delete(path)`; on forward, `workspace.create_new(change.file_path, change.after)`. Consider also Unreal's stronger answer (RuitkUiBuilderLedger.cpp ApplyDelta, 'Re-entering the tree keeps its ID'): re-insert the SAME Module object rather than minting a fresh one, which would also close the identity hole Unity documents — Godot's create_new -> Module.fresh mints a new id, so any later entry keyed to the old id silently degrades to path resolution. `Change.removed` already exists on the Change class (builder_ledger.gd:50) and could carry the module for CREATION exactly as it does for DELETION.

**Godot specifics:** `workspace.create_new` returns null on a path collision and the failure is swallowed at builder_window.gd:2126 (no `remounted` equivalent, no toast) — the same swallow Unity has. Since Change is a RefCounted inner class, holding the Module on it costs nothing and it will not outlive the window; the ledger is never serialised. The fix is pure model code and is fully headlessly testable from builder_chrome_test.gd's existing `_window()` fixture.

**Risk:** Silent destruction of work on a routine flow: 'I undid one step too far, let me go forward again'. The module reappears on the canvas as an empty card; the next action truncates the redo tail and the content is unrecoverable, with nothing on screen saying anything went wrong. No suite covers create->undo->redo; builder_chrome_test.gd tests create and delete but never a creation round trip.

### `L-04` Renaming a module records nothing in the ledger

**Unity does:** OnRenameConfirmed opens `_ledger.Begin("rename " + oldName + " to " + newName)` (BuilderWindow.cs:3723), captures imports, rewrites the export declaration, calls MoveModule, then `_ledger.RecordMove(full, newFull)` plus a `_ledger.Record` for every import rewrite ReconcileImports returned, then End() and RefreshHistoryPanel (BuilderWindow.cs:3780-3784). One entry, one Ctrl+Z, and the module and every importer go back together. UB-135 is the concrete damage from getting this wrong.

**Godot today:** absent. builder_window.gd:1897-1914 `_rename_to` calls `workspace.move_to(...)`, `reproject()`, `select_module(...)`, `preview.request_refresh()` — and touches the ledger nowhere: no begin, no record_move, no record of the returned rewrites. MEASURED: entries before a rename = 0, entries after = 0, can_undo = false, while the module and its importer's specifier both changed. In a session with prior history, Ctrl+Z after a rename silently undoes the PREVIOUS unrelated action while the rename stands.

**To build:** Wrap `_rename_to` the way `place_module` (builder_window.gd:1734-1743) already wraps a move: `ledger.begin("Rename %s to %s")`, capture `workspace.capture_imports()` BEFORE the name rewrites, call move_to, then `ledger.record_move(old_path, new_path)` and `ledger.record(...)` for each entry of `workspace.reconcile_imports(snapshot)`, then `ledger.end()`. The empty-scope drop at builder_ledger.gd:322 already makes the refused-rename path safe. Add a chrome-suite assertion: rename, undo, the module is back at its old path AND the importer's specifier is back.

**Godot specifics:** `workspace.move_to` already returns the rewrite array (builder_workspace.gd:321-325), so the data the ledger needs is being discarded at the call site, not missing. Replay needs nothing new: `_replay_change`'s MOVE branch (builder_window.gd:2134-2136) goes through move_to_path, whose `_move` re-captures and re-reconciles imports symmetrically. Purely model-level, testable from builder_chrome_test.gd.

**Risk:** A rename is one of the three commonest structural gestures and it is invisible to the history — and worse than invisible, because Ctrl+Z afterwards undoes something else. tests/builder_parity.gd:41 `["ShowRenamePrompt", "CardMenuId.RENAME"]` is green over it.

The owner case is not special-cased away from the ledger, and the module-drop case at :555-563 records a RecordMove for the module itself, so the entry always contains the structural change, not only its side effects.

**Godot today:** wrong, in two different ways depending on the branch. (a) THE COMMON CASE IS UNRECORDED: builder_window.gd:1681-1683 — when a module owns the folder, move_folder `return _move_one(module, target_folder, leaf)` BEFORE `ledger.begin` at :1698, and `_move_one` (:1751-1757) touches the ledger nowhere. MEASURED: moving `components/row` (owned by row.guitkx) to the tree root succeeded, rewrote the importer's specifier from "./components/row/row" to "./row", and left the ledger at 0 entries. (b) THE MULTI-MODULE CASE RECORDS ONLY TEXT: :1698-1713 opens a scope, moves every mover, and records ONLY the import rewrites — there is no `record_move` for any module. Undoing that entry rewrites the specifiers back to their pre-move form while every module stays in the new folder, leaving the tree importing paths that no longer resolve.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: (b) is worse than stated. The claim says the multi-module case 'RECORDS ONLY TEXT'. Measured, it records NOTHING: a three-module tree, `move_folder(app/pack -> app/moved)`, the importer's specifier demonstrably rewritten from './pack/row/row' to '~/.../moved/pack/row/row', and the ledger went 0 -> 0 entries. The cause is that `Workspace._move` (builder_workspace.gd:342-347), which `move_to`/`place_at` both funnel through, ALREADY calls `capture_imports()` + `reconcile_imports()` internally — so the OUTER pair at builder_window.gd:1700/:1710 always returns [], `ledger.record` never fires, and `ledger.end()` drops the empty scope. So the entry does not exist at all rather than being half an entry; the undo hazard the claim describes cannot occur because there is nothing to undo. Same defect at :2060/:2068 and :1735/:1742 — see missed gap PLACE-TREE.

**To build:** In the owner branch, hoist `ledger.begin("Move %s" % leaf)` above the delegation and have `_move_one` (or its caller) `record_move(module.file_path(), destination)` — `place_module` at :1734-1743 is the shape to copy. In the movers branch, add a `ledger.record_move(from, module.file_path())` inside the loop at :1701-1709 alongside the existing `layout.repath`. A single MOVE change per module is enough: replay's move_to_path re-reconciles the imports, so the recorded text rewrites are belt-and-braces rather than the whole entry.

**Godot specifics:** `layout.repath` is already called in the movers branch (:1707) and not in the owner branch — the same asymmetry, so fixing both together is natural (see L-09). All of this is `FileAccess`-free in-memory tree work and provable from builder_chrome_test.gd; the existing `_test_folder_pane_refiles` covers place_module but never move_folder's ledger.

**Risk:** Half of the folder-drop gesture is unrecorded and the other half records an entry whose undo produces a tree state the user never authored — imports pointing at where files used to be. That is the precise failure BuilderActionLedger.cs:7-17 exists to prevent.

### `L-06` The History panel's rows are unclickable: the jump is guarded off by state the history never sets

**Unity does:** Every history row is clickable; a PointerDownEvent runs JumpHistoryTo(i + 1, description), which walks the cursor with N undos or N redos through the same ApplyEntry the chords use, then applies once and toasts (BuilderWindow.cs:1436-1464, :5039-5041). This is UB-141's fix and the reason 'a jump is simply N undos or N redos'.

**Godot today:** wrong — the code is complete and unreachable. `_show_history` (builder_window.gd:155-172) builds the rows with payload `i + 1` and sets `_search_purpose = "history"`, but sets neither `_menu_target` nor `_menu_row`. The pick handler `_on_search_picked` (:1356-1360) opens with `if workspace == null or _menu_target.is_empty() or _menu_row == null: return` — a guard meant for the row-level menus — and returns BEFORE the `"history"` branch at :1367-1370 ever runs. MEASURED: two entries recorded, cursor 2; `_show_history()` then picking row 1 left cursor at 2 (`_menu_row` was null); calling `_jump_history_to(1)` directly moved the cursor to 1. So the jump logic itself is correct and nothing can invoke it unless the user happens to have right-clicked a card ROW earlier in the session and not pressed Escape since.

**To build:** Move the `"history"` branch above the row-menu guard in `_on_search_picked`, or give the history menu its own `picked` handler. While there, render `entry.file_summary()` (builder_ledger.gd:67-71) in the row's detail column — it is implemented, tested and never shown — and consider showing the cursor as a real marker rather than a leading '•' inside the label text.

**Godot specifics:** The history rows go through the same `SearchMenu` used for attribute and tag menus (chrome/builder_search_menu.gd:21 `signal picked`), which is why they inherited a row-context guard — the single-dispatcher pattern is the trap. Godot's PopupMenu would be the more honest host for a list whose rows mean something different from every other SearchMenu use. Fully headlessly testable: `w._show_history(); w._on_search_picked(1); assert w.ledger.cursor() == 1`.

**Risk:** THE PARITY GATE IS GREEN OVER A DEAD FEATURE. tests/builder_parity.gd:49 and :50 both grep for functions that exist, are correct, and cannot be invoked. Combined with L-01 this means the builder has NO working history navigation of any kind except Escape-on-a-seeded-editor: the panel opens, shows the history accurately, and does nothing when clicked.

### `L-07` Format-on-save rewrites every dirty buffer without a ledger entry, leaving every earlier entry's `after` text stale

**Unity does:** SaveAll wraps the formatter pass in its own scope: `Begin("format on save")` + FormatDirtyBuffers + `End()` (BuilderWindow.cs:5828-5853), so the reformat is a history entry like any other, it is undoable, and the ledger's recorded text keeps matching the buffers. UB-116 is why it exists: canvas edits splice LINES in with guessed indentation, so Save normalises through the AST formatter and records the result.

**Godot today:** absent. document/builder_workspace.gd:531 calls `_format(module)` inside save_all's write loop, and `_format` (:739-745) replaces `module.buffer_text` with the formatter output — the doc at :52-54 says so explicitly ('The formatted text becomes the BUFFER'). builder_window.gd's `save()` (:1949-1978) makes no ledger call at all. So after a save that reformatted anything, every prior EDIT change's `after` no longer matches the buffer, and undoing across the save silently discards the formatting as well as the edit, with no row saying it happened.

**To build:** Either record it — capture each dirty buffer's text before `_format`, and have save() open `ledger.begin("Format on save")`, `ledger.record(path, before, after)` per formatted module, `ledger.end()` (the empty-scope drop handles a save that formatted nothing) — or, if the Godot leg prefers formatting to be outside the history, state that in CLAUDE.md as a divergence and clear the ledger at save the way abort() does, so a stale entry cannot be replayed. Recording is the smaller change and matches the family.

**Godot specifics:** `Formatter.format` (guitkx_formatter.gd) is pure and headlessly runnable, so recording it costs one snapshot per dirty module inside the existing loop. builder_save_test.gd already drives save_all against exact disk state and is the natural place for the assertion.

**Risk:** A quiet divergence between what the ledger thinks a file says and what it says. The parity row is green because it greps for the string `format_on_save`, which exists — as a workspace flag, not as a ledger entry.

### `L-08` A replay that removes the focused module leaves the focus naming a file that no longer exists

**Unity does:** ApplyLedgerWrites runs RebindFocusIfMissing() between the model writes and the redraw (BuilderWindow.cs:1502-1505, :1680-1694): if `_focusFile` names a module the workspace no longer has, the focus moves to the first live module, and to null when the workspace is empty. UB-131 is the CRITICAL this answers ('after the change i ctrl Z and the card and source pane are empty'); UB-162 is the ghost card a stale focus produced; UB-163 is the null-focus audit the fix required.

**Godot today:** absent. `_replay` (builder_window.gd:2105-2114) applies the changes then calls `reproject()`, `_source.refresh_from_model()`, `preview.request_refresh()` — `_focus_path` is never validated. Undoing a creation, or the creation half of any future rename entry, leaves `_focus_path` naming a deleted module: `_source.refresh_from_model` (builder_source_pane.gd:150-155) sees no module and clears the pane, `graph.index_of(_focus_path)` returns -1 so nothing is selected on the canvas, and `_refresh_status` (:2455) still prints the dead filename in the title strip.

**To build:** Add a `_rebind_focus_if_missing()` — `if not _focus_path.is_empty() and workspace.try_get(_focus_path) != null: return`, else take the first of `workspace.modules()` (or "" when empty) and call `select_module` on it — and call it in `_replay` between the change loop and `reproject()`. Godot is already safe against Unity's UB-163 fallout: `builder_tree.gd:53-57`/`:62-65` treat an empty id and an empty path as NOT FOUND, and `Paths.canon("")` returns empty rather than throwing, so an empty focus needs no nine-site audit — but `_create_folder`/`create_module` read `_focus_path.get_base_dir()` (:1916-1919) and should be checked against an empty focus.

**Godot specifics:** `select_module` is re-entrancy guarded by `_choosing` (:2151-2176) so calling it from inside a replay is safe. Do NOT call it while `ledger.replaying` is set expecting suppression to matter — select_module makes no ledger calls, so it is inert either way.

**Risk:** Milder than Unity's version — Godot projects the graph from `workspace.modules()` so no ghost card is mounted — but the user still lands on an empty source pane with nothing selected after an undo, which is exactly the symptom UB-131 was filed for.

### `L-09` Card positions do not follow a module through a move, a rename, or an undone/redone move

**Unity does:** MoveModule is the ONE helper the rename command and the ledger replay share, and it re-keys the saved card layout on every move in both directions: RepathLayout(fromDir, toDir, isFolder:true) for an owned folder plus RepathLayout(from, to, isFolder:false) for the file, plus RepointFocus (BuilderWindow.cs:3665-3706, called from ApplyEntry at :1389). UB-140 states the rule: layout is keyed by PATH precisely so it must be re-keyed on every move including undo and redo.

**Godot today:** partial. `canvas/builder_canvas_layout.gd:180-205` implements `repath` correctly, and it has exactly ONE call site in the whole builder: builder_window.gd:1707, inside move_folder's multi-module branch. It is not called by `place_module`/`_move_one` (:1725-1757, the primary module-move path), not by `_rename_to` (:1897-1914), and not by `_replay_change`'s MOVE branch (:2134-2136). So a re-filed or renamed card loses its position, and undoing a move does not bring the card back to where it was.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Two refinements, one of which makes it worse and one milder. WORSE: it is not '1 of 4 paths re-keys the layout' but effectively 0 of 4. The single call site at :1707 is defeated by the `reproject()` five lines later at :1714, because `reproject` does `layout = CanvasLayout.for_graph(graph)` (builder_window.gd:825), which RELOADS the layout from disk and throws the in-memory repath away — `repath` never calls `save`. Measured on the movers branch: helper card pinned at 1234,4321 and saved, `move_folder` run, card came back at a seeded slot. MILDER: 'undoing a move does not bring the card back to where it was' is wrong. Measured, undo DOES restore 999,777 — precisely because nothing was ever re-keyed, so the layout file still holds the old path as its key. The damage is one-directional: forward moves lose the slot, undo accidentally finds it again.

**To build:** Give the move a single helper the way Unity does — one function that calls `workspace.move_to_path`, `layout.repath(from, to, owns_folder)` and the focus re-point — and route `place_module`, `_move_one`, `_rename_to` and `_replay_change`'s MOVE branch through it. That also removes the current split where only one of four paths re-keys the layout.

**Godot specifics:** `CanvasLayout.repath` is pure and file-backed via layout.save; nothing about it needs an editor. `reproject()` then `layout.apply_to(graph)` + `adopt_unplaced(graph)` (builder_window.gd:820-826) will seed a new slot for any path the layout does not know, which is exactly how a moved card loses its place — so repath must run BEFORE reproject.

**Risk:** The visible cost of an undo is wrong: the module goes back but its card jumps to a seeded slot, so 'undo' does not restore what the user was looking at. Layout is persisted (`layout.save`), so the damage outlives the session.

**Unity does:** Not a Unity feature (Trace is a Godot addition), but it is the Godot leg's stand-in for surfacing history state outside the History popup, and it is the only place that consumes undo_label().

**Godot today:** wrong. chrome/builder_console.gd:200-201 writes `ledger.entries.size()` — `entries` is a FUNCTION on the ledger (builder_ledger.gd:105-106), so this evaluates a Callable and calls `.size()` on it. MEASURED: `SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid call. Nonexistent function 'size' in base 'Callable'. at: RuitkBuilderConsole.trace (builder_console.gd:200)`. **Godot specifics:** A classic GDScript trap: `obj.method` without parentheses is a valid Callable, so this compiles and only fails at run time — and since `trace()` is fire-and-forget from a menu id, the error goes to the Errors dock where nobody is looking during a builder session.

### `L-12` A history jump re-projects and refreshes the panes once per entry crossed, not once for the walk

**Unity does:** JumpHistoryTo accumulates buffer writes across the WHOLE walk into one list and calls ApplyLedgerWrites once at the end, so 'a jump across ten entries redraws once, not ten times' and produces one toast, one MountCanvas and one debounced recompile (BuilderWindow.cs:1436-1464, :1345-1350).

**Godot today:** partial. builder_window.gd:176-183 loops `undo()` / `redo()`, and each of those runs a full `_replay` (:2105-2114) ending in `reproject()` + `_source.refresh_from_model()` + `preview.request_refresh()`. A jump across ten entries therefore re-projects the graph ten times and rebuilds the folder and library panes ten times. Only the toast is correctly once (:182-183), and the preview compile coalesces because request_refresh is debounced.

**To build:** Split `_replay` into the change application and the redraw: give `undo()`/`redo()` an optional `defer_refresh` argument, have `_jump_history_to` pass it and call `reproject()` / `_source.refresh_from_model()` / `preview.request_refresh()` once after both loops. This also makes L-08's focus rebind a single step at the end of the walk rather than one per entry.

**Godot specifics:** `preview.request_refresh()` is debounced by builder_preview.gd's is_due()/compile_dirty cadence pumped from `_process`, so the compile side is already once-per-jump; the projection side is not.

**Risk:** Cost and visible churn, not corruption — the end state is correct. It matters more on the canvas than in Unity because `reproject()` rebuilds the whole graph and re-runs CanvasLayout.for_graph, which is the expensive path the builder otherwise avoids by using `_after_model_change` for a single card.

### `L-13` record_move overwrites a correct module id with an empty one

**Unity does:** RecordMove sets `ModuleId = IdOf(fromPath)` and Unity documents that at both call sites the move has already happened so the id comes back null — 'harmless only because moves never go through the identity-resolved write path' (BuilderActionLedger.cs:225, BuilderWindow.cs:3780, :562).

Line 228 then overwrites it with `_id_for(from_path)`, which is now empty. The comment at :226-227 asserts the opposite of what the call site does.

**To build:** Delete the overwrite at builder_ledger.gd:228 and let `_change`'s `to_path` lookup stand, or make the call site record BEFORE the move so the from-path lookup is meaningful. Fix the comment either way. Then the capabilities-spec clause 'each change remembers its MODULE not only its path' becomes true for MOVE as well as EDIT — which the Unity leg cannot claim.

**Godot specifics:** Godot's `by_id` and `by_path` both treat empty input as NOT FOUND (builder_tree.gd:53-65), which is why this degrades silently instead of erroring — the same null-safety Unity had to add for UB-163.

**Risk:** Harmless today because `_replay_change`'s MOVE branch uses `change.before`/`change.after` directly and `by_id("")` is null-safe (builder_tree.gd:53-55). It becomes real the moment anything resolves a move by identity, and it makes the ledger's own doc comment wrong, which is how the next reader gets it wrong too.
