### `L-14` Crash recovery adopts a different tree without clearing the ledger

**Unity does:** Unity's reload journal restores the tree while the NonSerialized ledger comes back empty by construction — 'an undo whose other half was compiled away is worse than no undo' (BuilderActionLedger.cs:18-21). The history and the tree can never disagree.

**Godot today:** partial. `open_tree` calls `ledger.clear()` (builder_window.gd:766) and `abort()` calls it too (:2080) — both better than Unity, which never clears on Abort. But `restore_recovery` (:955-962) calls `Journal.try_restore` -> `workspace.adopt_tree(BuilderTree.from_dict(...))`, replacing the whole tree, and does not clear the ledger. Any entries recorded in the current session then reference a tree that has been swapped underneath them.

**To build:** Add `ledger.clear()` to `restore_recovery` alongside the reproject, and to any other `workspace.adopt_tree` caller. One line; it makes the invariant 'the ledger only ever describes the tree currently in the window' hold everywhere.

**Godot specifics:** `BuilderTree.from_dict` mints Module objects from serialised data, so a DELETION change's `removed` reference points at an object that is no longer part of the tree — `workspace.restore` would re-add a stale duplicate rather than refusing, since it only checks the PATH (builder_workspace.gd:283).

**Risk:** Narrow — the ledger is usually empty when a recovery is offered, since the offer follows a fresh open. But the plugin can offer recovery over a session that already has history, and then Ctrl+Z replays entries against modules with different object identities.

*low · risk · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/Document/BuilderActionLedger.cs:18-21 (drop the history, keep the tree), BuilderWindow.cs:1343; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:955-962 (restore_recovery, no clear), :766 (open_tree clears), :2080 (abort clears), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_journal.gd:70-79

### Create / rename / delete / move flows, save, abort, unsaved-tree placement, journal recovery

### `G-01` Rename rewrites neither the export declaration nor any importer's binding — it only moves the file

> **Duplicate of `DM-02`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** RenameModule is FOUR edits that land together or not at all (UB-124, UB-135): (1) RenameExportIn rewrites the module's own `export` declaration head with a count-of-1 regex `(\bexport\s+[^\r\n=;]*?\b)<old>\b`; (2) RenameReferencesIn rewrites, in every OTHER module resolved through EditSession (opened if needed), the import SPECIFIER stem and then the BINDING name with `\b<old>\b`; (3) MoveModule performs the file/folder move as one operation; (4) ReconcileImports re-derives the specifier PATHS. All inside one _ledger.Begin("rename X to Y")/End().

**Godot today:** absent. `_rename_to` (builder_window.gd:1897-1914) is nine lines: it calls `workspace.move_to(module.file_path(), folder, name)` and nothing else. `grep -rn "rename" addons/.../builder/ --include=*.gd` returns only the prompt strings, the ledger's `_open_default("rename")` and `DirAccess.rename_absolute` — there is no RenameExportIn, no RenameReferencesIn, no RenameTargetPath. `workspace.move_to` -> `_move` (builder_workspace.gd:317-322) does capture_imports + tree.move_to + reconcile_imports, which rewrites specifier PATHS only. So after renaming `card.guitkx` to `deck.guitkx`: the file is `deck.guitkx`, the buffer still says `export Card() -> RuitkVNode`, and every importer still says `import { Card } from "./deck"`. The specifier now resolves to a module that does not export `Card` — GUITKX2305 (unimported/unresolved ref) across the tree, and the project stops compiling. The comment at builder_window.gd:1903-1906 asserts move_to "is the one operation that knows a rename is four edits"; it is not, and the comment is what hid the gap.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The tree does NOT stop compiling and no GUITKX2305 is raised. I compiled the exact post-rename state through the real compiler (`RuitkGuitkxCodegen.compile_file`): `deck.guitkx` declaring `export Card()` and `app.guitkx` holding `import { Card } from "./deck"` both return ok=true, diags=[]. The resolver checks that a named import exists in the TARGET's export table, not that the export name matches the file basename, and `reconcile_imports` has already re-pointed the specifier at the moved file. The generated `deck.gd` declares `class_name Card` (codegen derives the class from the first exported decl, not the filename), so no duplicate-class or uid breakage either. The real defect is that the rename is COSMETIC: the file, the card title and the folder move, while the declaration, the generated `class_name` and every `<Card />` use site keep the old identifier -- a user renames Card to Deck and everything still says Card. Severity is high, not critical; the work to do is as described, but the risk paragraph and the "the project stops compiling" framing should be struck.

**To build:** Add `RuitkBuilderEdits.rename_export(source, old, new)` and `rename_references(source, old, new, stem)` next to the existing `bind_export`/`ensure_import` in builder/edits/builder_edits.gd (pure string ops, headlessly testable, already the home of this kind of surgery). Then rewrite `_rename_to` to: capture `workspace.capture_imports()` BEFORE any name text is touched; `ledger.begin("Rename %s to %s")`; apply_edit the module's own buffer through the funnel; for every other non-read-only module in `workspace.modules()` (not just the ones on the canvas) apply_edit the reference rewrite; `workspace.move_to(...)`; `ledger.record_move(from, to)`; record every rewrite `workspace.reconcile_imports(snapshot)` returns; `ledger.end()`. Note the `.style`/`.hooks` stem rule: the specifier for a companion carries the infix, so the specifier pass must match `(["'/])<old><stem>(?=["'])`.

**Godot specifics:** Route the buffer writes through `builder_window.apply_edit()` (builder_window.gd:859-880) — the ONE funnel — so each lands as a ledger record, a `_after_model_change` re-projection and a preview round; writing `module.buffer_text` directly is what `_format` already does wrong (G-04). The declaration regex must respect this leg's split: the FILE base name is snake_case but the exported component identifier is PascalCase (builder_edits.gd:900-909 `_pascal`), so `card.guitkx` declares `export Card()`. Renaming the file to `deck` must rewrite the declaration to `Deck` and the bindings to `Deck` — the old-name argument for the declaration pass is `_pascal(old_file_name)`, not the file name. Use `RegEx.create_from_string` once at file scope, not per call (a `@tool` static var initialiser does NOT run in the editor for a generated .gd, but builder_edits.gd is hand-written and `@tool`, so a `static var` is safe here — a const RegEx is not, GDScript cannot const a RegEx).

**Risk:** Every rename silently breaks the tree it renamed. The user sees the card retitle and the file move, then the next preview round and the next real build fail with import errors naming a symbol they just renamed away. Because nothing is in the ledger (G-02), Ctrl+Z cannot get back to the state that compiled.

*critical · logic · OVERSTATED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:3708-3789 (RenameModule), 3791-3803 (RenameExportIn), 3805-3821 (RenameReferencesIn); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1897-1914 (_rename_to, whole function), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:317-322 (_move). Third-leg corroboration: ruitk-unreal/.../SRuitkUiBuilderPanel.cpp:1650-1726 (CommitRename) opens a ledger entry, calls RenameIdentifier on the doc's own text AND on every other doc, then toasts "Renamed to X — applies on Save."

### `G-02` Rename and folder-move are not in the ledger; the folder-move entry that does exist reverts importer text without moving anything back

> **Duplicate of `DM-02`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** Every structural operation is one ledger entry holding every change the gesture produced. RenameModule wraps the export edit, each importer edit, the MoveModule and every ReconcileImports rewrite in one Begin/End (BuilderWindow.cs:3708-3789). MoveModule records `_ledger.RecordMove(full, newFull)` plus every rewrite the move produced, explicitly "so the entry describes the file contents completely - a redo that restored a buffer recorded BEFORE the rewrite would otherwise put the stale specifier back".

**Godot today:** wrong, three different ways. (1) `_rename_to` (builder_window.gd:1897-1914) touches the ledger not at all — a rename is invisible to undo. (2) `move_folder`'s common path, a component that owns its folder, returns at builder_window.gd:1684-1686 through `_move_one` — which is BEFORE `ledger.begin` at line 1697 — so `_move_one` (builder_window.gd:1751-1757) records nothing whatsoever. (3) `move_folder`'s general path opens an entry, moves every module, then records ONLY the import rewrites (builder_window.gd:1697-1713) and never calls `ledger.record_move`. Undoing that entry replays only EDIT changes: the importer buffers are restored to their pre-move specifiers while the modules stay at their new folders. The tree is then in a state the user never authored and cannot compile — every restored specifier points where the files no longer are. `_place_tree_in` (builder_window.gd:2059-2072) has the identical shape and the identical hole.

**To build:** In `move_folder`, move `ledger.begin` above the owner fast-path so `_move_one` is inside a scope, and have `_move_one` (or its callers) emit `ledger.record_move(from, module.file_path())` per module moved — the ledger already collapses nested begin/end into the outermost entry (builder_ledger.gd:139-160), so the shared helper can open its own scope safely. Same for `_place_tree_in`. For `_rename_to`, see G-01. Then add a suite case in tests/builder_chrome_test.gd that drives `w.move_folder(...)` / `w._rename_to(...)` and asserts `w.undo()` puts BOTH the paths and the buffers back — the existing tests/builder_save_test.gd:274-298 `_test_rename_then_save` drives `ws.move_to` on the model directly and never touches the window, which is why this has stayed green.

**Godot specifics:** `_replay_change` (builder_window.gd:2116-2137) already handles ChangeKind.MOVE via `workspace.move_to_path`, and `move_to_path` re-runs capture/reconcile itself (builder_workspace.gd:308-315), so the specifiers self-heal on replay — the only thing missing is the MOVE change ever being recorded. Note that `record_move` resolves identity from the ORIGIN path (builder_ledger.gd:218-230), so it must be called while the ledger's `id_of` callable can still find the module — verify `id_of` is wired (builder_window.gd) and that it is called after the move but with the from-path, exactly as the ledger's comment requires.

**Risk:** Ctrl+Z after a folder re-file produces a tree whose text and whose filesystem plan disagree, and there is no second Ctrl+Z that fixes it because nothing else was recorded. Ctrl+Z after a rename appears to do nothing, so the user presses it again and walks back an unrelated earlier edit.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:3708-3789 (rename as one entry), 3658-3706 (MoveModule records the move and every rewrite); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1684-1686 + 1751-1757 (owner path, no ledger at all), 1697-1713 (general path, rewrites but no record_move), 1897-1914 (rename, no ledger), 2059-2072 (_place_tree_in, same hole).

### `G-03` Journal recovery is never offered, and the first Save of any later session destroys the crashed session's only copy

**Unity does:** OnEnable schedules `EditorApplication.delayCall += OfferJournalRestore` (BuilderWindow.cs:149). OfferJournalRestore returns immediately if a tree is already loaded, TryPeeks the journal, and raises DisplayDialog("Restore unsaved work?", "<N> module(s) from <savedAt> that were never written to disk", "Restore", "Discard"); Discard clears it, Restore adopts the tree, rebinds focus, remounts and toasts "Restored N unsaved module(s)".

**Godot today:** absent at the call site, and actively destructive. The three accessors exist — `pending_recovery()` (builder_window.gd:950-951), `restore_recovery()` (955-962), `discard_recovery()` (964-965) — and `grep -rn "pending_recovery|restore_recovery|discard_recovery"` across the whole repo finds ONLY those definitions and tests/builder_parity.gd:111. Nothing in plugin.gd, `open_tree()` or `_build_ui()` calls any of them. Meanwhile `save()` calls `Journal.clear()` unconditionally at builder_window.gd:1977 and `abort()` at 2081. So: the editor crashes with unsaved work; the journal is on disk at user://ruitk_builder_tree.json; the user reopens the builder, is told nothing, opens some other tree, makes one edit, presses Ctrl+S — and the crashed session's only copy is deleted. builder_journal.gd:41-46 warns about precisely this failure ("Deleting here instead would destroy a crashed session's only copy the moment the user opened the builder on some other file, before anyone was ever asked about it") and the window then does it one function later.

**To build:** Call the offer from `open_tree()` (builder_window.gd:749) after the workspace exists, gated on `workspace.modules().is_empty()` the way Unity gates on Modules.Count == 0. Raise a `ConfirmationDialog` (the pattern `_confirmed_deletions` already uses at builder_window.gd:1998-2020) titled "Restore unsaved work?" naming `pending_recovery()`'s `modules` and `saved_at`, with ok_button_text "Restore" and a Discard path calling `discard_recovery()`. On restore, call `reproject()`, point `_focus_path` at the first module, and toast. Wire it once — a `_offered_recovery` bool so re-opening the same window does not re-ask.

**Godot specifics:** There is no domain reload here, so the ONLY thing the journal protects against is the process dying — which makes the offer the entire point of the feature, not a nicety. `open_tree` is called from plugin.gd:445 and :453 and can be called with an empty focus (the start screen), which is exactly the state Unity gates on. Use `call_deferred` or a one-frame `await` before popping the dialog: `open_tree` runs inside `_open_builder()` before `popup_centered()`, and a modal raised on a Window that is not yet visible does not show. `pending_recovery()` is pure FileAccess so the gating logic stays headlessly testable; only the dialog needs the editor.

**Risk:** The whole crash-recovery subsystem is write-only. Every 5 seconds the builder writes a file nobody will ever read, and the next successful Save deletes it. This is the single feature in this area whose absence loses work that existed.

*critical · feature · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:149 (delayCall += OfferJournalRestore), 6255-6282 (the dialog), 5905-5906 + 6207-6209 (Clear only after the work is saved or deliberately aborted, and only in a session that had already been offered); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:950-966 (uncalled accessors), 1977 + 2081 (unconditional Journal.clear), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_journal.gd:41-46 (the warning it violates). Third leg: ruitk-unreal/.../SRuitkUiBuilderPanel.cpp:264 calls OfferJournalRecovery() at construction, 3324-3358 implements it.

### `G-04` Format-on-save mutates every dirty buffer behind the UI's back: not through the funnel, not in the ledger, no re-projection — so the canvas's row spans are stale and the next canvas edit writes at the wrong offsets

**Unity does:** FormatDirtyBuffers runs BEFORE the save prompts, inside `_ledger.Begin("format on save")`, and for each buffer it changes it calls `session.ApplyEdit(formatted)`, `_ledger.Record(FilePath, before, formatted)`, pushes the text into the focused CodeField, `SyncLspBuffer`, and `_canvasHost?.RefreshGraph(session.FilePath)` — every surface that holds an offset into that buffer is told.

**Godot today:** wrong. `save_all` calls `_format(module)` at builder_workspace.gd:531, and `_format` (builder_workspace.gd:739-752) assigns `module.buffer_text = text` DIRECTLY — bypassing `Module.apply_edit`, bypassing `Workspace.apply_edit`, bypassing the window's `apply_edit` funnel. Nothing is recorded in the ledger. Then `save()` (builder_window.gd:1975-1981) finishes with `Journal.clear(); _capture_layout(); _folders.rebuild(); _refresh_status()` — no `reproject()`, no `_source.refresh_from_model()`, no `_after_model_change`. So after a save that reformatted anything: the source pane still displays the pre-format text, and `graph.cards[*].markup[*].source_line` / the offsets every `Edits.*` call uses still describe the pre-format buffer. builder_window.gd:1456-1459 states the hazard in its own words — "The `Line` the menu was opened on belongs to the old projection and is stale the moment the buffer changes -- editing through it writes at the offsets the row used to have." A right-click-delete-row or an inline edit made after a formatting save splices at those offsets into the reformatted text.

**To build:** Two independent fixes, both needed. (a) Move formatting out of `save_all` into the window, ahead of the write, as a ledger-scoped pass: `ledger.begin("Format on save")`, for each dirty non-read-only module compute the formatted text and route it through `apply_edit(path, formatted, ...)`, `ledger.end()`. Keep `Workspace.format_on_save` as the switch and keep `_format` as a pure helper (`static func formatted(text, options) -> String`) so the model layer stays headlessly testable, but stop it mutating. (b) Regardless, make `save()` end with `reproject()` and `_source.refresh_from_model()` so nothing downstream can hold a stale span — the same two calls `abort()` and `delete_module()` already make.

**Godot specifics:** `Module.apply_edit` (builder_module.gd:256-264) is the read-only and CR guard; `_format` skips both, so a formatter that ever emitted a CR would poison the buffer with no error. The graph is populated by `Service.populate_card(card, module.buffer_text)` (builder_window.gd:890-892) and every row carries `source_line`/offsets computed from that exact string; the reconciler does not re-derive them, so a buffer swap with no re-projection is invisible until the next edit corrupts the file. `_format` already correctly leaves an unparseable buffer alone (builder_workspace.gd:745-747) — keep that.

**Risk:** Silent corruption of the user's file on the FIRST canvas gesture after a save, with no error and no obvious cause. Compounded by the ledger gap: the formatting is not undoable, so a Ctrl+Z after a save replays an entry whose `before`/`after` no longer describe the buffer that is actually there.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:5825-5852 (FormatDirtyBuffers: ApplyEdit + _ledger.Record + SetContent + SyncLspBuffer + RefreshGraph), 5857-5862 (called inside Begin/End before the prompts); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:531 and 739-752 (_format assigns buffer_text directly), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1975-1981 (save() never re-projects), 1456-1459 (the file's own statement of the stale-span hazard).

### `G-05` is_path_available is the disk check Unity replaced: it has neither the pending-move escape (UB-222) nor the orphan escape (UB-172), and the create prompt does not use it at all

**Unity does:** IsPathAvailable is THE one availability rule, answered by the TREE not the disk, in four steps: empty -> false; a live module claims it -> false; no file there -> true; a file IS there but true anyway if either some module HasMoved and its DiskPath canonicalises to this path (Save vacates it first) or the path is in OrphanedPaths() ("which is exactly why SaveAll clears dead paths before it writes"). The name prompt's live validation, the creation guard, CreateNew and the relocation plan all ask this one function so they cannot disagree.

**Godot today:** partial and inconsistent. `is_path_available` (builder_workspace.gd:101-105) is three lines: `_tree.by_path(full) == null and not FileAccess.file_exists(full)`. Steps (4a) and (4b) are both missing, so: delete a module and try to re-create one at the same name — the tree no longer claims it (correct, deletion is absence) but the file is still on disk until Save, so `create_new` returns null. That is UB-172 verbatim. Move a module away and back before saving — the old copy is still at the origin, so any create at that path is refused, and no amount of retrying clears it because only Save can. That is UB-222 verbatim. And the failure is SILENT: `_validate_name` (builder_window.gd:1787-1815) does not call `is_path_available` at all — it asks `workspace.try_get(...)` (the tree only, line 1809), so validation PASSES, the prompt closes, `_create_named` (builder_window.gd:1885-1887) gets null back from `create_new` and returns "" with no toast, no console line, nothing.

**To build:** Add the two escapes to `is_path_available`: iterate `_tree.modules()` for any module where `has_moved()` and `Paths.same(module.disk_path, full)` -> true; and check `full` against `_tree.orphaned_paths()` -> true. Then replace `_validate_name`'s line 1809 tree lookup with `workspace.is_path_available(target)`, so the prompt, the guard and CreateNew share one answer. Add a toast on the null branch of `_create_named` ("Could not create %s (already exists)") so a refusal is never silent again.

**Godot specifics:** `orphaned_paths()` (builder_tree.gd:178-187) already exists and `save_all` already retires orphans before it writes (builder_workspace.gd:491-499), so escape (4b) is already SOUND here — only the query is missing. Keep the whole thing on `Paths.key()` (case-folded) comparisons, which is what `by_path` and `orphaned_paths` already use; mixing a case-sensitive compare in would reopen the duplicate-module hole `load_tree` guards against at builder_workspace.gd:160-162. All of this is FileAccess-only, so it belongs in tests/builder_model_test.gd, not the chrome suite.

**Risk:** Delete a component, realise you wanted it after all, try to create it again at the same name — the builder does nothing at all, with no message. The user has no way to learn that the answer is "save first".

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWorkspace.cs:60-95 (the four steps and the two escapes), BuilderWindow.cs:6144-6148 (ValidateNewName asks IsPathAvailable), UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md UB-172 and UB-222; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:101-105 (three lines, no escapes), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1809 (validation asks try_get, not is_path_available), 1885-1887 (silent null). Third leg: ruitk-unreal/.../RuitkUiBuilderWorkspace.cpp:229-245 keeps the disk check and documents why.

### `G-06` A rename has no collision check anywhere, and Save's DirAccess.rename_absolute overwrites the destination

**Unity does:** RenameModule refuses before it starts, with Toast("<newName> already exists"), when `File.Exists(newFull) || TryGet(newFull) != null || (ownsFolder && Directory.Exists(newDir))` — a check the inventory notes is strictly STRICTER than IsPathAvailable.

**Godot today:** absent. `_rename_to` (builder_window.gd:1897-1914) checks only that the module exists and is not read-only, then calls `workspace.move_to`, which calls `_tree.move_to` (builder_tree.gd:111-139) unconditionally — no path check, no directory check. `_validate_name` cannot cover for it because it validates the wrong path (G-07). So the tree can end up with two modules whose `file_path()` is identical; `_reindex` (builder_tree.gd:209-221) keys `_by_path` by that path, so one of them silently disappears from every lookup, and `validate()` would report "two modules claim <path>" — if anything called it (G-18). At Save, `_move_on_disk` (builder_workspace.gd:614-624) calls `DirAccess.rename_absolute(from, to)`; Godot's DirAccess removes an existing destination first on Windows and `::rename()` overwrites it on Unix. A file the builder does not own, sitting at the target path, is destroyed. The same hole is in `place_module` (builder_window.gd:1725-1749, only `Paths.same(module.folder, target_folder)`) and `move_folder` (builder_window.gd:1668-1717, only the move-into-itself guard at 1679).

**To build:** Introduce the missing `rename_target_path(full, old_name, new_name) -> { path, dir, owns_folder }` helper (Unity's RenameTargetPath, BuilderWindow.cs:6155-6180) so the prompt and the rename compute the same thing, and refuse in `_rename_to` when `not workspace.is_path_available(target)` or, for a folder-owning rename, when `DirAccess.dir_exists_absolute(new_dir)` and no module in the tree owns it. Add the same target check to `place_module` and to `move_folder`'s destination, matching `_place_tree_in`, which is the ONE move path that already does it correctly (builder_window.gd:2052-2056).

**Godot specifics:** `owns_folder()` (builder_module.gd:113-118) is the test for whether the folder travels; compute it BEFORE mutating, as `_tree.move_to` already does at line 115. `DirAccess.dir_exists_absolute` is available headlessly, so the refusal is testable in tests/builder_edits_test.gd or builder_save_test.gd without an editor. Note that once G-05's escapes are in, `is_path_available` correctly answers "available" for a path this same module has pending-vacated, which is the behaviour a rename-back needs.

**Risk:** Silent destruction of a file outside the tree at Save time, and a tree that holds two modules at one path with one of them unreachable through every lookup in the builder.

*high · risk · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:3714-3720 (the refusal), 6155-6180 (RenameTargetPath); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1897-1914 (no check), 1725-1749 (place_module, no check), 1668-1717 (move_folder, no destination check), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:614-624 (_move_on_disk overwrites).

### `G-07` _validate_name validates the wrong path on a rename, and never says "that is the current name"

**Unity does:** The rename prompt validates with `ValidateNewName(kind, name, n => RenameTargetPath(full, oldName, n, out _, out _))` — the SAME mapping RenameModule uses, "shared with RenameModule so the prompt and the rename can never disagree about what a name would produce" (UB-145). Before that it refuses `Equals(name, oldName, Ordinal)` with "that is the current name".

**Godot today:** wrong. The rename prompt (builder_window.gd:2225-2227) passes `func(name): return _validate_name(current.kind, name)`, and `_validate_name` derives its target from `_create_folder(kind, name)` (builder_window.gd:1808) — the CREATE birth-folder function. On a rename `_menu_target` is the card being renamed, so for a COMPONENT `_create_folder` returns `parent.folder/components/<NewName>` (builder_window.gd:1876-1878) — a path that by construction never exists. The file-collision arm of validation is therefore dead for every component rename; only the tree-wide component-uniqueness arm (builder_window.gd:1811-1814) still bites. Companion renames pass by accident, because `_create_folder` happens to return `parent.folder` for a non-component (line 1873). And there is no current-name refusal: renaming to the unchanged name reaches the try_get arm and reports the misleading "<name> already exists".

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One detail of the reasoning is off, and the truth is worse than stated. For a COMPONENT rename the analysis is exactly right: `_menu_target` is the module itself, so `_create_folder` returns `<its own folder>/components/<NewName>`, a path that by construction never exists, and the file-collision arm is dead. But for a COMPANION rename it does NOT "pass by accident because `_create_folder` returns parent.folder" -- the guard at builder_window.gd:1865-1866 fires first (`parent.kind != COMPONENT` for the style/hook module being renamed), so `_create_folder` returns `tree_root()` and the collision check is aimed at the TREE ROOT, a folder the companion does not even live in. So the arm is dead for both kinds, not just components.

**To build:** Add `rename_target_path()` (see G-06) and give `_validate_name` a `target_path_for: Callable` parameter the way Unity's third argument works, so the create prompt passes the birth-path function and the rename prompt passes the rename mapping. Add the `name == current.name -> "that is the current name"` arm to the rename prompt's validator lambda.

**Godot specifics:** Both prompts already go through `SearchMenu.open_name_prompt(title, placeholder, validate, at, initial)` (builder_search_menu.gd:109-122), which keeps the popup open and writes the reason into the inline error label (builder_search_menu.gd:196-207) — so this is a pure change of what the validator computes, with no UI work. Keep it a plain function on the window so tests/builder_chrome_test.gd can call `w._validate_name(...)` directly, which is how the existing coverage at tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:442-443 works.

**Risk:** A rename that collides is accepted by the prompt and then either overwrites (G-06) or produces two modules at one path. The unchanged-name case gives the user a message that is simply untrue.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:3618-3644 (ShowRenamePrompt, current-name refusal and the shared mapping), 6115-6157 (ValidateNewName's targetPathFor parameter), UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md UB-145; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:2225-2227 (prompt), 1787-1815 (_validate_name), 1861-1878 (_create_folder, the create mapping it wrongly reuses).

### `G-08` Name validation enforces Unity's PascalCase/camelCase/useX on the FILE basename, which contradicts this leg's snake_case convention — and the hook prompt's own default name fails its own validator

**Unity does:** ValidateNewName's casing rules exist because in the Unity leg the FILE name and the exported identifier are the same string: `NewComponent.uitkx` exports `NewComponent`, `newComponent.style.uitkx` exports `newComponent`, `useNewComponent.hooks.uitkx` exports `useNewComponent`. BuilderNaming.FamilyOf strips a leading `use` followed by an upper-case letter for exactly that reason (the `useful` trap is explicitly tested).

**Godot today:** wrong, and internally contradictory. `_validate_name` (builder_window.gd:1790-1797) copies Unity's three regexes verbatim: `^use[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$` for hooks, `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$` for components, `^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$` for style/util. But this leg's file convention is snake_case — every file in examples/ is `bailout_child.guitkx`, `doom_game_screen.hooks.guitkx` — builder_naming.gd:11-17 documents the family name as "simply the file BASENAME" and strips `use_` (snake), builder_edits.gd:900-909 exists solely because "a component declaration must be PascalCase (GUITKX2100) but the FILE it lives in is snake_case by this leg's convention", and the compiler detects a hook by `name.begins_with("use_")` (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit/guitkx/guitkx.gd:531, 1831). Consequences that are trivially reproducible: (a) creating a component named `left_panel` — the spelling of every existing file in the repo — is REFUSED with "PascalCase identifier required"; (b) `Module.default_name_for(Kind.HOOK)` returns "newHook" (builder_module.gd:144-146), which the prompt seeds into the field and which its own validator then rejects with "hook names start with 'use' (useSomething)" — pressing Enter on the default is an error; (c) once the user complies and types `useThing`, `Edits.template_for` emits `export use_%s()` (builder_edits.gd:886) producing the declaration `use_useThing`, and `Naming.family_of(HOOK, "useThing")` does not strip anything (builder_naming.gd:39-42) so the hook is not in its component's family at all.

**To build:** Pick one convention and make the four places agree. The leg's convention is snake_case files, so: replace the three regexes with `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` for every kind, plus `begins_with("use_")` for hooks; change `default_name_for(HOOK)` to `use_new_hook`, `STYLE` to `new_style`, `UTIL` to `new_util`, `COMPONENT` to `new_component`; change `template_for(HOOK, name)` to emit `export %s()` when `name` already begins `use_` and `export use_%s()` otherwise; keep `_pascal()` for the component declaration so `left_panel.guitkx` declares `export LeftPanel()`. Then update the placeholder strings and the error messages to name the real rule.

**Godot specifics:** The messages surface in `SearchMenu`'s inline error label, so no UI change is needed. The regexes are built with `RegEx.create_from_string` on every keystroke (builder_window.gd:1791, 1794, 1797) — hoist them to `static var` on this hand-written `@tool` script (safe here; it would NOT be safe in a generated .gd, which carries no `@tool` and whose static initialisers Godot never runs in the editor — the same hazard canvas_palette.gd exists to dodge). Existing tests will need updating: tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:442-443 asserts `_validate_name(COMPONENT, "Fresh") == ""`.

**Risk:** The builder refuses the naming convention of the project it edits, and its own hook default is un-submittable. A user who works around it produces `use_useThing` declarations and hook files that fall out of their component's family.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:6115-6157 (the three regexes, where file name == export name), Builder/Editor/Document/BuilderNaming.cs:22-41 (the `use` + upper strip); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1790-1797, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_module.gd:143-154 (default_name_for), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_edits.gd:884-894 (template_for), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_naming.gd:11-17 + 37-43, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit/guitkx/guitkx.gd:531 + 1831 (the compiler's `use_` rule), examples/demos/doom/doom_game_screen.hooks.guitkx (the convention in practice).

### `G-09` Delete REFUSES while a module is imported instead of stripping the references — Unity's removed behaviour, reintroduced and blessed by both the capability doc and the parity gate

**Unity does:** OnDeleteFile does NOT refuse. It guards read-only (naming the DIRECTORY, UB-164), guards missing, then `_ledger.Begin("delete <file>")`, `StripReferencesTo(full)` — which walks every other module, resolves each through EditSession so an UNOPENED importer is still reached, drops the import line and every brace-valued attribute reading a name that import bound — `_ledger.RecordDeletion(full, module)`, `_workspace.Delete(full)`, `_ledger.End()`, then toasts "Deleted <file> - applies on Save", RebindFocusIfMissing, RefreshChrome, MountCanvas. The refusal was removed deliberately: it "left the user to unpick every import by hand first - and since an import row had no delete of its own, a child component could not be removed at all."

**Godot today:** wrong, and confidently so. `delete_module` (builder_window.gd:2414-2440) calls `referrers_to(file_path)` and, when non-empty, toasts "Can't delete X — still imported by Y" and returns false. Its doc comment at builder_window.gd:2408-2413 cites "(capability reference §2)" and argues the refusal is the better answer — but the capability doc's line 52 is STALE relative to the Unity source it is supposed to describe (the source at BuilderWindow.cs:836-862 strips and deletes), and CLAUDE.md is explicit that the source is the reference and the plan is not. There is no `strip_references_to` / `remove_import_of` anywhere under builder/. Practical effect: in the house layout a parent component imports its children, so no child component can ever be deleted from the canvas — the primary tree-editing gesture is unreachable for exactly the modules a user most wants to remove. The read-only guard is also weaker: `delete_module` returns false silently for a read-only module (line 2418) where Unity toasts and names the directory (UB-164).

**To build:** Port StripReferencesTo/RemoveImportOf into builder/edits/builder_edits.gd as pure functions (`strip_references_to(source, importer_path, target_path) -> String`), built on the existing `Specifiers.imports_of` + `Specifiers.map` pair that `capture_imports` already uses (builder_workspace.gd:341-364) and the existing `Edits.remove_import` (builder_edits.gd:460). Rewrite `delete_module` to: read-only -> toast naming `file_path.get_base_dir()`; missing -> toast "Nothing to delete at X"; then `ledger.begin`, apply_edit each stripped importer through the funnel, `ledger.record_deletion(path, module)`, `workspace.delete(path)`, `ledger.end()`, toast "Deleted X — applies on Save", rebind focus, `reproject()`. Then fix the capability doc line 52 and the parity gate entry (G-19).

**Godot specifics:** Unity walks its CANVAS nodes and resolves through EditSession; here the whole tree is already in memory, so walk `workspace.modules()` directly — that is strictly better and avoids Unity's own "importers not already open were skipped" bug (UB-135). Route every importer rewrite through `builder_window.apply_edit()` so all of them land in the one open ledger scope (nested begin/end collapse, builder_ledger.gd:139-160) and each gets its `_after_model_change` re-projection. The attribute-stripping regex Unity uses only matches a brace value on one line; keep that limitation and say so, rather than inventing a multi-line matcher.

**Risk:** A child component cannot be deleted at all. The user's only route is to hand-edit every importer in the source pane first, which is the exact workflow UB-88's fix removed.

*high · feature · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:836-862 (OnDeleteFile: strips, records, deletes, toasts), 1574-1607 (StripReferencesTo), 1609-1673 (RemoveImportOf), UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md UB-88/UB-164; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:2405-2440 (delete_module refuses), 2387-2404 (referrers_to), tests/builder_parity.gd:41 (the gate encodes the wrong behaviour as the requirement), ruitk-unity/plans/UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:52 (the stale line the comment cites).

### `G-10` Birth path drops the house layout: a root-level create lands flat in the tree root, and the first module of a new tree does not own its folder

**Unity does:** BirthPathFor: no focus file -> `PathFor(UnsavedRoot, kind, name, asRoot: true)` = `<root>/<Name>/<Name>.uitkx` — the first component OWNS ITS OWN FOLDER. Otherwise root = ResolveRoot(...) and a Component -> `PathFor(root, kind, name)` = `root/components/<Name>/<Name>.uitkx`. With a parent from the card menu -> `parent/components/<Name>/<Name>.uitkx` for a component, `parent/<name>.<suffix>` for a companion. The house layout is stated in PathFor's own doc comment.

**Godot today:** partial. `_create_folder` (builder_window.gd:1861-1878) gets the card-menu case right — `parent.folder/components/<name>` for a component, `parent.folder` for a companion — but every other route returns `tree_root()` BARE. `tree_root()` (builder_window.gd:1816-1832) is the shallowest module folder, or `UNSAVED_ROOT` when the tree is empty. So: a canvas right-click on empty space (the primary create gesture, `_menu_target` cleared at builder_window.gd:711) puts a new component at `<root>/<Name>.guitkx`, a sibling of the root component rather than a child under `components/`; and the first module of a start-screen tree lands at `res://__ruitk_builder_unsaved__~/Fresh.guitkx`, not `.../Fresh/Fresh.guitkx`. tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:457-458 asserts the flat form and the placed result at `PLACED_ROOT/Fresh.guitkx` — the divergence is pinned by the suite. The knock-on is real: a component that does not sit in a folder named after it returns false from `owns_folder()` (builder_module.gd:113-118), so `BuilderTree.resolve_root_from` cannot find it (builder_tree.gd:296-303), `move_to` will not carry a subtree for it (builder_tree.gd:121), and a later rename cannot take its folder with it.

**To build:** In `_create_folder`, for a COMPONENT with no parent card: return `tree_root().path_join("components").path_join(name)` when the tree is non-empty, and `UNSAVED_ROOT.path_join(name)` (as-root, no `components/` level) when it is empty — mirroring Unity's asRoot flag. Leave the companion arm alone; a companion belongs beside its component. Keep `tree_root()` as-is; the bug is in what `_create_folder` does with it, not in the root resolution.

**Godot specifics:** `Paths.COMPONENTS_FOLDER` already exists and `_resolve_root_core` (builder_tree.gd:318-346) already understands `components/` as a nesting level only when it sits inside a folder that owns a module — so producing the house layout makes the root walk work rather than fighting it. The change is one function and is covered headlessly: tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:426-465 already drives the whole start-screen-to-placed-tree path and only needs its two path assertions updated.

**Risk:** Every tree the builder creates from scratch has a shape the rest of the builder does not recognise — no folder ownership, so renames and re-files silently stop carrying subtrees, and the root walk cannot find the root.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:5942-5990 (BirthPathFor), Builder/Editor/BuilderNewFileDialog.cs:21-53 (PathFor and the house-layout doc comment), UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md UB-207; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1861-1878 (_create_folder), 1816-1832 (tree_root), tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:446-459 (the flat shape asserted).

### `G-11` The card layout is never repathed on a rename, a re-file or an abort — and the one repath that is called is thrown away by the very next line

**Unity does:** MoveModule is "the view's half of the same move": it captures fromDir and ownsFolder BEFORE the move, then RepathLayout(fromDir, toDir, isFolder: true) + RepointFocus for a folder-owning module, then RepathLayout(from, to, isFolder: false), and re-points _focusFile. RepathLayout writes the layout config to disk IMMEDIATELY, with the stated reason: "the canvas remounts straight after a rename and reloads the config from disk, so an in-memory re-keying alone would be thrown away" (UB-140). AbortAll repaths every module that had moved, in reverse.

**Godot today:** wrong. `layout.repath()` exists and is correct (builder_canvas_layout.gd:180-206) but has exactly ONE caller: `move_folder`'s general path (builder_window.gd:1707). `_rename_to`, `place_module`/`_move_one`, `_place_tree_in` and `abort()` never call it. Worse, the one call that exists is immediately discarded: `move_folder` finishes with `reproject()` (builder_window.gd:1714), and `reproject()`'s second line is `layout = CanvasLayout.for_graph(graph)` (builder_window.gd:824), which re-reads the layout from `user://ruitk_builder/layouts/*.json` (builder_canvas_layout.gd:100-110). The in-memory re-keying is gone before it is ever saved — `layout.save()` is only reached through `_capture_layout()` from `_on_card_moved` and from `save()` (builder_window.gd:1033, 1978). And because `_capture_layout` writes `capture_from(graph, ...)` — the cards' CURRENT coordinates, which by then are the re-seeded ones — the next Save persists the reshuffle permanently.

**To build:** Call `layout.repath(old, new, is_folder)` followed by `_capture_layout()` (or a narrower `layout.save(...)`) BEFORE `reproject()` in `_rename_to`, `_move_one`, `move_folder` and `_place_tree_in`; and in `abort()`, capture the `has_moved()` set before `workspace.abort_all()` and repath each one back afterwards. Also re-point `_focus_path` for a folder-owning move the way `move_folder` already does per-module at builder_window.gd:1708-1709 but `_move_one` and `_rename_to` do not.

**Godot specifics:** `for_graph` resolves by MEMBERSHIP first and by root second (builder_canvas_layout.gd:100-110), so a folder-owning rename changes every member path AND the root file name at once — which is exactly the case builder_canvas_layout.gd:174-179 says the repath exists to handle, and exactly the case that currently loses the whole layout (overlap drops to zero, `load_for_root` misses the renamed key, a fresh Self.new() is returned). The layout store is `user://` state, deliberately outside the save-only contract, so writing it immediately is correct here — same justification as `_on_card_moved`.

**Risk:** Renaming or re-filing a module reshuffles the canvas the user arranged, and a folder-owning rename discards the arrangement entirely. The next Save writes the reshuffle down, so it is not recoverable.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:3658-3706 (MoveModule, both RepathLayout calls and RepointFocus), 6199-6228 (AbortAll repaths back), Builder/Editor/Canvas/BuilderCanvasHost.cs:934-946 (RepathLayout writes at once), UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md UB-140; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_canvas_layout.gd:180-206 (repath, one caller), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1707 (the only call), 824 (reproject re-reads from disk and discards it), 1897-1914 / 1751-1757 / 2042-2074 / 2076-2087 (the four paths that never repath).

### `G-12` A new card has no placement: the right-click world point is captured and thrown away, and nothing frames the module that was just created

**Unity does:** CreateModule seeds the layout slot BEFORE the card is built: PlaceNewCardUnder(full, parent.FilePath) with a parent, else PlaceNewCard(full, worldX, worldY). PlaceNewCard centres the card on the cursor on BOTH axes (`x - cardWidth*0.5, y - NewCardHeight*0.5`, NewCardHeight = 200) after UB-195/UB-200 found that a top-left placement put the card down-and-right of the pointer; with (0,0) — the library "+ new" and the empty-state buttons — it uses the viewport centre instead. PlaceNewCardUnder lays siblings out 40px apart on a row 48px below the parent's estimated bottom, advancing past anything Occupied (UB-212).

**Godot today:** absent. `_menu_world` is assigned on both canvas contexts (builder_window.gd:704, 707) and read NOWHERE — `grep -n "_menu_world"` returns the declaration and the two writes. `_create_named` (builder_window.gd:1879-1895) never touches the layout; the new card gets whatever `Service.seed_positions` gives it, which for an unwired module is "a column of its OWN past the deepest reachable one" (builder_graph_service.gd:1006-1010) — potentially far off screen. `select_module` (builder_window.gd:2151-2175) points the source pane, folder pane, library and preview at the new module but never scrolls or frames the canvas; `_canvas.frame_card` exists and is used only by `_on_library_framed` (builder_window.gd:543).

**To build:** Add `place_new_card(file_path, world: Vector2)` and `place_new_card_under(file_path, parent_path)` on the window (or on CanvasHost, beside `frame_card`), each calling the existing `layout.set_position(...)` (builder_canvas_layout.gd:168-169) before `reproject()` so `apply_to` picks the slot up and `adopt_unplaced` does not overwrite it. Call them from `_create_named` using `_menu_world` when it is non-zero and the viewport centre otherwise, and using the parent when `_menu_target` names a component. Failing that, at minimum call `_canvas.frame_card(graph.index_of(path))` after creating, so the user is taken to the module that appeared.

**Godot specifics:** Ordering matters: `reproject()` rebuilds `layout` from disk (builder_canvas_layout.gd:100-110) and then calls `apply_to` then `adopt_unplaced`, so the seed must be written into the layout FILE (via `_capture_layout()`) or set on the freshly loaded object after `for_graph` — setting it on the pre-reproject object is discarded, the same trap as G-11. Card width comes from `Metrics.card_width_for(lod)` (builder_canvas_metrics.gd), which is the one metrics definition every consumer shares here — so the centring maths has a single source, unlike Unity's two disagreeing LOD definitions.

**Risk:** Creating a module from the canvas produces a card the user cannot find. Combined with G-13 (no toast naming the folder) the create gesture can be indistinguishable from nothing happening.

*medium · gesture · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderCanvasHost.cs:524-556 (PlaceNewCard), 558-561 (NewCardHeight), 563-606 (PlaceNewCardUnder + Occupied), BuilderWindow.cs:6069-6112 (the seed happens inside CreateModule), UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md UB-195/UB-200/UB-212; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:133 + 704 + 707 (_menu_world, written and never read), 1879-1895 (_create_named, no layout seed), 2151-2175 (select_module, no framing), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:1006-1010 (where a new card actually lands). Third leg: ruitk-unreal/.../SRuitkUiBuilderCanvas.cpp:464 PlaceNewCard, called from SRuitkUiBuilderPanel.cpp:845.

### `G-13` No mutating operation confirms itself: create, rename, delete, save and abort are all silent, and "applies on Save" appears only on moves

**Unity does:** Every mutating toast ends with "- applies on Save": "Created <file> in <folderLeaf> - applies on Save" (the folder is named because "the convention can put a module somewhere other than where the user is looking... A file that appears silently in a folder you are not in is the same as a file that did not appear", UB-187), "Deleted <file> - applies on Save", "Renamed to <new> - applies on Save", "Moved... - applies on Save". Save toasts "Saved N file(s)"; Abort toasts "Discarded N buffer(s)"; a failed create toasts "Could not create <name> (already exists)".

**Godot today:** partial. `grep -n "toast("` over builder_window.gd finds 14 call sites and every one of them is a REFUSAL or a move. "Moved %s — applies on Save" appears twice (builder_window.gd:1716, 1756). There is no success toast for create (`_create_named`, 1879-1895), rename (`_rename_to`, 1897-1914), delete (`delete_module`'s success path, 2429-2439), save (`save()`, 1975-1981) or abort (`abort()`, 2076-2087) — and `save()`/`abort()` both return a count that no caller displays (`run_command` at builder_window.gd:995-1000 discards it). The failed-create branch is silent too (G-05).

**To build:** Add the five success toasts, and give the create toast the folder leaf Unity gives it — `"Created %s in %s — applies on Save" % [path.get_file(), folder.get_file()]` — since G-10's fix will put a component in `components/<Name>/`, which is emphatically not where the user right-clicked. Have `run_command(MenuId.SAVE)` and `(MenuId.ABORT)` toast the returned count. The toast machinery already exists (builder_window.gd:196-224, `toast_text()` accessor at 2442 for tests).

**Godot specifics:** `toast()` is already the single surface and is already asserted on in the suites through `toast_text()`, so each new toast is one line plus one assertion. Note `save()` can return 0 legitimately (nothing to write) and 0 after raising the placement dialog (builder_window.gd:1960-1962) — the toast must distinguish those, or the user gets "Saved 0 file(s)" where Unity would have said nothing and left the folder dialog up.

**Risk:** The two flows that produce no visible change on screen — a create that lands in a folder the user is not looking at, and a save — both produce no feedback at all, so the user cannot tell success from silent refusal.

### `G-14` The family / nearest-owner placement rule is written, tested, and wired to nothing — builder_naming.gd is dead code in production

**Unity does:** FamilyOwnerFor(kind, name) decides where a new COMPANION is born: it maps the prompt kind, returns null for a Util, scans the workspace for Components where SameFamily(kind, name, Component, module.Name), scores each by BuilderNaming.SharedPrefixLength(focusDir, module.Folder), keeps the highest and breaks an exact tie by ordinal-smallest FilePath "so the answer does not depend on the order the tree was loaded in". BirthPathFor then uses `FamilyOwnerFor(kind,name)?.Folder ?? root` for a companion. UB-187 exists because placement previously used "next to whatever is focused".

**Godot today:** absent from every code path. `addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_naming.gd` implements `family_of`, `same_family` and `shared_prefix_length` correctly and with good reasoning (segments not characters, at builder_naming.gd:57-63). `grep -rn "builder_naming|RuitkBuilderNaming|family_of|same_family|shared_prefix_length" --include=*.gd .` returns the file itself and tests/builder_model_test.gd:18 + 519-555. No production caller. `_create_folder` (builder_window.gd:1861-1878) decides a companion's home as `parent.folder` when a card was right-clicked and `tree_root()` otherwise — never by family, never by nearest owner. So a companion created from the canvas or the library lands at the tree root regardless of which component it is named for, and `Card/card.style.guitkx` + `Panel/card.style.guitkx` coexisting (the case the family rule is for) cannot be produced.

**To build:** Add `family_owner_for(kind, name) -> Module` to the window: return null for UTIL; scan `workspace.modules()` for `module.kind == Kind.COMPONENT and Naming.same_family(kind, name, Kind.COMPONENT, module.name)`; score by `Naming.shared_prefix_length(_focus_path.get_base_dir(), module.folder)`; tie-break by ordinal-smallest `module.file_path()`. Use it in `_create_folder`'s companion arm: `family_owner_for(kind, name).folder if found else tree_root()`. Note this makes `_create_folder` depend on the NAME, which it already takes as a parameter.

**Godot specifics:** Reference builder_naming.gd through a preload const like every other builder file (the class-cache hazard: `ProjectSettings.save()` truncates the editor class cache to what the running process loaded, so `RuitkBuilderNaming` as a global name is not safe from editor code). This is pure model logic, so the case belongs in tests/builder_model_test.gd beside the existing family tests rather than in the chrome suite. Godot's `family_of` strips `use_` (snake) — see G-08; whatever convention is settled there must be the one this scan uses, or the family match silently never fires for hooks.

**Risk:** A whole module exists, is documented at length, is covered by six test assertions, and does nothing. The parity sweep's own preamble names this exact failure class — "a mechanism that already existed with nothing wired to it" — and this is one more instance of it that the sweep does not list.

*medium · hollow-gate · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:5992-6028 (FamilyOwnerFor), Builder/Editor/Document/BuilderNaming.cs:22-73, UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md UB-187; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_naming.gd:1-75 (whole file, no production caller), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1861-1878 (_create_folder decides placement without it), tests/builder_model_test.gd:519-555 (the only consumers).

### `G-15` An empty module is skipped with a console warning where Unity stops and asks a three-way question

**Unity does:** ResolveEmptyModules runs before the deletion prompt and before the write. It collects every non-read-only, non-unlocated module whose buffer is whitespace, then raises DisplayDialogComplex("Empty module(s)", listing each file, "A .uitkx with no declaration does not compile, so saving one breaks the project until it is filled in or removed") with three answers: "Delete them" (ledger entry, StripReferencesTo each, RecordDeletion, Delete, rebind, remount), "Cancel save" (toast "Save cancelled", return false), "Save anyway" (return true and write them). UB-206: the owner hit this via a style module whose last export went away — the card still showed the export, Save wrote 0 bytes, and the file then failed to compile with nothing naming the cause.

**Godot today:** partial. `save()` (builder_window.gd:1969-1974) loops `workspace.blank_modules()` and pushes one console diagnostic per blank — "empty, so it was not written -- delete it, or give it something to hold" — then saves everything else; `save_all` independently skips them at builder_workspace.gd:517-522. So the module is never written and never deletable from that dialog, the user is not asked, and there is no "save anyway". Because the module stays dirty forever, `has_unsaved_changes()` stays true, the Save/Abort buttons stay enabled (builder_window.gd:2468-2469), and `_journal_tick` keeps writing the journal indefinitely — the tree can never reach a clean state until the user finds the console line and acts on it.

**To build:** Replace the console-warning loop with a dialog raised BEFORE `_confirmed_deletions()`, modelled on `_confirmed_deletions` itself (builder_window.gd:1989-2022): a ConfirmationDialog listing each blank path, ok_button_text "Delete them", plus a custom "Save anyway" button via `add_button("Save anyway", true, "anyway")` and the default Cancel. Delete-them routes each through `delete_module` (which after G-09 strips references) inside one ledger scope; save-anyway sets a one-pass flag `_blanks_agreed` that `save_all` consults, mirroring `_deletions_agreed`. Keep the console diagnostic as well — it is genuinely useful and Unity has no equivalent.

**Godot specifics:** `blank_modules()` (builder_workspace.gd:723-731) already exists and correctly excludes read-only, but unlike Unity it does NOT exclude unlocated modules — a start-screen module with an empty style template would appear in both prompts. Add the `is_unlocated` exclusion. The save-anyway path needs a corresponding skip-the-skip in `save_all` (builder_workspace.gd:517-522), which is currently unconditional; make it a `var write_blanks := false` on the workspace so the model stays headlessly testable.

**Risk:** An emptied module silently never saves, and the tree can never be made clean. The user's only signal is a console line they must think to open.

*medium · feature · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:5760-5817 (ResolveEmptyModules, the three-way dialog), 5857-5862 (called before the deletion prompt), UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md UB-206; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1969-1974 (console warning only), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:517-522 (unconditional skip), 723-731 (blank_modules, no unlocated exclusion).

### `G-16` No RebindFocusIfMissing: _focus_path dangles after a delete, an abort or a placement

**Unity does:** RebindFocusIfMissing is called after every operation that can remove the focused module from the tree — OnDeleteFile, AbortAll, ResolveEmptyModules' delete branch, OfferJournalRestore — so the focus always names something that exists.

**Godot today:** absent. `grep -n "rebind"` over builder_window.gd returns nothing. `_focus_path` is assigned at builder_window.gd:770 (open_tree), 1653 (_on_card_new), 1709 (move_folder), 2067 (_place_tree_in) and 2156 (select_module) and is never re-derived when the module it names leaves. `delete_module` (builder_window.gd:2414-2440) does not touch it; `abort()` (2076-2087) does not; `abort_all` re-loads the tree so a module created this session is simply gone. Downstream: `_refresh_status` (builder_window.gd:2459) prints the dead file's name in the status bar; `_delete_selection`'s fallback `delete_module(_focus_path)` (builder_window.gd:279) returns false in silence; `select_module` is never re-run so the source pane and preview keep showing the removed module.

**To build:** Add `_rebind_focus_if_missing()`: if `_focus_path` is empty or `workspace.try_get(_focus_path) == null`, pick the first module in `workspace.modules()` (or "" for an empty tree) and call `select_module` on it. Call it from `delete_module`, `abort()`, and after `restore_recovery()` — the same three places Unity does.

**Godot specifics:** `select_module` is re-entrancy guarded by `_choosing` (builder_window.gd:2154, 2178) so calling it from inside a reaction is safe. It also drives the preview compile and the source pane, so rebinding is the one call that fixes every surface at once. Handle the empty-tree case explicitly: `select_module` returns early on an empty path (line 2153), so the panes must be cleared some other way — `_sync_empty_state()` (builder_window.gd:815) already exists for that and `reproject()` calls it.

**Risk:** After deleting the module you were looking at, the status bar, the source pane and the preview all keep showing it, and the next Delete keypress does nothing with no explanation.

*medium · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:858 (after delete), 6222 (after abort), 5813 (after the empty-module delete), 6279 (after restore); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd — no `rebind` identifier anywhere; 2414-2440 (delete_module), 2076-2087 (abort), 269-280 (_delete_selection's dangling fallback), 2446-2460 (_refresh_status prints the dead name).

### `G-17` Style and util templates invent an export the user did not ask for — UB-112's decision reversed

**Unity does:** TemplateFor: "Style"|"Utils" -> the EMPTY STRING. "Hooks" and "Component" emit only the export the user just named, with the smallest legal body. UB-112, owner: "we should only export what the user add". The old templates invented members nobody asked for — a `nameRoot` for a style, a `nameText` for a util — that the user had to delete. Exports for style/util are then named one at a time through the card's "+ style" / "+ entry" affordances.

**Godot today:** divergent, undeclared. `Edits.template_for` (builder_edits.gd:884-894) emits, for STYLE and VALUE, `export <name> := {\n\t"bg_color": Color(0.2, 0.2, 0.24),\n}\n` — an invented `bg_color` entry — and for UTIL `export <name>() -> Variant { return null }`. Neither is listed among the deliberate divergences in CLAUDE.md or tests/builder_parity.gd's DELIBERATE table. There is a real engine-side tension behind it: `save_all` refuses to write a blank module (builder_workspace.gd:517-522) and `blank_modules()` surfaces it, so a genuinely empty template would produce a module that can never be saved — which is Unity's situation too, resolved there by the three-way empty-module dialog this leg does not have (G-15).

**To build:** Decide and record. Either (a) match Unity — empty templates for STYLE/UTIL/VALUE — and land G-15's dialog first so an empty module has a route to being written or deleted; or (b) keep a seeded entry and add the divergence to CLAUDE.md's list with the blank-module argument as its stated reason. Do not leave it undeclared: an unrecorded divergence is indistinguishable from a port that did not read the reference.

**Godot specifics:** If (a), `_is_blank` (builder_workspace.gd:734-735) and `blank_modules` become the primary path for every newly created style module rather than an edge case, so G-15's dialog stops being optional. If (b), the seeded key should at least come from the schema (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/lsp/guitkx_schema.gd, already preloaded by the window) rather than a hard-coded `bg_color`, so the invention is at least a real StyleBoxFlat property name.

**Risk:** Low functional risk, but it is the specific complaint UB-112 records from the owner, reproduced. And it is the kind of undeclared difference that makes the rest of the divergence list untrustworthy.

*medium · feature · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderNewFileDialog.cs:55-79 (TemplateFor, empty for Style/Utils), UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md UB-112; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_edits.gd:884-894, and the absence of any entry for it in ruitk-godot/CLAUDE.md's RUITK Builder divergence list or tests/builder_parity.gd:117-121 (DELIBERATE).

### `G-18` BuilderTree.validate() is never called — least of all on the one round trip that can break the invariants

**Unity does:** BuilderWindow.OnEnable calls _workspace.Tree.Validate() once per domain reload / window open and Debug.LogErrors each problem, prefixed "[RUITK Builder] tree invariant broken after reload: ". The stated point is not the check but that "a broken round trip that goes unreported resurfaces later as an inexplicable bug in whatever trusted it".

**Godot today:** absent at the call site. `validate()` is fully implemented (builder_tree.gd:230-257) and reports null modules, lost ids, duplicate ids, no derivable path, two modules claiming one path, and index/list disagreement. `grep -rn "\.validate()"` finds only tests/builder_model_test.gd:474, 479, 486, 492, 511, 727. Nothing in the window, the workspace or the journal calls it. Godot has no domain reload, so Unity's trigger does not exist here — but the round trip that DOES exist is the journal (`Journal.try_restore` -> `workspace.adopt_tree(BuilderTree.from_dict(...))`, builder_journal.gd:145-154 and builder_workspace.gd:74-80), which reads a JSON file that may be truncated, from an older schema, or hand-edited. `from_dict` (builder_tree.gd:274-284) does no checking beyond a type test, and `adopt_tree` does none. The `_by_path` index silently keeps only the last of two modules claiming a path (builder_tree.gd:218-220), which is precisely the failure `validate` names and which G-06's missing rename check can produce.

**To build:** Call `workspace.tree().validate()` from `adopt_tree` (or from `restore_recovery` right after it) and from `open_tree` after `load_tree`, pushing each problem with `push_error("[builder] tree invariant broken: %s")`. Consider refusing the restore outright when the problems include a duplicate path or a null module — a journal that does not read back cleanly is Unity's "Could not restore - the journal did not read back" case.

**Godot specifics:** `push_error` surfaces in Godot's Errors dock, which is append-only — the editor addon already de-duplicates diagnostics for that reason, so either emit once per open or route through `_console.add_diagnostics` the way `save()` does for blanks (builder_window.gd:1970-1973). `validate()` is pure and needs no editor, so the call sites stay headlessly testable.

**Risk:** A corrupt journal is adopted silently and the damage shows up later as a module that cannot be found by path, or a save that writes one file over another.

*medium · logic · UNVERIFIED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderTree.cs:255-295 (Validate), BuilderWindow.cs:133-138 (called on every OnEnable, logs each problem); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_tree.gd:230-257 (implemented), 274-284 (from_dict, unchecked), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:74-80 (adopt_tree, unchecked), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_journal.gd:145-154 — and no production caller anywhere.

### `G-19` The parity gate is green over four things in this area that are missing, hollow, or specified backwards

**Unity does:** n/a — this is a judgement on the gate itself, which greps for identifiers under builder/ and therefore cannot tell a wired feature from an unreferenced function.

**Godot today:** tests/builder_parity.gd passes on all four of these while the behaviour behind them is absent or inverted. (1) `["OfferJournalRestore", "func pending_recovery"]` (line 111) — `pending_recovery` exists and has no caller in the entire repo (G-03); the feature is 0% wired and the gate is green. (2) `["ReferrersTo (delete refused while imported)", "func referrers_to"]` (line 41) — the gate ENCODES THE WRONG REQUIREMENT: Unity's delete does not refuse, it strips references (BuilderWindow.cs:836-862, UB-88). A gate that demands the regression is worse than no gate (G-09). (3) `["ResolveEmptyModules", "func blank_modules"]` (line 105) — green over a function that only lists; Unity's behaviour is a three-way dialog that can delete or override (G-15). (4) `["ShowRenamePrompt", "CardMenuId.RENAME"]` (line 42) is the ONLY rename entry — it matches a menu enum constant, so it can never notice that RenameExportIn, RenameReferencesIn, RenameTargetPath and the whole ledger scope are missing (G-01, G-02, G-06, G-07). Not in the list at all: RenameModule, MoveModule/RepathLayout, PlaceNewCard/PlaceNewCardUnder, FamilyOwnerFor, BirthPathFor, StripReferencesTo/RemoveImportOf, IsPathAvailable, RebindFocusIfMissing, BuilderTree.Validate.

**To build:** Three changes. (a) Add the nine missing entries above, each keyed to an identifier that only the real mechanism can provide (`func rename_export`, `func strip_references_to`, `func family_owner_for`, `func place_new_card`, `func _rebind_focus_if_missing`, ...). (b) Correct entry 41 to `["StripReferencesTo (delete takes its references with it)", "func strip_references_to"]` and fix ruitk-unity/plans/UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:52, which is the stale line the Godot comment cites as authority. (c) For the entries where an identifier is not evidence of wiring — journal restore especially — replace the grep with a behavioural assertion in tests/builder_chrome_test.gd that instantiates the window and checks the offer actually fires, the way `_test_every_signal_is_listened_to` (tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:385) already does for signals.

**Godot specifics:** `_test_every_signal_is_listened_to` is the existing precedent for catching exactly this class of gap in this repo and it works — extend that pattern to "every public recovery/placement entry point has a caller" by grepping the sources for `func <name>` versus `<name>(` occurrences outside the definition. That check is cheap, headless, and would have caught G-03, G-14 and the dead `create_module` (G-20) on the day they were written.

**Risk:** A green gate over a hollow feature is worse than a red one: it tells the next person the area is done. Three of this area's four most serious gaps sit behind green entries.

### `G-20` create_module() is dead code implementing the birth-by-focus rule UB-207 exists to forbid

**Unity does:** There is one CreateModule and every route lands on it; BirthPathFor is stated by the gesture, never by what is focused, because "the structure recorded the ORDER OF THE CLICKS" (UB-207).

**Godot today:** `create_module(kind)` (builder_window.gd:1916-1934) derives its folder from `_focus_path.get_base_dir()`, auto-names via `_unused_name` ("NewComponent", "NewComponent2", ...), creates and records — a complete second create path that births by FOCUS. `grep -rn "create_module" --include=*.gd .` returns the definition and nothing else: no caller in the builder, the plugin, or any test. It is the pre-UB-207 shape, left in place beside the prompt-driven one that replaced it.

**To build:** Delete it, or if the auto-named path is wanted for a future "duplicate" gesture, rewrite it to call `_create_folder`/`_create_named` so there is one placement rule. Leaving a second, divergent create path in the file is how the next person implements a gesture against the wrong one.

**Godot specifics:** `_unused_name` (builder_window.gd:1935-1943) is the only thing it uniquely provides and is itself unused; both go together. Nothing else references either, so removal is safe — verified by the grep above, and the parity gate does not key on either identifier (it keys `CreateModule` to `func _create_named`, tests/builder_parity.gd:40).

**Risk:** Low today. It is listed because the parity sweep's own preamble names "a mechanism that already existed with nothing wired to it" as the failure class this builder keeps producing, and this is one — with the added hazard that the mechanism implements a rule the reference explicitly forbids.
