### `G-21` Nested capture/reconcile in move_folder and _place_tree_in records a `before` that is already half-rewritten

**Unity does:** MoveModule captures the import snapshot once per action and records every rewrite the move produced, so "the entry describes the file contents completely - a redo that restored a buffer recorded BEFORE the rewrite would otherwise put the stale specifier back".

**Godot today:** `move_folder` (builder_window.gd:1697-1713) and `_place_tree_in` (builder_window.gd:2059-2072) each take an outer `workspace.capture_imports()` and then call `workspace.move_to(...)` per module — and `move_to` -> `_move` (builder_workspace.gd:317-322) takes its OWN snapshot and reconciles on every call. So by the time the outer `reconcile_imports` runs, the buffers have already been rewritten N times; the `before` it reports, and therefore the `before` the ledger records at builder_window.gd:1711-1713, is an intermediate state rather than the text the gesture started from. Undoing the entry restores that intermediate. `place_module` (builder_window.gd:1725-1749) has the mirror problem: it discards the outer reconcile's result entirely (line 1743, return value unused), so its rewrites are in no entry at all — masked only because `_replay_change`'s MOVE branch re-reconciles on replay (builder_window.gd:2134-2136).

**To build:** Give the workspace a move primitive that does NOT reconcile — `move_to_raw(file_path, folder, name)` calling `_tree.move_to` directly — and have the multi-module callers use it inside one outer capture/reconcile pair. Then record the outer rewrites, which will finally have a truthful `before`. Keep `move_to`'s current capture+reconcile behaviour for the single-module callers that rely on it.

**Godot specifics:** `_move` is the shared helper (builder_workspace.gd:317-322) so the split is three lines. The ledger already collapses a same-file EDIT into one change whose `before` is the state the gesture started from (builder_ledger.gd:204-210) — that mechanism is correct and would give the right answer for free, if only the first `before` it saw were the pre-gesture text.

**Risk:** An undo of a multi-module move restores specifier text from a state that existed only momentarily inside the operation. In practice the MOVE replay re-reconciles over it, so this is latent rather than user-visible — but it stops being latent the moment G-02 adds the missing record_move calls and the two halves start interacting.

*low · logic · UNVERIFIED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:3658-3706 (one capture per action, every rewrite recorded); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1697-1713 (move_folder), 1743 (place_module discards the reconcile), 2059-2072 (_place_tree_in), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:317-322 (_move reconciles on every call).

### `G-22` Opening the card create prompt moves the focus before anything is confirmed

**Unity does:** OnCreateUnder passes the parent module to CreateModule as an argument; the focus moves only on success, via OpenAdditionalFile(full) at the end of the commit sequence.

**Godot today:** `_on_card_new` (builder_window.gd:1649-1655) assigns `_focus_path = _menu_target` before calling `prompt_create` — a side effect that lands whether or not the user submits. The assignment is also useless: `_create_folder` reads `_menu_target`, not `_focus_path` (builder_window.gd:1862), so nothing in the create path consumes it. Cancelling the prompt leaves the focus silently moved to the card that was right-clicked, without any of the surface updates `select_module` would have done — so the status bar, source pane and preview now disagree with `_focus_path`.

**To build:** Delete the assignment. If moving the focus onto the right-clicked card is wanted, call `select_module(_menu_target)` so every surface follows, and do it on submit rather than on open.

**Godot specifics:** `_focus_path` is read by `_delete_selection` (builder_window.gd:279), `_refresh_status` (2458) and `preview.compile_dirty(_focus_path)` (builder_window.gd:919) — assigning it without going through `select_module` (which is what keeps those in step, builder_window.gd:2151-2175) is the general hazard, and this is the only place in the file that does it outside a move.

**Risk:** Small: a cancelled create leaves the builder's internal focus and its visible focus disagreeing, so the next Delete keypress or preview round targets a module the user is not looking at.

*low · gesture · UNVERIFIED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:863-871 (OnCreateUnder passes the parent, does not move focus), 6069-6112 (focus moves via OpenAdditionalFile on success only); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1649-1655, and 1862 showing the assigned value is never read by the create path.

### Document model: workspace, tree, module, specifiers, dirtiness, projection, orphans, read-only, import reconciliation

### `DM-01` A load replaces the tree with no unsaved-work veto — right-clicking a .guitkx destroys the session

> Also filed as `shell.load-tree-veto` — one defect.

**Unity does:** LoadTreeFor(path) returns immediately if the path is empty or the tree already holds it; if HasUnsavedChanges it calls Open(path) ALONE and toasts 'Opened <file> on its own - save or abort first to load its whole tree'; only a clean session runs LoadTree, and if the scan still did not produce the focus it falls back to Open(path). Stated reason: 'Losing an unsaved buffer to a right-click in the Project window is not a trade worth making.'

**Godot today:** absent. plugin.gd:451-455 open_builder_on() calls _builder.open_tree(file_path) unconditionally; builder_window.gd:749-773 open_tree() calls workspace.load_tree(focus_path) with no dirty check, no already-holds-it check and no Open() fallback. load_tree ends in _tree.reset(loaded, projection) (builder_workspace.gd:203), which clears _modules outright — every dirty buffer, every created-but-unwritten module and every deletion is gone, and open_tree then calls ledger.clear() at :767 so Ctrl+Z cannot bring any of it back. The only mitigation is the 5-second crash journal (builder_window.gd:936-946), which is offered as a 'recovery' the user must notice and accept.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One nuance the report omits, in the port's favour: the MENU route already implements half of Unity's guard. `plugin.gd:439-446` refuses to re-point an open session at all ('re-pointing an open session at whatever the editor happens to be showing would take a tree with unsaved work away from under someone') and only calls `open_tree` when `_builder.focus_path().is_empty()`. The hole is exactly the FileSystem-dock route `open_builder_on`, which bypasses that guard — which makes the fix smaller than stated: `open_builder_on` is the one caller that needs `load_tree_for`.

**To build:** Port LoadTreeFor into builder_window.gd as the single entry the plugin calls. Guard: `if focus_path.is_empty() or workspace.try_get(focus_path) != null: return`; then `if workspace.has_unsaved_changes(): workspace.open(focus_path); toast(...); reproject(); select_module(...); return`; else load_tree, and after it `if workspace.try_get(focus_path) == null: workspace.open(focus_path)`. Point plugin.gd:454 at it. The toast surface already exists (builder_window.gd:194, toast()).

**Godot specifics:** workspace.open() is already written and headlessly proven (builder_model_test.gd:730-755); this is pure wiring. Keep ledger.clear() on the LOAD path only — an Open-into-an-existing-tree must not clear the ledger, or the veto trades one loss for another. Testable headlessly: the window builds without EditorInterface in builder_chrome_test.gd, so a suite can dirty a module, call open_tree on a sibling path and assert the buffer survived and toast_text() names the reason.

**Risk:** The single largest data-loss route in the builder. The FileSystem dock's 'Open in RUITK UI Builder' is the advertised entry point, and using it twice in a session silently throws away everything since the last Save.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:105-119 (LoadTreeFor); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:749-773 and addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/plugin.gd:451-455

### `DM-02` Rename does not rename: no export rewrite, no reference rewrite, no folder carry, no ledger entry

> Also filed as `G-01`, `G-02` — one defect.

**Unity does:** RenameModule is a text pass plus ONE move, in that order, inside one ledger entry. It refuses first (File.Exists(newFull) || tree holds newFull || (ownsFolder && Directory.Exists(newDir)) -> toast '<new> already exists'). Then: CaptureImports BEFORE any text changes; RenameExportIn rewrites the module's own export DECLARATION via `(\bexport\s+[^\r\n=;]*?\b)<old>\b` with exactly ONE replacement; for every OTHER module (through EditSession, not TryGet — 'an importer the user has not opened is still an importer') RenameReferencesIn rewrites `(["'/])<old><stem>(?=["'])` and then every `\b<old>\b`; then MoveModule to RenameTargetPath, which for a folder-owning component is Combine(GetDirectoryName(dir), newName) — THE FOLDER MOVES; then RecordMove plus every ReconcileImports rewrite into the same entry, and RepathLayout.

**Godot today:** wrong, and silently. builder_window.gd:1897-1915 _rename_to() is four lines of substance: `workspace.move_to(module.file_path(), module.folder, name)`. It passes the module's CURRENT folder, so a folder-owning component keeps a folder named after the old name. It never touches the module's own text, never touches any importer's binding or uses, never checks for a collision, never calls ledger.begin/record_move (so a rename is NOT undoable and is invisible to the history pane), never records the rewrites move_to returns (they are assigned to `rewrites` and used only as a did-it-happen flag), and never calls layout.repath. Probed on Godot 4.7 against a real fixture: renaming res://…/r/Panel/Panel.guitkx to 'Card' produced res://…/r/Panel/Card.guitkx (owns_folder=false — the folder is still 'Panel'), its own buffer still reading `export Panel() -> RuitkVNode {`, and the child at r/Panel/components/Leaf/ left under a folder no module owns any more.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Severity stands at critical; only one of the four clauses is refuted. CONFIRMED sub-claims: (a) no export-declaration rewrite anywhere — `grep -rn 'rename' addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder` returns no text-rewriting site at all; (b) no folder carry — `_rename_to` (builder_window.gd:1907-1908) passes `module.folder`, the module's CURRENT folder, so `tree.move_to`'s subtree carry (builder_tree.gd:122-138) sees `target == old_folder` and moves nothing, leaving the folder under the old name and `owns_folder()` false; (c) no collision check; (d) no `ledger.begin`/`record_move` — the rewrites `move_to` returns are assigned to `rewrites` at :1908 and used only as a did-it-happen flag at :1909, so a rename is not undoable and not in the history pane; (e) no `layout.repath` — `grep -rn 'layout.repath'` finds exactly ONE call site in the whole addon, builder_window.gd:1707. REFUTED sub-claim: 'never touches any importer's specifier'. The accurate statement is: the rename moves the FILE and re-spells the PATHS, and touches no NAME — so the file becomes Card.guitkx while it still declares `export Panel()` and every importer still binds `{ Panel }`.

**To build:** Port RenameModule wholesale into builder_window.gd. (1) A rename_target_path(module, new_name) helper — `owns := module.owns_folder(); new_folder := module.folder.get_base_dir().path_join(new_name) if owns else module.folder` — shared by _validate_name and the rename, exactly as Unity shares RenameTargetPath. (2) Refuse on FileAccess.file_exists(new_full) || workspace.try_get(new_full) != null || (owns && DirAccess.dir_exists_absolute(new_folder)), with a toast. (3) ledger.begin('Rename X to Y'); capture_imports(); rewrite the module's own export with a RegEx on `(\bexport\s+[^\r\n=;]*?\b)<old>\b` (RegEx.sub with the replacement count capped at 1); rewrite every other module's specifier stem + binding + uses; workspace.move_to(path, new_folder, new_name); ledger.record_move; record every reconcile_imports rewrite; ledger.end(). (4) layout.repath(old, new, is_folder := owns) — the function exists at canvas/builder_canvas_layout.gd:180 and is called from exactly one place today.

**Godot specifics:** Every text rewrite must go through the ONE FUNNEL (builder_window.gd:858 apply_edit) or the ledger and the preview round diverge; note apply_edit refuses when before == after, so the loop must skip unchanged peers itself. GDScript RegEx has no count-limited sub, so the single-replacement export rewrite needs `search()` + manual splice rather than `sub(..., true)`. The stem set is '.style'/'.hooks'/'' from Module.suffix_for — do not hand-roll it. Reconciling AFTER the move (not before) is load-bearing: the name-level surgery only has to be right about NAMES, and reconcile_imports re-derives every specifier from where modules actually ended up.

**Risk:** Every rename produces a tree that cannot compile: the file is called Card.guitkx and still exports Panel, and every importer still imports { Panel } from './Panel'. The user sees a green canvas because the canvas projects the BUFFER, and finds out at Save. Combined with the missing folder carry it also breaks resolve_root, which re-keys the canvas layout.

### `DM-03` is_path_available reintroduces UB-222 — and its own doc comment describes the fixed rule while the code implements the broken one

**Unity does:** IsPathAvailable: empty -> false; tree already holds it -> false; !File.Exists -> TRUE; otherwise the file is only an obstacle when the session cannot account for it — accounted for if some module HasMoved and its DiskPath canon-equals this path (Save vacates it), or if the path is in OrphanedPaths() (Save retires it first, which is exactly why SaveAll clears dead paths before it writes). The comment names the defect it fixes: reading File.Exists alone made moving a module BACK to where it started fail with 'already there', pointing at the module's own pre-move copy, which no retry could clear because only Save can.

**Godot today:** wrong. builder_workspace.gd:101-105 is the pre-fix rule verbatim: `return _tree.by_path(full) == null and not FileAccess.file_exists(full)`. The doc comment directly above it (builder_workspace.gd:98-100) asserts the opposite of what the code does: 'Nothing needs an exception for "deleted but not saved yet": a deleted module is not in the tree, so its name is free the instant it goes.' Probed on Godot 4.7: after deleting an on-disk module, is_path_available(its path) == false; after moving a module away, is_path_available(its old path) == false; and create_new at the vacated path returns null. Both accounted-for cases fail.

**To build:** Add the two exceptions to builder_workspace.gd:101-105: after the FileAccess.file_exists test, loop _tree.modules() for `module.has_moved() and Paths.same(module.disk_path, full)` -> true, then loop _tree.orphaned_paths() for `Paths.same(orphan, full)` -> true, else false. Both loops are over data the tree already computes.

**Godot specifics:** Use Paths.same(), never String ==, or the fix inherits the two-spellings-of-one-file hazard builder_paths.gd:1-24 exists to prevent. This is a pure-model change, fully testable in tests/builder_model_test.gd with no editor.

**Risk:** The user deletes a module, changes their mind and re-creates it under the same name: refused, with no message (see DM-08), until they Save. The user drags a module to the wrong folder and drags it back: refused. Neither can be cleared by retrying — only by a Save the user did not want yet.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/Document/BuilderWorkspace.cs:75-96; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:98-105

### `DM-04` Dropping a folder-owning component on a folder flattens its family into the destination

**Unity does:** MoveModuleToFolder: refuse read-only ('Read-only file'); destination = OwnsFolder ? Combine(target, Name) : target — a component that owns its folder goes to Target/Name/, a companion to Target/; refuse when OwnsFolder && IsInside(targetFolder, module.Folder) (dropping a folder-owner into its own subtree would make the folder its own ancestor); refuse when !IsPathAvailable(to) with '<file> is already there'; one ledger entry with the move plus its rewrites. MoveFolderToFolder delegates to it when a module OWNS the source folder — 'the same move by a shorter route, and the one that keeps the house layout'.

**Godot today:** wrong. builder_window.gd:1725-1749 place_module() computes `destination` for the ledger but hands `target_folder` itself to _move_one -> workspace.place_at(module, target_folder), with no OwnsFolder ? target/Name : target rule, no is_path_available check and no is-inside-its-own-subtree guard. builder_window.gd:1684, the owner-delegation branch of move_folder(), does the same: it computes `destination := target_folder.path_join(leaf)` at :1679 and then calls `_move_one(module, target_folder, leaf)` — dropping the computed destination on the floor. Probed on Godot 4.7: dragging res://…/r/Panel/Panel.guitkx (owning Panel/, holding panel.style.guitkx and components/Leaf/Leaf.guitkx) onto res://…/dest produced dest/Panel.guitkx (owns_folder=false), dest/panel.style.guitkx and dest/components/Leaf/Leaf.guitkx — the family flattened into the destination and a components/ folder dumped at its top level. Unity gives dest/Panel/Panel.uitkx, dest/Panel/panel.style.uitkx, dest/Panel/components/Leaf/Leaf.uitkx.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Two guards the report says are missing do exist on the FOLDER route only: `move_folder` refuses `Paths.is_under(destination, source)` with a toast (:1680-1682), and refuses a read-only member with a named toast (:1691-1693). Neither is reached by `place_module`, and neither is reached by the owner-delegation branch, which returns at :1685 before both. So: the flatten, the missing OwnsFolder destination rule, the missing `is_path_available` refusal and the missing per-module is-inside guard are all real; 'no is-inside guard' is true of `place_module` but not of `move_folder`.

**To build:** In place_module (builder_window.gd:1725) and in move_folder's owner branch (:1684): `var destination_folder := target_folder.path_join(module.name) if module.owns_folder() else target_folder`; refuse when `module.owns_folder() and Paths.is_under(destination_folder, module.folder)` with a toast; refuse when `not workspace.is_path_available(destination_folder.path_join(module.file_path().get_file()))` with '<file> is already there'; pass destination_folder to _move_one. Then add the missing layout.repath(from, module.file_path(), module.owns_folder()) that only move_folder's batch path has today (:1707).

**Godot specifics:** Paths.is_under (builder_paths.gd:70-78) is already path-boundary matched, so it is the right IsInside. Note the availability refusal is only meaningful once DM-03 is fixed — with today's is_path_available, dragging a module back where it came from would be refused for the wrong reason. Both entries are reachable from the folder pane's refile_requested signal and the canvas drop, so a headless test can call place_module directly.

**Risk:** A single drag destroys the house layout the whole document model is built around: the component no longer owns a folder, resolve_root stops finding the tree head, the canvas layout re-keys, and the component's companions and children are strewn across the destination. Nothing is refused when the destination already holds a same-named module, so _reindex (builder_tree.gd:209-221) is last-writer-wins and Save writes one module over the other.

### `DM-05` The external-change sweep is written, tested and never called

**Unity does:** Two triggers. OnUitkxImported (BuilderWindow.cs:179-205) runs ReloadCleanFromDisk over the imported paths whenever Unity imports .uitkx assets — a git pull, an IDE edit, a sync — then NotifyBufferChanged() so the preview rebuilds, RefreshGraph per path, re-sets the source pane if the focus changed and no source-edit snapshot is open, and ScheduleServerTokens. And an OnEnable sweep over EVERY module (BuilderWindow.cs:150-159) because changes made while the old domain was alive missed their import event. Rationale: 'a file changing on disk has to reload that node or the builder serves stale text and its next Save silently overwrites the external edit'.

**Godot today:** absent as a behaviour. builder_workspace.gd:237-251 reload_clean_from_disk is implemented correctly (skips unknown / dirty / read-only / missing, adopts, emits changed once, returns the touched paths) and has ZERO callers anywhere in the addon — `grep -rn reload_clean_from_disk` hits only its definition and tests/builder_model_test.gd:747-753. Nothing hooks EditorFileSystem.filesystem_changed for the builder (plugin.gd:144 connects it only for the .guitkx editor view), nothing sweeps on window focus, nothing sweeps on open. plugin.gd:279-283 _on_file_moved retargets the editor view but never tells the builder. So a tree held in memory across an hour of work serves the text it loaded, and the next Save writes it over whatever the user's IDE, a git pull or the FileSystem dock did in the meantime.

**To build:** Wire the sweep at two moments and report the conflict. (1) On the builder Window regaining focus — the Unreal leg does exactly this and says why: 'coming back to the window is exactly when a file is likely to have changed in the user's IDE, and polling disk for a whole tree on a tick would cost more than it is worth'. (2) On EditorFileSystem.filesystem_changed, debounced, filtered to .guitkx paths the tree holds. Feed both into one `sweep_disk()` on builder_window.gd that calls workspace.reload_clean_from_disk(every module path), and for each touched path re-populates the card (the machinery is already in _after_model_change, builder_window.gd:881-895), refreshes the source pane, and calls preview.request_refresh(). Add the conflict report Unity does not have: reload_clean_from_disk should also return the paths where BOTH the buffer and the file changed, and the window should say so — 'N file(s) changed on disk AND here — your version is kept: …'.

**Godot specifics:** The builder lives in a Window created at plugin.gd:429-437; a focus sweep is _notification(NOTIFICATION_WM_WINDOW_FOCUS_IN) on that Window, or NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_IN on the Control. EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem().filesystem_changed fires in bursts, so debounce it the way plugin.gd:138-144 already does for the editor view. Detecting the conflict needs the disk text compared against module.projected_text, not against buffer_text — projected_text is the common ancestor. Keep the whole thing out of builder_workspace.gd's disk layer so the model stays headlessly testable; the sweep itself already is.

**Risk:** The one failure in this window that destroys work the tool never created. A user edits a .guitkx in VS Code, comes back to the builder, presses Ctrl+S, and the external edit is gone with no message.

### `DM-06` Delete is refused while imported — the design Unity retired, ported from the stale capability spec

**Unity does:** Being referenced is NOT a refusal. OnDeleteFile checks read-only and existence, then opens ONE ledger entry, calls StripReferencesTo(full) — which for every other module drops the import of the target and every attribute whose value uses a name that import bound, recording each edit in the same entry — then RecordDeletion and Delete. The comment on RemoveImportOf names the reason: 'Leaving those behind would turn a delete into a broken build, which is the thing the old refusal was trying to avoid.' The inventory flags this explicitly: 'the capability spec still says … delete is refused while another module still imports it — both describe the retired design.'

**Godot today:** the retired design, argued for in a comment. builder_window.gd:2414-2437 delete_module() computes referrers_to(file_path) and, when non-empty, toasts 'Can't delete X — still imported by …' and returns false. Its doc comment at :2405-2413 cites 'capability reference §2' and explicitly rejects StripReferencesTo: 'This used to strip the importers' imports instead and delete anyway, which is a worse answer than it looks.' The parity gate agrees with it — tests/builder_parity.gd:42 is `["ReferrersTo (delete refused while imported)", "func referrers_to"]`, so the checklist derived from Unity enshrines a behaviour Unity removed.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Worth flagging explicitly: this IS a divergence with a stated reason, but the reason is stale, not agreed. It is absent from CLAUDE.md's deliberate list and absent from tests/builder_parity.gd's own DELIBERATE array (which holds only ImportUxml, CodeField and BuilderLspClient). Unity's source contradicts the Godot comment's premise sentence for sentence.

**To build:** Port StripReferencesTo. In delete_module, replace the refusal with: ledger.begin('Delete X'); for every other module in the tree (not just cards on the canvas — Godot loads the whole tree eagerly, so try_get is enough), compute a buffer with the import of the target removed plus every attribute whose value uses the binding that import introduced, and route each through apply_edit so it lands in the same entry; then workspace.delete + ledger.record_deletion; ledger.end(). Then fix tests/builder_parity.gd:42 to name StripReferencesTo, not the refusal. Edits.imports_specifier already exists (used by referrers_to at builder_window.gd:2395-2402) and edits/builder_edits.gd holds the attribute machinery.

**Godot specifics:** The import removal must be span-based off RuitkGuitkx.scan_imports, the way builder_specifiers.gd:81-99 already reads them, not a text search — a specifier is an ordinary string and appears elsewhere. Removing the import alone is not enough here either: an unused import is GUITKX2304 and an unimported reference is GUITKX2305, so both the import and its uses have to go or the delete trades one compile error for another. Every rewrite must go through builder_window.gd:858 apply_edit so the ledger, the preview round and the re-projection stay in step.

**Risk:** A child component is undeletable. The whole house layout puts a child under its parent and has the parent import it, so the single most common delete in the builder is the one that is always refused — and the user's only route out is to open each importer's source and unwire it by hand.

### `DM-07` First Save of a new tree loses every card position — UB-220 at full strength

**Unity does:** ResolveUnsavedLocation plans every destination first (a collision cancels the whole move), then snapshots wasAt[module] = FilePath for EVERY MODULE IN THE TREE — not just the pending ones — before the PlaceAt pass, and afterwards reconciles the canvas layout and focus by comparing each module's path against that snapshot, with the focus read ONCE before the loop. UB-220 is the reason: 'a module its parent already carried has ALREADY changed path by the time the loop reaches it, so a before/after read around its own PlaceAt compares two identical strings, the layout treats it as did not move, and every passenger card kept a key under the provisional root, stopped resolving, and was handed a default slot that AdoptUnplaced then wrote down. One dragged card survived and the other four fell into a column at x=60.'

**Godot today:** the pre-snapshot shape, plus no layout repath at all. builder_window.gd:2042-2074 _place_tree_in() plans in full (good — a collision returns false before anything moves) and opens one ledger entry (good), but it only tracks _focus_path inside the loop (`if Paths.same(_focus_path, from)`), reading `from` per-iteration — exactly the read that compares two identical strings for a carried passenger. There is no wasAt map and, more simply, there is no layout.repath call anywhere in the function. `grep -rn 'layout.repath'` finds ONE call site in the whole builder (builder_window.gd:1707, move_folder's batch path); place_module, _rename_to and _place_tree_in have none. Every card's key changes at the first Save, canvas/builder_canvas_layout.gd's load_for_members finds zero overlap, and reproject() -> layout.adopt_unplaced(graph) (builder_window.gd:827) mints and persists a default slot for every card.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One mitigation the report does not credit, which does not save this case: the layout store has a by-MEMBERSHIP fallback (builder_canvas_layout.gd:64-93 `load_for_members`) written precisely so a re-keyed root does not lose the file. It cannot help here because a whole-tree relocation changes every member path at once, so `overlap == 0` for every candidate and `load_for_root` then misses too. The claim's mechanism survives the mitigation intact. Also, credit where due: `_place_tree_in` DOES plan in full before moving (a collision cancels everything, :2049-2057) and DOES record the reconcile rewrites in the ledger (:2069-2071) — it is only the snapshot and the repath that are missing.

**To build:** Before the plan executes, build `var was_at := {}` over EVERY module in workspace.modules() keyed by module.id -> module.file_path(), and read the focus once. After the loop, for each module whose current file_path() differs from was_at[module.id], call layout.repath(was_at[module.id], module.file_path(), false); repoint _focus_path from the snapshot. Add the same repath to place_module/_move_one and to _rename_to (see DM-02, DM-04).

**Godot specifics:** Key the snapshot on module.id, not on the object — builder_module.gd:24-28's whole point is that the id survives the path changing, and a Dictionary keyed on a RefCounted is fine but the id reads correctly. layout.repath exists at canvas/builder_canvas_layout.gd:180 with an is_folder flag; a component that owns its folder needs the folder form. Note the second-order effect: adopt_unplaced WRITES the default slot down, so the damage is persisted to user://ruitk_builder/layouts and survives a reopen.

**Risk:** The first Save of anything built from the start screen scatters the canvas. The user arranges five cards, presses Ctrl+S, picks a folder, and the arrangement is replaced by a default column — permanently, because the default is written to the layout store.

On a brand-new tree tree_root() is UNSAVED_ROOT, so the very first component of every tree is res://__ruitk_builder_unsaved__~/NewComponent.guitkx and owns_folder() is false from birth — which then propagates into resolve_root, the layout key, and _place_tree_in's relative-path computation (builder_window.gd:2048-2050 yields relative == "", so the placed tree is chosen/NewComponent.guitkx). _create_named also raises no toast at all, success or failure.

**To build:** Split a `path_for(folder, kind, name, as_root)` out of _create_folder mirroring BuilderNewFileDialog.PathFor, and have the no-card branch return path_for(tree_root(), kind, name, as_root := workspace.modules().is_empty()). Add the create toast naming the destination folder, and a failure toast when create_new returns null.

**Godot specifics:** Get this right before DM-11: the flat first component is precisely what makes resolve_root_from's owns_folder predicate answer 'nothing owns this folder' for a new tree, which is the case UB-189 was about. Fully headlessly testable — _create_named is driven directly in tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:444.

**Risk:** The builder never produces the house layout it is designed around for a tree started from the empty state, so every downstream rule that keys on folder ownership (root resolution, folder carry on rename/move, the layout key) degrades from the first module onward.

### `DM-10` The family rule is fully implemented and entirely unwired — there is no FamilyOwnerFor

**Unity does:** FamilyOwnerFor(kind, name): a Util returns null; otherwise scan the tree's Components for SameFamily, keeping the one with the greatest SharedPrefixLength(focusDir, module.Folder), ties broken by ordinal-smallest FilePath so the answer does not depend on load order. BirthPathFor then puts a new companion in FamilyOwnerFor(...)?.Folder ?? root — 'a new companion whose name matches a family lands in that component's folder wherever it lives'. UB-187, agreed with the owner: placement used to depend on what the user happened to be looking at rather than on what the module IS.

**Godot today:** the primitives exist, nothing calls them. document/builder_naming.gd:37-75 implements family_of (with the use_ strip), same_family and shared_prefix_length — and shared_prefix_length is BETTER than Unity's, counting path SEGMENTS rather than characters so res://ui/card and res://ui/cardigan do not score as near neighbours. `grep -rn 'RuitkBuilderNaming\|builder_naming\|same_family\|family_of\|shared_prefix_length'` across the whole repo hits only the file itself and tests/builder_model_test.gd:516-556. builder_window.gd never preloads it. So a style module created from the canvas lands at tree_root(), never beside the component it companions.

**To build:** Preload builder_naming.gd in builder_window.gd and add family_owner_for(kind, name) — skip UTIL, scan workspace.modules() for kind == COMPONENT && Naming.same_family(...), keep the greatest Naming.shared_prefix_length(_focus_path.get_base_dir(), module.folder), break ties on the ordinal-smallest file_path. Use it in _create_folder's companion branch when there is no card under the cursor.

**Godot specifics:** Preload const, not the global class_name — RuitkBuilderNaming resolves through the editor class cache and ProjectSettings.save() truncates that cache to whatever the running process loaded, which is why every other builder file already does this (builder_naming.gd:23-30 says so about itself). The tie-break must be deterministic or the destination depends on load order, and load order here is builder_workspace.gd:172's files.sort().

**Risk:** A gap that is invisible until it isn't: companions accumulate at the tree root instead of beside their components, and the folder convention the whole model depends on is only maintained when the user happens to right-click the right card.

*medium · feature · CONFIRMED* — unity ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:5996-6023 (FamilyOwnerFor) and Document/BuilderNaming.cs:20-73; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_naming.gd:37-75 (no non-test callers)

### `DM-11` tree_root() is a third, different answer to 'where is the root of this tree'

**Unity does:** One walk, two oracles, and BOTH are the same walk: ResolveRootCore climbs while the parent folder owns a module named after itself, treating components/ as a nesting level only where a component owns the folder above it. BirthPathFor uses the MODULES overload; LoadTree uses the DISK one. The root must be 'the same answer from EVERY module in the tree, imported or not' — UB-185 and UB-189 are both about a different definition producing a different root and re-keying the saved layout.

**Godot today:** the walk is ported faithfully (builder_tree.gd:296-346, both oracles) and used by the loader and the graph service — but the window does not use it. builder_window.gd:1816-1826 tree_root() is a fourth definition: the module folder with the shortest STRING. That is not depth (res://a/bbbbbbbbbbbb is 20 characters and one level deep; res://abcdefg/h is 15 and two), and it is not membership-aware: load_tree's import closure (builder_workspace.gd:189-201) legitimately pulls in modules from outside the root, so a shared module at res://shared/ (12 chars) outranks a tree head at res://ui/Panel (14) and every new component is born under res://shared/.

**To build:** Replace builder_window.gd:1816-1826's body with BuilderTree.resolve_root_from(workspace.modules(), _focus_path), falling back to Workspace.UNSAVED_ROOT when the tree is empty — the same call canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:156-165 already makes. Keep the fallback: resolve_root_from returns the focus's own directory when nothing owns anything, which is the right answer for a tree that has not been placed.

**Godot specifics:** builder_tree.gd:296-303's predicate asks owns_folder() of the MODULES, which is the overload a never-saved tree needs (UB-189) — the disk overload at :308-311 would answer from files that do not exist yet. Do this after DM-09, or the modules oracle will find nothing owning anything because the first component was born flat. Pure model call, headlessly testable.

**Risk:** Two subsystems disagree about the same fact. The canvas keys its layout from resolve_root_from while creates are placed from tree_root(), so a tree whose import closure reaches outside its root grows new modules in a folder that is not its own.

### `DM-12` Hook naming contradicts itself: the default name fails its own validator and the template emits use_useX

**Unity does:** One convention, applied consistently: ValidateNewName requires ^use[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$ for a hook, TemplateFor emits 'export (int value) <Name>() { … }' with the export named exactly what the user typed — 'templates emit only the export the user NAMED' (UB-112) — and FamilyOf strips a leading 'use' when name.Length > 3 && starts with 'use' && char[3] IsUpper.

**Godot today:** three files, three conventions. builder_window.gd:1791-1793 _validate_name demands camelCase ^use[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$. builder_module.gd:154-165 default_name_for(HOOK) returns 'newHook', which FAILS that regex — so opening 'New hook module' pre-fills the prompt with a name its own inline validator immediately rejects (builder_window.gd:1777 passes default_name_for as the prompt's initial text; verified against the regex on Godot 4.7). edits/builder_edits.gd:886-887 template_for(HOOK) emits `export use_%s()`, so a hook legitimately named 'useThing' produces `export use_useThing()`. And builder_naming.gd:37-44 family_of strips a leading `use_` (snake_case), which never matches a name the validator accepted.

**To build:** Pick one convention and make the four sites agree. Given the compiler's own rules (GUITKX2100 wants PascalCase components) and the rest of this leg's snake_case file convention, the cheapest coherent choice is: validator ^use_[a-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ (or keep camelCase and change the other three). Then default_name_for(HOOK) must return a name that passes it, template_for must emit `export <name>()` with the name as typed rather than prefixing use_ again, and family_of's strip must match the accepted spelling.

**Godot specifics:** template_for already does this correctly for components — builder_edits.gd:892-894 derives the PascalCase export from the file name via _pascal rather than prefixing anything. The hook branch is the odd one out. Cover it in tests/builder_model_test.gd: assert default_name_for(k) passes the validator's regex for every Kind, which is a two-line invariant that would have caught this.

**Risk:** The hook create flow is broken out of the box: the prompt opens showing an error, and any name that clears it produces a module whose export name is wrong and whose family never matches its component.

**Unity does:** The window mirrors HasUnsavedWork into EditorWindow.hasUnsavedChanges on every Changed, and overrides SaveChanges() to route through its own SaveAll so Unity's prompt cannot bypass the location prompt or the format pass — if the location prompt is cancelled the window stays dirty and base.SaveChanges() is NOT called. The 5-second journal (builder_window.gd:936-946) softens it but requires the user to notice and accept a recovery offer on the next open.

**Unity does:** OwnsFolder compares GetFileName(Folder.TrimEnd('\\','/')) against Name with StringComparison.Ordinal — the inventory calls it out as 'the one case-SENSITIVE comparison in the layer: Panel/panel.uitkx does not own Panel/'.

The practical exposure is Linux-only, since NTFS and default APFS make the collision unrepresentable.

## The chrome: shell, panes, menus, inline editors and the source surface

74 distinct gaps — 9 critical, 18 high, 30 medium, 17 low, plus 9 marked as duplicates.

### Folder pane: tree rendering, state column, selection, re-filing by drag, folding

### `FP-01` A re-file onto a folder that already holds that file name silently creates two modules claiming one path -- and Save overwrites the resident file

**Unity does:** `MoveModuleToFolder` computes the destination and refuses before touching anything: `string to = Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(destination, Path.GetFileName(modulePath))); if (!_workspace.IsPathAvailable(to)) { Toast(Path.GetFileName(to) + " is already there"); return; }` (BuilderWindow.cs:549-554). `IsPathAvailable` (BuilderWorkspace.cs:75-96) refuses when the tree already holds that path, and treats a disk file as available only when a module has moved off it or it is a known orphan. It is one of the five toasts this gesture can produce.

**Godot today:** ABSENT. `is_path_available` exists (builder_workspace.gd:101-105) and is called only by `create_new` (:258); no move path consults it. The pane's drop reaches `place_module` (builder_window.gd:1725) -> `_move_one` (:1754) -> `workspace.place_at` (builder_workspace.gd:309-312) -> `_move` (:342-347) -> `builder_tree.gd:111-139 move_to`, which assigns `module.folder = target` unconditionally and calls `_reindex()`. `_reindex` (builder_tree.gd:209-221) does `_by_path[k] = module` with no collision check, so the second module silently shadows the first while both derive the same `file_path()`. PROVEN on Godot 4.7: with res://X/A/Card.guitkx and res://X/B/Card.guitkx open, `place_at(A_module, "res://X/B")` gives `modules: [res://X/B/Card.guitkx, res://X/B/Card.guitkx]`; `tree.validate()` returns ["two modules claim res://X/B/Card.guitkx"]; `save_all()` returns 1; A's file is gone from disk and B/Card.guitkx now contains A's text. The resident module's content is never written back -- `save_all` skips it because it is neither dirty nor moved. `_move_on_disk` uses `DirAccess.rename_absolute`, which overwrites on Windows, so the clobber does not even reach the trash. `validate()` catches it (builder_tree.gd:248-251) but nothing on the move path calls it.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The defect is confirmed but the prescribed fix is subtly wrong as written. Godot's `is_path_available` is NOT Unity's: it is `_tree.by_path(full) == null and not FileAccess.file_exists(full)` (builder_workspace.gd:101-105), missing BOTH exemptions Unity's has (BuilderWorkspace.cs:84-93) -- a disk path some module has already MOVED OFF this session, and a known orphan. Gating a move on it as-is would refuse the legitimate case of dragging B back into a folder whose same-named file was moved away a moment ago and not yet saved. Port Unity's two exemptions into `is_path_available` first, or the guard trades a silent clobber for a silent refusal.

**To build:** Gate every re-file on `workspace.is_path_available(destination_path)` before the model is mutated. In `builder_window.gd place_module`, after computing the destination: `if not workspace.is_path_available(destination): toast("%s is already there" % destination.get_file()); return false`. Same in `move_folder` (builder_window.gd:1668-1720): check every entry's computed `to` BEFORE `ledger.begin`, and refuse the whole move on the first collision -- the all-or-nothing rule that file already applies to read-only modules. Belt and braces: put a refusal inside `builder_tree.gd move_to` when another module already derives the target path, so the canvas drop, the card menu and any future caller inherit it.

Do NOT put the guard in the pane: `_drop_target_for` is pure and has no workspace, and duplicating the rule there is exactly how Unity ended up with two `IsInside` predicates that disagree. The refusal must be `toast()` from the window, not `push_error` -- the console is behind Trace and nobody is looking at it during a drag. Keep the preload-const referencing in builder_tree.gd (no `class_name`), per the ProjectSettings class-cache truncation hazard. Fully headlessly testable; add it beside `_test_folder_pane_refiles` (tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:945), which today moves only `app.style.guitkx`, a companion with no name twin -- so this case has never been exercised.

**Risk:** The one gesture the pane exists for silently destroys a file the user did not touch, with no toast, no diagnostic and no undo that can bring the bytes back. Two modules named `Card.guitkx` in different folders is the most likely shape a component library has.

### `FP-02` Re-filing a component that OWNS its folder dissolves the folder instead of carrying it -- the house layout is destroyed on the drag

**Unity does:** "Dropping a component that OWNS its folder moves that FOLDER, rather than tipping its file out into the destination: the house layout is ComponentName/ComponentName.uitkx with its children inside" (BuilderWindow.cs:536-539). The code is `string destination = module.OwnsFolder ? Path.Combine(targetFolder, module.Name) : targetFolder;` followed by `if (module.OwnsFolder && IsInside(targetFolder, module.Folder)) { Toast("Can't move " + module.Name + " inside itself"); return; }`. `MoveFolderToFolder` delegates to it for exactly this reason -- "the same move by a shorter route, and the one that keeps the house layout".

**Godot today:** WRONG on both routes. `place_module` passes `target_folder` unchanged to `_move_one` -> `place_at` -> `_tree.move_to`, which sets `module.folder = Paths.canon(target_folder)` (builder_tree.gd:118). `move_folder` computes the correct `destination = target_folder.path_join(leaf)` at :1682 and then throws it away for the owner case: `if module.owns_folder() and Paths.same(module.folder, source): return _move_one(module, target_folder, leaf)` -- `target_folder`, not `destination`. PROVEN on Godot 4.7: {Card/Card.guitkx (owner), Card/Card.style.guitkx, Card/components/Bit/Bit.guitkx} after `place_at(owner, "res://X/Other")` becomes res://X/Other/Card.guitkx, res://X/Other/Card.style.guitkx, res://X/Other/components/Bit/Bit.guitkx. The `Card/` folder is gone; the companion and the nested child are loose in `Other`, and `Bit` now sits in an `Other/components/` folder belonging to whatever else lives there. Unity would have produced Other/Card/Card.uitkx with everything under it. The subtree guard is also absent from `place_module` -- only `move_folder` has one (:1686-1688) -- so dragging the owner FILE into its own subtree is unguarded. Untested: builder_chrome_test.gd:945-968 re-files `app.style.guitkx`, a companion that by definition never owns its folder.

Fixing FP-02 by routing `move_folder`'s owner case through a corrected `place_module` fixes those four at the same time, which strengthens the case for that shape.

**To build:** In `place_module`, compute `var into := target_folder.path_join(module.name) if module.owns_folder() else target_folder` and use `into` for both the `place_at` call and the `destination` the ledger records. Add the missing subtree guard before it: `if module.owns_folder() and Paths.is_under(target_folder, module.folder): toast("Can't move %s inside itself." % module.name); return false`. In `move_folder`, route the owner delegation through the corrected `place_module` (which is what Unity does) so there is one implementation of the rule. Note the ledger's `record_move` destination at :1733 must move with it -- today the two agree only because both are wrong in the same direction, and fixing one alone would make undo replay a move to a path nothing occupies.

**Godot specifics:** `builder_module.gd owns_folder()` (:113-119) already encodes the rule correctly including the companion exclusion -- only the call sites ignore it. `builder_tree.gd move_to` (:104-139) already re-roots the subtree correctly relative to whatever folder it is given, so no document-layer change is needed; pass it the right folder. Keep the preload-const referencing (`const Paths = preload(...)`) rather than `RuitkBuilderPaths`, per the class-cache hazard. The `layout.repath(from, module.file_path(), false)` call in `move_folder` (:1710) will need the folder-first form Unity uses (BuilderWindow.cs:3674-3706) once the owner carries its folder, or every child's card position on the canvas is orphaned. Headlessly testable end to end -- builder_chrome_test.gd already builds a real window over an in-memory workspace.

**Risk:** Every component library in this repo uses the owner layout (`components/row/row.guitkx`). One drag in the folder pane flattens it, scatters companions and nested children into the destination, and -- combined with FP-01 -- the resulting `Other/components/` collision is a live overwrite. Nothing warns; the toast says "Moved Card -- applies on Save".

### `FP-03` Folding is destroyed by every rebuild -- collapse a folder, type one character, it springs open

**Unity does:** The collapsed set is the ONE piece of state the pane owns, "because that is a fact about the viewer rather than about the tree" (BuilderFolderPane.cs:23-24). `_collapsed` is a path-keyed, case-insensitive HashSet (:43-44); `Toggle` flips membership and rebuilds (:319-324); `Emit` re-reads it on every rebuild (`folded = hasContents && _collapsed.Contains(node.Path)`, :145) and returns early after the folder row (:147-148). A rebuild therefore restores exactly the fold shape the viewer left, and a nested folder's own state is preserved and re-applied when its ancestor reopens.

**Godot today:** ABSENT. There is no collapsed set and no restore. `rebuild()` calls `Tree.clear()`, which frees every TreeItem, and `_ensure_folder` creates fresh items whose `collapsed` defaults to false. Only the SELECTION is restored. `rebuild()` runs on every model change -- `_after_model_change` (builder_window.gd:891) fires on every `apply_edit`, i.e. every applied source edit, every canvas gesture and every replayed undo -- plus on reproject (:848) and after save (:1979). PROVEN on Godot 4.7: setting `collapsed = true` on the root folder row and calling `rebuild()` leaves `collapsed = false`. Scroll position goes with it -- `clear()` resets it, and only a selected row is scrolled back to (`select_path` -> `scroll_to_item`, :296).

**To build:** Add `var _collapsed := {}` keyed by `Paths.key(folder_path)`. In `_ensure_folder`, set `item.collapsed = _collapsed.has(Paths.key(path))` after creating the item. Connect `Tree.item_collapsed(item)` and write the item's folder path into or out of `_collapsed`, read from its metadata dictionary. Capture and restore the vertical scroll across `rebuild()` as well -- a pane that jumps to the top on every keystroke is the same defect wearing a different hat. Do not prune the set on a folder move; Unity does not either, and a moved folder losing its fold is Unity's behaviour and acceptable.

**Godot specifics:** `Tree.item_collapsed(item)` is the signal (it fires both directions; read `item.collapsed`). The folder item's path is already on the item as `item.get_metadata(0)["folder"]` -- the pane's own Dictionary-vs-String type discrimination (:248-250) makes this a one-line lookup with no second index, which is the property that comment was written to buy. `Tree.clear()` frees the items, so the state must live on the pane. Use `Paths.key()` for the dictionary key so the set is case-folded the way Unity's OrdinalIgnoreCase HashSet is. `TreeItem.collapsed` is readable under --headless (the probe above proves it), so assert it beside `_test_folder_pane` at tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:521.

**Risk:** The pane's only viewer-owned state does not survive a keystroke. A user who folds three folders to see the fourth gets them all back the moment they type -- which makes folding useless in a tree of any size, and the tree that needs folding is exactly the one the pane exists for.

### `FP-05` The FOLDERS header does not fold, and no pane view state is persisted

**Unity does:** UB-208: the pane sits in the left panel above the library, "fixed height, expanded by default, foldable for when the library needs the room". The header reads exactly "(caret)  FOLDERS", is `MouseCursor.Link`, carries the tooltip "fold the tree away and give the library the height", and a left PointerDown toggles the fold and StopPropagation()s (BuilderWindow.cs:367-374). `ApplyFoldersFold` sets `display = None/Flex` and retexts the label. **Godot today:** ABSENT. `pane_header` builds an HBoxContainer with an uppercased Label and an optional trailing Control -- no caret, no gesture, no tooltip -- and builder_window.gd:327 calls it with no trailing control. The left column is a VSplitContainer with `split_offset = -210` hard-set at assembly; grep across builder/ finds exactly that one line, so the user's own drag is never captured. `builder_layout.gd` persists camera, zoom and card positions per tree but no pane geometry.

**To build:** Pass a small toggle Button as `pane_header`'s trailing control (the parameter already exists for this), or make the header label clickable, and have it set `_folders.visible` plus a caret in the header text. Persist the choice alongside the VSplitContainer's `split_offset` -- the builder already writes per-tree view state through `builder_layout.gd`, which is the natural home, or an EditorSettings metadata key.

**Godot specifics:** A Label's `mouse_filter` defaults to `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE`, so a click handler on the header label needs `mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` plus a `gui_input` connection -- exactly the Control.mouse_filter trap this kind of port falls into, which is why a trailing Button is the lower-risk shape. `visible = false` on the pane is the analogue of Unity's `display: None` and correctly removes it from the VSplitContainer's layout. Because the builder Window is hidden rather than freed on close, a session-local fold already survives closing the window; only an editor restart loses it, so persistence is the smaller half.

**Risk:** On a small editor window the folder tree takes 240px the library cannot reclaim, and UB-208's stated reason for the fold -- the library needs the room -- is unmet. Losing the splitter position on every editor restart is the same complaint in slower motion.

**Unity does:** Once a drag passes the threshold the folder under the pointer tints to `Color(1f, 0.835f, 0.310f, 0.15f)` -- the builder's selection gold at 15% alpha, the same colour the canvas rings a selected card with. **Godot today:** ABSENT. `drop_mode_flags` is never set, so Tree renders no drop indicator, and nothing else in the pane paints a row background during a drag. Give the ghost the builder's chrome (a PanelContainer carrying the kind tint) while you are there.

Colours must come from `canvas_palette.gd` (the hand-written @tool script, per the recorded divergence) -- do not add a literal here, which is the drift BuilderPalette.cs:8-16 exists to prevent.

**Risk:** The pane's one destructive gesture is aimed blind. With FP-01 and FP-02 unfixed, aiming blind is how a user drops onto the wrong folder and loses a file.

### `FP-09` Refusals are silent or generic -- the specific toasts Unity produces are unreachable from the pane

**Unity does:** One drag produces five distinct toasts plus two deliberate silences. The pane toasts "Can't move a folder into itself" on a self/subtree drop. The window toasts "Read-only file", "Can't move X inside itself", "X.uitkx is already there", "Could not move X.uitkx", and on success "Moved X.uitkx - applies on Save". The read-only case is worse: `_drop_target_for` does not consult `read_only`, so the drop is accepted by the cursor, reaches `place_module`, which returns false at :1729 with no message, and the window's generic handler toasts "Couldn't move %s into %s." -- the same sentence for read-only, for a collision (once FP-01 lands) and for an unknown module. Success is toasted correctly.

**To build:** Two halves. In the pane: keep `_drop_target_for` refusing the illegal folder drops (the forbidden cursor is legitimate feedback and is more than Unity gives), but emit a refusal signal -- or extend `refile_requested` with a reason -- so the window can toast the sentence, since the capabilities spec's rule is that every outcome is reported (UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:263-265). In the window: replace the single generic toast at :671-674 with specific ones, by having `place_module` return a reason or toast at each refusal site where the fact is known. The read-only case most needs its own words, because the state column already tells the user the file is read-only and a generic "couldn't move" does not connect the two.

**Godot specifics:** `toast()` already exists on the window and is the right channel -- the console is hidden behind Trace and comes forward only on a failed compile round (builder_window.gd:735-737), so a drag refusal sent there is invisible. Godot polls `_can_drop_data` continuously during a drag, so it must stay pure and cheap -- never toast from inside it; emit on `_drop_data` or route the refusal through the window. All of this is headlessly testable by calling `place_module`/`move_folder` directly, which is how tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:945-995 already works.

**Risk:** A refused gesture reads as "the builder ignored me" -- the exact failure the window's own toast-layer comment (builder_window.gd:387-391) says the toast exists to prevent. And a dead toast in `move_folder` is a maintenance trap: it looks covered and is not.

### `FP-10` `place_module` computes the import rewrites and throws them away instead of recording them in the ledger

**Unity does:** `MoveModule` records every rewrite `_workspace.MoveToPath` returns into the ledger "beside the move, so the entry describes the file contents completely - a redo that restored a buffer recorded BEFORE the rewrite would otherwise put the stale specifier back". UB-184/UB-188 make it load-bearing: free placement is only safe because a move carries its imports.

**Godot today:** HALF DONE. `move_folder` gets it right -- it captures a snapshot and records every rewrite (`for rewrite in workspace.reconcile_imports(snapshot): ledger.record(...)`, :1712-1715). `place_module` does not: it takes a snapshot at :1734, calls `_move_one` (which internally does its own capture/reconcile inside `workspace._move`), then calls `workspace.reconcile_imports(snapshot)` at :1743 and DISCARDS the array. So a single-module re-file leaves the rewritten importers dirty with nothing in the ledger naming them, and the history panel reports the move as touching one file when it touched several. The double reconcile is also redundant -- the inner one already fixed the tree.

**To build:** Mirror `move_folder`: `for rewrite in workspace.reconcile_imports(snapshot): ledger.record(str(rewrite["file_path"]), str(rewrite["before"]), str(rewrite["after"]))`, inside the `ledger.begin`/`ledger.end` scope that already wraps the move. While there, decide whether the outer capture/reconcile pair is wanted at all given `place_at` reconciles internally -- if it is kept it should record; if it is dropped, take the rewrites from `place_at`'s return value, which already passes them through.

**Godot specifics:** `reconcile_imports` returns an Array of Dictionaries with `file_path`/`before`/`after` (see the `move_folder` call site) -- use `str()` on the reads, per this codebase's untyped-Dictionary discipline. `ledger.record` inside an open `begin`/`end` scope joins the same entry (builder_ledger.gd:137), so no extra undo step appears. Assert it by counting `w.ledger.entries()[-1].changes.size()` after re-filing a module something imports; the fixture at tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:138-143 already has an importer relationship.

**Risk:** Lower than it looks, because undo replays a MOVE through `workspace.move_to_path` (builder_window.gd:2134-2136), which reconciles again and self-heals the specifiers. What is genuinely wrong today is the history: an entry claiming to have moved one file while silently editing three, so a user reading the ledger cannot see what a move did -- which is the visibility Unity's comment says the record is for.

**Unity does:** n/a -- this is a gap in the Godot leg's own verification, and it is why the four defects above survived. Unity's pane is verified by use rather than by suite, but Unity's `MoveModuleToFolder` also carries all four guards inline in one method where no call site can bypass them.

The gap is real but narrower than 'nothing exercises this pane' -- it is that no test routes a payload through the Tree's own hit-test, and no test uses a fixture in which the two critical defects could show.

**To build:** Three additions, ascending cost. (1) Drive `_can_drop_data`/`_drop_data` with real payload Dictionaries against a laid-out pane after `await process_frame`, the way the canvas payload table at :370-380 already does -- that covers FP-06 and the folder-vs-file target rule. (2) Extend `_test_folder_pane_refiles` with an owner-carries-its-folder case and a name-collision case; both are pure model assertions and cost nothing. (3) Add a folder-pane block to addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd: pick up a file row, hover a folder row, release, print OK/BROKEN -- that rig is the only thing in the repo that tests input routing rather than model calls, and this pane is the builder's only other drag surface.

### `FP-12` The folder caret is a frozen glyph that contradicts Godot's own fold arrow beside it

**Unity does:** The caret is part of the label text and states the fold: U+25B8 collapsed, U+25BE expanded, each followed by two spaces so the file rows' three-space indent lines up under it. A node with no contents gets three spaces instead.

**Godot today:** WRONG. `_ensure_folder` sets the collapsed caret unconditionally and nothing ever re-texts it. Proven by probe: an expanded folder row still shows the collapsed caret. Meanwhile Tree draws its OWN expand/collapse arrow to the left of the text, so every folder row shows two carets that disagree the moment anything is expanded -- which, since everything is always expanded (FP-03), is always.

**To build:** Drop the text caret: Godot's Tree already draws a real, correct, clickable arrow, and a second static one is noise. If a visual marker is wanted (Unity's reason is that indentation alone reads as a wall of text), use a folder glyph that does not encode state, consistent with the pane's existing per-kind glyph vocabulary at :36-44. If the text caret is kept, drive it from `_collapsed` once FP-03 lands and update it on `item_collapsed`.

**Godot specifics:** Tree draws the arrow from the theme icons `arrow`/`arrow_collapsed` for any item with children; it is not suppressible per item and should not be. Text glyphs remain the right call for headless testability (the pane's own stated reason at :34-35) -- the fix is to remove one glyph, not to add an icon.

**Risk:** Cosmetic, but it is a UI element asserting a fact that is false on every row, in a pane whose job is to tell the truth about the tree.

### `FP-13` Files and subfolders interleave by lexical path order instead of being grouped

**Unity does:** `Emit` fixes the order at every level: the folder's own row, then all subfolders recursively (case-insensitively alphabetical via SortedDictionary), then the files sitting directly in it. Subfolders always precede files.

**Godot today:** INTERLEAVED. `rebuild()` makes one pass over modules sorted by full canonical path and creates each folder item lazily on first encounter, so a folder item is inserted wherever its first module's path sorts to. Proven by probe: files came before the `components/` subfolder because 'a' < 'c'; a file named `zeta.guitkx` in the same folder would fall after it. Godot's sort key is better than Unity's (full canonical path, stable and matching what is displayed, where Unity sorts on `module.Name` while displaying the file name, with an unstable introsort that lets a component and its style companion swap between rebuilds -- BuilderFolderPane.cs:153-154), but there is no category grouping at all.

**To build:** Two passes instead of one: create every folder item first (walk the distinct folders, sorted), then attach modules to their folder items. Or keep the single pass and reorder with `TreeItem.move_before`/`move_after`. Either way decide the rule deliberately -- the three legs disagree (Unity: subfolders then files; Unreal: a folder's files then the next folder; Godot: interleaved) -- and Unity is the reference.

**Godot specifics:** TreeItem children are ordered by creation, with `move_before`/`move_after` available afterwards. The two-pass shape is cheaper and clearer -- the `folders` Dictionary already exists at :176. Keep `Paths.key` as the sort key; case-folded is correct for the filesystems this ships on (builder_paths.gd:12-16).

**Risk:** Low. The order is stable and alphabetical, so nothing reshuffles under the user; it just does not read as a file tree, where the convention everywhere else in the editor is folders first.

### `FP-15` `_common_root` is unguarded for a tree with no shared segment or a module outside res://

**Unity does:** Unity has the same hole and does not guard it either: two modules on different drives give `rootPath = ""`, the root row renders as caret-plus-nothing and the drive letter becomes a visible first segment; two sharing only the drive give `rootPath = "C:"` and `Path.Combine("C:", segment)` produces drive-RELATIVE child paths that will not compare equal to the modules' own canonicalised folders, breaking the drop-target link. Neither case is guarded or commented.

**Godot today:** SAME HOLE, different shape. `_common_root` trims `res://` and rejoins. When nothing is shared, `common` is empty and `base` is `"res://"`, whose `get_file()` is "" -- so the root folder row renders with an empty label, exactly Unity's caret-plus-nothing. A module whose folder is not under `res://` survives `trim_prefix("res://")` unchanged, so `_folder_item` builds bogus child paths like `res://c:/foo` that can never match the module's real folder -- and those are the strings the drop target compares against.

**To build:** Guard both ends. When `common` is empty, label the root row something honest ("project root") rather than nothing. When a module's folder does not begin with `res://` after canon, either exclude it from the common-prefix fold and hang it under a separate root, or refuse to derive a folder path for it -- a folder item whose path can never match a real module folder is a drop target that silently does nothing.

**Godot specifics:** `Paths.canon` already folds an absolute OS path back under res:// when it names something inside the project and returns it simplified-but-untouched when it genuinely does not, so the test for 'genuinely outside' is `not path.begins_with("res://")` after canon -- and `_common_root` should be using `Paths.canon(module.folder)` rather than the raw field in the first place. `"res://".get_file()` returns "" in Godot; `"res://".path_join("a")` correctly yields `res://a` (the leading-slash branch), so the join arithmetic itself is sound -- only the labelling and the out-of-project case need work.

**Risk:** Rare: the import closure has to pull in a module from outside the project, or the tree has to span two disjoint top-level folders. But when it happens the pane draws an unlabelled root and a drop onto that branch resolves to a folder path no module holds.

### Library pane: sections, search, drag sources, selection sync, card framing, "+ new"

### `LIB-01` The library's drag source is unreachable: every row is a Button with the default MOUSE_FILTER_STOP, which stops Godot's drag walk before it reaches the pane

**Unity does:** A library pill is `draggable` and arms `BuilderDragService.Begin(payload, label, row, pointerId, pos)` on PointerDown, which CAPTURES the pointer to the row (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:701-729, BuilderDragService.cs:30-98). Past a 5px travel threshold a ghost chip appears at the window root and follows the cursor; the drop resolves from a fresh hit-test on release. Capability spec §10 states the contract flatly: "Entries drag onto the canvas."

**Godot today:** absent in practice, present on paper. `_get_drag_data` is implemented on the PANE (builder_library_pane.gd:267-280) and correctly returns `{source:"library", kind, name}` when called directly. But rows are plain `Button`s created in `_entry_row` (:295-321) with no `mouse_filter` override, and `Button`'s default is `MOUSE_FILTER_STOP`. Godot 4's `Viewport::_gui_get_drag_data` walks up from the pressed control and BREAKS at the first STOP filter, so the pane's `_get_drag_data` is never called. VERIFIED on the shipped class with Godot 4.7 headless, pushing real InputEventMouseButton/MouseMotion at a laid-out pane (260x800, row rect [P:(0,103) S:(260,31)], press at (130,118.5), 12 moves of (15,8)): AS SHIPPED -> `gui_is_dragging()=false`, `gui_get_drag_data()=null`; with only `row.mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_PASS` changed -> `dragging=true`, data `{"source":"library","kind":"element","name":"VBoxContainer"}`. Nothing else was changed between the two runs. The `ScrollContainer` between `_body` and the pane is already PASS, so the row filter is the only blocker.

**To build:** In `_entry_row` (builder_library_pane.gd:295-321) set `row.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_PASS` on every entry Button. PASS keeps the Button's own press/hover behaviour (so click-to-insert and the double-click handler still work) while letting the event continue up to the pane. Then add a REAL routing test to `tests/builder_chrome_test.gd`: push InputEventMouseButton(press) + a run of InputEventMouseMotion at a row's centre through `root.push_input` and assert `get_viewport().gui_is_dragging()` and `gui_get_drag_data()["name"]` — not `has_method("_get_drag_data")`.

**Godot specifics:** This is a pure `Control.mouse_filter` / input-routing defect and it is the exact same class of bug the canvas already fixed and documented (builder_canvas_host.gd:230-244: "A card is a PanelContainer full of Labels, and Godot's default mouse_filter for those is STOP -- so a press anywhere on a card was consumed... all of them worked only in the gaps BETWEEN cards"). The lesson was learned on the canvas and not applied to the library. Note that headless CAN test this: the viewport's drag machinery runs headless even though BaseButton's `pressed`/`button_down` signals do not fire there, so a drag-routing assertion is CI-able while a click assertion is not.

### `LIB-02` Both gates over LIB-01 are green over a dead gesture: the parity sweep greps an identifier and the chrome test asserts `has_method`

**Unity does:** n/a — this is a gate-quality finding about the Godot leg. Unity's equivalent behaviour is exercised by the drag service's own capture/threshold/hit-test path (BuilderDragService.cs:30-171).

**Godot today:** wrong. `tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:362` reads `_check(w.library_pane().has_method("_get_drag_data"), "the library is a drag SOURCE")` — a method-existence probe that passes for a method no input can reach. `tests/builder_parity.gd:81` maps "drag sources" -> `func _get_drag_data`, a grep. `addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd:229` calls `lib0._get_drag_data(grab)` DIRECTLY and then `canvas._can_drop_data`/`canvas._drop_data` directly, so the rig prints "DND HANDSHAKE OK" and "DND DROP OK" while the real gesture is dead — it tests the two ends of a handshake and skips the engine that has to connect them. The section comment at builder_chrome_test.gd:355-359 even says the drag "existed as a promise and not as a gesture"; the test written to close that hole reproduces it.

**To build:** Replace the `has_method` assertion with the real-input assertion described in LIB-01. In `addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd`, drive the drag through `Viewport.push_input` (press on the row, N motions, release over a markup row) instead of calling `_get_drag_data`/`_drop_data`, and print OK only when `gui_is_dragging()` went true and the buffer changed. Keep the direct-call check as a second, separate line so a failure distinguishes "the payload is wrong" from "the gesture never started".

**Godot specifics:** `has_method` is never evidence in Godot for anything routed through `_gui_input`/`_get_drag_data`/`_can_drop_data` — those are engine callbacks whose reachability depends entirely on `mouse_filter`, `clip_contents` and the control's rect, none of which a grep or a method probe sees. A headless suite CAN push input at a Control if the pane is given an explicit size (a Control parented straight to the root Window does not get one from `set_anchors_preset` in the headless SceneTree — set `.size` explicitly, or the ScrollContainer measures 0 tall and every hit-test misses).

### `LIB-03` The selection mirror is visually dead: `button_pressed` is set before `toggle_mode`, which Godot ignores

**Unity does:** `SetSelected` paints the matching pill with a gold outline (BuilderPalette.Select 1.000,0.835,0.310) and a 15%-alpha gold wash, and every rebuild re-derives it from `IsSelected(entry)` (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:86-109, :655-668). The library is "the natural place to see WHAT the selected thing is" (:70-73).

**Godot today:** wrong. `_entry_row` does `row.button_pressed = true` on line 313 and `row.toggle_mode = true` on line 314 — in that order. Godot 4's `BaseButton::set_pressed()` early-returns when `toggle_mode` is false, so the assignment is a no-op and the row is never drawn pressed. VERIFIED headless on Godot 4.7: `Button.new(); a.button_pressed = true; a.toggle_mode = true` -> `button_pressed == false`; the reverse order -> `true`. VERIFIED end to end on the shipped pane: `select_component("VBoxContainer")` then walking `_body` for any row with `button_pressed` -> `false`. So `select_component` rebuilds the whole pane on every focus change and changes nothing on screen.

**To build:** Swap the two lines in builder_library_pane.gd:313-314 (`toggle_mode` first, then `button_pressed`). Better: stop using a toggle Button's pressed look as the selection paint — it borrows the editor theme's pressed style, which is not a selection colour. Give the row a `StyleBoxFlat` override (border + tinted bg) from `canvas_palette.gd`/`builder_chrome_parts.gd` so the selected pill reads like the canvas's gold ring, matching Unity's Select colour. Add a test that calls `select_component` and asserts the selected row is visually distinguished.

**Godot specifics:** `BaseButton::set_pressed` is a silent no-op without `toggle_mode` — no warning, no error, and GDScript property assignment order in a builder function is easy to get wrong. Because the pane is hand-written `@tool` GDScript rather than a `.guitkx` module, there is no reconciler prop-diff to catch it either; the reconciler's bailout is irrelevant here. If the paint moves to a StyleBoxFlat, source it from `canvas_palette.gd` (a hand-written `@tool` script) and NOT from a `.style.guitkx` module — a generated `.gd` carries no `@tool`, so its `static var` initialisers never run in the editor and the style comes back empty.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity: ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/Library/BuilderLibraryPane.cs:86-109 (SetSelected/IsSelected) and :655-668 (selected border + wash). godot: addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_library_pane.gd:312-315 and :363-367 (`select_component`); confirmed by headless probe on Godot 4.7.

### `LIB-04` The parity entry `SyncLibrarySelection -> func select_component` is green over a function that does nothing visible and mirrors the wrong thing

**Unity does:** `SyncLibrarySelection` (BuilderWindow.cs:1737-1787) is a real resolver: a markup row's text is trimmed to its tag, the tag is looked up in `_workspace.Modules` (the MODULE wins over a native of the same name) and `SetSelected(file, null)` or `SetSelected(null, tag)` is called; a card selection calls `SetSelected(node.FilePath, null)` (BuilderWindow.cs:711-718). The mirror matches by FILE first (survives a rename) and by NAME second.

**Godot today:** partial/wrong. `tests/builder_parity.gd:54` answers `SyncLibrarySelection` with `func select_component`, which exists — but (a) it takes a NAME, never a file path (builder_library_pane.gd:363), (b) it is only ever fed `card.exports[0]` of the FOCUSED module (builder_window.gd:2160-2164), so a module with no exports or a second export is unmatched, (c) `_entry_row` only applies it when `kind == ENTRY_COMPONENT` (:312), so selecting a style/util/hook-module card highlights nothing, and (d) `_on_row_clicked` (builder_window.gd:1007-1021) calls `select_module(card.file_path)` and never resolves the clicked row's TAG, so clicking a `<Button>` markup row does not light `<Button>` in NATIVE ELEMENTS. Combined with LIB-03 the whole feature is invisible anyway. No test anywhere calls `select_component` (grep over tests/ finds only builder_parity.gd's string).

**To build:** Change the signal to `select_entry(file_path: String, name: String)` mirroring Unity's `SetSelected`: match a workspace row by canonical file path (`Paths.canon`/`Paths.same`) first, falling back to a bare-name match for native tags and built-in hooks only when the entry has no file. Store `file_path` in each workspace row's meta (`row.set_meta("entry_path", card.file_path)`) so a component exporting two names lights both rows, as Unity's does. Add the markup-row resolver in `builder_window.gd::_on_row_clicked`: trim the row text to its tag, look it up in `graph.cards` exports (module wins), else pass it as a native name. Then make the parity entry point at the resolver, not at `select_component`.

**Godot specifics:** Store the path in `set_meta` rather than closing over it, so `entries()` and `_row_under` can both read it. `Paths.canon`/`Paths.same` already exist in `builder/document/builder_paths.gd` — use them instead of raw string compare, because the workspace keys on canonical paths. Keep the early-return-on-unchanged guard (`select_component` has one at :364-365) so the mirror does not rebuild the pane on every re-selection; the pane is hand-written, so there is no reconciler bailout to absorb the churn.
