### `LIB-05` Double-clicking a workspace row FRAMES the card and also INSERTS the component into the focused module, once or twice

**Unity does:** The double-click runs INSTEAD of arming the drag and instead of anything else: `if (evt.clickCount >= 2 && FocusComponent != null && !IsNullOrEmpty(captured.FilePath)) { FocusComponent(captured.FilePath); evt.StopPropagation(); return; }` (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:706-725). Unity has NO click action on a library row at all, deliberately: "there is no click handler on the library body, so a misjudged click never mutates the buffer at a position the user did not choose" (:701-705, UB-32 at UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:648-661).

**Godot today:** wrong. `_entry_row` wires BOTH `row.pressed` -> `entry_activated` (line 316) and `row.gui_input` -> `entry_framed` on `double_click` (lines 317-320), with no mutual exclusion. Godot's Button uses `ACTION_MODE_BUTTON_RELEASE`, so the FIRST click of a double-click emits `pressed` on its release, before any `double_click` event exists — `_on_library_activated` (builder_window.gd:556-583) then runs `apply_edit`, inserting `<Name />` after the last markup row of the focused card. The second press carries `double_click=true` and fires `entry_framed`, and its own release fires `pressed` again. So a double-click to frame a card inserts one or two elements into a file the user was not editing, records one or two ledger entries, and triggers a preview round each. `entry_framed`'s only consumer (`_on_library_framed`, builder_window.gd:536-544) also calls `select_module`, which moves the focus onto the framed card — so the second insert can land in a different file than the first.

**To build:** Move the double-click test AHEAD of the activation path, the way Unity does. Concretely: drop the `pressed` connection and drive both gestures from one `gui_input` handler that inspects `InputEventMouseButton` — on `double_click` emit `entry_framed` and `accept_event()`; on a single release emit `entry_activated`. Or keep `pressed` but set `row.button_mask`/gate it behind a short timer that a subsequent `double_click` cancels (worse — prefer the single handler). Add a chrome test that feeds a row a synthetic double-click InputEvent through `gui_input` and asserts the focused module's buffer is UNCHANGED while `entry_framed` fired once.

**Godot specifics:** `Control.gui_input` is emitted before `_gui_input` in `Control::_call_gui_input`, so a `gui_input` handler can `accept_event()` and suppress BaseButton's own handling — that is the clean single-funnel here. Note the first insert calls `apply_edit` -> `reproject()` -> `_library.rebuild()`, which `queue_free`s the very Button being clicked mid-gesture; the second press then lands on a freshly built Button, so the behaviour is timing-dependent and will look intermittent in a field test. Headless cannot reproduce it (BaseButton emits no signals under the headless DisplayServer — verified), so the test must call `gui_input.emit(event)` directly rather than push viewport input.

### `LIB-06` Framing a card fits BOTH axes — UB-85, already found and fixed in Unity, reintroduced from scratch

**Unity does:** `FocusNode` solves the zoom so the card's WIDTH occupies 88% of the viewport width, never the height: `cardW = CardWidthFor(LodOf(zoom)); zoom = Clamp(width * 0.88f / cardW, 0.10f, 2.2f)` solved twice because card width is LOD-dependent; a card taller than the viewport is pinned at 6% of viewport height instead of centred (BuilderCanvasHost.cs:482-523). UB-85 records why: "UB-80's frame fitted BOTH axes, so a card with hundreds of markup rows solved to ZoomMin — it did zoom, all the way out, which is indistinguishable from not zooming. FIX: fit WIDTH only... the gesture now lands at the same readable zoom for every card instead of one that swings with how much markup a file happens to hold."

**Godot today:** wrong, identically to pre-fix Unity. `builder_canvas_metrics.gd:361-368` computes `zoom = clamp_zoom(minf(usable.x / size.x, usable.y / size.y))` against `drawn_height(card, Lod.SECTIONS)` and always centres on both axes. VERIFIED headless with synthetic cards in a 900x600 viewport: 5 markup rows -> zoom 2.200 (LOD 2); 40 rows -> zoom 0.496 (LOD 1); 200 rows -> zoom 0.105, i.e. ZOOM_MIN, LOD 0 = a PILL. Double-clicking a large component in the library zooms all the way out to a pill. The comment at :359-360 ("Measured at the SECTIONS layout, then clamped: a card is drawn at whatever band the solved zoom lands in, and solving against the band's own height would be circular") acknowledges the circularity and resolves it by ignoring it rather than by Unity's two-pass convergence.

**To build:** In `builder_canvas_metrics.gd::frame_card`, drop the height term: solve `zoom = clamp_zoom(viewport.x * 0.88 / card_width_for(lod))`, run it twice (pass 1 with the current/SECTIONS width, pass 2 with `card_width_for(lod_of(zoom_1))`) — it converges because there are only three bands. Keep the horizontal centring; replace the vertical centring with Unity's rule: if `drawn_height(card, lod_of(zoom)) * zoom > viewport.y`, set `camera.y = viewport.y * 0.06 - card.y * zoom` so the title stays on screen, else centre. Replace the fixed 60px margin with the 0.88 fraction so a small viewport cannot drive `usable` negative. Add a metrics test asserting that a 5-row and a 200-row card frame to the SAME zoom.

**Godot specifics:** Pure static math in `builder_canvas_metrics.gd`, headlessly testable with a synthetic `Graph.Card` — no EditorInterface, no window, no input routing. `builder_canvas_host.gd:201-206` already routes through `set_camera`, which emits `camera_changed` and so persists the framed view through `_on_camera_changed` — that half matches Unity's SaveLayout+ZoomChanged and should be left alone.

### `LIB-07` No live drop-band hint: the drag is resolved blind and the user cannot see before/inside/after

**Unity does:** Every pointer move during a drag re-runs the canvas hit-test, stores the result on the drag machine, and repaints the edge overlay from it: `Target = HitTester?.Invoke(panelPos); RepaintHints?.Invoke();` (BuilderDragService.cs:100-114, BuilderCanvasHost.cs:190-198, BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:915-948). UB-31 is explicitly about reading the band from render-state closures instead. The capability spec makes the hint part of the contract: "a drop lands exactly where the hint is drawn: middle band — a tinted outlined box over the row; bottom band — a dashed caret in the gap under the row; top band — a dashed caret above the row" (UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:254-263).

**Godot today:** absent. The three-band resolution itself exists and is correct (`builder_drag.gd:96-153` with `Metrics.row_hit`'s BAND_EDGE = 1/3 vs Unity's 0.3/0.7 — an acceptable engine-side difference), but nothing paints it. `builder_canvas_host.gd:457-459` answers `_can_drop_data` with `return data is Dictionary and data.has("source")` — unconditionally true, computing no target and requesting no redraw — and grep for a drop hint across `builder_canvas_edges.gd`, `canvas_view.guitkx` and `canvas_view.gd` returns nothing. The user drags with no feedback beyond the engine's drag preview and finds out where it landed after the fact.

**To build:** In `builder_canvas_host.gd::_can_drop_data`, when the payload is a library/row payload, run `Drag.resolve(graph, at_position, camera, zoom)`, store `{card_index, section, row_index, band}` on the host, and `queue_redraw()` the overlay when it changed (guard on change, or every motion repaints). Paint it in the screen-space `_draw` overlay that already exists for the Bezier edges (`builder_canvas_edges.gd`): a caret above/below the row for bands 0/2 and an outlined box over the row for band 1, using `Metrics.section_stack`/`row_hit` for the row's exact rect so the hint and the drop cannot disagree. Clear it on `NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END`.

**Godot specifics:** `_can_drop_data` IS Godot's per-move hook — it is called on every motion while a drag is in flight, which is the natural place to update the hint; there is no separate move callback. The overlay must be a Control with `mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE` (as `builder_canvas_edges.gd:64` already is) or it will itself break the hit-test. Use `NOTIFICATION_DRAG_BEGIN`/`NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END` to arm and clear, and remember that `_can_drop_data` still has to keep returning true for the payloads the window accepts — do not start refusing there, the comment at :450-456 is right that the resolve is the window's.

### `LIB-08` "+N more" appends the hidden rows at the BOTTOM of the pane, below every other section, and forgets itself on the next rebuild

**Unity does:** `_expanded` is a `HashSet<string>` keyed by section, held on the pane precisely so it survives a rebuild: "Collapse is a VIEW state... rebuilding the list from a new graph must not close a drawer the user just opened" (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:65-67). The fold row flips to "show less" when the section is open, is emitted at every section END, and the expanded rows render IN their section (:539-581, :614-657).

**Godot today:** wrong. `_show_all` (builder_library_pane.gd:246-251) calls `rebuild()` and then appends `entries[FOLD_AFTER..]` to `_body` — i.e. after every subsequent section has already been added. VERIFIED headless on the shipped pane: after clicking "+ 50 more" on NATIVE ELEMENTS the body reads `[hdr]NATIVE ELEMENTS (55) | 5 rows | [hdr]+ 50 more | [hdr]HOOKS (23) | 5 rows | [hdr]+ 18 more | <AspectRatioContainer> ... <VirtualJoystick>` — the 50 native elements land under the HOOKS fold row. The "+ 50 more" row is not replaced by "show less" and there is no way to re-fold. And the state is not remembered: a plain `rebuild()` immediately after took the row count from 60 back to 10, so any edit (which runs `reproject()` -> `_library.rebuild()` at builder_window.gd:849-850) silently re-folds a drawer the user just opened. The pane's own comment at :63-64 claims the opposite ("A VIEW state -- it survives a rebuild"); `_expanded` does survive, but it governs the section HEADER collapse, not the 5-row fold, and it already defaults to true so `_expanded[kind] = true` in the fold handler is a no-op.

**To build:** Delete `_show_all` and make the 5-row fold read the same per-section state the header toggle uses: a second dictionary `_fold_open := {}` keyed by section kind. In `_add_section`, `limit = filtered.size() if (not _search.is_empty() or _fold_open.get(kind, false)) else mini(filtered.size(), FOLD_AFTER)`, and emit the closing row as "show less" when open and "+N more" when not — at the section's end, so one call site cannot forget it. The fold row's handler flips `_fold_open[kind]` and calls `rebuild()`; the rows then land in their section by construction.

**Godot specifics:** `rebuild()` currently does `child.queue_free()` then `_body.remove_child(child)` in a loop over a `get_children()` snapshot — safe, and it is called from inside the fold Button's own `pressed` handler, which frees the emitting node. That works because `queue_free` is deferred; keep it that way rather than `free()`. Nothing here needs the reconciler — the pane is hand-written `@tool` GDScript, so the fold state is plain member state and is fully headlessly testable through `entries()` and a walk of `_body`.

### `LIB-09` An empty section renders no header at all, and a zero-match search renders literally nothing

**Unity does:** "POC buildLibrary() emits all five headers unconditionally, in order, whether or not the tree contributes a row to any of them — an empty section still tells you the drawer exists. Filtering hides headers" (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:632-634); the gap-filling emission at :645 and :750-757 guarantees it. A zero-match query still renders the hint paragraph, so the pane is never blank (:759-774).

**Godot today:** wrong on both counts. `_add_section` returns early on `filtered.is_empty()` (builder_library_pane.gd:213-214) with no test for whether a filter is active, so a tree with no style modules shows no STYLE MODULES header — the user cannot tell the drawer exists. VERIFIED headless with `graph == null`: the pane renders only NATIVE ELEMENTS and HOOKS; CUSTOM COMPONENTS, STYLE MODULES, UTIL MODULES and HOOK MODULES are entirely absent. A zero-match search (`set_filter("zzzznope")`) renders an empty `_body` — no header, no "no matches" row, no hint.

**To build:** Gate the early return on the filter: `if filtered.is_empty() and not _search.is_empty(): return` — emit the header (with `(0)`) when unfiltered. For the zero-match case add one dim row (`Parts.placeholder("no matches for \"%s\"" % _search)`) so the pane is never blank; the searchable menu already has such a row (`builder_search_menu.gd`), so this is consistent with the rest of the chrome.

**Godot specifics:** `Parts.placeholder` and `Parts.section_heading` already exist in `builder_chrome_parts.gd:47-55, :88-93` and are hand-written `@tool` code, so they are safe to call from editor code — unlike a `.style.guitkx` module, whose `static var` initialisers never run in a non-`@tool` generated `.gd`. Note the current headers are `Button`s carrying the fold arrow and a count, not Labels; an empty section's header should still be clickable (collapsing an empty section is harmless) or made a Label — either is fine, but keep it out of `entries()` by leaving it without the `entry_name` meta.

### `LIB-10` A module created from "+ new" is not placed in the viewport — it lands at a projection slot the camera never moves to

**Unity does:** `ShowCreateMenuAtPointer` computes the world point at the viewport centre `((width*0.5 - camX)/zoom, (height*0.5 - camY)/zoom)`, and `PlaceNewCard(full, x, y)` centres the card on it (`SetPosition(x - cardWidth*0.5, y - 200*0.5)`) — BuilderCanvasHost.cs:525-562, :797-837. UB-195: "The library's '+ new' has no cursor at all and passed a fixed world point, which is wherever the user has panned away from. It now places the card in the middle of the viewport - the middle of what they are looking at." A toast follows: "Created X in <folder> - applies on Save".

**Godot today:** absent. `_create_named` (builder_window.gd:1879-1893) creates the module, records the ledger entry, calls `reproject()` and `select_module(path)` — and never places the card. `reproject()` (:821-851) runs `Service.project` (which seeds positions by BFS from the root) then `layout.adopt_unplaced(graph)`, which merely records whatever slot the projection produced. `layout.set_position` EXISTS and its doc comment says exactly the right thing — "Places one card, for a card created at the point the user right-clicked rather than at the next default slot" (builder_canvas_layout.gd:166-169) — but grep shows its only production caller is `_on_card_moved` (builder_window.gd:1032), the drag-persist path. So neither "+ new" nor the canvas right-click create ever uses it, and the camera does not move: on a panned canvas the new card can appear entirely off-screen with no feedback. There is also no create toast (grep for "applies on Save" finds only the two MOVE toasts at :1716 and :1756).

**To build:** After `workspace.create_new(...)` in `_create_named`, compute the world point — `Metrics.screen_to_world(_canvas.size * 0.5, _canvas.camera, _canvas.zoom)` for the library's "+ new", or `Metrics.screen_to_world(_menu_at, ...)` for the canvas right-click — subtract half the card's drawn size (`Metrics.card_width_for(lod)`, `Metrics.drawn_height(card, lod)`) and call `layout.set_position(path, at)` BEFORE `reproject()`, so `adopt_unplaced` finds the slot already taken. Add `toast("Created %s in %s — applies on Save" % [name, folder])`. Test it headlessly: create from a panned camera and assert the new card's `x`/`y` are inside the viewport rect.

**Godot specifics:** `Metrics.screen_to_world` and `world_to_screen` are exact inverses and already carry a comment saying a disagreement "puts the new card somewhere the user did not point" (builder_canvas_metrics.gd:156-159) — use them rather than open-coding the transform. `_canvas.size` can be zero in a window that has not been laid out (the same case `_centre_when_sized` already defers for), so fall back to the projection slot when `size.x <= 0`, exactly as Unity's ShowCreateMenu falls back to (0,0). All of it is `FileAccess`-free and headlessly testable.

**Unity does:** `RevealSelected()` walks the sorted entries counting per-section runs and adds the selected entry's section to `_expanded` when it sits past row 5, before the rebuild that draws the highlight: "A selection that names a folded row OPENS its section, since a highlight nobody can see is not a highlight" (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:82-85, :111-128). Assert it in a test: seed a workspace with seven components, select the last alphabetically, and check `entries()` contains it.

**Godot specifics:** Cheap and pure — `_component_entries()`/`_module_entries()` are already sorted, so the index lookup is a `PackedStringArray.find`. Do it before the rebuild, not after, or the pane repaints twice. Headlessly testable through `entries()` with no window, input routing or EditorInterface.

### `LIB-12` Row tooltips carry generic prose instead of the entry's description — a workspace row never shows its file path

**Unity does:** `tooltip = entry.Description` (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:661). For a native that is the schema's element documentation; for a workspace row it is `node.FilePath` (:420-466), so hovering a component tells you which file it comes from — the one way to disambiguate two same-named things without opening them.

The gesture hint belongs in the hint bar, not on 78 rows.

**Godot specifics:** The path meta is needed anyway for LIB-04's file-keyed selection mirror and for a correct `entry_framed`, so do them together. Reading from the LSP layer is safe from editor code because it is hand-written `@tool` GDScript reached through a preload const; do NOT reach it through a global `class_name`, since `ProjectSettings.save()` truncates the editor class cache to what the running process loaded.

### `LIB-13` `entry_framed` carries only a NAME, so framing resolves to the first card that exports it — regardless of kind

**Unity does:** The row carries `captured.FilePath` and `FocusComponent(path)` is called with it; `FocusNode` resolves `_graph.IndexOf(full)` and returns false when the module has no card, at which point the window toasts "That module has no card on this canvas." (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:706-725, BuilderWindow.cs:1032-1038, BuilderCanvasHost.cs:482-490).

**Godot today:** partial. `entry_framed.emit(name)` (builder_library_pane.gd:320) drops the kind and the file. `_on_library_framed` (builder_window.gd:536-544) then scans `graph.cards` for the FIRST card whose `exports` contains that name and frames it — so a component `Card` and a style module exporting `Card` (exactly the pairing `_validate_name`'s comment at builder_window.gd:1782-1786 says the folder convention is built around) resolve to whichever sorts first by path. There is also no failure branch: when nothing matches, the function returns silently rather than toasting, so a double-click on a row whose card is absent gives no feedback at all.

**To build:** Emit the file path (and kind) with the signal: `signal entry_framed(file_path: String, name: String)`, sourced from the `entry_path` meta added in LIB-12. In `_on_library_framed`, resolve with `graph.index_of(Paths.canon(file_path))` and `toast("That module has no card on this canvas.")` when the index is negative — matching Unity's refusal message and the builder's own "every outcome is reported" rule.

**Godot specifics:** `Graph.index_of` and `Paths.canon` already exist and key on canonical paths, which is what the workspace and the layout store both use; matching on raw strings would break for a module reached through a different path spelling. Keep the signal's payload flat (String, String) so `tests/builder_chrome_test.gd`'s signal-listener sweep and any harness can drive it without constructing a Card.

### `LIB-14` A style or util module with no exports disappears from the palette entirely

**Unity does:** Style and util modules contribute ONE row each, named by `node.Title` (the filename minus the companion infix), independent of what they export — `case BuilderNodeKind.Style: _entries.Add(new Entry { Name = node.Title, ... })` (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:432-466). Only components and hook modules are listed per-export.

**Godot today:** divergent, with a hole. `_module_entries(kind)` (builder_library_pane.gd:165-175) lists one row per EXPORT for style, util AND hook modules. Per-export is a defensible improvement — `drop_module_export` (builder_window.gd:2290-2320) binds a specific export, so dragging a named export is more precise than dragging a module. But a module with zero exports contributes zero rows and vanishes from the pane with no trace. Today `Edits.template_for` seeds every kind with exactly one export (builder_edits.gd:884-894), so a freshly created module does appear — but a user who comments out or deletes the last export loses the module from the library while its card is still on the canvas.

**To build:** Keep the per-export listing, and fall back to one row named `card.title` when `card.exports.is_empty()`, tagged with the module's file path so it still drags and still frames. Assert it: a style module whose buffer has no `export` still has a STYLE MODULES row.

**Godot specifics:** `card.exports` comes from the compiler's `analyzed_decls`, so a module whose buffer momentarily fails to parse also reports zero exports — which is precisely the moment the user most needs to see it is still there. The fallback row therefore also guards the mid-edit case, which the canvas already handles with a placeholder card (canvas_view.guitkx's placeholder branch).

**Unity does:** `BuilderSearchMenu.RememberPointer(evt.position, focusedWindow)` records the press point so "the popup lands under the cursor instead of at the host window's centre" (BuilderSearchMenu.cs:41-50), and `NewFile()` toasts "Open a tree first - new files are created beside it" when `_focusFile` is empty rather than doing nothing (BuilderWindow.cs:5921-5933).

The menu therefore opens under the word LIBRARY, several tens of pixels from the thing that was clicked. And `_on_library_create` -> `prompt_create` returns silently when `workspace == null` (builder_window.gd:1768-1770), so pressing "+ new" with nothing open produces no menu and no message.

**To build:** Anchor on the button: keep a reference to `new_button` and use `new_button.get_screen_position() + Vector2(0, new_button.size.y)`. In `prompt_create`, replace the silent `return` with `toast("Open a tree first — new files are created beside it.")`. Both are one-liners and both are checkable by the shots rig, which already opens this menu (`addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd:508-518`).

The `PopupMenu` is a child of the pane (:99) and so is freed with it — keep it that way rather than making it a `Window` of its own.

### `LIB-16` The drop grammar is written down only in the global hint bar, and it omits the module-drop rule

**Unity does:** A dim wrapped paragraph closes every rebuild of the list, verbatim: "Drag onto a JSX row: top edge inserts before, bottom edge after, middle nests inside. Drag hooks onto BODY; style/util modules onto a card (adds the import). Drag existing rows to reorder." It is the last child of `_listHost` so it scrolls with the content, and it renders even when a search matched nothing — in that case it is the only thing on screen (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:50-53, :759-774).

**Godot today:** partial. The three bands and the hooks-onto-BODY rule are in the window's global hint bar (builder_window.gd:407-416: "Drag Library items onto rows (top=before, bottom=after, middle=inside) or BODY (hooks)"), which is a reasonable engine-side relocation. But the module rule — style/util onto a card adds the import, style onto an ELEMENT applies it — is implemented (`drop_module_export`, builder_window.gd:2290-2320, a genuinely richer behaviour than Unity's) and stated nowhere the user can read. The hint strip is also `clip_text = true` (builder_chrome_parts.gd:83), so on a narrow window the later hints are cut off silently.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The hint bar (builder_window.gd:407-416) carries the short form, and `RuitkBuilderConsole.show_help` (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_console.gd:208-225, reached from the window at :987) carries a long form that spells the bands out on their own line: "LIBRARY — drag an element, hook or component onto a card. The band you drop on decides: / top third = before the row, middle = inside it, bottom third = after it." That is a legitimate engine-side relocation of Unity's per-pane paragraph, it is not `clip_text`-truncated, and it is one keystroke away. What IS genuinely missing from both surfaces is the module-drop rule — that a style/util/hook module dropped on a card adds the import and a style dropped on an ELEMENT applies it — which `drop_module_export` (builder_window.gd:2299-2325) implements and which is richer than anything Unity does. Add that one clause to `show_help` (the natural home, given the hint bar's `clip_text = true` at builder_chrome_parts.gd:86); a per-pane footer is optional and belongs with LIB-09's blank-state fix if it is done at all.

**To build:** Append the missing clause to the hint bar list, or add a per-pane footer Label as the last child of `_body` on every `rebuild()` (which also fixes LIB-09's blank zero-match state). Given `clip_text`, a per-pane wrapped footer is the more reliable of the two: `autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART` on a Label with `size_flags_horizontal = SIZE_EXPAND_FILL`.

**Godot specifics:** `Parts.hint_bar` sets `clip_text = true` deliberately for the one-line strip; a pane footer should NOT reuse it — use a plain Label with autowrap so a long sentence grows taller instead of vanishing, which is exactly the reasoning behind Unity's `whiteSpace = Normal` on the same paragraph.

### `LIB-17` NATIVE ELEMENTS lists 55 curated tags while the compiler's tag vocabulary is open — and the class doc claims 140

**Unity does:** UB-10 (UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:390-396) is precisely the bug of using the seven curated POC tags as a SOURCE list rather than as an ORDER: "Add child element" offered 7 of 72 because it did. The curated array is ordering only; the section is filled from the live schema (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:32-40, :308-331).

**Godot today:** partial, self-consistent. `_element_entries` (builder_library_pane.gd:178-190) leads with five `LEAD_ELEMENTS` and then appends every key of `Compiler.host_tags()` alphabetically — ordering-only, exactly right in shape. But `host_tags` holds 55 entries (verified against addons/reactive_ui_toolkit/guitkx/vocabulary.json), while `guitkx_vocabulary.gen.gd:10` states that "host_tags is the CURATED set (IDE metadata) — the compiler additionally accepts ANY instantiable ClassDB Node class as a tag (open vocabulary, emitted as V.h)". So the palette shows 55 of an open vocabulary. This is NOT UB-10's disagreement bug — `_tag_items` (builder_window.gd:1327) and the unknown-tag check (:1227) read the same 55, so nothing internally contradicts — but the class doc-comment at builder_library_pane.gd:11-12 says "The full host vocabulary is a hundred and forty Godot classes", which the file's own data source contradicts.

**To build:** Decide and record which it is. Either (a) accept the curated 55 as the palette's source, matching the LSP's completion list, and fix the doc-comment at :11-12 to say 55 and why; or (b) fill the section from `ClassDB.get_inheriters_from_class("Node")` filtered by `ClassDB.can_instantiate`, keeping `host_tags` as the lead order — which is Unity's shape and would make the palette match what the compiler actually accepts. If (b), the same source must feed `_tag_items` so the two lists cannot diverge, which is the whole point of UB-10.

**Godot specifics:** `ClassDB.get_inheriters_from_class`/`can_instantiate` are available in `@tool` editor code and headlessly, so option (b) is testable in CI. It would take the section from 55 to several hundred rows, which makes LIB-08's per-section fold load-bearing rather than cosmetic — fix that first. Note `host_tags` values are the tag name itself (no descriptions), so neither option gives native rows a real tooltip; see LIB-12.

### `LIB-18` Search matches the bare name, not the displayed text, so a user cannot type the bracket they can see

**Unity does:** `entry.Name.IndexOf(_filter, OrdinalIgnoreCase)` matches against the stored name, which for natives and components INCLUDES the angle brackets (`"<" + prop.Name + ">"`) and for hook modules includes the `" (module)"` suffix (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:614-624, :308-331, :444-452). The query is used RAW — untrimmed — so a trailing space matches nothing.

**Godot today:** divergent, mostly better. `_add_section` filters on the bare entry name (builder_library_pane.gd:210-212) while `_entry_row` renders `"<%s>" % name` for elements and components (:307-308), so typing what is on screen (`<but`) matches nothing. Godot also `strip_edges()`es the query (:105, :336), which is a genuine improvement over Unity's raw-query quirk and should be kept. The mismatch is only between the searched string and the displayed string.

**To build:** Either strip `<`/`>` from the query before matching (`_search = text.strip_edges().to_lower().lstrip("<").rstrip(">")`), or build the display text once per entry and match against that. The first is one line and preserves the current bare-name semantics for everything else.

**Godot specifics:** Trivial, pure, and covered by the existing `_test_library_pane` filter assertions in tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:590-601 — extend them with a `<` query. Note the test's helper `_count_matching` constructs a LibraryPane and calls `set_filter` WITHOUT adding it to the tree, so `rebuild()` runs against a `_body` that was built in `_init` — fine today, but it is why the helper must keep working headlessly if the pane ever moves construction into `_ready`.

### Row and card context menus, and every structural edit they dispatch

### `ctx-01` "Remove <directive>, keep its contents" is offered on every directive row, and corrupts the buffer on four of the six

> **Duplicate of `LANG-02`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** Unity offers "Remove directive (unwrap)" only when `row.BadgeKind != 14 && IsSingleClauseConstruct(node, rowIdx)` — never on a @switch, never on a multi-clause @if. On a CONTINUATION clause (ClauseIndex > 0) `AddDirectiveHeadItems` adds "Delete clause" and RETURNS: no header edit, no wrap, no unwrap, no block delete. The reason is written down at the other end of the same rule — OnDirectiveEdited routes an emptied continuation clause to DeleteClause because "the construct unwrap assumes it starts at a construct head and corrupts the brace balance from a clause line".

**Godot today:** wrong. `builder_window.gd:1101-1105` adds UNWRAP for EVERY row whose `kind == Graph.LineKind.DIRECTIVE`, with no clause-count test, no @match test and no continuation test. I drove `Edits.unwrap_directive` (edits/builder_edits.gd:775-834) through the real projection under Godot 4.7 headless: (A) on a multi-clause `@if`/`@else` head it walks brace depth to the WHOLE construct's final `}`, then strips the first `return (` and the LAST `)` — leaving `<Label text="a" />` / `)` / `} @else {` / `return (` as loose lines; compile ok=false. (C) on the `@else` continuation, depth goes 0 on the head line itself so `close` lands on the very next line, and the edit deletes `} @else {` plus its `return (`; compile ok=false. (G) on a `@match` head it removes the match and leaves `@case (0) { ... }` orphaned at the return root; compile ok=false. (H) on a `@case` it leaves `@match (0) { return ( ... ) }` — a match whose body is markup; compile ok=false. All four are one left-click from the menu, and Save writes the wreck to disk.

**To build:** In `builder_window.gd:_on_row_context`, gate the UNWRAP item. Port Unity's two predicates into `builder_edits.gd` as pure statics so they are headlessly assertable: `static func is_single_clause_construct(card, row) -> bool` and `static func construct_clause(card, row, badge) -> Graph.Line`, both walking Unity's depth rule — from the head row forward, skip rows deeper than `clause_depth` (`row.depth + 1` for a @match head, `row.depth` otherwise), return/observe a DIRECTIVE row at `clause_depth` with `clause_index > 0`, and BREAK on anything else. Then: offer UNWRAP only when `row.clause_index == 0 and row.badge != Graph.Badge.MATCH and is_single_clause_construct(card, row)`. On a continuation row (`clause_index > 0`) build the Unity shape — "Delete this <badge> clause" and nothing else. Additionally make `unwrap_directive` itself refuse: `if row.clause_index > 0 or row.badge == Graph.Badge.MATCH: return source`, so the operation is safe even if a future caller forgets the gate (every other edit in that file already refuses rather than guesses — see the `close_line` check at :603).

**Godot specifics:** `Graph.Line` already carries `clause_index`, `badge` and `depth` (canvas/builder_graph.gd:91-106) and `builder_graph_service.gd:666-726` fills them correctly — a @match head is `clause_index 0`, its arms are `clause_index k+1` at `depth + 1`, exactly the asymmetry Unity's depth rule encodes. So the data is there and only the predicate is missing. Keep the predicates in `builder_edits.gd` reachable through the existing preload const (`const Edits = preload(...)` at builder_window.gd:37) — never a global class_name, per the class-cache hazard. They are pure `(card, row) -> bool`, so `tests/builder_edits_test.gd` can assert them with no editor and no canvas.

**Risk:** A user who wraps a row in @if, adds an @else, then changes their mind and picks the item labelled "Remove @if, keep its contents" loses the markup of both branches. The card's markup section then fails to project (populate_card falls back to export detail, builder_graph_service.gd:209-214), so the canvas shows the component as if it had no markup at all — which reads as the builder having eaten the component.

### `ctx-02` delete_clause has only half of Unity's brace bookkeeping: deleting a MIDDLE clause destroys the next clause's head

> **Duplicate of `LANG-03`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** DeleteClause branches on what the clause's CLOSE line is. Branch A — the close line contains '@', i.e. it IS the next clause's shared head (`} @else {`): `RemoveRange(head, close - head)`, which deliberately does NOT remove the close line, then if the deleted clause had a separate head but the next one is shared, strip that leading '}' and re-indent. Branch B — the close line is a plain '}': `RemoveRange(head, close - head + 1)` and, if the deleted head was shared, insert a lone '}' back at `head`. The 2026-08-16 review finding is quoted in the source: "a middle clause's close line carries the NEXT head (its leading '}' takes over closing the previous clause); the last clause is replaced by a lone '}' that closes the previous one."

**Godot today:** partial — branch B only. `builder_edits.gd:635-656` always removes `head..close` INCLUSIVE and then re-inserts a '}' when the deleted head was shared. Verified on `@if (true) { } @elif (false) { } @else { }`: the graph gives the `@elif` row `directive_line = 5, close_line = 7`, and line 7 is `} @else {` — the NEXT clause's head. The edit deletes lines 5-7, taking the `@else` head with it, and re-inserts a bare '}'. Result: `@if (true) { return (…) }` / `}` / `return ( <Label text="c" /> )` / `}` — the third branch's body left as loose markup at the return root. Compile ok=false. The gate is green over this because `tests/builder_edits_test.gd:727-771` only ever exercises a SINGLE-CLAUSE @if grown by one @else, i.e. only branch B.

**To build:** Port branch A into `delete_clause`. Concretely: after computing `head` and `close`, test `str(lines[close]).contains("@")`. If it does, remove the range `head .. close - 1` (exclusive of the close line), then compute `next_shared = str(lines[head]).strip_edges().begins_with("}")` on the line that has slid into `head`, and when `not shared_head and next_shared` strip that leading '}' and re-indent with `_indent_of_line`. Only when the close line is a plain '}' keep today's inclusive removal plus the compensating brace. Add a suite section that builds an `@if`/`@elif`/`@else` and deletes each of the three clauses in turn, asserting `Compiler.compile(...).ok` for every one — the shape the current test cannot reach.

**Godot specifics:** The projection already distinguishes the two: `builder_graph_service.gd:678-679` gives a head `construct_close` (the whole chain's end) and a continuation `_body_close_line(source, body_at)` (its own boundary, which for a middle clause is the next shared head). So the branch test can key on the line text exactly as Unity's does. Keep the operation pure `(source, row) -> String` so `builder_edits_test.gd` asserts it as before/after strings, which is what makes this class of bug visible at all.

**Risk:** Reached from two places — the row menu item "Delete this <badge> clause" (builder_window.gd:1104) and the Delete key when a clause row is selected — so a user deleting the middle branch of a three-branch @if silently loses the last branch's markup and gets an unparseable file.

### `ctx-03` "Add @else" is offered on an @if that already has one, and both clause adds append after it

> **Duplicate of `LANG-06`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** On an @if head the menu adds "Add @else if" always, and "Add @else" only when `!ConstructHasClause(node, rowIdx, "@else")`. ConstructHasClause is a thin wrapper over the ConstructClause depth walk, which exists as a separate function precisely because UB-71 needed the clause ROW and not just its existence.

**Godot today:** absent. `builder_window.gd:1097-1100` adds both items whenever `row.badge_text == "@if" and row.clause_index == 0`, with no test for what clauses the construct already has — no `construct_clause` / `has_clause` helper exists anywhere under `builder/` (grepped). Verified: `add_if_clause` on an `@if`/`@else` construct writes the new clause at the construct's closing brace, which is the @else's, producing `@if (true) { … } @else { … } @else { … }`; compile ok=false. The same append point means "Add @elif" on a construct that already has an @else produces `@else { } @elif (true) { }` — an elif after the fallback.

**To build:** Use the `construct_clause(card, row, badge)` walk from ctx-01. Hide "Add @else" when it returns non-null for `@else`. For "Add @elif", follow Unity's own AddSwitchClause precedent rather than its @if defect: when an `@else` clause exists, insert the new `@elif` at the @else's `directive_line - 1` instead of at the construct close, guarded by Unity's three-part sanity test (the fallback's line is > the head's line and <= the close index) so a stale `close_line` cannot insert outside the construct. Belt and braces: make `add_if_clause` itself refuse a second `@else` — it already refuses when the close line is not a lone brace (:603), so the shape for "the row and the buffer disagree, do nothing" is established.

**Godot specifics:** `_on_row_context` has the `Graph.Card` in hand (`card` at builder_window.gd:1068) but never passes it to the clause logic; the walk needs it to see sibling rows. Note this is a case where the parity gate is actively misleading: `["AddIfClause", "func add_if_clause"]` (tests/builder_parity.gd:71) greps a function name and cannot see that the caller never asks whether the clause is legal.

**Risk:** One click on a routine menu item produces a file the compiler rejects; the card's markup projection then collapses to export detail, so the user loses the view of the component they were editing as well.

### `ctx-04` A @match head offers no clause operations at all — no Add @case, no Add @default, no next-label allocator

> **Duplicate of `LANG-08`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** On a @switch head the menu adds "Add @case…" always and "Add @default" only when the construct has none. AddSwitchClause inserts a case at the @default arm's line when one exists (UB-71: appending at the closing brace put every case the user added BELOW the catch-all and left no way to author one above it) and at the closing brace otherwise; @default always goes last. The seeded label comes from NextCaseLabel — the lowest non-negative integer no arm of that switch already uses — so the seed compiles and cannot collide with an existing arm. Only a @case opens the header editor.

**Godot today:** absent. `builder_window.gd:1097` gates every clause add behind `row.badge_text == "@if"`, so a `@match` head's menu is exactly: Edit header… / Remove @match, keep its contents (which corrupts, ctx-01) / Delete @match. There is no `add_match_clause`, no `next_case_label`, and `@case` / `@default` appear nowhere in `edits/builder_edits.gd` except inside the `wrap_in_match` literal (:704-705). The consequence compounds: "Wrap in… @match" seeds a match with exactly ONE `@case (0)`, so a match the builder itself created can never gain a second arm or a default from the builder. The third leg solved this — Unreal offers Add @case / Add @default on a `bIsMatch` head.

**To build:** `static func add_match_clause(source, head: Graph.Line, card: Graph.Card, is_default: bool) -> String` in `builder_edits.gd`, mirroring `add_if_clause`'s shape: refuse when `head.close_line <= 0` or the close line is not a lone '}'; indent one unit deeper than that brace; for a case, insert `@case (N) {` where N is `next_case_label(card, head)` and, when a `@default` clause exists, insert at that clause's `directive_line - 1` rather than at the close; for a default, always insert at the close. Body per this language: `return (` / `<Control />` / `)` / `}`, the same GUITKX0303 placeholder `add_if_clause` already uses (:610-622). `static func next_case_label(card, head) -> int` walks the clause depth rule (`head.depth + 1` for a match) collecting `int` labels off rows whose `badge == Graph.Badge.CASE` — the label is the parenthesised text in `row.text`, e.g. `@case (0)` — and returns the lowest unused non-negative integer. In the menu, add both items on `row.badge == Graph.Badge.MATCH and row.clause_index == 0`, hiding "Add @default" when the walk finds one, and set `_seed_header_edit` for the case so the header editor opens on the new arm.

**Godot specifics:** The label spelling differs from Unity's and matters: Unity's arm is `@case 0:` (colon form, BadgeText `@case` + Text `0:`); this language's is `@case (0) { … }`, so the label parse is "the text inside the parens of `row.text`", not "strip a trailing colon". `builder_graph_service.gd:716-718` already emits `@case` rows with the value in the header position, so `row.text` is `@case (0)`. Everything is pure text over `(source, card, row)`, so it belongs in `builder_edits_test.gd` as before/after strings with a `Compiler.compile(...).ok` assertion per arm added.

**Risk:** @match is one of the four wraps the builder offers, and it is the only one whose seeded construct is incomplete by design (one arm, no default). Offering the wrap without the clause operations means the builder can create a shape it cannot then edit.

### `ctx-05` The row menu has no row-KIND gate: import rows, hook chips, code lines and the setup island all get the ELEMENT menu, and its items write into the wrong place

> **Duplicate of `GP-04`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** Right-click is routed per SURFACE in CanvasView. Markup rows, directive badges and attribute values go to the row menu. Import rows go to their own import menu, and only when `imp.SourceLine > 0`. Style/export rows go to the style-row menu. Hook chips, code islands, "+ hook" and "+ code" `return` WITHOUT StopPropagation, so the event bubbles to the card frame and the CARD menu opens instead — they have no menu of their own and falling through is the only behaviour available.

**Godot today:** wrong. `builder_canvas_host.gd:433-449` hit-tests with `row_at`, which returns any of `Section.{SIGNATURE, IMPORTS, BODY, MARKUP, EXPORTS, ISLAND}` (canvas/builder_canvas_metrics.gd:209, :504-536), and emits ONE `row_context_requested` for all of them. `builder_window.gd:1083-1120` special-cases only EXPORTS, then tests `row.kind == DIRECTIVE`, and everything else falls into the ELEMENT branch. So an IMPORT row, a HOOK chip, a plain code line and the setup island (which `_row_of` at :1544-1547 resolves to `card.markup[0]`, i.e. an entirely different row) all show "Add attribute… / Add child element… / Wrap in… / Delete element". I ran the operations those items dispatch against the real projection: `wrap_in_directive` on an import row rewrites the head of the file to `@if (true) { return ( import { Card } from "./card" ) }`; on a hook row it wraps `var count = Hooks.useState(0)` in a directive; and worst, `set_attribute` on a hook row scans forward from the row's offset for the next `>` and lands on `<VBoxContainer>` — it silently writes the attribute onto an element the user was not pointing at.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Two refinements. (1) A SIGNATURE row does not get the element menu — `_row_of` (builder_window.gd:1530-1550) has no SIGNATURE case, so it falls to `_: return null` and `_on_row_context` returns at :1065 with no menu at all. The claim's list of harmed surfaces (import row, hook chip, code line, setup island) is right; SIGNATURE is a silent no-op, not a wrong menu. (2) The "belt and braces" precedent already exists in one operation: `set_directive_header` refuses on `row.kind != Graph.LineKind.DIRECTIVE` (builder_edits.gd:321). So the fix has one in-file pattern to copy rather than none.

**To build:** Gate `_on_row_context` on the section and the row kind before building any items. `Section.SIGNATURE` and `Section.ISLAND`: no row menu — fall through to `_open_card_menu(card.file_path, …)`, which is Unity's rule for surfaces with no menu of their own. `Section.BODY` (hook chips, code lines): either fall through to the card menu, or give it its own two-item menu ("Edit this line…" reusing the existing `{ "kind": "body" }` inline token at :1505-1510, and "Delete this line"). `Section.IMPORTS`: its own menu (remove the import; edit the specifier), never the element menu. In the element branch, require `row.kind in [ELEMENT, COMPONENT]` and refuse otherwise. Belt and braces, make `wrap_in_directive` / `wrap_in_match` / `insert` / `set_attribute` refuse a row whose `kind` is not ELEMENT/COMPONENT — `set_attribute`'s forward scan is the one that fails SILENTLY and wrongly rather than loudly, so the refusal has to be in the operation.

**Godot specifics:** `Graph.LineKind` (canvas/builder_graph.gd:26-36) already labels every row, so the gate is one match on data that is already there. The canvas is drawn by the reconciler from `canvas_view.guitkx`, but the right-click routing is not — it is hand-written `_gui_input` on the host Control, so `Control.mouse_filter` and event bubbling do not enter into it: `builder_canvas_host.gd:449` calls `accept_event()` for every right-click regardless. That is why there is no analogue of Unity's "fall through by not stopping propagation" and the fall-through has to be written explicitly as a call to `_open_card_menu`.

**Risk:** The hint bar promises exactly this gesture — "Right-click rows / cards / canvas for typed attributes, directives, delete, create" (builder_window.gd:411) — so the user is told to right-click rows. Doing it on the wrong kind of row either mangles the preamble or, in the `set_attribute` case, writes a correct-looking attribute onto the wrong element with no error anywhere.

### `ctx-06` The return-root delete guard is the wrong predicate, and the Delete KEY has no guard at all

**Unity does:** "Delete element" is added only when `rowIdx != BuilderCanvasDrawing.FirstElementRow(node)`, and FirstElementRow is explicitly the first row whose Kind is NOT Directive, "not literally index 0 — a directive head wrapping the root occupies index 0, so every root-row guard keys on this". DeleteSelection routes to DeleteElementRow after the SAME root check, so the keyboard and the menu enforce one rule.

**Godot today:** wrong, twice. (1) `builder_window.gd:1118` guards with `if row_index > 0 or section != Metrics.Section.MARKUP` — literally index 0, which is the predicate Unity's comment names as the mistake. Verified: after "Wrap in… @if" the card's markup rows are `[0] @if (true)`, `[1] <Label>`; row 1 satisfies `row_index > 0`, so "Delete element" is offered on what is now the return root, and taking it leaves `@if (true) { return ( ) }`. (2) `_delete_selection` (:269-279) has no root check whatsoever — it calls `Edits.remove(module.buffer_text, _menu_row)` for whatever `_on_row_clicked` last set (:1016-1018 sets `_menu_row` for ANY row it can hit). Pressing Delete on the unwrapped return root gives `return ( )`, a component with nothing to return.

**To build:** Add `static func first_element_row(card: Graph.Card) -> int` to `builder_edits.gd` — the index of the first `card.markup` row whose `kind != Graph.LineKind.DIRECTIVE`, -1 when there is none — and use it in BOTH places: the menu condition becomes `row_index != first_element_row(card)` (for `Section.MARKUP`), and `_delete_selection` runs the same test before calling `Edits.remove`, toasting Unity's reason when it refuses ("a component must return one node"). While there, route `_delete_selection` the way Unity's does: a row with `clause_index > 0` goes to `delete_clause`, not to `remove` — today it goes to `remove`, which on a continuation clause takes the `@else { … }` span and leaves the brace the shared head carried away, producing an unbalanced file (verified, compile ok=false).

**Godot specifics:** `_menu_row` is set by plain LEFT-click (`_on_row_clicked`), which the port added deliberately so Delete would act on the row rather than falling through to the module — so the keyboard path is now reachable on every row on the canvas, which makes the missing guard more exposed here than in Unity, not less. `first_element_row` is pure over `Graph.Card`, so `builder_edits_test.gd` can assert it directly.

**Risk:** A directive-wrapped root is the normal state after any "Wrap in…", so the offered-but-illegal delete sits one click away from the most common structural edit the builder makes.

### `ctx-07` `_menu_row` is captured once and never re-resolved, so Delete after any menu edit cuts at stale offsets

**Unity does:** Unity's menu handlers take `(filePath, sourceLine, rowIdx)` and re-read `node.Markup[rowIdx]` from the CURRENT projection at pick time — there is no row object held across an edit. The one place a row must survive a re-projection (the header editor opened on a fresh wrap) goes through WithCanvasElement, which re-queries and retries.

**Godot today:** wrong. `_menu_row` holds a `Graph.Line` OBJECT (builder_window.gd:1017, :1077), and every edit calls `_after_model_change` → `Service.populate_card` (:882-890), which rebuilds the card's rows as NEW `Line` instances — leaving `_menu_row` pointing at an object whose `at` / `end_at` / `source_line` describe the buffer as it was BEFORE the edit. Nothing clears or refreshes it on the success path: `_on_search_picked` ends at :1433 without touching it, and `_delete_selection` (:270-275) reads it straight. So: click a row, right-click → "Add attribute…" → pick one (the buffer grows by the attribute's length), then press Delete — `Edits.remove` cuts `row.at .. row.end_at`, both now short by that length. The port KNOWS about this hazard and solved it for exactly one path: `_row_after_reproject` (:1455-1473) exists with a comment saying "the `Line` the menu was opened on belongs to the old projection and is stale the moment the buffer changes -- editing through it writes at the offsets the row used to have", and it is called only from the seeded-wrap branch (:1447).

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The mechanism in the claim is wrong in one detail, and the real one is worse. `Edits.remove` snaps to line boundaries (`_line_start`/`_line_end`, builder_edits.gd:177-181 and :958-965), so a stale row never tears a span mid-character and an attribute-add (which changes no line count) is harmless. The damage comes from any edit that changes the LINE COUNT above the row — add child, wrap, add clause, apply style with an import — after which the stale offsets name a different whole line range and the delete removes a different whole element, silently and with a clean compile. Replace "cuts at stale offsets, both now short by the attribute's length" with "deletes the wrong element outright after any line-count-changing edit"; the remedy (coordinates re-resolved through `_row_of`) is unchanged.

**To build:** Stop holding the object. Replace `_menu_row` with the coordinates Unity uses — `(_menu_card, _menu_section, _menu_row_index)` — and resolve through the existing `_row_of(card_index, section, row_index)` (:1530-1550) at the moment of use, in `_delete_selection`, `_on_row_menu` and `_on_search_picked`. Where the index itself can shift (an edit that inserts a row above), re-resolving still beats a stale object because `_row_of` reads the live projection; belt and braces, clear the coordinates in `_after_model_change` for any card that was re-populated, so a Delete after an unrelated edit falls through to the module rather than cutting at a guessed span.

**Godot specifics:** This is the Godot-specific face of Unity's own lesson: the port went further than Unity by making every row carry absolute character offsets (`at`/`end_at`, canvas/builder_graph.gd:80-81) so edits are span-exact — which is a real improvement, and it is exactly what makes a stale row silently destructive rather than merely wrong by a line. `parent_of` (edits/builder_edits.gd:78-88) already documents the same trap for containment lookups ("a row a caller is holding is routinely from an earlier projection"); the chrome never took the same lesson.

**Risk:** Silent: the cut lands on real text at a plausible offset, so the result looks like an edit the user made rather than like a bug, and nothing reports it until the preview fails to compile.

*high · risk · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:1789-1852 (handlers take filePath+rowIdx and re-read), Builder/Editor/Canvas/BuilderCanvasHost.cs:391-405 (WithCanvasElement re-query) | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:102, :1017, :1077, :269-275, :882-890, :1455-1473 (the fix that exists for one path only)

### `ctx-08` Card and canvas menus are positioned in viewport coordinates while the row menu uses screen coordinates — exactly one can be right, and the only rig that drives real input runs in the mode the plugin does not ship in

**Unity does:** Every menu opens AT the click. RememberMenuPointer records the panel-space point, Place() converts it through the host window's screen rect, and the result is clamped to the display on both axes with a +8px nudge below the cursor. The conversion is the whole point of the function: "Event.current is null outside OnGUI — UITK pointer callbacks hand us the panel-space point instead, which the hosting window's screen rect turns into a screen point."

**Godot today:** wrong, and inconsistently. The ROW menu uses `_canvas.get_screen_position() + at` (builder_window.gd:1088, :1122) and `_menu_screen_at()` (:1319) — real screen coordinates. The CARD menu and the CANVAS menu use `get_global_mouse_position()` (:679, :705, :712), which is a `CanvasItem` API returning the position in the VIEWPORT's canvas coordinates, and assign it straight to `PopupMenu.position` (:2210), a `Window` property. The builder lives in its own `Window`, `popup_centered()`d on the editor base control (plugin.gd:429-437), so those two spaces differ by the window's screen position. Whether it is the row menu or the card menu that is wrong flips with `gui_embed_subwindows`: unembedded (the shipped path — editor subwindows are real OS windows unless single-window mode is on) the card/canvas menus open near the top-left of the display; embedded, `Popup::_popup_adjust_rect` clamps the row menu's screen-space point into the embedder's corner. And the gesture rig cannot see either: `addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd:486` sets `_window.gui_embed_subwindows = true` so a screenshot captures the popup, and :502-505 opens the card menu by calling `_open_card_menu(path, canvas.global_position + canvas.size * 0.5)` — viewport space, reproducing the same assumption rather than testing it.

**To build:** One helper, used by all four menus: `func _screen_at(local: Vector2) -> Vector2` returning `get_screen_position() + local` when the containing viewport is NOT embedding subwindows and `local` when it is (`get_viewport().gui_embed_subwindows`), so the coordinate space follows the mode instead of being assumed. Feed it from the gesture: `card_context_requested` and `canvas_context_requested` already carry a WORLD position but not the raw event position — add the event position to those signals the way `row_context_requested` already does (builder_canvas_host.gd:443-444), so the card menu opens at the click rather than at whatever `get_global_mouse_position()` means today. Then teach the shots rig to run BOTH modes, or at least to assert the popup's final `position` against the pointer it pushed, since "the menu opened" is all it checks now.

**Godot specifics:** This is the single most Godot-shaped defect in the area: `Control.get_screen_position()`, `CanvasItem.get_global_mouse_position()` and `Window.position` are three different spaces, and which pair agrees depends on a viewport flag set by the host, not by the builder. `Popup::_popup_adjust_rect` clamps to the usable parent rect, so a wrong point never opens off-screen — it opens in a plausible-looking wrong place, which is why this survived.

**Risk:** A right-click on a card produces a menu somewhere else on the display. Nothing errors; the user reads it as the menu having missed.

*high · engine-translation · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/Controls/BuilderSearchMenu.cs:38-50, :150-208 (RememberPointer + Place + ScreenBoundsAround), Builder/Editor/Canvas/BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:337-346 | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:679, :705, :712, :2210 vs :1088, :1122, :1319; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/plugin.gd:429-437; addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd:486, :502-505

### `ctx-16` The parity gate and the edits suite are green over four of the corrupting operations, and name none of the missing ones

**Unity does:** n/a — this is a judgement on the Godot gates, requested by the brief.

**Godot today:** Five `tests/builder_parity.gd` entries in this area are answered by identifiers that exist and are wrong or unreachable: `["RemoveDirectiveBlock", "func unwrap_directive"]` (:70) is green over an operation that corrupts on four of six directive shapes (ctx-01); `["DeleteClause", "func delete_clause"]` (:72) over one that destroys the next clause on a middle-clause delete (ctx-02); `["AddIfClause", "func add_if_clause"]` (:71) over a caller that offers it when it is illegal (ctx-03); `["DeleteElementRow", "RowMenuId.DELETE_ROW"]` (:65) and `["OnDirectiveEdited", "RowMenuId.EDIT_HEADER"]` (:73) are satisfied by ENUM MEMBERS — a token that cannot fail as long as the enum exists, whatever the handler does. The suite behind them never reaches the failing shapes: `tests/builder_edits_test.gd:727-803` builds exactly one fixture, a SINGLE-CLAUSE `@if` with one `<Label>`, and every clause and unwrap assertion runs against it. And the checklist has no entry at all for AddSwitchClause, NextCaseLabel, ConstructClause/ConstructHasClause/IsSingleClauseConstruct, ShowForeachWrapMenu, WarnOnDirectiveDrift, FirstElementRow, RememberMenuPointer or the menu keyboard — so the gate reads as complete over an area where six behaviours are simply not listed. `tests/builder_chrome_test.gd` contains no reference to `_on_row_context`, `_on_row_menu`, `RowMenuId` or `_open_card_menu` at all, so nothing tests which items a menu offers. The one rig that pushes real input (`addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd:309, :337`) asserts only that `row_context_requested` fired.

**To build:** Three things. (1) Change the five hollow entries from identifiers to BEHAVIOURS the suite asserts — replace the `RowMenuId.*` enum tokens with the guard function names they should be calling (`func first_element_row`, and the empty-header routing), which cannot be satisfied by an enum. (2) Add the six missing entries, pointing at the functions ctx-01/03/04/06/12/13 build. (3) Extend `builder_edits_test.gd` with a fixture matrix rather than a fixture: `@if` alone, `@if`+`@else`, `@if`+`@elif`+`@else`, `@match` with one arm, `@match` with two arms and a default — and for each, run every clause/unwrap/delete operation the menu can dispatch and assert `Compiler.compile(...).ok`. That single loop would have caught ctx-01, ctx-02 and ctx-03 on the day they were written; I found all three with a twenty-line script against the real projection.

**Godot specifics:** Everything needed is already headlessly reachable: `Service.populate_card(Graph.Card.new(), source)` gives a real projection with no editor, no canvas and no `EditorInterface`, and `Compiler.compile(source, name)` gives the verdict. That is how I produced the evidence in ctx-01 through ctx-06 — under `godot --headless --script`, in one file, in a few minutes. There is no engine reason these shapes are untested.

**Risk:** A green gate over a corrupting feature is worse than a red one: it is the artefact that let ctx-01 through ctx-03 ship, and it is the reason the port's own parity sweep — written expressly because "this builder was written from a plan document while the source sat unread" — reports this area as answered.

### `ctx-09` The rename prompt and the create prompt open where the last ROW right-click was, not where the gesture that opened them was

**Unity does:** Unity records this as a defect in its own source: s_pointer is not cleared after use, "so a menu opened without a fresh RememberMenuPointer lands wherever the previous menu gesture was" — the import row's comment names it as the bug it had. The remedy everywhere else is that each gesture that will open a menu records its own point first.

**Godot today:** wrong — the same defect, reintroduced. `_menu_at` is assigned in exactly one place, `_on_row_context` (builder_window.gd:1079). The card menu's Rename (:2225-2227) and `prompt_create` (:1776) both position through `_menu_screen_at()`, which is `_canvas.get_screen_position() + _menu_at`. So renaming a module from its card menu opens the name prompt over wherever the user last right-clicked a markup ROW — or, when `_menu_at` is still `Vector2.ZERO`, at `get_screen_position() + size * 0.3`, a fixed third of the way into the window that has nothing to do with the card.

**To build:** Set `_menu_at` from every gesture that can lead to a menu, exactly as Unity's RememberMenuPointer is called from every such handler: the card-context lambda (:302-306), the canvas-context lambda (:307-314), the folder-pane context (:279-280) and the library's "+ new" (:152-154). Combine with ctx-08's `_screen_at` so all of them convert the same way. The library's create is the one legitimate exception — Unity notes a menu opened from a toolbar has no pointer to go back to — and there the current `get_screen_position() + size * 0.3` fallback is the right answer, but it should be reached because there was no gesture, not because a stale field happened to be zero.

**Godot specifics:** `card_context_requested` currently carries only the world position (builder_canvas_host.gd:30, :446); adding the raw event position to that signal is the change that lets the card path record a point at all.

**Risk:** Polish rather than corruption, but it is the surface where the user types a module name — a prompt that appears over an unrelated part of the canvas reads as a misfire and invites a second right-click.

### `ctx-10` An emptied directive header writes `@if ()` instead of removing the directive

> **Duplicate of `LANG-13`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** OnDirectiveEdited with whitespace-only text REMOVES the directive: a continuation clause goes through DeleteClause (because the construct unwrap corrupts the brace balance from a clause line), everything else through RemoveDirectiveBlock. Clearing the field is how you say "I do not want this wrapper".

**Godot today:** absent. `_on_inline_committed`'s "directive" branch (builder_window.gd:1499-1501) unconditionally calls `Edits.set_directive_header(before, row, text)`. With an empty `text` that writes `@if ()` — an empty condition, i.e. a syntax error. The one saving grace is accidental: `set_directive_header` (edits/builder_edits.gd:320-332) returns the source unchanged when the clause has no parenthesis at all, so `@else` and `@default` are safe by falling into a different guard, not by the rule being implemented.

**To build:** In the "directive" branch, test `text.strip_edges().is_empty()` first and route: `row.clause_index > 0` → `Edits.delete_clause`; otherwise → `Edits.unwrap_directive` (once ctx-01's gate is in, and refusing when the gate would refuse). The port already has the matching rule one branch below for attributes — "AN EMPTIED VALUE TAKES THE ATTRIBUTE WITH IT" at :1513-1518 — so this is making the two consistent, which is also how a user will expect it to behave having learned the attribute one.

**Godot specifics:** The inline editor is one floating control dispatched by a token dictionary (:1486-1524), so the change is local to one match arm; the operations it would call are already pure statics in `builder_edits.gd` and already reachable through the file's preload const.

**Risk:** Low blast radius (one broken header, obvious in the console) but it removes the only route Unity offers for "delete this wrapper by clearing it", and it leaves the buffer non-compiling from a gesture that reads as a cancel.

### `ctx-11` "Add @elif" does not open the header editor, so the seeding is not Escape-undoable and the user must find the new clause

**Unity does:** AddIfClause with a condition ends in BeginEditOnDirectiveLine on the new clause's line, and that editor is opened with UndoAction as its cancel handler — so Escape on it undoes the whole clause add (UB-93). The wrap path does the same, and the two are deliberately symmetrical: a header the builder just seeded is a header the user is expected to be typing over.

**Godot today:** partial. The mechanism exists and works — `_seed_header_edit` (builder_window.gd:106), `_row_after_reproject` (:1458), `_inline.open_at(..., true)` (:1449-1450) and the Escape-undoes-the-seeding wiring (:292-299) — but only the WRAP branch sets it (:1409). `RowMenuId.ADD_ELSE_IF` (:1147-1149) applies the edit and stops, so the new `@elif (true)` is committed with no editor over it and no seeded-undo semantics: Escape does nothing, and the user has to find the clause on the card and click its header to type the condition.

**To build:** Set `_seed_header_edit = "@elif (true)"` in the ADD_ELSE_IF branch and let the existing post-edit block at :1437-1451 do the rest. That block currently re-finds the row with `_row_after_reproject`, which is written for the wrap case ("the nearest directive at or above where the wrapped row was"); for a clause add the new head is BELOW the head that was clicked, so it needs a second locator — the clause the `construct_clause` walk from ctx-01 finds for `@elif`, taking the LAST one, is the natural answer and reuses the helper. Do the same for Add @case once ctx-04 lands. Leave Add @else alone: it has no header, which is Unity's rule too.

**Godot specifics:** The port's seed is `@elif (true)` rather than Unity's `(condition)`, so this is a usability gap rather than a compile one — worth stating plainly, since the port fixed the sharper half of UB-72 here and only left the editor-opening half undone.

**Risk:** Low. Nothing breaks; the clause is simply harder to finish than the wrap it sits beside, and the two gestures behave differently for no reason the user can see.

### `ctx-12` No collection menu behind the loop wrap: `@for` seeds `range(1)` and never asks what to iterate

> **Duplicate of `LANG-15`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** "@foreach…" (the only wrap entry carrying an ellipsis, because only it opens a further menu) opens a searchable menu titled "@foreach — collection" listing in-scope enumerable component props labelled with their type and hook-state locals labelled "hook state", plus the warn-orange freeform "loop over \"x\"" row. The loop variable is singularised from the pick and collision-checked against every identifier already bound in the body. UB-03's first finding is that the literal `@foreach (var item in items)` names a collection that is not in scope and a variable the wrapped row never references.

**Godot today:** absent. `Edits.WRAPS` (edits/builder_edits.gd:675-682) is three literal headers and the row menu maps them straight to `wrap_in_directive` (builder_window.gd:1401-1408) with no intermediate menu. The seed `@for (item in range(1))` is a genuine improvement on Unity in one respect — the comment at :677-679 explains that `range(1)` keeps the wrapped row on screen where an empty collection would make it vanish — but it still means the user's first act after every loop wrap is to retype the header, which is precisely UB-03's complaint. The third leg implemented the menu, citing UB-03 by number.

**To build:** A `_collection_items(card)` builder in `builder_window.gd`, feeding the search menu the same way `_tag_items` and `_style_items` already do (:1275-1342), with a freeform label of `"loop over \"%s\""`. Two sources, both already projected: the component's declared props (`Attributes.props_of_component(card)`, edits/builder_attributes.gd:33-59) filtered to types that look enumerable — for this language `Array`, `PackedStringArray`/`Packed*Array`, `Dictionary`, `PackedScene`-free generics like `Array[T]` — labelled with the type; and the hook-state / setup locals the card already carries as BODY rows (`card.body`, whose `Line.name` is the bound name). Then singularise the pick for the loop variable and collide-check it against every `\b\w+\b` token in the card's body and markup, appending `_i` or falling back to `item` when taken. Route `@for` to this menu instead of to `wrap_in_directive` directly, and keep `range(1)` as the freeform default so the current behaviour is still one keystroke away.

**Godot specifics:** Godot's enumerable test is a real type check, not Unity's substring heuristic (`LooksEnumerable` matching "List", "[]", "Set" — which the Unity source itself notes will match a type named `SettingsSet`): `Attributes.props_of_component` parses `name: Type` out of the card's own signature, so the type string is exact and can be matched against a small explicit set. The whole thing is pure over `Graph.Card`, so it is assertable in `builder_edits_test.gd` without a canvas.

**Risk:** Not a correctness bug — `range(1)` compiles. It is the difference between a wrap that finishes the thought and one that only starts it.

### `ctx-13` No directive-drift warning: the schema has eight control-flow directives and the builder silently answers six

> **Duplicate of `LANG-14`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** WarnOnDirectiveDrift checks the LSP schema's controlFlow list against a hard-coded support table (if/foreach/for/while/switch = offered as a wrap; else/case/default = clause names that ride their construct head's menu) and logs one warning per unknown name, once per domain reload. The rule it enforces is written down: "A schema name missing here trips the drift warning — the builder must never silently trail the language again." Only the names are used; the schema's descriptions are documented as stale and must never be displayed.

**Godot today:** absent. Nothing under `builder/` references `GuitkxSchema.control_flow()` — the only callers are `lsp/guitkx_completion.gd:224` and `guitkx_schema.gd:174`. The schema (`addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/data/guitkx-schema.json:16-25`) lists eight: `@if @elif @else @for @while @match @case @default`. The builder offers four as wraps and two as clause adds, and `@case` / `@default` are answered by nothing at all (ctx-04) — with no warning anywhere that they exist and are unhandled. This is the mechanism whose absence let ctx-04 happen unnoticed.

**To build:** A `const DIRECTIVE_SUPPORT := { "if": true, "elif": false, "else": false, "for": true, "while": true, "match": true, "case": false, "default": false }` in `builder_edits.gd` beside `WRAPS`, and a `_warn_on_directive_drift()` in `builder_window.gd` called when the wrap menu opens, guarded by a `static var` so it runs once per load. Godot's schema entries key on `"directive"` (with the `@`), not Unity's `"name"`, so strip the `@` before the lookup. Print through the builder's own console (`Console.SEVERITY_WARNING`, builder_window.gd:2267-2268) rather than only `push_warning`, so the drift is visible where the user is already looking. Then make `WRAPS` and the clause-add table DERIVE from that dictionary rather than being a second list — two lists of legal directives is one list that is wrong, which is the reasoning `_tag_items` already applies to tags (:1322-1323).

**Godot specifics:** `GuitkxSchema` is loaded through the LSP layer, which the builder already preloads (`const Schema = preload(".../lsp/guitkx_schema.gd")`, builder_window.gd:45), so no new dependency. The `static var` guard is the Godot-idiomatic once-per-load latch — and it must live in a `@tool` script, since a non-tool script's static initialisers never run in the editor (the same hazard `canvas_palette.gd` documents); `builder_window.gd` is `@tool`, so this is safe there and would NOT be safe in a generated `.gd`.

**Risk:** The failure mode is exactly the one the rule exists to prevent, and it has already happened: `@case` and `@default` shipped in the schema with nothing in the builder to answer them, and no gate, test or log noticed.
