### `ctx-14` Deleting the only child of a directive body leaves an empty body — the orphan Unity's delete rule exists to prevent

**Unity does:** DeleteElementRow: if the row carries a directive (`row.DirectiveLine > 0`), the delete takes the directive's WHOLE block via MatchingCloseLine, not the element's own span. The POC rule is quoted in the source: "the NODE goes, and with it the directive that was a property of that node — so a directive-wrapped row takes its whole block, never leaving an orphan `@if (…) { return ( ); }`."

**Godot today:** wrong for a different structural reason. This leg models the directive as its own ROW rather than as a property of the element row (builder_graph_service.gd:646-648 states that choice and why), so no element row ever has a `directive_line` and the Unity branch has no trigger. "Delete element" therefore removes only the element's span, and deleting the sole child of an `@if` leaves `@if (true) { return ( ) }` — verified. The port's own listed divergence sharpens this rather than excusing it: it accepts that a directive body cannot be empty here (GUITKX0303) and pays for it by seeding `<Control />` into every new clause (edits/builder_edits.gd:610-622) — then leaves the delete path free to produce the very shape the seeding exists to avoid.

**To build:** In the DELETE_ROW branch for an ELEMENT row, ask whether this row is the only markup child of an enclosing directive. `Edits.parent_of(card, row)` (edits/builder_edits.gd:78-88) already answers "the smallest row whose span strictly encloses it" by containment, and `can_place` (:65-68) already uses it to detect a directive parent — so the test is `var p := parent_of(card, row); p != null and p.kind == DIRECTIVE and <no sibling markup row inside p>`. When true, follow Unity: delete the whole block (`Edits.remove` on the directive row, whose span is already the construct's, per `_directive_head` at builder_graph_service.gd:815-819). The honest alternative, given GUITKX0303, is to replace the deleted child with `<Control />` — but Unity's answer is the block, and it is the one the user means.

**Godot specifics:** `parent_of`'s containment approach is what makes this cheap: it does not depend on holding a row from the same projection, which is the trap ctx-07 describes. Note the whole thing is pure over `(source, card, row)`, so the sibling count and the resulting text are both assertable in `builder_edits_test.gd`.

**Risk:** Not corruption — `@if (true) { return ( ) }` compiles here — but the card then shows a directive wrapping nothing, and the user's next Delete (on the directive row) is a second gesture for what should have been one.

*medium · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:4414-4455 (DeleteElementRow), :4314-4325 (MatchingCloseLine) | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1141-1143, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:646-648, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_edits.gd:610-622 (the GUITKX0303 seeding this contradicts)

### `ctx-15` The searchable menu has no keyboard walk of its own, and its list will not scroll to follow focus

**Unity does:** One OnListKeyDown serves both menu shapes "so neither can drift from the other": arrows move a highlight painted at accent-14%-alpha, Enter takes it, `_list.ScrollTo(rows[highlight])` keeps it visible, and -1 means "the first pickable row" so Enter-without-arrows still works. UB-122 built the arrows onto the search field, which left every menu without one mouse-only (UB-126); the keys were moved off the field for that reason.

**Godot today:** partial, and by accident rather than design. `builder_search_menu.gd` handles only Escape (:214-219) and Enter-takes-the-first-Button (:196-211). Arrow keys are not handled at all — they work only because Godot's `Viewport` falls back to `find_valid_focus_neighbor` when a focused `LineEdit` ignores up/down, which walks into the list geometrically. There is no highlight (the focus ring stands in), and `ScrollContainer.follow_focus` is left at its default `false` (:63-66), so arrowing past the visible rows moves focus to a row that is scrolled out of sight — the exact failure ScrollTo exists to prevent, on a list whose `maxHeight` Unity caps at 300px for the same reason.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One detail worth adding for whoever fixes it: `follow_focus = true` is already used elsewhere in this same chrome — `builder_library_pane.gd:113` sets it on its scroll — so the fix is applying an established local pattern, not introducing one.

**To build:** `scroll.follow_focus = true` in `_init` is the one-line half of it. For the rest, handle `ui_up` / `ui_down` explicitly in `_input` while visible: keep an index, `grab_focus()` the row at it, and clamp rather than wrap (Unity clamps). Leave Enter as it is — `text_submitted` already gives "Enter takes the first match", and Godot's Button consumes Enter once focus has moved, which reproduces "-1 means the first row" for free.

**Godot specifics:** `ScrollContainer.follow_focus` is the Godot equivalent of `ScrollTo` and is off by default — this is the kind of engine default that turns a ported behaviour into a silently missing one. Note also that `_row()` returns a `Button` with default `focus_mode`, so the geometric walk works at all; a flat `Button` with `FOCUS_NONE` would have made the menu keyboard-dead.

**Risk:** Polish, but it bites hardest on the menus that most need the keyboard: the attribute menu for a `Control` lists well over a hundred rows, and the tag menu every host tag in the schema.

### The source editing surface: syntax colouring, completion, diagnostics, gutters, scrolling, apply

### `SRC-01` Typing in edit mode writes the model on every keystroke, and apply then records nothing and re-projects nothing — a source edit is silently absent from undo and the canvas keeps showing the old file

**Unity does:** Unity separates the two jobs cleanly. `OnCodeEdited` runs on EVERY keystroke and does three things unconditionally: `session.ApplyEdit(bufferLf)`, `_ledger.RecordTyping(_focusFile, before, bufferLf)` (which coalesces into ONE history entry inside a typing window), and `ScheduleCanvasRefresh(_focusFile)` — so the model, the history and the card are always in step, mid-edit-mode or not. `ApplySourceEdit` is then PURELY a gate plus a mode exit: it re-parses, and on a clean parse drops the snapshot, leaves edit mode, `ScheduleCanvasRefresh` and `NotifyBufferChanged`. The inventory states it flatly: 'Apply does NOT write the text into the session — typing already did that keystroke-by-keystroke'.

**Godot today:** wrong, and it corrupts history. The pane's `_on_text_changed` has NO `_editing` guard: every keystroke calls `workspace.apply_edit(_path, after)`, mutating the module buffer, and then emits `buffer_edited`. The window's `_on_buffer_edited` returns EARLY while `_source.is_editing()`, so `ledger.record_typing` and `_after_model_change` are both skipped. By the time `apply_edit()` succeeds and the window's `apply_edit(path, text, "Edit …")` runs, `before := module.buffer_text` ALREADY equals `after`, so it hits `if before == after: return false` and never reaches `ledger.begin/record/end` or `_after_model_change`. Verified by probe against a real window: after typing `<Label>` → `<Button>` in edit mode and applying, `can_undo` is `false` and the card's first markup row is still `<Label>` while the model says `<Button>`. The canvas, the folder pane, the preview request and the status line are all skipped too. The class doc claims the opposite — 'the pane hands the buffer over once, on apply, after it has parsed' — which is the behaviour that was designed and not the behaviour that runs.

**To build:** Pick ONE of the two disciplines and make the code match it. (a) Unity's: delete the `is_editing()` early-return in `builder_window.gd:902-906` and let `record_typing` coalesce as it already knows how to (`builder_ledger.gd:170-194` is a faithful port of `RecordTyping`, TYPING_WINDOW_MSEC and all); apply then stays a gate that only needs to leave edit mode. (b) The pane's own stated discipline: add `if _editing: return` before the `workspace.apply_edit` call in `builder_source_pane.gd:195`, so the model is untouched until apply, and let apply's `edit_applied` be the single write that reaches the window's funnel. (b) is closer to what the doc promises and cheaper for the preview, but it must also fix SRC-02. Either way, add a chrome-suite assertion that after an edit-mode apply `ledger.can_undo()` is true, one `undo()` restores the pre-edit buffer, and `graph.cards[i].markup[0].text` reflects the new tag.

**Godot specifics:** `TextEdit.text_changed` fires on real keystrokes but NOT on `text = …` assignment — which is why the existing chrome test (`tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:216-232`) assigns `.text` and therefore never exercises this path at all. Any new test must use `insert_text_at_caret`/`delete_selection` like `_test_source_pane` does at line 651-653. Note also that `select_all(); delete_selection(); insert_text_at_caret(x)` emits `text_changed` TWICE, and the intermediate emission carries an EMPTY buffer straight into `workspace.apply_edit` — so option (b)'s guard also closes a window where the module is momentarily blank and the 5s journal could capture it.

**Risk:** The commonest editing gesture in the builder is unrecoverable. Ctrl+Z after a source edit walks past it to an older action, and the canvas silently disagrees with the buffer until some unrelated edit happens to re-project the card.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:1697-1713 (OnCodeEdited: ApplyEdit + RecordTyping + ScheduleCanvasRefresh) and :1163-1189 (ApplySourceEdit is gate-only) AND godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:185-197 (no _editing guard), builder_window.gd:902-906 (early return), builder_window.gd:865-874 (before == after → return false, so no ledger entry and no _after_model_change), builder_source_pane.gd:230-248

### `SRC-02` Abandoning an edit — switching module, or the module being deleted — leaves the typed text in the model with no snapshot and no ledger entry; Save writes it to disk

**Unity does:** Unity's snapshot exists to make abandonment safe: `BeginSourceEdit` stores `_sourceSnapshot = session.BufferText`, and `CancelSourceEdit` restores it and records the restore as one undoable edit ('The snapshot is the text EXACTLY as it stands, so cancel restores whitespace the user has since deleted as well as characters they added' — the Unreal leg states the same rule). Because Unity records typing continuously, an abandoned edit is still in the ledger and still undoable even if cancel is never pressed.

**Godot today:** absent. `show_module` resets `_editing`, the toggle and the buttons and drops `_snapshot` by simply not touching it, without restoring or committing anything (`builder_source_pane.gd:130-150`). Probe: enter edit mode on app.guitkx, type `this is not guitkx at all <<<`, then select another card — the module's buffer_text is permanently `this is not guitkx at all <<<`, `ws.has_unsaved_changes()` is true, `ledger.can_undo()` is false. Nothing on disk yet (deletion-is-absence means Save is the only writer), but Save will write it, and the 5s journal (`builder_window.gd:JOURNAL_INTERVAL_MSEC`) will have captured it before that. `clear()` (`:173-176`) is worse: it blanks `_path` and the text but leaves `_editing` true, `_editor.editable` true, `_apply`/`_revert` visible and `_snapshot` holding a deleted file's text.

**To build:** `show_module` and `clear` must both route through one `_leave_edit(restore: bool)` that decides: either commit through the funnel (Unity's model, where the ledger already has the keystrokes) or restore `_snapshot` through `workspace.apply_edit` before dropping it. Reset `_editing`, `_editor.editable`, `_edit_toggle.button_pressed`, the two button visibilities AND `_snapshot` in one place, so a future exit path cannot forget half of it. Cover it in `builder_chrome_test.gd`: type in edit mode, `show_module` elsewhere, assert the first module's buffer is unchanged (or that the ledger holds the change).

**Godot specifics:** `clear()` is reached from `refresh_from_model` when `workspace.try_get(_path)` returns null, i.e. when the open module is deleted from the canvas or by an undo. Deletion-is-absence means the module vanishes from the tree the moment the gesture lands, so this path runs during ordinary use, not only in error cases.

**Risk:** A user who types into the source pane, decides against it, and clicks another card has silently changed a file they did not mean to change — and the change survives to Save with nothing in the history to reverse it.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:1147-1161 (BeginSourceEdit snapshots) and :1191-1210 (CancelSourceEdit restores + records) AND godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:130-150 (show_module resets the flags, restores nothing), :173-176 (clear leaves edit state live), :42 (_snapshot never cleared on exit)

### `SRC-03` Ctrl+Enter does not apply and Escape does not cancel — the source pane has no keyboard at all

**Unity does:** `OnKeyDown` is registered TrickleDown on the input and intercepts three chords before the field acts: Escape → `CloseCompletionPopup(); CancelRequested?.Invoke()`; `(ctrlKey || SingleLine) && (Return || KeypadEnter)` → `StopImmediatePropagation(); imguiEvent?.Use(); ApplyRequested?.Invoke()`; Ctrl+Space → `ShowCompletions()`. The pane-title mini-buttons literally read `apply (Ctrl+Enter)` and `cancel (Esc)`. The capabilities contract states it as a line item: '§8 … Ctrl+Space completion; Ctrl+Enter applies.'

**Godot today:** absent. `builder_source_pane.gd` defines no `_gui_input`, `_input`, `_unhandled_key_input` or `Shortcut` at all; the only routes to apply/cancel are clicking the `apply` / `revert` Buttons. The window's own key model (`builder_window.gd:226-252`) deliberately bails whenever a text surface holds focus (`_typing_focused()`, :255-260), so Escape inside the pane reaches `_cancel_active_edit` never. Inside the editor, Ctrl+Enter falls into `GuitkxCodeEdit._gui_input`'s command branch, matches no case, and `return`s WITHOUT `accept_event()` — so CodeEdit's default newline handling runs and Ctrl+Enter inserts a line break. The buttons are labelled plain `edit`/`apply`/`revert`, so the chord is not even advertised, and the hint bar says only 'Source pane: edit → apply re-parses'.

**To build:** Add `_gui_input` (or better `_unhandled_key_input` on the pane with a focus check) that handles KEY_ESCAPE → `cancel_edit()` and `is_command_or_control_pressed() && (KEY_ENTER or KEY_KP_ENTER)` → `apply_edit()`, each with `accept_event()`. Relabel the buttons `apply (Ctrl+Enter)` / `cancel (Esc)` to match the reference's affordance. Add the chord to the hint bar string at `builder_window.gd:407-414`.

**Godot specifics:** The handler must run BEFORE `GuitkxCodeEdit._gui_input` or it will never see the key: a child Control's `_gui_input` fires first and CodeEdit consumes Enter. Put it on the pane as `_unhandled_key_input` (which runs only after no Control consumed it — wrong here, CodeEdit consumes Enter) or, correctly, add the two cases INSIDE `guitkx_code_edit.gd`'s existing command-branch match guarded by an exported `apply_on_ctrl_enter` flag, or connect a `Shortcut` on the pane's Buttons (`Button.shortcut` fires from `_shortcut_input`, which runs BEFORE `_gui_input` and so beats CodeEdit). The `Shortcut` route is the smallest correct change and is headlessly testable by pushing an `InputEventKey` through `Input.parse_input_event`.

**Risk:** The commit gesture the contract names does not exist, and the cancel gesture the whole snapshot machinery was built for is unreachable from the keyboard.

### `SRC-04` No diagnostics on the editing surface: the diagnostics gutter is allocated and never populated, and the ready-made renderer that would populate it is never called

**Unity does:** The CodeField root's SECOND child is a `_diagnosticsScroll` band (flexShrink 0, maxHeight 90) that runs local diagnostics when the buffer goes quiet and renders them under the text being edited; it is scrollable, selectable and copyable (§8: 'The diagnostics console is scrollable and selectable, holds every diagnostic, and supports Ctrl+A / Ctrl+C plus a copy-all menu'). Fragment mode is the ONE case that hides it, and UB-77 records that hiding it must be reversible in both directions. §11 states three merged tiers: structural `UITKX####`, unknown element/attribute against schema ∪ runtime registry, and compile errors.

**Godot today:** absent on the surface. `GuitkxCodeEdit.configure()` allocates a dedicated icon gutter (`diag_gutter`, width 24, clickable) and exposes `set_line_diagnostics()` and the `gutter_diagnostic_clicked` signal — and the builder calls NONE of it: grep for `diag_gutter`, `set_line_diagnostics`, `set_line_gutter`, `DiagnosticsRenderer` across `builder/` returns nothing. `editor/guitkx_diagnostics_renderer.gd` is a complete, tested implementation of exactly this (gutter icon + `set_line_background_color` tint + structured records + hint-tier suppression) used only by the `.guitkx` view. The result is a permanently empty 24px gutter in a 380px pane and zero per-line diagnostics. The only diagnostic surface is `builder_console.gd`, a SEPARATE mid-column pane that is `visible = false` until a preview round fails, and its `add_diagnostics` is called from exactly two places — a refused drop and a blank-module case — never with the focused module's structural diagnostics.

**To build:** On every settled buffer for the focused module, compile with the preview's own call shape and hand the diagnostics to `GuitkxDiagnosticsRenderer.render(_editor, _editor.diag_gutter, diags, err_icon, warn_icon)` plus `_editor.set_line_diagnostics(by_line)` so the hover card carries the message. Connect `_editor.gutter_diagnostic_clicked` to something (the console, or a tooltip). Feed the same list to `_console.add_diagnostics(_path, diags)` so warnings and hints that do NOT fail the build still appear. Icons come from `EditorInterface.get_editor_theme().get_icon("StatusError"/"StatusWarning", "EditorIcons")`.

**Godot specifics:** `GuitkxDiagnosticsRenderer.render` calls `clear()` first, which walks every line — cheap enough for a side pane but it should be debounced off the typing path, not run per keystroke. The renderer is reached in the builder by preload const, not by its global `class_name`, per the class-cache rule. It needs `EditorInterface` for the icons, so guard it the way `canvas_palette.gd:32` does and pass `null` icons headlessly — `set_line_gutter_icon(l, g, null)` is legal, so the tint and the metadata still work in the suites.

**Risk:** A file with a structural error shows no mark anywhere on the surface you are editing it on; the only signal is a one-line console entry, in a hidden pane, carrying only the FIRST error and no line number.

### `SRC-05` UB-86 reintroduced: clicking a card row always re-centres the source pane, including when the line is already on screen

**Unity does:** `ScrollRowIntoView` adjusts ONLY the vertical offset, preserves `offset.x` verbatim, and short-circuits with a bare `else return` when the row is already fully inside the viewport. The doc names the owner report: 'revealing one row yanked the pane sideways to a position nobody asked for, which read as the pane scrolling on its own in random directions (owner report 2026-08-17). A row already fully in view is left alone.' The Unreal leg reached the same rule independently ('VERTICAL ONLY (UB-86): scrolling horizontally as well throws away the user's column and reads as a jump'), and §8 states it as contract: 'Clicking a markup row scrolls the pane to that line (vertically only).'

**Godot today:** wrong. `goto_line` ends with `_editor.center_viewport_to_caret()`, which unconditionally scrolls the clicked line to the middle of the viewport whether or not it was already visible. So clicking three adjacent rows on a card makes the pane jump three times for no reason — the exact symptom UB-86 names. Godot already does the right thing without the call: `set_caret_line(line, adjust_viewport = true)` defaults to a MINIMAL adjustment that is a no-op when the line is on screen. The explicit centre overrides it.

**To build:** Delete `center_viewport_to_caret()` from `goto_line` (the default `adjust_viewport` on `set_caret_line`/`set_caret_column` already gives UB-86's behaviour), or replace it with `adjust_viewport_to_caret()` if an explicit call is preferred for readability. Add a chrome-suite assertion: set a scroll offset, `goto_line` a line already inside the viewport, assert `get_v_scroll()` is unchanged.

**Godot specifics:** `set_caret_column(0)` also forces the horizontal scroll to 0. That is defensible here (the pane goes to the line's start) but it is not Unity's rule, which preserves X exactly; if the pane later gains horizontal scrolling of consequence, prefer `set_caret_column(0, false)` and let the vertical adjust stand alone.

**Risk:** The pane jumps on every row click, which is the single most frequent canvas→source gesture. This is a defect Unity found in the field, wrote down, and fixed; the port reintroduced it because centring is the obvious one-liner.

### `SRC-17` The parity gate reports this whole area answered: one token is matched by three unrelated functions, and the CodeField 'deliberate' entry exempts the entire behaviour inventory

**Unity does:** n/a — this is about the Godot gate's coverage of the Unity behaviours listed above.

**Godot today:** hollow in three specific ways. (1) `["ApplySourceEdit", "func apply_edit"]` greps the whole of `builder/` for the token `func apply_edit`, which is defined in `builder_source_pane.gd:230`, `builder_window.gd:859` AND `builder_workspace.gd:290` — three different functions with three different jobs. **To build:** Replace the ambiguous token with one that names the pane's own function unambiguously (e.g. a `## PARITY:` marker comment, or a token like `func apply_edit() -> void:` plus a per-file scope in `_found`). Add parity rows for the behaviours the reuse does NOT deliver: an apply chord, an Escape chord, `set_error`, a diagnostics render call, `set_trace_names`. Narrow the DELIBERATE entry's wording to 'the CONTROL is reused; its behaviours are listed separately'. In the chrome suite, drive the edit cycle with `insert_text_at_caret` and assert the ledger and the card after apply. Add a source-pane block to the shots rig: enter edit mode, type, Ctrl+Enter, and print OK/BROKEN on the ledger entry.

**Godot specifics:** `_found` does a plain `text.contains(token)` over the concatenation of every `.gd` under `builder/` — it cannot distinguish files, so any token that is a common GDScript function name is answerable by accident. Scoping `_found` to a (file, token) pair costs three lines and removes the entire class of false green.

**Risk:** Every finding above sits behind a gate that currently prints '72/72 answered'. A green gate over an edit cycle that loses undo history is worse than a red one, because it is the reason nobody looked.

### `SRC-06` A failed apply has no visible mark on the field — only a toast that has already faded by the time the user looks back at the text

**Unity does:** `SetError(true)` paints a 1px border in (0.94, 0.38, 0.38) on all four sides of the CodeField root and it stays until the next successful parse; `ApplySourceEdit` sets it alongside the `"Parse failed: " + failure` toast and clears it on a clean apply and on cancel. The Unreal leg made the same call and said why the console alone is not enough: 'The BOX's surround turns red, not only the console. A message below the fold is easy to miss when the eye is on the text that caused it.' The POC rule is `textarea.err`.

**Godot today:** absent. `apply_edit` emits `complained("Parse failed: %s")`, the window turns that into a toast (`_source.complained.connect(toast)`), and nothing on the field changes. There is no `SetError`-equivalent anywhere in the pane, and the toast is time-limited (`_tick_toast`), so a user who reads the message, looks back at the code and then looks away has no standing indication that the buffer is still un-applied.

**To build:** Give the pane a `set_error(on: bool)` that applies a `StyleBoxFlat` panel override around `_editor` (or an owning `PanelContainer`) with `border_color = Color(0.94, 0.38, 0.38)` and `set_border_width_all(1)`, cleared to transparent/0. Call it `true` in the failure branch of `apply_edit`, `false` on a successful apply and in `cancel_edit`, mirroring `BuilderWindow.cs:1163-1198`.

**Godot specifics:** `CodeEdit` takes its frame from the `normal`/`focus` StyleBox theme items — `add_theme_stylebox_override("normal", box)` and `"focus"` both need setting or the border vanishes the moment the editor has focus, which in edit mode it always does. Wrapping `_editor` in a `PanelContainer` and styling that is the simpler route and does not fight the editor theme.

**Risk:** The one state where the pane is holding text the rest of the builder has refused looks identical to the state where everything is fine.

### `SRC-07` Hovering a hook chip warms the canvas rows but never the source pane — half of the contract line the parity gate calls answered

**Unity does:** `SetTraceNames(spaceSeparated)` pushes the hovered chip's state names into the CodeField, which bands every source LINE naming one of them with `TraceBand` = rgba(255,183,77,0.15) (POC `.srcline.hl`), deduped on the raw string so a repeated hover is free, and the selected line always outranks a trace line. §4 of the contract: 'hovering one highlights every usage of those names in the markup rows AND the source pane'.

**Godot today:** partial — canvas only. `builder_canvas_host.gd:_track_hover` computes `highlight_names` from the chip's projected text and `canvas_view.guitkx:223` paints `P.row_highlighted()` on matching MARKUP ROWS via `Metrics.row_mentions`. Nothing carries those names to `builder_source_pane.gd`: the pane has no `set_trace_names`, and `_canvas` exposes `highlight_names` to no one but its own render. So the source pane — the surface where the state is actually read and written — is the one place the answer does not appear.

**To build:** Emit the names from the canvas host when `highlight_names` changes (it already dedupes at `builder_canvas_host.gd:157-159`), connect it in `builder_window.gd`'s wiring block to a new `RuitkBuilderSourcePane.set_trace_names(names: PackedStringArray)`, and paint the matching lines with `TextEdit.set_line_background_color(line, Color(1.0, 0.718, 0.302, 0.15))` — reusing `Metrics.row_mentions`' word-boundary test against the raw line text. Clear every line's background on an empty set.

**Godot specifics:** `set_line_background_color` is per-line state on the TextEdit and must be cleared explicitly — the same reset `guitkx_diagnostics_renderer.gd:24-30` does. It also COLLIDES with SRC-04's diagnostic tint and SRC-08's selected-line band on the same property, so one function must own the per-line background and resolve the three sources in Unity's order (selected > trace > diagnostic > transparent). Do NOT drive it off `_render`-style per-frame work: the canvas host re-renders on hover and the pane must only repaint when the name set actually changes, or the reconciler-adjacent hover path pays for a full line walk per mouse move.

**Risk:** The gate reports this feature answered while the half the contract emphasises is missing.

### `SRC-08` The line a card row points at gets no band of its own — only the caret-line tint, which cannot say 'this is the row you clicked'

**Unity does:** `FocusLine(line1)` sets `_selectedLine1` and every recolour bands that row with `SelBand` = rgba(255,213,79,0.18) — the POC's `.srcline.sel` gold, chosen explicitly so it is NOT Unity's selection blue: 'POC ".srcline.sel": the focused line gets a gold band, not Unity's selection blue.' There is no persistent mark identifying the clicked row, and no line selection in edit mode.

**To build:** Track `_selected_line` on the pane, set it in `goto_line`, and paint it with `set_line_background_color(line, Color(1.0, 0.835, 0.310, 0.18))` through the same single owner as SRC-07/SRC-04, clearing the previous one. In edit mode also `select(line, 0, line, get_line(line).length())` to match `FocusLine`'s sanctioned selection. Reset `_selected_line` in `show_module` — Unity's `_selectedLine1` is never reset and its own edge-case note records the resulting stale band on the same line NUMBER of a different file; that defect is free to avoid here.

**Godot specifics:** `set_line_background_color` is the exact primitive (already proven in `guitkx_diagnostics_renderer.gd:64`). `highlight_current_line` draws over it, so the band colour should be chosen to read under the theme's `current_line_color`, or `highlight_current_line` disabled in this pane.

### `SRC-09` Double-clicking the source listing does not enter edit mode

**Unity does:** A `PointerDownEvent` on the read-mode ScrollView with `clickCount >= 2` raises `EditRequested`, which the window answers with `BeginSourceEdit` (snapshot + `SetSourceEditing(true)` + `FocusEditor()`), or with a `Toast("Read-only file")` when the session is read-only. The doc cites the POC directly: 'srcpane.addEventListener("dblclick", enterSrcEdit)'. The `edit` mini-button is the SECOND route, not the only one.

**Godot today:** absent. The only route into edit mode is the `edit` toggle Button (`_edit_toggle.toggled.connect(_set_editing)`). A double-click on the listing does what a non-editable `CodeEdit` does — selects a word — and the pane stays read-only.

**To build:** Connect a `gui_input` handler on `_editor` (or override in a thin subclass) that, while `not _editing`, sees `InputEventMouseButton` with `double_click == true` and calls `_set_editing(true)` plus `_edit_toggle.set_pressed_no_signal(true)`. Keep the read-only bounce: it already toasts through `complained`.

**Godot specifics:** `InputEventMouseButton.double_click` is Godot's `clickCount >= 2` equivalent and arrives through the child CodeEdit's `_gui_input`, so the pane must connect to `_editor.gui_input` (the signal, which fires alongside the virtual method) rather than adding a handler on itself — a `CodeEdit` with `MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` (the default) never lets the click reach the parent VBoxContainer. `editable = false` does not stop mouse input on a TextEdit, so the event does arrive.

**Risk:** The fast route into the pane's primary mode is missing, and the mode toggle is a small flat button in a title row.

### `SRC-10` Any change from elsewhere replaces the buffer under an open edit and destroys the editor's undo history — while the control already ships the fix and the pane does not use it

**Unity does:** Unity's `SetContent` is guarded on the file path (case-insensitive) and only resets the scroll on a real switch, and the ONE path that could land under a live edit — external file change — checks `_sourceSnapshot == null` before pushing. The Unreal leg added the echo guard Unity lacks ('the pane is bidirectional, so it must be able to tell its own echo from a real change'). Unity has no undo-history problem because the field's value assignment does not clear it.

**Godot today:** partial, with two distinct holes. (1) `refresh_from_model` has the echo guard Unity lacks (`if module.buffer_text == _editor.text: return`) — genuinely better — but NO `_editing` guard, and it is called from `_after_model_change`, i.e. on every canvas edit, every undo/redo and every recovery restore. Any of those, landing while the user is mid source-edit, replaces the text under them; the caret is preserved but the selection and the scroll are not. (2) All three write paths (`show_module:150`, `refresh_from_model:167`, `cancel_edit:261`) assign `_editor.text = …`, which in Godot CLEARS `TextEdit`'s undo history. `GuitkxCodeEdit.set_text_undoable()` exists precisely for this — its doc records the same defect from the `.guitkx` view ('Assigning `.text` clears the undo history — with format-on-save enabled that meant every Save destroyed Ctrl+Z (parity plan G33)') — and the builder's pane never calls it.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: CONFIRMED: `refresh_from_model` has no `_editing` guard. Reproduced — with the pane in edit mode and the user's typed text in the buffer, an external `workspace.apply_edit` + `refresh_from_model()` replaced the editor text wholesale ('wholly different') while `is_editing()` stayed true. Its caller is `_after_model_change` (builder_window.gd:892), i.e. every canvas edit, undo and recovery restore.

REFUTED: `.text =` does NOT clear TextEdit's undo history on Godot 4.7. Measured on a bare TextEdit: type 'X' → `has_undo()` true → `text = "wholly different"` → `has_undo()` STILL true, and `undo()` walked back through the assignment ('wholly different' → 'Xalpha' → 'alpha'). `TextEdit::set_text` with undo enabled is itself a complex operation. The `set_text_undoable` doc comment at guitkx_code_edit.gd:379-381 that the gap cites as evidence is stale for this engine version.

ALSO REFUTED — the godot_specifics: `set_text_undoable` does NOT emit two `text_changed` with an empty intermediate. Measured: it emits exactly ONE, carrying the FINAL text (`begin_complex_operation` suppresses the intermediate). So the prescribed 'add a `_loading` flag FIRST' is guarding against a hazard that does not exist, and the same note attached to SRC-01's godot_specifics is wrong for the same reason. (Verified separately that plain `.text =` emits nothing, so the pane's stated comparison-not-flag reasoning at :181-184 is correct.)

The real, worse consequence of the one-editor design is a different defect the gap does not name — see missed finding 1.

**To build:** Add an `_editing` check (or a snapshot-is-live check) to `refresh_from_model` so a canvas gesture cannot overwrite an open edit; if it must adopt, tell the user. Switch the three assignments to `set_text_undoable` so in-editor Ctrl+Z survives a canvas edit — but see the godot_specifics: it needs a suppression flag first.

**Godot specifics:** `set_text_undoable` uses `select_all(); delete_selection(); insert_text_at_caret(t)` inside a complex operation — each of those EMITS `text_changed`, and the intermediate emission carries an EMPTY buffer into `_on_text_changed` → `workspace.apply_edit(_path, "")`. The pane's doc explicitly chose `.text =` because assignment emits nothing and so needs no loading flag. So the correct order is: add a `_loading` suppression flag to `_on_text_changed` FIRST, then switch to `set_text_undoable`. Note the pane's stated reasoning ('The guard is the COMPARISON, not a loading flag… a flag would have to be right about the engine's behaviour') is correct about the engine and wrong about the consequence — it is exactly what pins the pane to the history-destroying assignment.

**Risk:** Ctrl+Z inside the source pane stops working the first time anything touches the canvas, and an open edit can be silently overwritten.

### `SRC-11` The inline editor is a bare LineEdit: no syntax colouring, no completion, no glyph scaling at zoom, and no multiline island editing

**Unity does:** The inline editor is a CodeField in `FragmentMode` — the regex colouring passes still run while the whole-file parse, local diagnostics and server tokens are skipped — with `UseCompactChrome()` (6px/2px on the input AND the listing, per the UB-128 invariant), `CenterSingleLine(boxHeight)`, `SingleLine = !multiline`, and a `FontSize` scaled from the anchor's `worldBound` height (`Mathf.Clamp(rowHeight * 0.55f, 11f, 26f)`, box sized FROM the font as `font * 1.65 + 8` per UB-106). §5: 'It carries syntax colouring, Ctrl+Space completion mapped to the exact file position, and overlay diagnostics… a single-line editor matches its row's height and glyph size at any zoom.' UB-99's owner quote: 'the selected wrap is big and the input is ugly.'

**Godot today:** partial. `builder_inline_editor.gd` is a plain `LineEdit`. It gets the important contract clauses right — `select_all_on_focus = false`, caret to end, Enter commits, Escape cancels, focus-out commits, Escape on a SEEDED editor undoes the seeding, one editor rather than many — but it has no colouring, no completion, no diagnostics, and no font scaling: `_body_row_rect` scales the RECT by `_canvas.zoom` (`row_height * zoom`) while the LineEdit keeps the theme font size, which is UB-99's symptom exactly. Multiline is not possible at all: a `LineEdit` cannot hold `\n`, so 'code islands (multiline)' is unreachable, and `_row_of` for `Metrics.Section.ISLAND` returns `card.markup[0]` instead (see SRC-12's sibling defect below).

**To build:** At minimum, scale the glyphs: `add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", clampi(int(rect.size.y * 0.55), 11, 26))` in `open_at`, and size the box from the chosen font rather than the other way round (UB-106). For colouring and completion, the cheapest faithful route is to swap the LineEdit for a one-line `GuitkxCodeEdit` (the reused control already has the highlighter and completion) with wrap off, gutters off, `scroll_fit_content_height`, and Enter mapped to commit — which is precisely Unity's `SingleLine` flag over a multiline field.

**Godot specifics:** A `LineEdit`'s font scales only through `add_theme_font_size_override`; there is no per-instance size property. If swapping to `GuitkxCodeEdit`, note it calls `configure()` in `_init` (allocating gutters and completion) and its `_ready` short-circuits when `not Engine.is_editor_hint()`, so headless suites see an uncoloured control — assert behaviour, not colour. Also keep `mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_STOP`: the current LineEdit sets it explicitly so a click lands on the editor rather than starting a canvas pan, and a CodeEdit defaults to STOP but its child scrollbars do not.

**Risk:** At Layer-3 zoom — the band the contract designates for in-place editing — the editor is a large box holding tiny unhighlighted text, over a row drawn at 2x. The one surface designed to be edited at high zoom is the one that ignores zoom.

### `SRC-12` Completion and go-to-definition resolve against DISK only, so the builder's own in-memory modules are invisible — and Ctrl+click renders a navigation affordance that is wired to nothing

**Unity does:** `SetKnownElements` refreshes the classification/completion set without touching the buffer or caret, comparing by REFERENCE so a repeated identical set is free (UB-160 records that the CALLER must cache it too). The set is schema element names ∪ the runtime element registry's `RegisteredNames` ∪ COMPONENT exports FROM THE LIVE GRAPH (§4: 'A module is therefore wired into the tree the moment its import is typed, with no file behind it'), and null until both are live so startup cannot storm false unknown-element errors. Unity also calls `SyncLspBuffer(_focusFile, bufferLf)` on every keystroke so the language server sees unsaved text.

**Godot today:** partial. Host-element completion works well (probe: 108 items for `<M`, native classes first) and the highlighter's host-vs-component split is decided from the host VOCABULARY, not an index, so in-memory components DO colour as components — that half is right. But `GuitkxCompletion.for_caret` sources user components from `GuitkxWorkspace`, a STATIC DISK index built with `FileAccess`/`DirAccess`; probe confirms `is_component('MyBuilderComp')` is false for a module that exists only in the builder's tree. Since nothing reaches disk until Save, a whole new tree's components are uncompletable. `GuitkxWorkspace.reindex(path, text)` exists and is exactly the hook needed; grep shows `builder/` never references `GuitkxWorkspace`, `GuitkxCompletion` or `GuitkxSchema` at all. Worse, `GuitkxCodeEdit._on_symbol_validate` calls `set_symbol_lookup_word_as_valid(true)` for any indexed component — drawing the underline and the pointer cursor — and its `definition_requested` signal is connected NOWHERE in the builder, so Ctrl+click on a component tag promises navigation and does nothing.

**To build:** Either (a) connect `_editor.definition_requested` to `select_module` + `goto_line` (mapping the returned offset through `RuitkGuitkxDiag.line_col`) and push the builder's in-memory buffers into the index on focus change, or (b) if poisoning the shared index is unacceptable, give `GuitkxCodeEdit` an optional `extra_components: Callable` the builder fills from `graph.cards` and have `_on_symbol_validate` consult it. (b) is safer. Either way, stop `set_symbol_lookup_word_as_valid(true)` from firing when nothing can answer the click.

**Godot specifics:** `GuitkxWorkspace` is STATIC and shared with the live `.guitkx` editor view, so calling `reindex` with unsaved builder buffers poisons the real editor's index for the rest of the session — which is the same class of hazard the preview mirror was designed against. Note the mirror is already safe: `_collect_guitkx` honours `.gdignore` (guitkx_workspace.gd:111) and the preview root writes one, so `res://__ruitk_builder_preview__~/` never enters the index. That interaction is correct today and must stay correct if the index gains a builder feed.

**Risk:** On a brand-new tree — the builder's own primary use case — completion never knows the components you just created, and a Ctrl+click affordance is drawn over text that will not navigate.

### `SRC-13` Read mode — the state the pane is in almost all the time — draws the whole file at half opacity

**Unity does:** Read mode is the DEFAULT and shows the listing at full-strength ink: 12px mono `BuilderPalette.Text` #D6D6DC on Ground #17171B, with the same colours as edit mode. The whole two-view architecture exists so that read and edit look identical apart from the caret.

**Godot today:** divergent-defect. The pane opens read-only (`_editor.editable = false`) and returns to read-only after every apply/cancel/module switch, and it never overrides `font_readonly_color`. Godot's TextEdit draws a non-editable buffer through that theme colour, and where a SyntaxHighlighter supplies a colour the engine keeps the hue but forces the read-only ALPHA. Probed default: `font_color = (0.875,0.875,0.875,1.0)`, `font_readonly_color = (0.875,0.875,0.875,0.5)` — so the source pane is a 50%-faded file until the user clicks `edit`.

**To build:** `_editor.add_theme_color_override("font_readonly_color", _editor.get_theme_color("font_color"))` in the pane's `_init`, next to the other editor configuration at lines 94-102. If a read/edit distinction is still wanted, make it the pane header or a border, not the legibility of the text.

**Godot specifics:** The editor theme sets its own `font_readonly_color`; the override must be applied per-instance on the CodeEdit and re-applied if the theme changes (`GuitkxCodeEdit` already connects `EditorInterface.get_base_control().theme_changed` at :56-58 for the highlighter — hook it there or re-apply in `_on_theme_changed`).

**Risk:** The default state of the pane is the least legible one, on a narrow side column where legibility is already tight.

*medium · visual · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/Controls/CodeField.cs:241-409 (Ground + Text everywhere, no read-mode dimming), :447-461 (SetEditing(false) restores identical ink) AND godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:102 (`editable = false`), :145-147 + :244 + :257 (returns to read-only on every exit), no `font_readonly_color` override anywhere in the file; probed Godot 4.7 default theme font_readonly_color alpha = 0.5

### `SRC-14` Clicking a code-island row sends the source pane to the wrong line and arms Delete on the wrong row

**Unity does:** Every row the canvas lists carries an exact source span and `FocusLine` takes the source pane to THAT span; §5 lists code islands as editable in place ('a code island editor replaces its island exactly'), so an island row resolves to the island, not to something else.

**Godot today:** wrong. `_row_of` for `Metrics.Section.ISLAND` returns `card.markup[0]` — the card's FIRST MARKUP ROW — with the comment 'The SETUP block is edited whole, not row by row'. `_on_row_clicked` then does `_menu_row = row` and `_source.goto_line(row.source_line)`, so clicking a setup-code line (a) jumps the source pane to the top of the markup instead of to the island, and (b) arms `_delete_selection` (`builder_window.gd:270-276`) on the first markup row — so Delete after clicking a setup line removes an element the user was not pointing at.

**To build:** Return a real island line from `_row_of` (the island rows already carry `island_start_line` + index, as `_seed_island_editor` at builder_window.gd:1619-1624 proves), so `goto_line` lands on it and `_menu_row` is the island span. If the island genuinely cannot be row-deleted, return `null` rather than a substitute row — `_on_row_clicked` already handles null by returning, which is strictly safer than pointing at the wrong thing.

**Godot specifics:** `_row_of` is a plain lookup with no signal wiring, so this is headlessly testable in `builder_chrome_test.gd` today: `_on_row_clicked(card, Metrics.Section.ISLAND, 0)` then assert `w.source_pane().editor().get_caret_line() + 1 == card.island_start_line`. The existing row-spine test (`tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:251-266`) covers only `Section.MARKUP`.

**Risk:** A click on setup code silently re-aims a destructive key at unrelated markup, and the row→source contract lies for one whole section of every card.

*medium · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/Controls/CodeField.cs:588-619 (FocusLine takes the row's own line), Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:1743-1752 (OnCanvasRowClicked), plans/UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:170-172 AND godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1543-1547 (`return card.markup[0]` for ISLAND), :1007-1021 (_menu_row = row; goto_line(row.source_line)), :270-276 (_delete_selection acts on _menu_row)

### `SRC-18` The reused control's dependency on six global class_names sits inside the very hazard the builder's own layers were written to avoid

**Unity does:** n/a — Godot-specific.

**Godot today:** risk, not yet observed. Every file under `builder/document/` and `builder/canvas/` carries the same header comment: 'ProjectSettings.save() rewrites that cache from whatever the running process loaded', and they reference each other exclusively through preload consts. `builder_source_pane.gd` correctly preloads `editor/guitkx_code_edit.gd` by path — but that script resolves `GuitkxCodeHighlighter`, `RuitkEditorSettings`, `GuitkxContext`, `GuitkxCompletion`, `GuitkxWorkspace` and `GuitkxHover` as bare global class_names at parse time. If the editor class cache is truncated in a session that has not loaded those, the preload fails to parse, `builder_source_pane.gd` fails to load, and the builder window fails to assemble — not with a missing pane, but with a script load error. The rest of the builder is immune by construction; the source pane is the one place the immunity stops.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Real and correctly located: guitkx_code_edit.gd resolves `GuitkxCodeHighlighter` (:52), `RuitkEditorSettings` (:155, :408, :518), `GuitkxContext` (:159, :411, :480, :522), `GuitkxCompletion` (:412, :459-465), `GuitkxWorkspace` (:471, :486) and `GuitkxHover` (:471, :492, :523, :559) as bare global class_names, while `SignatureScript`/`BridgeScript` (:33-36) already use preload consts with the stated cold-cache reason. That inconsistency is worth closing.

But 'the rest of the builder is immune by construction' is wrong. `builder/canvas/builder_canvas_host.gd:270-272` calls `RuitkRoot.create(...)` and `V.fc(...)` as bare globals, and the COMMITTED generated `builder/canvas/canvas_view.gd` names `V` 44 times and `RuitkVNode` 7 times; `builder_graph_service.gd` names `RuitkVNode` and `Hooks`. Those resolve through the same `global_script_class_cache.cfg`. A truncated cache takes out the canvas layer whether or not the source pane is fixed, so the fix is worth making but the risk framing ('the source pane is the one place') should be corrected before it is written down as a finding.

**To build:** Convert the six global references inside `guitkx_code_edit.gd` to preload consts (it already does exactly this for `SignatureScript` and `BridgeScript` at :33-36, with the comment 'Preload (not the global class name): cold class caches' — so the precedent and the reasoning are already in the file). This costs nothing to the `.guitkx` view and closes the builder's exposure.

**Godot specifics:** `GuitkxCodeHighlighter` and `RuitkEditorSettings` are referenced from `_ready`/`configure`, i.e. at runtime, but GDScript resolves global class identifiers at PARSE time, so an unresolved name is a load failure of the whole script, not a runtime error at the call site. That is why preload is the fix and a `ClassDB`/`has_method` guard is not.

**Risk:** A cache truncation takes out the whole builder window rather than degrading one pane — the exact failure mode the document layer's preload discipline was adopted to prevent.

*medium · risk · OVERSTATED* — unity n/a AND godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/editor/guitkx_code_edit.gd:33-36 (the two dependencies that already use preload, with the stated reason) vs :52, :155, :159, :412, :471, :523 (six that do not); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:24 and six sibling files (the class-cache header comment); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:18 (preloads the control correctly)

### `SRC-15` The apply gate compiles with a different call shape from the preview, so it green-lights buffers the build will refuse

**Unity does:** `ApplySourceEdit` runs `BuilderLanguage.Parse(text, _focusFile)` — the same parse the model and the cards use — and scans for the first `ParseSeverity.Error`. The gate and the rest of the builder read the buffer through one front door.

**Godot today:** divergent. `apply_edit` calls `Compiler.compile(text, _path.get_file().get_basename())` with `self_path` and `root` defaulted to `""`, while the preview calls `Compiler.compile(buffer, mirrored_basename, [], {}, mirrored, scratch_root)`. Probed with a buffer containing `import { Row } from "./row"`: the apply gate returns `ok = true`; the preview shape returns `ok = false` with `GUITKX2300 unknown import specifier './row'`. So the gate is strictly LOOSER — import resolution, cross-file binding and unknown-component checks are all switched off in it — and 'applied cleanly' does not mean 'will build'. The failure then surfaces only in the console, which is hidden until a round fails. Separately, the gate runs FULL CODEGEN (emitting `gd`) where a parse would do.

**To build:** Give the gate the same call shape as `builder_preview.gd:260-262` (or better, expose one `compile_for(module)` helper both call) so 'apply refused' and 'the preview refused' are the same verdict, and so the message the user gets names the same diagnostic the console will. If full resolution is deliberately out of scope for a keystroke-cheap gate, say so in the doc — the current comment ('a buffer that does not parse is not a state to hand the rest of the builder') reads as a stronger guarantee than the call makes.

**Godot specifics:** `RuitkGuitkx.compile` also has an `env_error` return (`{ ok:false, env_error:true, … GUITKX2507 }`) for a transient tooling state where the vocabulary could not be read. The gate treats that identically to a source error and refuses the edit with a confusing 'Parse failed: … vocabulary.json could not be loaded' — it should let the apply through (or retry) rather than blocking the user on the compiler's own startup.

**Risk:** Low on its own, but it is the seam through which a 'successful' apply becomes a failed build with no explanation on the surface the user is looking at.

*low · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:1163-1189 (Parse with _focusFile) AND godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:234 (compile(text, basename) — no self_path, no root) vs addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/preview/builder_preview.gd:259-262 (compile(buffer, basename, [], {}, mirrored, scratch_root)); probe: same source, ok=true vs ok=false GUITKX2300

### `SRC-16` A diagnostic row with a line number can never open its file — the row's stored path has the line appended to it

**Unity does:** Console rows are locations: activating one navigates to the file and, in the panes that carry it, the line.

**Godot today:** latent defect. `add_diagnostics` builds `where = "%s:%d" % [file_path, line + 1]` when `line >= 0` and passes it as `_add_row`'s `file_path` parameter, which stores it verbatim in `_rows.append({ "path": file_path })`. `_on_item_activated` emits that string as `location_activated`, and the window connects it straight to `select_module` — which does `workspace.try_get("res://…/app.guitkx:12")` and finds nothing. Both current callers pass `line = -1`, so it never fires today; it will the moment SRC-04 is built, which is exactly the caller that WILL pass real lines.

**To build:** Store the bare path in `_rows` and keep the `:line` only in the display string; carry the line as a second field and widen `location_activated(file_path, line)` so the window can call `select_module` then `_source.goto_line(line)` — which is what makes a console row worth clicking.

**Godot specifics:** `Paths.key`/`Paths.same` are case-folded canonical comparisons; a path with `:12` appended survives `canon` and simply never matches, so the failure is silent — no push_error, no toast.

**Risk:** Small now, guaranteed to bite whoever wires real diagnostics into the console.

*low · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/Controls/CodeField.cs:939-940 + :1034-1035 (diagnostics rendered against real lines) AND godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_console.gd:131-138 (where = path:line), :140-148 (_add_row stores it as path), :163-168 (location_activated emits it), builder_window.gd:728 (connected to select_module)

### Window shell, layout, toolbar, commands, status, console, help, keyboard model

### `shell.keyboard-focus-dead` The entire keyboard model is unreachable: nothing ever gives — or gives back — keyboard focus to the window Control

**Unity does:** Unity treats "who holds the keyboard" as a first-class problem with two named mechanisms. `FocusExisting(bool focusRoot)` focuses the window AND its root element, because "a KeyDownEvent is dispatched to the focused ELEMENT, and closing an inline editor leaves none. The root takes it back so Ctrl+Z reaches OnKeyDown rather than falling through to Unity's global undo" (UB-108). The inline editor calls it on ALL THREE exit paths — commit, cancel and blur. `ReclaimKeyboard(4)` re-asserts focus four times at 30 ms after a create prompt closes, because "a state test cannot see a closing window that has not taken focus back YET" (UB-197 / UB-199); UB-209 later moved the real fix upstream so the search menu focuses its invoking window synchronously before opening.

**Godot today:** absent. `builder_window.gd:139` sets `focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_ALL` and then NOTHING in the builder ever calls `grab_focus()` on the window. The only `grab_focus()` targeting the shell is `plugin.gd:455`, on the FileSystem-dock context route alone — `_open_builder()` (plugin.gd:422-446), which is what the main-menu item and the Tools fallback both call, never focuses it. `builder_canvas_host.gd:91` sets `mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` but leaves `focus_mode` at the Control default FOCUS_NONE, so clicking the canvas focuses nothing. `builder_inline_editor.gd:100-107` (`_close`) returns focus to no one on commit, cancel or blur. I verified the routing consequence on Godot 4.7 headless: a Shell Control (focus_mode ALL, `_gui_input` counting keys) with a focused child, pushing Ctrl+Z, gave `shell hits = 1` when the shell itself held focus, `0` when a Button held it, `0` when a plain focusable child held it, and `0` with no focus owner at all. Godot delivers key events to the focus owner's `_gui_input` ONLY — there is no bubbling to ancestors, which is the assumption `builder_window.gd:226 _gui_input` is written on. Net: Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y, Delete and Escape work at most once (after the dock-context open) and stop permanently at the first click on any Button, the source pane's CodeEdit, the console ItemList, the folder Tree or a library row. Opened from the main menu they never work at all. `_delete_selection` and `_cancel_active_edit` have exactly one caller each — `_gui_input` — so both are dead in practice, and the tests covering them (tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:1054, :1063) call them directly, bypassing routing entirely.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One overstatement in the phrasing: "work at most once (after the dock-context open)" understates it slightly — after `plugin.gd:455` the shortcuts work for as long as the shell keeps focus, i.e. until the first click on any focusable control, not literally one keypress. Everything else is accurate, including the claim that they never work at all when opened from the main menu or the Tools fallback.

**To build:** 1) Give `RuitkBuilderWindow` a `_reclaim_keyboard()` that calls `grab_focus()` on itself, and call it from: the end of `_open_builder()` in plugin.gd (not just `open_builder_on`), the inline editor's three exits (via a signal the window listens to — the editor must not reach for its host), the SearchMenu picked/submitted/hide paths, and `run_command` after every toolbar Button press. 2) Set `focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_CLICK` on `builder_canvas_host.gd` so clicking the canvas puts the keyboard somewhere the model can see. 3) The robust alternative, and the one I would take: move the key handling off `_gui_input` onto `_shortcut_input(event)` on the window, which Godot delivers tree-wide regardless of focus owner, keeping the existing `_typing_focused()` guard (builder_window.gd:257-261) to stand down while a TextEdit/LineEdit/CodeEdit owns the keyboard. That removes the focus dependency instead of chasing it. 4) Add a real routing test that pushes an `InputEventKey` at the viewport rather than calling `_gui_input` by hand, and asserts the ledger moved.

**Godot specifics:** The most Godot-specific defect in the area, and invisible from the Unity source because UI Toolkit's KeyDownEvent DOES propagate up the visual tree while Godot's `_gui_input` does not: `Viewport` dispatches `InputEventKey` to `gui.key_focus` and stops. `_shortcut_input` and `_unhandled_key_input` are the tree-wide hooks and neither is used anywhere under `builder/` (only `builder_search_menu.gd:214` uses `_input`, inside its own PopupPanel viewport). Two further wrinkles: the builder lives in a `Window` (plugin.gd:429), its own Viewport with its own `gui.key_focus`, so focus does not carry from the editor; and in the editor's single-window mode the Window is EMBEDDED, so an unhandled Ctrl+S can reach the editor's own Save Scene shortcut instead of the builder's Save — a keystroke meaning "write my tree" doing something else. Note the parity gate answers Unity's `OnKeyDown` with `func _typing_focused` (tests/builder_parity.gd:97), `DeleteSelection` with `func _delete_selection` (:98) and `CancelActiveEdit` with `func _cancel_active_edit` (:102) — three green entries over a gesture that cannot be performed; `FocusExisting` and `ReclaimKeyboard` are not on the checklist at all.

*critical · gesture · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderWindow.cs:45-62 (FocusExisting), :660-683 (ReclaimKeyboard), :6103-6109 (ReclaimKeyboard(4)), Controls/BuilderInlineEditorOverlay.cs:207,:287,:293, Plans~/UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:3345-3349, :3374-3388, :3647-3658 | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:139, :226-253, :269-293; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_canvas_host.gd:91; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_inline_editor.gd:100-107; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/plugin.gd:422-446, :451-455; tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:1054, :1063; tests/builder_parity.gd:97-102

### `shell.load-tree-veto` Opening a file while the builder holds unsaved work destroys the whole session, silently

> **Duplicate of `DM-01`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** `LoadTreeFor(path)` refuses to replace the tree when there is unsaved work: it returns immediately if the path is empty or already in the tree (`_workspace.TryGet(path) != null`), and when `_workspace.HasUnsavedChanges` it calls `_workspace.Open(path)` — a SINGLE-file open — and toasts "Opened <file> on its own - save or abort first to load its whole tree". The comment states the rule: "A load REPLACES the tree, which is why unsaved work vetoes it... Losing an unsaved buffer to a right-click in the Project window is not a trade worth making." It also falls back to `Open(path)` when the tree scan could not reach the file, so it gets its own card rather than an empty canvas.

**Godot today:** absent, and worse than "no veto". `builder_window.gd:749-773 open_tree()` unconditionally calls `Preview.clear_scratch()`, `workspace.load_tree(focus_path)` and `ledger.clear()`. `builder_workspace.gd:161-203 load_tree()` ends in `_tree.reset(loaded, projection)` — every in-memory buffer thrown away and re-read from disk. No `has_unsaved_changes()` check, no already-in-the-tree short-circuit, no toast, and the ledger that could have taken it back is cleared in the same breath. `plugin.gd:451-455 open_builder_on()` calls `open_tree(file_path)` unconditionally on EVERY dock-context invocation, including on a file already loaded. So: right-click any .guitkx in the FileSystem dock while the builder holds an hour of unsaved edits — even the very file being edited — and the work is gone with no prompt, no toast and no undo. The single-file open the veto path needs already exists and is dead code: `builder_workspace.gd:210 open()` has ZERO callers anywhere in the repo.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One detail to keep the plan honest: the MAIN-MENU path is already partly guarded. `_open_builder()` (plugin.gd:444-445) only calls `open_tree` when `_builder.focus_path().is_empty()`, with a comment saying re-pointing an open session "would take a tree with unsaved work away from under someone" — so the reasoning already exists in the file. The unguarded path is `open_builder_on` (the FileSystem-dock right-click) alone. That narrows the reproduction but not the severity: the dock route is the documented way to open an existing tree, and it destroys the session including the file being edited.

**To build:** In `builder_window.gd:open_tree`, before touching the workspace: return early when `Paths.canon(focus_path)` is already in `workspace.modules()` (mirroring Unity's `TryGet != null` short-circuit — this alone stops the re-open-the-same-file case); then, when `workspace.has_unsaved_changes()`, call the existing `workspace.open(focus_path)` instead of `load_tree`, toast "Opened %s on its own — save or abort first to load its whole tree", re-project, and do NOT clear the ledger. Only on the clean path do the full `load_tree` + `ledger.clear()`. Add Unity's fallback too: if after `load_tree` the path still has no module, `workspace.open(path)` so it gets its own card.

**Godot specifics:** `workspace.open()` re-checks disk for a clean module before returning it (builder_workspace.gd:210-220), which is exactly what the veto branch wants — no new model code, only wiring. Guard the re-entrancy the window already thinks about elsewhere: `open_tree` calls `select_module`, which is `_choosing`-guarded (builder_window.gd:2151-2178), so the veto branch must still end in `reproject()` + `select_module()` or the canvas keeps showing the pre-open graph. Leave `Preview.clear_scratch()` (builder_window.gd:764) on the clean branch only — it wipes the mirror at `res://__ruitk_builder_preview__~/`, and on a veto that would throw away every built script for nothing. All three branches are pure model operations and drive headlessly in builder_chrome_test.gd.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderWindow.cs:96-121 (LoadTreeFor), :73-94 (OpenFor) | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:749-773; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:161-203 (`_tree.reset`), :210-220 (`open`, zero callers); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/plugin.gd:451-455

### `shell.external-change-adoption` External .guitkx edits are never adopted, and Save writes the stale buffer over them

**Unity does:** `OnUitkxImported(fullPaths)` runs on Unity's asset-import event: `_workspace.ReloadCleanFromDisk(fullPaths)`, and for every path that actually changed it calls `NotifyBufferChanged()` (a preview rebuild), `_canvasHost.RefreshGraph(path)`, and — when the focus changed and no source-pane edit is in flight (`_sourceSnapshot == null`) — `_codeField.SetContent(...)`, then `RefreshChrome()`. Dirty sessions keep the user's buffer by design. Recorded reason: "An external change alters what the preview would render, so it has to rebuild. This was simply missing: the card refreshed and the preview kept showing the pre-change build."

**Godot today:** absent. `builder_workspace.gd:237 reload_clean_from_disk()` — the exact model primitive — EXISTS, is documented and is tested (tests/builder_model_test.gd:747-753), and has zero production callers: grep returns the definition plus three test lines and nothing else. `builder_module.gd:277-285 adopt_disk_text()` likewise. Nothing in `builder_window.gd` or `plugin.gd` subscribes the builder to filesystem change: `plugin.gd:144` connects `filesystem_changed` to a debounce whose handler `_on_fs_settled` (plugin.gd:337-340) refreshes `GuitkxWorkspace` and `_view` — the .guitkx main-screen editor — and never mentions the builder. The consequence is not merely a stale card: `builder_workspace.gd:475-548 save_all()` writes `module.to_disk_text()` for any module where `is_dirty()`, with no mtime, hash or content check against what is on disk now. Open the builder on a tree, switch to the .guitkx editor (or another IDE, or `git pull`), change a file, come back, edit anything, press Save — the external change is silently reverted. For this project that is the NORMAL workflow: the builder and the .guitkx editor are the same plugin, and plugin.gd:270-278 (`_save_external_data` / `_apply_changes`) actively flushes the .guitkx view's buffer to disk behind the builder's back on Save All and on Play.

**To build:** 1) In `plugin.gd:_on_fs_settled`, after `GuitkxWorkspace.rescan()`, call a new `_builder.adopt_external_changes()` when `_builder != null`. 2) Implement it in `builder_window.gd` as Unity's `OnUitkxImported`: collect every open module path, `var changed := workspace.reload_clean_from_disk(paths)`, return when empty, then `preview.request_refresh()`, re-populate each changed card with the `Service.populate_card` + `Service.refresh_edges_for` pair `_after_model_change` already uses, `_source.refresh_from_model()` guarded by `_source.is_editing()` (Unity's `_sourceSnapshot == null` guard), and `_refresh_status()`. 3) Independently, give `save_all` a conflict check: a module whose disk content no longer matches its `projected_text` must not be blind-written — refuse it, name it, let the user choose. That is the only thing that makes the contract safe even if the event wiring is missed.

**Godot specifics:** `EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem().filesystem_changed` is the analogue of Unity's import event and plugin.gd already has it debounced at 0.5 s (plugin.gd:139-144) — the builder just has to be told. But the editor addon's own hard-won lesson (CLAUDE.md, editor plugin section) applies: a `.guitkx`-only external edit does NOT reliably flip Godot's changed flag, which is why the .guitkx watcher also recompiles on editor FOCUS-IN with an mtime staleness guard. The builder needs the same belt-and-braces — sweep on the builder Window's own focus-in notification as well, comparing mtimes so it stays cheap. Everything here is `FileAccess`-only, so it stays headlessly testable by writing to the sandbox and calling the new method directly.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderWindow.cs:175-207 (OnUitkxImported), :123-160 (OnEnable sweep at :158) | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:237 (dead), :475-548 (save_all, no conflict check); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_module.gd:277-285 (dead); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/plugin.gd:139-144, :270-278, :333-340; tests/builder_model_test.gd:747-753

### `shell.no-save-door` Nothing outside the builder knows it is dirty: no quit prompt, no close prompt, and plugin teardown frees the window with unsaved work in it

**Unity does:** UB-118. `hasUnsavedChanges = _workspace.HasUnsavedChanges` is set on every `RefreshChrome()`, `saveChangesMessage` is set in `OnEnable`, and `SaveChanges()` / `DiscardChanges()` are OVERRIDDEN so the framework's own save door routes through the builder's Save rather than straight to `_workspace.SaveAll()`. The recorded lesson is the general one: "a save-only contract cannot be enforced by a string comparison at one call site, because the framework has its own save door." `SaveChanges` calls `base.SaveChanges()` only when the save actually cleared everything, so a cancelled location prompt leaves the window dirty rather than reporting a save that did not happen.

**Godot today:** absent, and the signal built to carry it is dead. `builder_window.gd:52` declares `signal dirty_changed(has_unsaved: bool)` "for the plugin's title, or a prompt on close" and `:2470-2472` emits it — and grep finds no `connect` anywhere in the repo. Godot's framework save door is `EditorPlugin._get_unsaved_status`, and `plugin.gd:252-257` asks only `_view.dirty_files()`, so quitting Godot with an unwritten builder tree gets no prompt at all. `plugin.gd:435` wires the Window's `close_requested` to `hide()` with no dirty check (fine and deliberate — the session survives). But `plugin.gd:162-165` (`_exit_tree`, which runs on plugin disable AND editor shutdown) does `_builder_window.queue_free()` with the comment "a disabled plugin leaves no window" — taking every unsaved buffer with it, silently. There is no `_save_external_data` participation either, so Godot's Save All does not reach the builder. Combined with the dead recovery offer, an editor quit with unsaved builder work loses it with no prompt at any point and no way back.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Worth adding to the ask: `builder_window.gd:146-147 _exit_tree()` is `preview.teardown()` and nothing else — it does not capture the journal either, so the teardown path loses up to `JOURNAL_INTERVAL_MSEC` (5 s, :932) of work even on top of everything else. A one-line `Journal.capture(...)` there is the cheapest half of this fix and is independent of the plugin-side wiring.

**To build:** 1) In plugin.gd, connect `_builder.dirty_changed` when the builder is created; stamp the Window title (`"RUITK Builder *"`) so the state is visible, and cache the flag. 2) Extend `_get_unsaved_status(for_scene)` to append the builder's status when dirty — Godot joins every plugin's string into its own quit-confirmation dialog, which is precisely Unity's `saveChangesMessage`. 3) Decide `_save_external_data` explicitly: a silent flush would violate "nothing is written until Save", so declining with a comment is probably right, but it must be a decision rather than an omission. 4) In `_exit_tree`, when the builder is dirty, do not `queue_free()` blind — capture the journal first, or raise the same ConfirmationDialog `save()` already uses for deletions. 5) On `close_requested`, keep `hide()` but toast once when dirty so the user knows work is still held.

**Godot specifics:** `EditorPlugin._get_unsaved_status` is the exact analogue of Unity's `hasUnsavedChanges` + `saveChangesMessage` pair, and plugin.gd already implements it for the OTHER surface (plugin.gd:252-257) — the pattern is in the file, the builder is just not in it. Two Godot-specific hazards make this worse than in Unity: (a) the builder Window is a child of `EditorInterface.get_base_control()`, so it is freed by editor shutdown whether or not `_exit_tree` runs cleanly; (b) an editor script reload — Godot's nearest thing to a domain reload — re-binds `@tool` scripts on live nodes, and `workspace`, `ledger`, `graph` and `_focus_path` are plain non-exported vars with no serialisation contract, so a reload while the builder is open is a second silent-loss path. Both are why the journal restore offer is not optional here.

### `shell.journal-never-offered` Unsaved work is journalled every 5 s and never offered back — the recovery path is dead code behind a green parity entry

**Unity does:** `OnEnable` arms `EditorApplication.delayCall += OfferJournalRestore` — DEFERRED on purpose, because "the window may be opening ON a file, and that load runs after this. Asking then would offer to restore over a tree the user just asked for." `OfferJournalRestore` bails when `_workspace.Modules.Count > 0`, peeks the journal, raises a modal Restore/Discard dialog naming the module count and the timestamp, and on Restore calls `TryRestore`, `RebindFocusIfMissing`, `RefreshChrome`, `MountCanvas` and toasts "Restored N unsaved module(s)". `beforeAssemblyReload += JournalTree` captures it.

**Godot today:** absent at the point of use. The capture half works: `builder_window.gd:936-947 _journal_tick()` writes the tree every `JOURNAL_INTERVAL_MSEC` (5000) whenever `workspace.has_unsaved_changes()`, and `save()` / `abort()` clear it so its presence means exactly one thing. `builder_journal.gd:40 capture` / `:60 peek` / `:70 try_restore` / `:82 clear` all exist. The three window-level accessors `pending_recovery()` (builder_window.gd:950), `restore_recovery()` (:955) and `discard_recovery()` (:964) exist — and grep for all three across the repo returns ONLY those definitions plus one line in the parity gate. Nothing calls them. The builder faithfully writes a crash journal every five seconds and has never once offered it back. tests/builder_parity.gd:111 maps Unity's `OfferJournalRestore` to the token `func pending_recovery` and passes — a green gate over a safety net wired to nothing.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One more reason to prioritise this, and one more thing the fix must handle: `abort()` (builder_window.gd:2076-2084) clears the journal as well as the ledger, with no confirmation of any kind (see my missed finding on Abort). So the single most likely way to destroy a session is also the one that erases the recovery file the offer would read.

**To build:** Call the offer from `open_tree()` when it lands on the start screen (empty `focus_path`) AND from `plugin.gd:_open_builder()` immediately after the window is first created, deferred one frame so a load already in flight wins — `call_deferred` is the direct analogue of `EditorApplication.delayCall`. Guard exactly as Unity does: skip when `workspace.modules()` is non-empty. Raise a `ConfirmationDialog` (the builder already builds one by hand at builder_window.gd:2005-2020 for deletions, so reuse that shape) naming the module count and `saved_at` from `Journal.peek()`; Restore -> `restore_recovery()` + a toast; Discard -> `discard_recovery()`. Then FIX THE GATE: `func pending_recovery` proves nothing — replace the token with one only the wired path can satisfy, and add a builder_chrome_test.gd case that captures a journal, builds a fresh window on an empty tree, and asserts the offer restores the modules.

**Godot specifics:** The Godot trigger set is wider than Unity's, which makes this more valuable here: an editor script reload re-binds `@tool` scripts and can drop the builder's non-exported model state; `plugin.gd:162-165` frees the window on plugin disable; the editor can be killed outright. `Journal` is static and `FileAccess`-only, so the whole restore path is headlessly testable with no Window at all. One ordering trap: `open_tree("")` constructs the workspace and calls `reproject()` synchronously (builder_window.gd:751-757), so the offer must run AFTER that or `workspace` is null when Restore fires — use `call_deferred` for exactly the reason Unity used `delayCall`.
