### `history.jump-gated-on-unrelated-selection` Clicking a history row does nothing unless a canvas row happens to be selected

**Unity does:** Each History panel row carries `PointerDownEvent -> JumpHistoryTo(target, entry.Description)`, which "walks the buffers to that point in one atomic step, which is the same operation Ctrl+Z performs one entry at a time" (UB-73). Nothing about the jump depends on canvas selection — the panel is the ledger made visible and is usable the moment the builder opens.

**Godot today:** present but dead on the common path. `builder_window.gd:155-172 _show_history()` builds the row list correctly — cursor marker, applied/undone detail, a "(before everything)" row — sets `_search_purpose = "history"` and opens the SearchMenu. It sets NEITHER `_menu_target` NOR `_menu_row`. But `builder_window.gd:1356-1358`, the handler those picks land in, opens with `if workspace == null or _menu_target.is_empty() or _menu_row == null: return` — a guard written for the attribute/child/wrap purposes — and the `"history"` case at :1367-1370 sits BELOW it. Both fields start empty (`var _menu_target := ""` at :132, `var _menu_row = null` at :102) and are only ever set by a row click or right-click (`_on_row_clicked` :1019-1021, `_on_row_context` :1078-1081). So: open the builder, press History, click any row — nothing happens, no toast, no error. It starts working only after the user happens to click a markup row, and stops again the moment `_menu_row` is cleared, which `_cancel_active_edit` (:292) and the inline editor's cancel handler (:688-696) both do. Intermittent, silent, untested. tests/builder_parity.gd:49-50 answers `JumpHistoryTo` and `ToggleHistory` with `func _jump_history_to` and `func _show_history`; both exist, both are reachable, and the click that drives them is not.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Two corrections to the remedy, not the finding. (1) The guard has a THIRD condition the write-up omits: `module.read_only` at :1359-1360. So History is also dead when the selected row belongs to a read-only module (anything under `addons/`) — the fix must hoist above that too, not just above the `_menu_target`/`_menu_row` check. (2) "Audit `rename` and the create purposes in the same pass — they are similarly row-independent" is wrong: both go through `_on_search_submitted` (:1477-1482), a separate handler with no guard at all, and both work today. `history` is the only row-independent purpose routed through `_on_search_picked`.

**To build:** Hoist the `"history"` case above the guard in `_on_search_picked`: handle purposes that do not act on a row before the `_menu_target`/`_menu_row` check, then let the row-scoped purposes fall through. Audit `"rename"` and the create purposes in the same pass — they are similarly row-independent. Add a builder_chrome_test.gd case: build a window, make three edits, call `_show_history()`, invoke `_on_search_picked(1)` with nothing selected, assert `ledger.cursor() == 1`.

**Godot specifics:** `_search_purpose` is a single shared field "because only one menu is open at a time" (builder_window.gd:98-99), which is fine, but one handler now serves purposes with genuinely different preconditions — a `match` on `_search_purpose` placed BEFORE the shared guard is the cheapest correct shape. Note also that `SearchMenu` is a `PopupPanel`, i.e. its own Window with its own viewport (builder_search_menu.gd:2), so a pick fires from a different viewport than the shell — one more reason the shell's focus is gone by the time the jump lands, and one more caller for the `_reclaim_keyboard()` from gap shell.keyboard-focus-dead, or the user's next Ctrl+Z after jumping does nothing.

### `toolbar.trace-crashes` The Trace button raises a runtime error mid-function, and is a one-shot state dump rather than the per-round trace it is named after

**Unity does:** UB-201. `Trace` is a TOGGLE whose state is `[SerializeField] bool _tracePreview` (it survives a domain reload); the button label flips to "Trace ON" and a toast says "Preview trace ON - the console names what each edit rebuilds". While on, EVERY preview compile writes one multi-line log naming, per round: `considered:` (the batch after the focus closure trimmed it), `rebuilt:` as `Name (reason)` pairs, `FAILED:` as `Name: error`, and `skipped:` as `Name (needs <blocker>)`. The recorded reason: "three separate fixes to this pipeline each read correctly and each failed, and the reason is that its failures are invisible: a module missing from the batch looks exactly like a module that compiled and changed nothing."

**Godot today:** partial and broken. `builder_window.gd:982-984` makes Trace a one-shot: show the console, call `_console.trace(workspace, ledger, preview)`. That function (`builder_console.gd:176-206`) dumps modules with dirty/moved/read-only flags, then at `:200-201` evaluates `ledger.entries.size()`. `entries` is a METHOD (builder_ledger.gd:97 `func entries()`), so `ledger.entries` yields a Callable and `.size()` on it fails. I confirmed on Godot 4.7: with the parameter untyped (as it is) the parser lets it through and it fails at runtime — `SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid call. Nonexistent function 'size' in base 'Callable'`. The function ABORTS there, so the history line never prints and the `preview:` line at :204-205 is never reached. No test touches it (no caller of `console.trace` outside builder_window.gd). Separately, even fixed it is not the feature: no toggle, no per-round logging, and neither `considered` nor `reasons` is ever shown — although `builder_preview.gd`'s Summary carries BOTH (`var considered := PackedStringArray()`, `var reasons := {}` with values "text changed" / "dependency rebuilt"), and `builder_console.gd:96-119 report()` prints only failures, skipped and budget exhaustion. The exact question UB-201 built Trace to answer — why did this rebuild, and why was that one not even a candidate — cannot be asked in the Godot builder at all. tests/builder_parity.gd:94 answers `TogglePreviewTrace` with the token `func trace`, which matches the crashing one-shot.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Godot reports the error at line 200 rather than 201 (it attributes the whole `_add_line(...)` statement to its first line); the failing sub-expression is on 201 as stated. No substantive change.

**To build:** 1) Fix the call: `ledger.entries().size()` at builder_console.gd:201, and TYPE the parameters (`workspace: Workspace, ledger: Ledger, preview: Preview` via the preload consts already at the top of the file) so the parser catches the next one at load time instead of at click time. 2) Make Trace a toggle: a `_trace_preview` bool on the window, the button text flipping to "Trace ON", a toast on each transition, the state persisted alongside the canvas layout. 3) Have `tick()` (builder_window.gd:915-923) pass the Summary to a `console.trace_round(summary, focus)` while the flag is on, rendering `considered` and `reasons` as well as the failures and skipped it already prints — the data is in the Summary, only the rendering is missing. 4) Add a builder_chrome_test.gd case calling `console.trace(...)` with a real ledger and asserting the row count, which is all it would have taken to catch this.

**Godot specifics:** A pure GDScript hazard with no Unity analogue: C# would not compile `ledger.entries.size()`, and GDScript only rejects it when the receiver is statically typed — with an untyped parameter it is a runtime error on a code path nobody runs headlessly. Every builder file already references its peers through preload consts (the documented class-cache rule), so typing these parameters costs nothing and buys static checking. The wider lesson: untyped parameters on cross-file boundaries are where the preload discipline stops paying for itself, and a headless test is the only other net.

**Unity does:** `UndoAction`/`RedoAction` toast "Nothing to undo" / "Nothing to redo" at the ends, and a successful walk toasts the reverted action by name (`"Undo <desc>"` / `"Redo <desc>"`) through `ApplyLedgerWrites`. The History panel shows the live cursor as a translucent accent band with the redo tail dimmed, and each row carries `Entry.FileSummary` on the right — the first file the action touched plus `+N` — so "a gesture that touched two files reverts as one step" is visible.

**Godot today:** partial. `builder_window.gd:2089-2103` returns `false` on an empty ledger and says nothing — no toast, no console line, no button state change. A successful undo is also silent: `_replay` re-projects and refreshes but never names what it reverted, even though `ledger.undo_label()` exists and is tested (tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:821). `_jump_history_to` (:176-184) toasts `"History — %d action(s) applied"` — a cursor position, not the action clicked. **To build:** In `undo()`/`redo()`: capture `ledger.undo_label()`/`redo_label()` before stepping, toast `"Undo <label>"` on success and `"Nothing to undo"`/`"Nothing to redo"` on the null return. In `_jump_history_to`, name the entry jumped to rather than the count. In `_show_history`, put `entries[i].file_summary()` into the SearchMenu row — `SearchMenu.item(label, payload, detail)` already takes a detail field, currently spent on "applied"/"undone", so either concatenate or widen the row.

**Godot specifics:** `toast()` is reachable from everywhere (builder_window.gd:196) and `_tick_toast` runs off `_process`, so this is pure wiring. One ordering note: `_jump_history_to` calls `undo()` in a loop, and each per-step toast would reset the single pill's timer — which is the behaviour you want, but it means the final message should be raised after the loop, not inside it.

### `layout.footer-hint-clips` The permanent gesture hint bar clips instead of wrapping, so the vocabulary silently disappears on a narrow window

**Unity does:** The footer is a `Label` with `whiteSpace = Normal` (it WRAPS), `minHeight = 26.95f` computed from the POC's line box, a 1 px top rule in the line colour, and NO-BREAK-SPACE bullets so a wrap never orphans one. The Unreal leg records why it is permanent rather than behind the help button: "it is the only place the drag/right-click/zoom vocabulary is written down, and none of those gestures is discoverable by looking at the canvas."

**Godot today:** partial. `builder_window.gd:407-416` builds the strip with the right seven clauses (and correctly says "L3" where Unity's still carries the stale 0-based "L2"). But `builder_chrome_parts.gd:81-88 hint_bar()` sets `clip_text = true` and leaves `autowrap_mode` at OFF. A single Label joining seven clauses with "  •  " runs to roughly 400 characters; at the builder's 900 px minimum width it is cut off after the first clause or two with no way to see the rest. The clauses that fall off the end are the most important ones — the library drop bands and the right-click vocabulary. Neither the min-height nor the top rule Unity pins is present, so the bar's height also moves with the theme font.

**To build:** In `builder_chrome_parts.gd:hint_bar`, set `autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART`, drop `clip_text`, and give the Label a `custom_minimum_size.y` so it cannot collapse. Use U+00A0 around the bullet as Unity does. Add a 1 px top separator (a ColorRect, or a PanelContainer with a top border) to match the reference's rule.

**Godot specifics:** Godot Labels default to `clip_text = false` and `AUTOWRAP_OFF`; the file turns clipping ON explicitly, so this is a decision to reverse rather than a default to override. Because the hint is the last child of the top-level `VBoxContainer` (builder_window.gd:416) with default size flags, a wrapped label grows upward and takes height from the body — correct (Unity's `flexShrink = 0` does the same) and safe at the 560 px window minimum, since the canvas layer already carries `custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, 420)` (builder_window.gd:348).

**Unity does:** The toast is a pill on the window root at `bottom = 44f`, `left = 50%`, `translate (-50%, 0)` — bottom-centre, just above the footer hint — with `pickingMode = Ignore`, fading over the last 0.6 s of its 3.2 s life (`opacity = left < 0.6 ? left / 0.6 : 1f`). Label's default `mouse_filter` is IGNORE, so the pill is already inert to the pointer as Unity's `pickingMode = Ignore` guarantees. Structurally the placement is right and better than Unity's overlays: it is added to `self` after the layout VBox with `z_index = 100` (builder_window.gd:393-405), so it survives a canvas remount.

### `status.refresh-early-return` On the start screen the status refresh returns before the command gating and the dirty signal

**Unity does:** `RefreshChrome()` sets `hasUnsavedChanges` FIRST, then writes the status text — the framework's dirty flag is updated on every path including the empty one. Save and Abort are always enabled (Unity's deliberate choice; the Unreal leg binds them to `Workspace.IsDirty()` instead).

**Godot today:** divergent-defect, minor. `builder_window.gd:2446-2472` computes `dirty` at the top but returns at :2453 when the workspace is null or empty — before the Save/Abort disable loop (:2462-2468) and before `dirty_changed.emit` (:2470-2472). So on the start screen the two destructive commands keep whatever enabled state they last had (they are built enabled), and a transition to "nothing open" never notifies a listener. Godot's choice to gate Save/Abort on dirtiness follows the Unreal leg rather than Unity, which is defensible — but it has to run on every path to be one.

**To build:** Move the button-gating loop and the `dirty_changed` emit above the early return, or restructure so only the text assignment branches. Two lines.

**Godot specifics:** `dirty_changed` currently has no listeners at all (gap shell.no-save-door), so this is latent — but it becomes a visible bug the moment the plugin connects it for the window title or the quit prompt, which is exactly what that gap asks for. Fix them together.

### `layout.folders-fold-absent` The FOLDERS header does not fold, so the library cannot be given the height, and the split it substitutes for is not persisted

**Unity does:** UB-208. The left column carries a click-to-fold `▸ / ▾  FOLDERS` header (10 px dim caps, letterSpacing 1, tooltip "fold the tree away and give the library the height", link cursor) over a 270 px folder pane; only button 0 folds; the state is `[SerializeField]` and re-applied by `ApplyFoldersFold()` at the end of CreateGUI "so it survives a reload like every other view state".

**Godot today:** absent. `builder_window.gd:322-333` builds a plain `Parts.pane_header("Folders")` (a Label with no input handling) over a `folders_column` with `custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, 240)`, inside a `VSplitContainer` with `split_offset = -210`. No fold, no arrow glyph, no persisted state — and the `split_offset` the user drags instead is not saved either, so the choice does not survive a session.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Low value confirmed, and the write-up's own alternative is the right call: the VSplitContainer already lets the user drag the folder pane to nothing by a native gesture, so the honest resolution is to record the divergence and persist `split_offset` with the layout, not to port the fold.

**To build:** Either add the fold — `Parts.pane_header` gains an optional collapsible flag; the header Label gets `mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` and a `gui_input` handler ignoring anything but `MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT`, toggling `folders_column.visible` and rewriting the glyph — or record it as a deliberate divergence on the grounds that `VSplitContainer` already lets the user drag the folder pane to zero, which is the same outcome by a native gesture. If the latter, persist `split_offset` with the canvas layout so the choice survives.

**Godot specifics:** Godot's default `Label.mouse_filter` is IGNORE, so a header built by `builder_chrome_parts.gd:31-45` cannot receive input as written — the fold needs an explicit STOP plus `mouse_default_cursor_shape = CURSOR_POINTING_HAND`. Persisting the state belongs with `CanvasLayout` (`_capture_layout`, builder_window.gd:2139-2149), which is already the builder's view-state store and already survives a session; a `@tool` script's plain vars do not.

*low · feature · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderWindow.cs:334-390 (foldersHeader), :478-499 (ApplyFoldersFold), :484-486 | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:319-336, :2139-2149; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_chrome_parts.gd:31-45

### `layout.cursor-affordances-absent` No pointer affordances anywhere — no pan cursor on the canvas, no pointing hand on clickable rows, and no toolbar tooltips

**Unity does:** `BuilderCursor.Set(element, MouseCursor)` reflects into an internal member of `Cursor` to set editor cursor ids, and the shell uses it for: canvas pane -> `Pan`, toolbar and mini buttons -> `Link`, the FOLDERS fold header -> `Link`, history rows -> `Link`, splitter anchors -> `ResizeVertical`/`ResizeHorizontal`. The reflection is guarded so a Unity build that renames the member degrades to arrows rather than throwing. Every mini button also carries a tooltip.

**Godot today:** absent. `grep -rn 'mouse_default_cursor_shape|CURSOR_' addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/` returns nothing. The canvas is a drag-to-pan surface showing an arrow, library rows are draggable showing an arrow, and only the SplitContainer draggers get a correct cursor (by Godot default). Just two tooltips exist in the whole builder — `builder_folder_pane.gd:196` and `builder_library_pane.gd:309`; the toolbar buttons (History, Trace, "? How to drive it", Save, Abort) have none, and the first three are opaque labels.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Small factual correction: there are THREE tooltips in the builder, not two — builder_folder_pane.gd:196, builder_library_pane.gd:309, and builder_console.gd:145 (`set_item_tooltip` on every diagnostic row, giving the full path and message). Does not change the finding.

**To build:** Set `mouse_default_cursor_shape` on `builder_canvas_host.gd` -> `CURSOR_DRAG`, on library and folder rows -> `CURSOR_POINTING_HAND`, and on the toolbar buttons -> `CURSOR_POINTING_HAND`. Add `tooltip_text` in `_tool_button` (builder_window.gd:658-664) naming what each command does.

**Godot specifics:** One of the few places the Godot port is structurally advantaged and has not taken the win: Unity needed private reflection into `Cursor.m_DefaultCursorId` and accepted silent degradation on any engine bump, whereas Godot exposes `Control.mouse_default_cursor_shape` as a plain enum property — one line per Control with no fragility. Note that Controls with `mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE` (nearly everything `canvas_view.guitkx` produces, deliberately) do not show their own cursor, so the shape must be set on the picking ancestor — the canvas host itself — not on the cards.

*low · visual · CONFIRMED* — unity Controls/BuilderCursor.cs:1-42, BuilderWindow.cs:366, :398, :5158, :5297, :5307, :5039, :5409, :5382-5411 (MiniButton tooltips) | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/ (no `mouse_default_cursor_shape` or `CURSOR_` anywhere); builder_window.gd:658-664; builder_folder_pane.gd:196; builder_library_pane.gd:309

### `console.never-hides` The console comes forward on a failed round and never goes away once the failure is fixed

**Unity does:** No direct analogue — Unity logs to its own Console, which the user opens and closes. The Godot console is a leg-specific addition, so the retract rule is its own to define.

**Godot today:** divergent-defect. `builder_window.gd:733-736` sets `_console.visible = true` on any failed compile, and no path ever sets it back to false; `run_command` forces it visible for Trace and Help too (:982, :986). `builder_console.gd:238-245 _sync_visibility()` only sizes the inner `ItemList` and ends in a bare `pass`, with a comment explicitly deferring the on-screen decision to the window — a decision the window makes in one direction only. After a single transient compile error the console keeps a strip of the middle VSplit for the rest of the session showing "N module(s) rebuilt, no problems", which is precisely the permanent-fixture-reporting-the-absence-of-news state the file's own header says it was redesigned to avoid.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The focus hazard flagged in godot_specifics is real and I verified the mechanism: builder_console.gd:53 gives the ItemList `FOCUS_ALL` for its Ctrl+A/Ctrl+C support, and Godot releases focus when a focused Control is hidden — my probe confirmed that with no focus owner the shell's `_gui_input` receives nothing. So whatever hides the console must hand the keyboard back, or it makes shell.keyboard-focus-dead worse.

**To build:** In the `compile_finished` handler, hide the console again when the round is clean AND the console is not showing a Trace or Help dump — track which of the three modes filled it (a small enum set by `report` / `trace` / `show_help`) so a clean round only retracts a report. Give the console header a close affordance so a Trace or Help dump can be dismissed without waiting for a round.

**Godot specifics:** The console is the second child of a `VSplitContainer` (builder_window.gd:369), so toggling `visible` genuinely returns the height to the canvas — Godot containers skip invisible children when sorting. One trap: hiding a Control that currently holds keyboard focus (the ItemList takes FOCUS_ALL at builder_console.gd:53 for its Ctrl+A/Ctrl+C support) drops the viewport's focus owner to null, which — per gap shell.keyboard-focus-dead — kills the builder's keyboard model until something re-focuses the shell. Whatever hides the console must call the same `_reclaim_keyboard()` that gap introduces.

*low · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderWindow.cs:4616-4650 (Unity logs to its own Console instead) | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:367, :733-737, :982-988; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_console.gd:36-56, :96-119, :238-245

### `cmd.dead-history-menu` A second, unreachable history menu and a button-gating loop that matches no button

**Unity does:** n/a — Unity has one History surface (the panel) and always-enabled Save/Abort; there is no second menu and no dead gating branch.

**Godot today:** divergent-defect, cosmetic but misleading. `builder_window.gd:55` declares `MenuId._HISTORY_OLD` and `:975-979` still implements its branch — popping a `_history_menu` PopupMenu carrying only Undo and Redo, built at `:464-467` and added to the tree — with no toolbar button, menu item or keystroke that can produce that id. Separately, `_refresh_status` (:2462-2468) loops the toolbar looking for buttons whose `command` meta is `MenuId.UNDO` or `MenuId.REDO` to enable/disable them; `_build_toolbar` (:591-635) creates buttons for HISTORY, TRACE, HELP, SAVE and ABORT only, so those two branches can never match. A reader auditing this file concludes there are Undo/Redo buttons and a second history surface; there are neither.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Understated — there are two MORE dead ids in the same enums, and one of them is not merely unreachable but wrong. `MenuId.REVEAL` (:55) has no menu item and no branch in `run_command` (:970-999) anywhere. `CardMenuId.REVEAL_CARD` (:69) is never added to `_card_menu` (built at :425-437: separator, New submenu, separator, Open, Rename…, separator, Delete) yet has a handler at :2229-2232 whose body is `select_module(_menu_target)` under a comment about the RENAME prompt — a branch that is dead, misnamed and misdocumented at once. And "reveal in the FileSystem dock" genuinely does not exist: `navigate_to_path` appears nowhere in the addon, and the only `get_file_system_dock()` uses are plugin.gd:131 and :175 (rename/move signal wiring). Whatever resolution is chosen for `_HISTORY_OLD` should take these three with it.

**To build:** Delete `MenuId._HISTORY_OLD`, its branch and the `_history_menu` construction — or, if the intent was a quick Undo/Redo pair on the toolbar, add the two buttons and let the existing gating loop light up. Either resolution is fine; leaving both halves half-built is what makes the file lie.

**Godot specifics:** Note the enum-id hazard the file documents twice (builder_window.gd:66-77): `add_submenu_item` takes no id and Godot assigns from the low end, which is why the card and row menus start at 100 and 200. `MenuId` starts at 0 and `_canvas_menu` mixes `add_submenu_item` with `MenuId`-numbered items (builder_window.gd:449-454), so `MenuId.SAVE = 0` shares the range Godot auto-assigns from. Removing `_HISTORY_OLD` shifts nothing (it is last), but any future insertion into `MenuId` must follow the same started-past-zero rule the other two menus already learned.

## Preview, language intelligence and the defect register

70 distinct gaps — 9 critical, 31 high, 24 medium, 6 low, plus 2 marked as duplicates.

### Language intelligence: completion, diagnostics plumbing, schema cache, element/hook classification

### `LI-01` The "add attribute" menu offers 139 rows whose NAME is a stringified Dictionary, and picking one writes it into the tag

**Unity does:** BuilderSchemaCache.Register stores List<AttrInfo> of (name, type, description) per element; AttributesFor yields the element's own attributes then the common tail, deduped by name; DefaultValueFor(name, type) picks a value from the DECLARED TYPE (string -> "text", bool -> {true}, int -> {0}, float -> {0f}, delegates/objects -> {null}, enums -> a real CssHelpers token) so the inserted attribute always compiles. UB-14 records the previous name-heuristic version as "the second way the builder writes broken code into the user's file".

**Godot today:** wrong. builder_attributes.gd:64-75 props_of_host() iterates Schema.godot_properties(godot_class), which returns an Array of Dictionaries {name, type} (guitkx_schema.gd:93-107), but does `var name := str(prop)` — stringifying the whole Dictionary. Verified live under Godot 4.7: props_of_host("Button") returns 139 entries whose name is the literal text `{ "name": "text", "type": "String" }`. Schema.property_info(class, <that garbage>) then returns {} so every type is "Variant", and default_value("Variant") returns {value:"null", quoted:false}. Line 73-74 has the identical bug for events (events_for_class returns {name, signal}; `str(event)` stringifies it). builder_window.gd:1382-1389 then calls Edits.set_attribute(before, row, name, "null", false), so choosing the first row writes `{ "name": "text", "type": "String" }={ null }` into the open tag. There is a SECOND defect underneath: even with the name fixed, property_info returns `type` as a Variant.Type INT (guitkx_schema.gd:117-121) while default_value matches String type NAMES, so every default would still be null.

**To build:** In builder/edits/builder_attributes.gd:64-75, read the Dictionary: `var info := prop as Dictionary; out.append({"name": str(info["name"]), "type": str(info["type"])})` — godot_properties already returns `type` as a type_string() ("String", "bool", "int", "float", "Vector2", "Color"), which is exactly the vocabulary default_value(:83-103) matches on, so the property_info round-trip should be deleted outright. Same for events: `str((event as Dictionary)["name"])`, type "Callable". Then add the missing gate to tests/builder_edits_test.gd: assert props_of_host("Button") contains {name:"text", type:"String"} and that menu_for produces no label containing '"name":'.

**Godot specifics:** Schema is already reached through a preload const (builder_attributes.gd:17), which is correct under the class-cache rule — do not change that. godot_properties() filters on PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR and skips category/group headers and subresource (a/b) names, so it is ClassDB-live and needs no editor singleton: the whole fix is assertable headlessly with `godot --headless --script`, no EditorInterface, no window. The canvas re-projects on every settled keystroke, so keep props_of_host allocation-free of RegEx.

**Risk:** The primary way a user adds a property to an element writes markup that cannot compile, and the ledger records it as a successful edit. The preview then fails with an opaque "did not parse" line (see LI-04), so the user is told the module is broken but not why.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/Lsp/BuilderSchemaCache.cs:18-29,56-98,109-137 + Library/BuilderLibraryPane.cs:308-332 + Plans~/UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:386-387,444-465; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_attributes.gd:64-75 (str(prop) / str(event)), :83-103 (default_value), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/lsp/guitkx_schema.gd:93-107,112-122,134-143, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1172-1178,1382-1389

### `LI-02` "Add a style entry" writes a stringified Dictionary as the dict key, producing a style module that does not parse

> **Duplicate of `LANG-01`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** The style-key menu is sourced by reflection off CssHelpers so it can never name a key that does not exist — UB-08 forced that discipline after a hand-written table shipped two keys (Gap, UnityTextAlign) that were not real. Every value the builder inserts is required to compile.

**Godot today:** wrong. builder_window.gd:1243-1250 _style_key_items(): `for key in Schema.style_keys(): items.append(SearchMenu.item(str(key), {"export": owner, "key": str(key), "value": _style_seed(str(key))}))`. Schema.style_keys() (guitkx_schema.gd:126-128) returns the schema's [{name, type, detail}] Dictionaries, so str(key) is the whole record. Verified live: the menu label is `{ "name": "bg_color", "type": "Color", "detail": "StyleBoxFlat.bg_color (primary StyleBox fill)." }`, and Edits.insert_style_entry (builder_edits.gd:547) then writes into the style module:
	"{ "name": "bg_color", "type": "Color", "detail": "..." }": null,
The embedded double quotes terminate the GDScript string literal, so the module is a SYNTAX error, not merely a wrong key. _style_seed(:1253-1258) also never matches (the stringified record does not end with "_color"), so every entry is seeded null even after the name is fixed.

**To build:** builder_window.gd:1243-1250: `var spec := key as Dictionary; var name := str(spec["name"])`, label `name`, payload key `name`, detail `str(spec["type"])`. Rewrite _style_seed to be TYPE-driven off spec["type"] (Color -> Color(0.2,0.2,0.24), int -> 8, float -> 0.0, String -> ""), which is Unity's schema.default-value-type-driven rule and removes the name-suffix heuristic entirely. Cover it in tests/builder_edits_test.gd with a compile assertion on the resulting style module.

**Godot specifics:** style_keys() is the ONE vocabulary Godot's own tooling cannot supply (guitkx_schema.gd:124-125) — ClassDB has no notion of the RuitkStyle dict — so the schema JSON is genuinely the source of truth here and must be read as records, not stringified. builder/canvas/canvas_palette.gd is the standing reminder that a style module read from editor code needs @tool; that is unrelated to this bug but it is why the style vocabulary lives in JSON rather than in a .style.guitkx module.

**Risk:** A single right-click gesture ("+ entry" on a style card, or Add style entry on a row) makes the style module unparseable. Every module that imports it then fails to build, and the console reports only the first failure by file name.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/Lang/BuilderStyleSurface.cs:62-90 + Plans~/UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:339-366 (UB-08); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1240-1258, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/lsp/guitkx_schema.gd:126-128, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_edits.gd:547-560

### `LI-03` Every hook dragged or clicked from the library writes `var _ = <hook>()`, which is a GDScript PARSE ERROR

**Unity does:** UB-11 records the Unity leg's own version of this defect: hook insertion hardcodes declaration text for the four templates and falls back to `var value = name();` for the other 17, "though HookRegistry already emits real stubs". Unity's fallback at least parses.

**Godot today:** wrong, and worse than Unity's. builder_window.gd:572 (library CLICK) and :2248-2251 (library DROP) both call Edits.insert_setup_line(buffer, card, "var _ = %s()" % name). Two independent failures: (1) `var _ = ...` is not legal GDScript — verified at engine level on Godot 4.7 by reloading a GDScript whose body is `var _ = 1`: "Parse Error: Expected variable name after \"var\"" (`var _x = 1` reloads OK). (2) calling the hook with no arguments is wrong for roughly ten of the 23: hooks.gd declares useEffect(effect: Callable, deps = null):226, useMemo(factory: Callable, ...):187, useCallback(cb: Callable, ...):191, useReducer(reducer: Callable, ...):141, useContext(key):266, provideContext(key, value):288, useSignal(sig: RuitkSignal, ...):458, useTween(ref, property, to, duration, ...):511. Verified end to end: Compiler.compile returns ok=true (it lowers to `var _ = Hooks.useState()`), and only script.reload(false) in builder_preview.gd:279-281 fails, so the console says "the generated script for X.guitkx did not parse (Parse error)" — no line, no hook name, no clue. The card's own "+ hook" chip (builder_window.gd:1575-1577) writes the CORRECT `var state = useState(null)`, so the same gesture has two spellings and one of them is broken.

**To build:** One hook-stub table, used by all three call sites. The data already exists: GuitkxHover.HOOKS (lsp/guitkx_hover.gd:12-40) carries every hook's real signature in its doc string, and hooks.gd is the ground truth. Emit `var state = useState(null)`, `useEffect(func(): pass, [])`, `var memo = useMemo(func(): return null, [])`, `var ref = useRef(null)`, etc. Never `var _`. Then bind the inline editor over the inserted line exactly as the "+ hook" chip already does (builder_window.gd:1598-1605), so the seed is a starting point rather than a guess.

**Godot specifics:** `_` is a reserved discard token in GDScript's match patterns and is NOT a legal variable name — this is engine behaviour, not a compiler quirk, and it is invisible to the .guitkx compiler because guitkx.gd:138 only validates markup and emits text. That is precisely why the gate misses it: tests/builder_edits_test.gd:136-137 _compiles() calls Compiler.compile() and never GDScript-parses the emitted .gd. builder_preview.gd:271-281 already does that reload; three lines lift it into _compiles.

**Risk:** The builder's headline advertised gesture ("LIBRARY — drag an element, hook or component onto a card", builder_console.gd:216) corrupts the module it lands on, for all 23 hooks, every time. The card still draws normally; only the preview stops updating.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/Library/BuilderLibraryPane.cs:42-48 + Plans~/UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:400-416 (UB-11); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:572 and :2248-2251 (`"var _ = %s()"`) vs :1575-1577 (`"var state = useState(null)"`), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit/core/hooks.gd:111-578, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/preview/builder_preview.gd:279-283

### `LI-04` The builder has NO diagnostics plumbing: the gutter it embeds is permanently blank and the console shows one first-error line per failed module

**Unity does:** textDocument/publishDiagnostics is drained on EditorApplication.update, converted to a local path, and raised as BuilderLspService.DiagnosticsPublished — the one notification of all of them the builder acts on. BuilderWindow subscribes at the SERVICE (UB-06) and paints the source pane. The Unreal leg reached the same conclusion independently and wrote the post-mortem out: "THE FILE'S OWN DIAGNOSTICS, continuously. The console used to speak only when an APPLY failed — so a file that had been broken since it was opened showed 'No diagnostics.' and the user had nothing to go on but a preview that would not render."

**Godot today:** absent. builder_source_pane.gd:83-85 instantiates GuitkxCodeEdit, which OWNS a diagnostics gutter (guitkx_code_edit.gd:102-109 diag_gutter, clickable), a per-line store (set_line_diagnostics:511), a hover composer that prepends the line's diagnostics (compose_hover:539-548) and an unreachable-code dimmer (set_dim_lines:394). A grep of addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/ finds ZERO references to set_line_diagnostics, GuitkxDiagnosticsRenderer, set_dim_lines or GuitkxScanDiags — every one of those is used only by editor/guitkx_editor_view.gd:616-693. So in the builder the gutter is a 24px empty column and hover never shows a diagnostic. The only diagnostics surface is builder_console.gd, fed by builder_window.gd:922 _console.report(summary) with Preview.Summary.failures — one row per module whose message is Preview._first_error (builder_preview.gd:286-291), i.e. the FIRST error only, or for a reload failure the string "the generated script for X.guitkx did not parse (Parse error)" with no code and no line. Warnings never surface anywhere. Graph.Card (builder_graph.gd:146-182) has no diagnostics field at all, unlike the Unreal leg's FRuitkUiBuilderCard::Diagnostics.

**To build:** The pipeline is already written — editor/guitkx_editor_view.gd:616-693 does compiler diags + GuitkxScanDiags.unknown_tags + .diags.json sidecar merge + the analyzer's embedded-GDScript tier -> GuitkxDiagnosticsRenderer.render -> gutter icons + set_line_diagnostics + the problems records. Extract it into a shared function and call it from the builder's single funnel: (a) after each apply_edit for the focus buffer, feed the records to _source.editor(); (b) hang the per-card list on Graph.Card so a failing card can be marked on the canvas (the Unreal precedent); (c) give builder_console._add_row a real line so item_activated can jump the source pane to it via SourcePane.goto_line, which already exists (builder_source_pane.gd:112-117).

**Godot specifics:** GuitkxDiagnosticsRenderer.render takes two icons; guitkx_editor_view gets them from EditorInterface, so the builder path must pass null and skip icons when Engine.is_editor_hint() is false, keeping the suite headless. The renderer writes gutter metadata per line, so the source pane must re-render after every refresh_from_model (:156-170) or the icons anchor to shifted text. Diagnostics must be computed on the WORKSPACE buffer, not from the .diags.json sidecars — builder_console.gd:6-14 already explains why (nothing is written until Save). Use the preview's existing 300 ms debounce rather than adding a second timer.

**Risk:** A user cannot see where anything is wrong. The most common markup mistake — a typo'd tag — produces "did not parse (Parse error)" and nothing else (see LI-05 for why even the compiler stays silent about it).

### `LI-05` GUITKX0105 (unknown element, with did-you-mean) is switched OFF everywhere in the builder, because known_components is always []

**Unity does:** BuildKnownElements returns the union of BuilderSchemaCache.ElementNames, the runtime ElementRegistryProvider names, and every COMPONENT node's exports plus title — and returns NULL until both the schema and the graph are live, because DiagnosticsAnalyzer skips the unknown-element check on a null set (that is the deliberate startup suppression) and would report every PascalCase element on an EMPTY one. Style and util export names are deliberately excluded so `<BgDeep />` still fails.

**Godot today:** absent, and the compiler already implements the same contract. Verified on Godot 4.7: Compiler.compile(src_with_<Labell/>, "Card", [], {}) returns ok=true with ZERO diagnostics and lowers to `V.fc(Labell.render, ...)`; the same call with known=["Card"] returns ok=false and `GUITKX0105 unknown element <Labell> -- did you mean <Label>?`. An EMPTY array suppresses, exactly like Unity's null. Every builder call site passes empty: builder_preview.gd:259-262 `Compiler.compile(module.buffer_text, basename, [], {}, mirrored, scratch_root)`, builder_source_pane.gd:234 `Compiler.compile(text, basename)`, tests/builder_edits_test.gd:137. The builder also never runs GuitkxScanDiags.unknown_tags (lsp/guitkx_scan_diags.gd:20), which is the parse-independent tier written precisely because a typo'd open tag makes the close tag mismatch and masks the one report that explains it. Verified: with an unknown tag the builder's whole user-visible output is the reload failure string from LI-04.

**To build:** Compute the union off the graph — for every Graph.Card of kind COMPONENT, its exports plus card.title (never style/util exports, for exactly Unity's <BgDeep /> reason) — and thread it into Preview._build's compile call and the source pane's apply-parse. Return an EMPTY array while graph == null so startup does not storm (the Godot compiler's empty==suppress semantics give you Unity's null discipline for free). Also run GuitkxScanDiags.unknown_tags(buffer, known) alongside, deduped by (code, offset) the way guitkx_editor_view.gd:657-664 does. Verified safe: a real `import { Card } from "./card"` + `<Card />` is NOT flagged with known=["Use"].

### `LI-06` Nothing tells the language layer about the in-memory tree, so completion and go-to-definition answer from DISK in a builder that writes nothing until Save

**Unity does:** SyncLspBuffer pushes every buffer the builder touches to the server — didOpen the first time a path is seen, debounced didChange after — so completion, go-to-definition and diagnostics all resolve against the unsaved document. The post-mortem in the source is specifically about a rename making that routine, "since the module arrives at a path nothing has opened".

**Godot today:** absent. GuitkxWorkspace (lsp/guitkx_workspace.gd) is the index behind user-component tag completion (guitkx_completion.gd:116 component_tags()), Ctrl+hover validation (guitkx_code_edit.gd:471 is_component) and go-to-definition (:486 lookup). It is built entirely from disk: _collect_guitkx("res://") + FileAccess.get_file_as_string (:28-37). reindex(path, text) EXISTS and takes live text (:46-55) — its only caller in the whole addon is editor/guitkx_editor_view.gd:857, on save. The builder never calls reindex or rescan. Import-brace completion and namespace completion go through RuitkGuitkxResolve.decl_table(path), which is FileAccess.get_file_as_string (guitkx_resolve.gd:56) — also disk. Consequence inside a session where "nothing is written until Save": a component created in the builder is not offered as a tag and Ctrl+click on it resolves nothing; a component renamed in the session is still offered under its OLD name and jumps to a path that no longer describes it; import completion lists the exports the target had before the session's edits.

**To build:** Push each dirty buffer through GuitkxWorkspace.reindex(path, buffer_text) from the single apply_edit funnel in builder_window.gd, debounced on the preview's existing cadence. Add a decl_table overlay keyed by path so RuitkGuitkxResolve prefers a live buffer over the file when the builder has one. On rename, reindex the new path and drop the old (reindex already erases entries pointing at a path, :48-51).

**Godot specifics:** GuitkxWorkspace's index is PROCESS-GLOBAL static state shared with the .guitkx editor view, which Unity's per-client model does not have: an aborted builder session would leave the .guitkx editor completing against work the user threw away, so abort_all and window close must call GuitkxWorkspace.rescan(). Keep the reindex off the keystroke path — _index_source runs the compiler's analyzed_decls per file. Do not point the sweep at the preview mirror: _collect_guitkx already skips `~`-suffixed folders (:122-123) and honours .gdignore (:111-112), which is the same double-hiding the mirror relies on.

**Risk:** The builder's own components are second-class in its own source pane. The user writes `<MyNewCard` and gets no completion, then Ctrl+clicks it and nothing happens, in a tool whose entire premise is that the tree is what you are working on.

**Unity does:** BuilderAssetEvents synthesizes workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles from Unity's AssetPostprocessor, and separately raises UitkxImported BEFORE the LSP null-check so an LSP-less session still gets it. BuilderWindow.OnUitkxImported then ReloadCleanFromDisk (dirty sessions keep the user's buffer), NotifyBufferChanged so the preview rebuilds ("This was simply missing"), RefreshGraph per path, and re-SetContent on the source pane unless it is in explicit edit mode.

**Godot today:** absent, with the mechanism already built and tested. builder_workspace.gd:237-251 reload_clean_from_disk() implements exactly Unity's rule (clean modules adopt the new disk text, dirty ones keep the user's buffer, returns the changed paths) and is exercised at tests/builder_model_test.gd:747-753 — and is called from NOWHERE in addons/. plugin.gd:137-144 already owns a debounced filesystem_changed hookup, but _on_fs_settled (:337-340) only rescans GuitkxWorkspace and pokes _view; the builder is not in that path, and neither are the FileSystemDock files_moved/file_removed handlers (:132-135). Separately, record a per-module mtime at load/save and have save_all refuse — or ask — when the file on disk is newer than the module was read from.

**Godot specifics:** plugin.gd already has the 0.5 s Timer debounce because filesystem_changed fires in bursts; reuse it rather than adding a second. Feed reload_clean_from_disk only the paths the tree holds — the tree is the authority, and a res:// sweep would rediscover the preview mirror. Godot's EditorFileSystem also auto-scans on window focus, so the builder currently self-heals for the WORKSPACE index but never for its own buffers. Everything here is FileAccess-only and stays headlessly testable, which is how reload_clean_from_disk got tested without ever being wired.

**Risk:** A git pull, an external IDE save, or an edit in Godot's own .guitkx view while the builder is open leaves the builder serving a stale buffer with no notification, and the next Save silently overwrites the newer content. This is the one item in this area that destroys work rather than merely failing to help.

**Unity does:** FragmentCompletion pushes a SYNTHESIZED buffer (the real file with the in-progress fragment spliced in) so the inline editor gets real completion at a real position, and ResyncLspBuffer restores the server's view when the editor closes — "Completion requests push SYNTHESIZED buffers to the LSP; when the editor closes the server must see the real one again."

A CodeEdit swap must keep the two properties the current editor is careful about: select_all_on_focus = false and caret at end (:38, :76). GuitkxCompletion is UI-free by design (its own docstring) so the item set is assertable headlessly without instantiating the overlay.

**Risk:** The builder's promise is that you can shape a UI without knowing the vocabulary. The attribute NAME menu delivers on that (once LI-01 is fixed); the attribute VALUE does not, which is where the enum tokens and the style keys live.

### `LI-08` No directive-drift warning: the wrap vocabulary is a hand-written 3-entry const sitting beside an 8-entry schema

> **Duplicate of `LANG-14`** — same defect, same fix, filed twice because two areas read the same code. Kept for its evidence; not counted.

**Unity does:** s_directiveSupport maps all eight schema controlFlow names to a bool meaning 'offered as a wrap'; WarnOnDirectiveDrift logs one console warning per unmapped name the first time the wrap menu opens, and RETRIES (returns without arming) while ControlFlow is still null. The stated reason is blunt: "A schema name missing here trips the drift warning — the builder must never silently trail the language again."

**Godot today:** absent. Edits.WRAPS (builder_edits.gd:675-682) is @if, @for, @while; @match is special-cased at builder_window.gd:1163-1164. GuitkxSchema.control_flow() returns eight (@if @elif @else @for @while @match @case @default, verified live). Nothing compares the two. The clause half is covered by RowMenuId.ADD_ELSE / ADD_ELSE_IF, which is the right shape — but a directive added to the language tomorrow would appear in the schema, in completion and in hover, and be silently missing from the builder with nothing to notice it.

**To build:** A {name: offered_as_wrap} dictionary covering every schema controlFlow name (if/for/while/match true; elif/else/case/default false — they ride their construct head's menu), and one push_warning per unmapped name the first time AddWrapItems runs. Follow Unity's retry rule exactly: return WITHOUT arming the latch when control_flow() is empty, so a schema that has not been read yet does not permanently disarm the check.

**Godot specifics:** A `static var` latch on a @tool script re-arms per editor session, which is the behaviour you want (Unity's is once per domain reload — the same thing). The check must live in the builder and reach the schema through a preload const, not the GuitkxSchema global, per the class-cache rule. Godot's own vocabulary difference is already agreed: @elif not @else if, and a directive body cannot be empty (GUITKX0303) so a seeded clause needs a placeholder child — the drift map should encode that, not fight it.

**Risk:** tests/builder_parity.gd:67 answers Unity's AddWrapItems with `const WRAPS`, so the gate is permanently green over a list that structurally cannot notice the language growing. That is the exact failure mode the parity gate's own preamble was written about.

**Unity does:** CheckSchemaDrift compares the schema's element names against the live runtime registry on canvas mount, DETACHED so a slow answer delays a warning rather than the tree, and warns once per DRIFT SET per session (SessionState key, because "the same seven names repeated eleven times buried real console output"). The must-never half is honoured by construction: GuitkxSchema.is_host_tag (:53-57) and _tag_kind (builder_graph_service.gd:860-861) both check ClassDB FIRST, so a registered-but-uncurated class is never false-flagged. The report half is absent — nothing warns, and builder_library_pane.gd:11-12 claims "a hundred and forty Godot classes", which is not what Compiler.host_tags() holds.

Fix the stale comment in builder_library_pane.gd:11-12 while you are there.

**Godot specifics:** ClassDB.get_class_list() + can_instantiate + is_parent_class is the registry side and is available headlessly, so this is testable in tests/builder_chrome_test.gd with no editor. Keep it to Control subclasses or the count is meaningless — the open vocabulary is any Node, and warning about AudioStreamPlayer2D would be noise. Godot's palette curation (LEAD_ELEMENTS then the rest, folded) is a deliberate and correct display choice; the gap is only that the difference is unreported.

### `LI-10` A missing or unreadable schema is silent AND permanently latched for the process

**Unity does:** UB-09 named the hazard precisely: Register has one call site inside an async Attach; if the LSP throws, the catch returns early, s_byElement stays empty, and every element silently degrades "with no warning. The user cannot tell a real schema from a dead one." The fix was to make the degradation VISIBLE — a red-brown "Palette unavailable: {ex.Message}" row, HasSchema, and a "schema offline — common attributes only" menu header.

**Godot today:** wrong. guitkx_schema.gd:23-26 sets `_loaded = true` BEFORE attempting the read, so a failed or transient read is permanent for the whole editor process; the only signal is a push_warning at :34 or :38. Nothing in the builder ever asks whether the schema is live. With the schema absent (a partial install, or the editor's first-scan environment), the source pane's tag completion offers nothing (guitkx_completion.gd:114 iterates GuitkxSchema.host_tags()), the style-entry menu is empty (builder_window.gd:1245), and hover_for_directive/hover_for_attribute return "" — all silently. Contrast the compiler, which handles exactly this editor-first-scan case explicitly: guitkx.gd:139-146 returns env_error with "compiler environment not ready: vocabulary.json could not be loaded -- retrying on the next compile".

**To build:** Move `_loaded = true` to AFTER a successful parse so a transient read retries — the compiler's own env_error precedent is one file away and is the right pattern. Add a `has_schema()` (non-empty _tags) and render a visible row in the library pane and a menu header in the style-entry menu when it is false, mirroring Unity's two surfaces.

**Godot specifics:** guitkx_schema.gd is correctly @tool, so its static var initialisers DO run in the editor (the trap canvas_palette.gd exists to avoid does not apply here). The read is FileAccess only, so there is no EditorInterface dependency and the retry is free. Note the _tags map and the _schema dict answer different questions — is_host_tag falls back to ClassDB and keeps working, while style_keys()/control_flow()/structural_attributes() go dark — which is the same split Unity documents between HasSchema and s_commonFromSchema.

**Risk:** An installed addon missing data/guitkx-schema.json degrades a whole tier of intelligence with a single push_warning nobody reads, permanently, for the session.

### `LI-12` "+N more" dumps the rest of a section at the BOTTOM of the pane, outside its heading, and throws away the user's search

**Unity does:** AddFoldRow is called where a section ENDS ("so one call site cannot be the one that forgets"); the label toggles between "+N more" and "show less"; the fold row returns early while a filter is active, because "a search reaches the whole library, collapsed rows included: folding is about the resting state, and a filter that could not see past it would be a search that lies about what is there"; _expanded is a VIEW state that survives a rebuild.

**Godot today:** wrong. builder_library_pane.gd:246-251 _show_all() calls rebuild() — which re-emits every section header and its first five rows — and THEN does _body.add_child(_entry_row(kind, ...)) for entries 5..N. add_child appends, and _body is a plain VBoxContainer, so clicking "+ 50 more" under NATIVE ELEMENTS puts those fifty rows at the very bottom of the pane, below HOOK MODULES, with no heading over them. There is no "show less" — the code comments call the expansion "a one-shot: the next rebuild folds it again". The handler also does _search_field.text = "" and _search = "" (:239-241), discarding a filter the user typed. tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:582-599 asserts the fold COUNT and the filter override but never clicks the fold row, so the gate is green.

**To build:** Make full expansion part of the model the rebuild reads — a second `_expanded_fully` set keyed by section — and have _add_section honour it, so the rows land inside their own section and the fold row reads "show less" when open. Delete the _search_field.text reset. Add a chrome test that clicks the fold row and asserts the last child of _body still belongs to the last section.

**Godot specifics:** Order in a VBoxContainer is child order, so a post-pass can only append; move_child would be a patch on a design problem. Keep the state where _expanded already lives (:65-68) — the pane's own comment already gives the right reason ("rebuilding the list from a new graph must not close a drawer the user just opened"), and _show_all violates it.

**Risk:** Fifty element rows appear detached from any heading at the bottom of the palette, and the search the user typed to find one of them is silently cleared at the moment they ask to see the rest.

**Unity does:** No analogue — C# has no equivalent hazard. The applicable contract is the Godot-side one CLAUDE.md states: builder files reference each other through preload consts, never global class_names, because ProjectSettings.save() truncates the editor class cache to what the running process loaded.

**Godot today:** wrong (a cost the deliberate divergence did not account for). builder_source_pane.gd:18 preloads editor/guitkx_code_edit.gd, which is correct. It costs nothing, changes no behaviour, and removes the coupling between the builder's availability and the editor class cache. Do the same in guitkx_completion.gd, which names GuitkxSchema/GuitkxContext/GuitkxWorkspace/GuitkxHover/RuitkGuitkxResolve/RuitkGuitkxConfig/RuitkGuitkx globally.

In practice plugin.gd loads the .guitkx view in _enter_tree so the classes are usually registered — this is a latent risk, not a live failure, but it is the failure mode that produced the rule in the first place (49/49 false parse fails on a fresh clone, per CLAUDE.md's test-order note).

**Risk:** A truncated editor class cache takes down the whole builder window with a parse error, not a degraded source pane.

### `LI-17` The source pane drops go-to-definition and gutter-click: the widget resolves them and nothing listens

**Unity does:** The builder consumes what its editing surface produces — diagnostics land in the pane, and navigation is a first-class gesture on the same surface.

**Godot today:** absent. GuitkxCodeEdit emits definition_requested(path, offset) after resolving a component tag through GuitkxWorkspace, a hook through hooks.gd, or an embedded identifier through the analyzer (guitkx_code_edit.gd:485-507), and gutter_diagnostic_clicked(line, record) when the diagnostics gutter is clicked (:399-401). editor/guitkx_editor_view.gd:176-177 connects both. builder_source_pane.gd connects NEITHER — its only connection is text_changed (:103). So Ctrl+click on a component tag in the builder's source pane does all the resolution work and then throws the answer away, and the gutter is unclickable because it is empty (LI-04).

**To build:** Connect definition_requested in builder_source_pane.gd and re-emit it upward; in builder_window, resolve the path against the workspace and — when it is a module in the open tree — frame its card on the canvas and jump the source pane with the existing goto_line (builder_source_pane.gd:112-117), falling back to EditorInterface for a res://*.gd target. Connect gutter_diagnostic_clicked once LI-04 puts records in the gutter.

**Godot specifics:** definition_requested carries a CHARACTER OFFSET, not a line — convert with the same count("\n") the graph service uses (builder_graph_service.gd:1076-1079). The builder's tree is in memory, so a resolved path must be looked up in workspace.try_get before falling back to disk, and a component created in the session will not resolve at all until LI-06 is fixed. Connecting the signal is safe headlessly; only the EditorInterface fallback needs an Engine.is_editor_hint() guard.

**Risk:** A wired, working navigation gesture is invisible in the builder — the user Ctrl+clicks a tag, the cursor changes to signal it is a link, and nothing happens.

### `LI-13` Empty library sections are hidden, and rows are untinted, so the palette does not tell you what it holds

**Unity does:** All five section headers are emitted unconditionally in a fixed order whether or not the tree contributes a row — "an empty section still tells you the drawer exists. Filtering hides headers." Rows are tinted per kind (Accent for natives, ComponentTint, HookTint, StyleTint, UtilTint) so a glance says what a row is.

**Godot today:** partial. builder_library_pane.gd:213-214 _add_section returns when filtered.is_empty(), so on a tree with no style modules the STYLE MODULES header never appears — while the `+ new` menu two rows up offers "New style module (.style.guitkx)" (:95). The fixed order is right (:135-144). _entry_row (:295-321) sets no per-kind colour at all; elements and components read as `<Tag>` and everything else as a bare identifier, which is the only visual distinction. Tooltips are the generic "%s -- drag onto a card, or click to insert" (:309), carrying none of the schema's descriptions.

**To build:** Emit every section header unconditionally when no filter is active (keep hiding them while filtering, which is Unity's rule too). Tint rows per kind from canvas_palette.gd, which already holds the builder's colours.

**Godot specifics:** canvas_palette.gd is the hand-written @tool script that exists precisely so editor code can read colours — a generated .gd is not @tool and Godot never runs a non-tool script's static var initialisers in the editor, so reading tints from a .style.guitkx module here would come back empty and silently. Use canvas_palette.gd, reached through a preload const.

**Risk:** The palette advertises three of six drawers on a fresh tree, so a user has no way to learn from the library that style, util and hook modules are things it holds.

### `LI-14` Attribute and tag menus carry no documentation, though the schema and ClassDB both have it

**Unity does:** AttrInfo carries (name, type, description) and UB-09 records that dropping the description was itself the bug — "so the menu can never show docs". Menu rows read `name  :  type`, library rows carry the schema description as tooltip.

**Godot today:** partial. builder_attributes.gd:142-146 sets `detail` to the TYPE only; builder_window.gd:1324-1328 _tag_items sets no detail at all. The data exists and is unused: the bundled schema's structuralAttributes and commonAttributes each carry a `description` (verified), and GuitkxSchema.hover_for_attribute (:185-201) already renders them. Separately, the STRUCTURAL const in builder_attributes.gd:21-25 is a hand-written duplicate of Schema.structural_attributes() with the descriptions stripped — UB-09's "hand-written common list" pattern. The two agree today (key, ref, style — all real, so none of UB-09's three fabricated attributes), so the live cost is only the missing docs plus the drift risk.

**To build:** Replace the STRUCTURAL const with Schema.structural_attributes() and put its `description` into the menu row's detail. For host properties, ClassDB has no doc string, but the type + the resolved signal name is already more than is shown for events (props_of_host loses the signal each event binds to — Schema.events_for_class returns it and builder_attributes.gd:73-74 discards it).

**Godot specifics:** Read the schema through the existing preload const, never the GuitkxSchema global. The whole change is data-shape only and is assertable headlessly.

### Language surface: directive vocabulary, style key surface with value helpers, text/labels, element classification

### `LANG-01` The style-key menu writes a stringified Dictionary as the key — every "Add entry…" corrupts the module

> Also filed as `LI-02` — one defect.

**Unity does:** BuilderStyleSurface.Build() reflects public settable instance properties off the real `Ruitk.Props.Typed.Style` type and returns typed KeyInfo records; the menu row is `{Name}  :  {TypeLabel}` and the value written is the property NAME. UB-08 calls the hand-written alternative "the single most damaging item in the register: the builder actively breaks the user's file". Unity: Lang/BuilderStyleSurface.cs:81-116, :118-134; Plans~/UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:339-366.

**Godot today:** WRONG, and it corrupts the file. `GuitkxSchema.style_keys()` returns an Array of DICTIONARIES `{name,type,detail}` (guitkx-schema.json), but `_style_key_items` iterates them and calls `str(key)` on each — stringifying the whole dictionary. Verified in Godot 4.7 headless: the menu label and the inserted key are both `{ "name": "bg_color", "type": "Color", "detail": "StyleBoxFlat.bg_color (primary StyleBox fill)." }`. `insert_style_entry` writes that verbatim as a quoted key, the .guitkx compiler reports ok=true, and the generated .gd fails GDScript parse: `Parse Error: Expected ":" or "=" after dictionary key`. The seed is equally garbage — `_style_seed(str(key))` substring-matches the DETAIL PROSE, so `border_width_all` gets `8` because its description contains "width". Save writes it to disk. No test drives `_style_key_items` at all.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One addition the claim misses: the very same stringify-a-Dictionary bug exists in `edits/builder_attributes.gd:69-74` (`props_of_host`), where it breaks the entire "Add attribute..." menu. See the missed-gaps list — fixing LANG-01 alone leaves the larger instance standing.

**To build:** In `chrome/builder_window.gd:1242-1250`, read `str((key as Dictionary).get("name",""))` and pass the entry's `type`/`detail` to the label and the seed. Then remove the possibility: give `_style_key_items` a typed KeyInfo shape (a small `builder_style_surface.gd` with `keys() -> Array[Dictionary]` returning `{name, type, detail}`) so no call site can stringify a container again, and add a `builder_chrome_test.gd` case that asserts the inserted key is a bare identifier (`not key.contains("{")`) and that the resulting buffer's generated .gd `load()`s.

**Godot specifics:** The .guitkx compiler does NOT validate dictionary keys, so `ok=true` hides this — the failure only surfaces at `GDScript.reload()` inside `preview/builder_preview.gd:279`, which reports "the generated script for X did not parse" with no line and no hint that the builder itself wrote it. Fix in a hand-written .gd (builder_window.gd is not a .guitkx). Fully headlessly testable — `Edits.insert_style_entry` + `Compiler.compile` + `GDScript.reload` all run under `--headless`.

**Risk:** Every use of the one gesture the parity gate lists as "AdvanceStyleEntry" writes an unparseable module. The user sees a preview failure about a script they did not write, and Save persists it.

### `LANG-02` "Remove <badge>, keep its contents" is offered on every directive row; Unity offers it on exactly one

> Also filed as `ctx-01` — one defect.

**Unity does:** AddDirectiveHeadItems: a `ClauseIndex > 0` row gets "Edit condition" + "Delete clause" and RETURNS — no separator, no unwrap, no delete-block. Unwrap is appended only when `BadgeKind != 14` (never on @switch) AND `IsSingleClauseConstruct`. The OnDirectiveEdited comment states why: "the construct unwrap assumes it starts at a construct head and corrupts the brace balance from a clause line". Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:1929-2003, :1990-1995, :2071-2086, :2971-3002.

**Godot today:** ABSENT — all three guards are missing. `_on_row_context` adds `RowMenuId.UNWRAP` unconditionally for every `LineKind.DIRECTIVE` row. Verified in Godot 4.7 headless against a real card projection, all four cases produce files that do not compile: (a) unwrap on a MULTI-clause @if head — brace counting stops at the `} @else {` line, deleting the head and leaving a dangling clause; (b) unwrap on an @else CONTINUATION — the head line's `}` and `{` cancel, so `close` lands on the very next line and the `return (` is deleted; (c) unwrap on a @match head — deletes the match and leaves a bare @case; (d) unwrap on a @case — deletes the case and leaves an empty @match. `builder_edits_test.gd:775-805` only ever tests case (single-clause @if head), so the suite is green.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Case (b)'s mechanism differs slightly from the claim: the brace walk from the `} @else {` line does not stop "on the very next line" — it deletes through the construct's real close, orphaning the @else body's `<Label text="c" />` after a dangling `)`. Same outcome, different arithmetic; the fix (refuse `clause_index > 0`) is unchanged.

**To build:** Port the three guards into `_on_row_context` (`chrome/builder_window.gd:1094-1105`): skip UNWRAP when `row.clause_index > 0`, when `row.badge == Graph.Badge.MATCH`, and when the construct has more than one clause. The clause walk Unity uses (`ConstructClause`/`IsSingleClauseConstruct`, walking siblings at `head.depth`, with @match arms at `head.depth + 1`) does not exist here and must be added — put it beside `Edits.delete_clause` in `edits/builder_edits.gd` so it is pure and headlessly testable. Also make `unwrap_directive` itself refuse a `clause_index > 0` row rather than trusting its caller.

**Godot specifics:** The projection already carries everything the walk needs: `Graph.Line.clause_index`, `.depth`, `.badge` (`canvas/builder_graph.gd:42-56, 103-105`), and `_walk_match` puts arms at `depth + 1` exactly like Unity. So this is a menu-guard + walk, not a projection change. `builder_edits.gd` is preload-const-referenced and pure — the walk can be tested directly by `builder_edits_test.gd` with no editor.

**Risk:** Four one-click routes to a file that will not compile, from the menu the builder documents as "the builder's primary editing gesture".

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:1929-2003, :1990-1995, :2071-2086 | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1094-1105 (menu), :1150-1152 (dispatch), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_edits.gd:775-833 (unwrap_directive), tests/builder_edits_test.gd:775-805 (only the single-clause head)

### `LANG-03` Deleting a MIDDLE clause takes the next clause's head with it

> Also filed as `ctx-02` — one defect.

**Unity does:** DeleteClause branches on whether the close line is really the NEXT clause's head: `if lines[close] contains '@'` → `RemoveRange(head, close-head)` KEEPING the next head, then strips its leading `}` when this clause was separate-form and the next is shared-form. Only a real lone closer is removed inclusively. The comment cites the review that found it: "leaving the next head's leading `}` after deleting a separate middle clause before a shared next head — unbalances the file (review findings, 2026-08-16)". Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:2155-2205.

**Godot today:** PARTIAL — only the shared/separate half was ported. `delete_clause` always removes `head..close` INCLUSIVE and re-inserts a `}` when the head was shared. For a middle clause, `close_line` IS the next clause's head line (the graph service sets a continuation's close to `_body_close_line(source, body_at)`, and in the shared form the `}` that closes an @elif's body is the `} @else {` line). Verified headless on a three-clause `@if/@elif/@else`: deleting the @elif produces `@if (…) { … }` followed by an orphaned `return ( <Label text="c" /> ) }` and the file does not compile. `builder_edits_test.gd:761-768` only deletes the LAST clause, where head..close inclusive happens to be right.

**To build:** Add Unity's branch to `Edits.delete_clause` (`edits/builder_edits.gd:635-657`): before removing, test whether `lines[close]` carries a directive keyword (search for `@` outside a string, or better, reuse the projection — the next sibling clause row's `directive_line`); if so remove `head..close-1` and, when `not shared_head and next_shared`, strip the surviving head's leading `}`. Add three suite cases: first clause, middle clause, last clause, each asserting `Compiler.compile(...).ok`.

**Godot specifics:** Unity's `'@'` test is textual and its own comment admits an @-bearing attribute value on that line misclassifies it. Godot can do better and should: `builder_graph_service.gd` already emits every clause as a row with `directive_line`, so "is the close line the next clause's head" is a lookup in `card.markup`, not a string scan. Keep the operation pure (`source, row -> String`) so `builder_edits_test.gd` covers it headlessly.

**Risk:** Silent structural corruption of the user's markup from a menu item that reads as the safe way to remove one branch.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:2155-2205 | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_edits.gd:635-657, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:678-680 (a continuation's close_line is its own body close, which in shared form is the next head's line), tests/builder_edits_test.gd:761-768

### `LANG-04` The directive header seed and its commit are not inverse — editing a header writes `@if (@if (true))`

**Unity does:** The pair is deliberately inverse: FillDirectiveText strips exactly the punctuation OnDirectiveEdited re-adds (leading `}`, trailing `{` for brace heads; everything from the single `:` onward for colon heads), and the commit rewrites the WHOLE line body: `indent + (sharedClose ? "} " : "") + cleaned.TrimStart('}',' ').TrimEnd('{',' ') + " {"`. The doc says the two "must stay inverse". Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:2971-3021; Canvas/BuilderGraphService.cs:1167-1192.

**Godot today:** WRONG — the two halves disagree. The editor is opened on `row.directive_text`, which `_directive_head` builds as the FULL header including the keyword (`"%s (%s)" % [label, head]` → `@if (true)`). `Edits.set_directive_header` then replaces only what is INSIDE the parentheses. Verified headless: committing the seed unchanged yields `@if (@if (true)) {`; the .guitkx compiler reports ok=true (only the unrelated GUITKX2320 deprecation), so nothing warns, and the generated .gd carries `@if (true)` as a GDScript expression and fails at load. The same non-inverse pair backs the seeded-wrap flow at builder_window.gd:1445-1451, which opens the editor on the literal `@if (true)`.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The claim's repro sentence "committing the seed unchanged yields `@if (@if (true))`" cannot happen through the UI: `InlineEditor.commit()` (chrome/builder_inline_editor.gd:88) only emits when `value != was`. The defect fires the moment the user EDITS the seed — the ordinary case, since the caret lands at the end of `@if (true)` with nothing selected (:75) and the natural act is to change the `true`. Severity and fix unchanged.

**To build:** Pick one convention and make both ends obey it. Cheapest correct fix: seed the editor with the HEADER TEXT ONLY (`row.text` minus the badge, i.e. the parenthesised expression) at `chrome/builder_window.gd:1206-1208` and at the seeded-wrap open at :1447-1450, keeping `set_directive_header`'s parens-only replacement. Alternative (closer to Unity): seed the full header and make `set_directive_header` rewrite the whole line, stripping a leading `}`/trailing `{` and re-adding them. Either way add a round-trip assertion to `builder_edits_test.gd`: seed → commit unchanged → the source is byte-identical.

**Godot specifics:** `Graph.Line` already separates the two (`badge_text` = `@if`, `text` = `@if (true)`, `directive_text` = the same) — the projection has no field holding the bare condition, so add one or derive it. Note this is also the path GUITKX0303 constrains: a directive header cannot be empty here, which is why the LANG-13 removal rule matters alongside it.

**Risk:** The obvious way to use "Edit header…" — edit the text you can see — breaks the file, and the compiler says nothing.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:2971-3021 + Canvas/BuilderGraphService.cs:1167-1192 | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1204-1208, :1445-1451, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_edits.gd:320-333, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:822-826 (directive_text = the full header)

### `LANG-05` "Delete <badge>" is offered on a continuation clause and deletes only its head line

**Unity does:** A `ClauseIndex > 0` row's menu is edit-condition + "Delete clause", and RETURNS. "Delete block" — the whole `DirectiveLine..CloseLine` range — is offered only on a construct HEAD. Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:1929-1955.

**Godot today:** WRONG — `_on_row_context` adds "Delete this <badge> clause" (DELETE_CLAUSE) AND "Delete <badge>" (DELETE_ROW) on the same clause row. DELETE_ROW routes to `Edits.remove`, which deletes `_line_start(row.at) .. _line_end(row.end_at-1)`. Verified headless: "Delete @else" on a shared-head `} @else {` removes only that line and leaves the else body and a surplus `}` behind — the file does not compile. Two adjacent menu items, one correct and one corrupting, with labels the user cannot tell apart.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The mechanism is not "removes only that line". A directive row's span runs `at..close_at` (builder_graph_service.gd:816-818), so `Edits.remove` deletes the whole @else clause INCLUDING the `}` that closed the @elif above it — which is why the file unbalances. Corrupting either way, but the guard has to be the menu-side `clause_index > 0` return, not a span fix.

**To build:** In `chrome/builder_window.gd:1102-1105`, when `row.clause_index > 0` add only DELETE_CLAUSE and return; keep DELETE_ROW (the block delete) for construct heads. Cover both in a chrome test that drives `_on_row_menu` rather than `Edits.*` directly — today no test touches the row menu at all.

**Godot specifics:** `Graph.Line.clause_index` is already correct for every clause of every construct (`builder_graph_service.gd:669-726`), so the guard is one condition. The row menu is a plain `PopupMenu` reachable headlessly by calling `_on_row_context` / `_on_row_menu` directly — no real input routing needed to cover it.

**Risk:** Adjacent, indistinguishable menu items where one is safe and one silently unbalances the construct.

### `LANG-06` "Add @else" is offered on an @if that already has one, producing two @else clauses

> Also filed as `ctx-03` — one defect.

**Unity does:** "Add @else" is appended only when `ConstructClause(node, rowIdx, "@else") == null`; the exact-match on BadgeText is deliberate so an existing `@else if` does not suppress it. "Add @default" gets the same treatment on a @switch. Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:1957-1975, :2005-2036.

Note `@match` arms sit at `depth + 1` here exactly as in Unity (`builder_graph_service.gd:716`), so the same `clause_depth = depth + (badge == MATCH ? 1 : 0)` rule ports unchanged.
