### `LANG-07` The style-key vocabulary is a hand-written 45-entry JSON list against a live ~74-key surface — 29 real keys are unreachable and nothing gates the two

**Unity does:** The key list is REFLECTED from the real `Style` type so "the menu can never offer a key the type does not have". UB-08 is explicit that the hand-written table shipped two invalid keys (Gap, UnityTextAlign) and left 66 of 92 real keys unreachable, and calls it the register's most damaging item. Unity: Lang/BuilderStyleSurface.cs:10-18, :81-116; Plans~/UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:339-366.

**Godot today:** PARTIAL and unguarded. `_style_key_items` reads `GuitkxSchema.style_keys()` — the 45 hand-maintained `styleKeys` entries in `data/guitkx-schema.json`. The real vocabulary `RuitkStyle` accepts is three layers: ~24 flat keys in `_apply_key`, EVERY `StyleBoxFlat` property (derived LIVE from ClassDB by `_stylebox_props()`) plus the 4 `*_all` umbrellas, 6 theme channels and 5 state slots. Measured in Godot 4.7: 29 StyleBoxFlat properties the menu cannot reach (border_width_left/top/right/bottom, all four corner_radius_*, all four content_margin_*, all four expand_margin_*, shadow_color/size/offset, draw_center, skew, border_blend, corner_detail, anti_aliasing…) plus 4 flat keys (material, texture_filter, texture_repeat, z_as_relative). No key in the 45 is currently invalid — but nothing enforces that, and `style.gd`'s own `_RENAMED_STYLE_090` table exists precisely because this vocabulary has shifted before.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Two details to fix before implementing: (1) `RuitkStyle._stylebox_props()` (core/style.gd:152-163) does NOT filter the four `resource_*` properties — it skips only GROUP/SUBGROUP/CATEGORY — so the remediation's "filtered the same way" would offer `resource_path` as a style key. Filter `resource_*` explicitly. That also makes the real unreachable count 25, not 29. (2) The schema's own `detail` prose already documents the per-side keys as "also accepted verbatim", so the vocabulary is documented and unofferable — which is worse than undocumented, and worth saying in the gate's message.

**To build:** Two things. (1) Make the box layer LIVE: union the schema's curated head with `ClassDB.class_get_property_list("StyleBoxFlat")` filtered the same way `RuitkStyle._stylebox_props()` filters it (skip GROUP/SUBGROUP/CATEGORY and the four `resource_*`), so the per-side/per-corner keys become reachable and cannot drift from the engine. (2) Add a gate to `tests/builder_model_test.gd` (or a new `builder_lang_test.gd`) asserting every schema `styleKeys[].name` is accepted by `RuitkStyle` — i.e. is in `BOX_ALL_KEYS`, `_stylebox_props()`, `THEME_CHANNELS`, `STATE_SLOTS`, or an `_apply_key` arm — so a schema edit that invents a key fails CI instead of shipping.

**Godot specifics:** `RuitkStyle._stylebox_props()` is already a static ClassDB-derived cache in the RUNTIME addon (`core/style.gd:152-163`), reachable from editor code with no @tool hazard because it is a static FUNC, not a static VAR initialiser — exactly the distinction `canvas_palette.gd` is documented around. Reference it through a preload const, not the `RuitkStyle` global, per the class-cache rule. `_apply_key`'s flat arms are a `match` statement with no introspectable list, so those 24 stay curated — say so in the gate rather than pretending otherwise.

**Risk:** The exact mechanism UB-08 documents, re-created from scratch: two hand-maintained lists of what the style system understands, and no gate between them.

### `LANG-08` A @match head has no "Add @case" or "Add @default", and there is no next-case-label rule

> Also filed as `ctx-04` — one defect.

**Unity does:** AddSwitchClause: "Add @case…" inserts at the @default arm's line when one exists (so a new case lands ABOVE the catch-all — UB-71) and at the closing brace otherwise; "Add @default" always appends last. NextCaseLabel seeds the lowest non-negative integer no arm already uses, so the arm compiles against the seeded subject and cannot collide. Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:2038-2069, :2116-2153; Plans~/UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:838-869, :871-890.

**Godot today:** ABSENT. `_on_row_context` gates every clause-add on `row.badge_text == "@if"`, so a `@match` head's menu is only Edit header / Remove / Delete. Grepping `builder/` for `@case`, `@default`, `next_case`, `add_switch` finds them only in the PROJECTION (`builder_graph_service.gd:716, 723`) and in `wrap_in_match`, which seeds exactly one `@case (0)` and offers no way to add a second. A user who wraps a row in @match can never add a second arm from the canvas — the source pane is the only route.

**To build:** Add `Edits.add_match_clause(source, head, is_default) -> String` beside `add_if_clause`, plus `Edits.next_case_label(card, head) -> int` walking the arms at `head.depth + 1` and parsing `row.text` (`@case (0)` arrives as badge `@case` + text `(0)` here, not `0:` — the language uses parens, not colons). Wire both into `_on_row_context` under `row.badge == Graph.Badge.MATCH and row.clause_index == 0`. Remember GUITKX0303: a new arm needs a body, so seed `<Control />` inside `return ( … )` exactly as `add_if_clause` already does at builder_edits.gd:614-618.

**Godot specifics:** Unity's `SingleColonIndex` / `::` rule has no analogue — this language writes `@case (value) { … }`, so the label is a parenthesised expression and the whole colon-termination behaviour drops out. That is a legitimate language translation, not a gap; what does port is the ordering rule (new cases above an existing @default) and the collision-free integer seed. `@match` arms are already projected at `depth + 1` with correct `close_line`s, so the insert point is a lookup, not a brace scan.

**Risk:** @match is a one-arm construct on the canvas. The builder can create it and never grow it.

### `LANG-09` Every style entry the builder seeds is `null`, which is a render-time error and a silent mutation

**Unity does:** TemplatesFor(type) opens a second "{Key} — values & helpers" menu keyed on the key's DECLARED TYPE: StyleLength → Px(8)/Px(16)/Pct(100)/Pct(50)/StyleAuto; Color → Hex("#1b1b1f")/Rgba(…); int → 0/1/8; enums → the CssHelpers tokens or the first four members; plus a freeform row. UB-08 killed the previous version precisely because its ~35 literals were keyed on invented pseudo-types. Unity: Lang/BuilderStyleSurface.cs (TemplatesFor); Plans~/UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:339-366.

**Godot today:** ABSENT, and the substitute is harmful. There is no second menu — `_style_seed(key)` is a three-branch string heuristic run on the key NAME: `*_color` → a Color literal, name containing width/radius/margin/separation or starting with `font_size` → `8`, EVERYTHING ELSE → the literal `"null"`. That is 26 of the 45 keys, including `visible`, `modulate`, `scale`, `rotation`, `mouse_filter`, `custom_minimum_size`, `anchors_preset`, `size_flags_horizontal/vertical`, `z_index`, `outline_size`, `font`, and all 5 state slots. Verified in Godot 4.7: `RuitkStyle.apply(label, {}, {"visible": null})` raises `Invalid assignment of property or key 'visible' with value of type 'Nil'` at core/style.gd:262 AND leaves the Label hidden. `font_sizes` matches `begins_with("font_size")` and is seeded `8` — a theme CHANNEL wants a Dictionary, so it silently no-ops. `min_width` seeds `8` while `min_height` seeds `null`.

**To build:** The schema already carries a `type` per key (`"Color"`, `"int"`, `"Dictionary"`, …) and the builder throws it away. Read it, and add a second search menu (`_search_purpose = "style_value"`) offering type-appropriate literals: Color → `Color(0.2, 0.2, 0.24)` / `Color.WHITE`; int → `0` / `4` / `8`; Vector2 → `Vector2(0, 0)`; bool → `true` / `false`; enum-ish (mouse_filter, size_flags_*, anchors_preset) → the constant NAMES `RuitkStyle` already accepts as strings (`"MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE"`, `"SIZE_EXPAND_FILL"`, `"PRESET_FULL_RECT"` — see `_SIZE_FLAGS`/`_MOUSE_FILTERS`/`_ANCHOR_PRESETS`); the 6 channels and 5 state slots → `{}`. Keep `BuilderSearchMenu`'s freeform row as the escape hatch, which it already provides.

**Godot specifics:** `RuitkStyle`'s enum-name-as-string acceptance (`core/style.gd:334-346`) is a gift this menu should use — the templates can be readable constant names instead of magic ints. A `{}` seed for a channel or state slot is correct and inert (`_apply_theme_map` with an empty dict does nothing), unlike `null`. Every value here is a GDScript literal in a dictionary, so the whole thing is string generation and is headlessly testable through `Edits.insert_style_entry` + `Compiler.compile` + `GDScript.reload`.

**Risk:** A style entry added from the canvas errors on every render and can silently hide the element it was applied to.

### `LANG-10` Format-on-save rewrites the buffer but nothing re-projects, so the canvas and the source pane hold stale offsets

**Unity does:** FormatDirtyBuffers runs inside one ledger entry named "format on save", and per formatted module: `session.ApplyEdit(formatted)`, `ledger.Record(FilePath, before, formatted)`, push into the code field, `SyncLspBuffer`, and `canvasHost.RefreshGraph(FilePath)`. "The source pane and every affected card visibly re-shape at Save." Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:5819-5855, :5857-5863.

**Godot today:** PARTIAL — the format happens, nothing downstream is told. `Workspace._format` sets `module.buffer_text = text` directly (no ledger record, so the reformat cannot be undone), and `save()` afterwards calls only `_capture_layout()`, `_folders.rebuild()`, `_refresh_status()` — not `reproject()` and not `_source.refresh_from_model()`. `workspace.changed` is emitted and NOTHING is connected to it (grepped: the only `.changed.connect` in builder/ is the ledger's). `format_on_save` defaults to true. So after any Save that changes a file's shape, every `Graph.Line.at` / `.source_line` on the canvas points at the pre-format text, and the next canvas gesture writes at those offsets. The doc comment at builder_workspace.gd:52-54 asserts the opposite of what happens: "the formatted text becomes the BUFFER … otherwise the card and the file disagree the instant the save lands".

**To build:** In `chrome/builder_window.gd` after `workspace.save_all()` (line 1974), call `reproject()` and `_source.refresh_from_model()`. Better: have `Workspace._format` route through the same funnel as everything else — record `before`/`after` on the ledger inside one `ledger.begin("format on save")` / `end()` pair so the reformat is one undo step, which is what Unity does and what the builder's own "one funnel" doctrine demands. Add a save-suite case that formats a badly-indented buffer and asserts `graph.card_of(path).markup[0].source_line` matches the formatted text.

**Godot specifics:** `_after_model_change` already does exactly the right work (re-populate the one card, refresh edges, refresh the source pane, request a preview round) — Save simply does not call it. Note the ledger lives in the window and the formatter in the workspace, so either the workspace gains a ledger reference or Save moves the format into the window; the latter matches Unity and keeps `builder_workspace.gd` FileAccess-only and headlessly testable.

**Risk:** After a Save the canvas is a projection of text that no longer exists; the next drag or menu edit writes at the wrong offsets.

### `LANG-12` Dropping an element INSIDE a directive clause silently does nothing; the bottom band writes a bare element after `return ( … )`

**Unity does:** TryClauseNestTarget walks the clause's body to its FIRST element row and nests there, because "a clause return has ONE root, so siblinging the root would not compile". An EMPTY clause instead gets a whole `return (` / tag / `);` scaffold in the same commit. Two situations refuse with a user-facing reason: a body on its label line ("expand it to a block first") and a drop on the @switch head itself ("Drop into a specific @case arm, not the @switch head"). The band is FORCED to inside when the row is the first element row or a `ClauseIndex > 0` directive. Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:2361-2429, :2613-2619.

**Godot today:** ABSENT in both directions. `Edits.insert` with `Placement.INSIDE` on a directive head calls `_insert_inside`, which looks for a tag to re-open, finds none, and returns the source unchanged — the window then toasts the generic "Couldn't place <X> there." with no reason and no way in. Worse, `Drag._placement_of` maps the BOTTOM band to `FIRST_CHILD` whenever the next listed row is deeper — which is always true for a directive head with a body — and `FIRST_CHILD` on a directive row inserts after `_open_tag_end`, which finds the `>` of the first `/>` inside the clause body. Verified headless: dropping `<Button />` on the lower third of an `@if` head produces a bare `<Button />` after `return ( <Label … /> )` inside the block → GUITKX2103. No band forcing for directive rows exists (`DIRECTIVE` appears in edits/ only at builder_edits.gd:66 and :321).

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The bottom-band result raises GUITKX0108 ("a directive-body `return` must return exactly one root element (got 2)"), not GUITKX2103. That matters for triage: unlike LANG-01 and LANG-16, the compiler DOES catch this one, so the user gets a console error rather than a silent bad file. The gesture is still wrong in both bands.

**To build:** Two pieces. (1) In `edits/builder_drag.gd:143-154`, force band → INSIDE when the hit row is a `DIRECTIVE` (any clause_index) or the card's first element row, mirroring Unity's rule. (2) Add `Edits.insert_into_clause(source, card, head, markup) -> Dictionary {text, reason}`: find the clause's first non-directive descendant and delegate to `insert(..., INSIDE)`; on an empty clause write the `return ( <tag> )` scaffold; on a `@match` head refuse with "Drop into a specific @case arm, not the @match head." Route the reason to `toast()` instead of the generic message.

**Godot specifics:** `can_place` already refuses BEFORE/AFTER inside a directive body with a good reason string (builder_edits.gd:64-68) — the missing half is the INSIDE path. The clause-body walk is a scan over `card.markup` forward from the head while `depth > head.depth`, skipping `DIRECTIVE` rows; the projection already guarantees clause bodies are at `depth+1` (`depth+2` under a @match arm). Note the `Control.mouse_filter` angle does not apply here: the canvas is a single `_draw` surface with position hit-testing (`Metrics.row_hit`), so this is arithmetic, not input routing, and `builder_canvas_test.gd` can drive it headlessly.

**Risk:** The natural gesture for "put this inside the @if" either does nothing or writes markup the compiler rejects, depending on which third of the row you release over.

### `LANG-16` The `+ style` chip hardcodes `bg_color` on `exports[0]`, and pressing it twice makes the module unloadable

**Unity does:** Style-entry adds go through the reflected key menu; keys already present on that export are filtered out at the call site so a duplicate cannot be offered. Unity: Lang/BuilderStyleSurface.cs:103-115 + the '+ entry' call site.

**Godot today:** WRONG on three counts. `_on_card_add`'s `"style", "entry"` branch inserts the fixed key `bg_color` with the fixed value `Color(0.2, 0.2, 0.24)` into `card.exports[0]` — not into the export the section is showing, and with no menu and no inline editor (unlike `+ hook` / `+ code`, which both open one). Filter that list against the export's existing keys — `builder_graph_service._dict_entries` already parses them into `export_detail` rows carrying `erow.name` — and make `Edits.insert_style_entry` refuse a key the dictionary already holds. Then either fix the chip to add a new export or relabel it; the code and its own doc comment must agree.

**Godot specifics:** The duplicate is invisible to every gate the builder has: `Compiler.compile(...).ok` is true, and only `GDScript.reload()` in the preview catches it. That argues for the refusal being in `Edits.insert_style_entry` (pure, headlessly assertable) rather than only in the menu.

**Risk:** Two clicks on a chip labelled '+ style' make the module unloadable, and the compiler reports success.

### `LANG-17` The `+ entry` row is a synthetic Line at offset 0 — selecting it and pressing Delete removes the file's first line

**Unity does:** The '+ entry' affordance is a row you click (or press Enter on when armed) to open the key menu; it is an affordance, not a text range. Unity: Lang/BuilderStyleSurface.cs (the '+ entry' call site) + Canvas/BuilderGraphModel.cs:54-58 (BadgeKind 9 as an affordance marker).

**Godot today:** WRONG. `_fill_export_detail` appends a bare `Graph.Line.new()` with `badge = ADD_ENTRY` and `text = "+ entry"` — `at`, `end_at` and `source_line` all keep their defaults of 0. `_on_row_clicked` then stores ANY clicked row in `_menu_row` ("Any row the canvas lists is selectable"), and `_delete_selection` runs `Edits.remove(module.buffer_text, _menu_row)`, which for `at = end_at = 0` computes `from = 0`, `to = end of line 1`, and deletes the file's FIRST LINE — on a `.style.guitkx` that is the `export <name> := {` declaration. Left-clicking the row also does nothing useful: the key menu is only on right-click → "Add entry…", and `_source.goto_line(0)` jumps nowhere.

**To build:** Two guards. (1) In `_delete_selection` (`chrome/builder_window.gd:269-279`) and in `Edits.remove` (`edits/builder_edits.gd:175-182`), refuse a row whose `end_at <= at` — a row with no span is an affordance, not text. (2) Make left-clicking an `ADD_ENTRY` row open the key menu, which is what the affordance promises and what Unity does; today the only route is the context menu.

**Godot specifics:** `Graph.Line`'s fields all default to 0 (`canvas/builder_graph.gd:60-91`), so any synthetic row is a zero-span row — this will recur for `ADD_STYLE` / `ADD_EXPORT` the moment they are used. A sentinel (`at = -1`) or an `is_affordance()` predicate on `Line` is the durable fix. Both guards are pure and coverable in `builder_edits_test.gd` / `builder_chrome_test.gd`.

**Risk:** Click an affordance, press Delete, lose the export declaration — with no warning and nothing in the menu to suggest it was possible.

### `LANG-21` The parity gate is green over six directive/style entries whose functions corrupt files, and has no line for nine more Unity behaviours

**Unity does:** The Unity behaviours these entries claim to answer: AddWrapItems (five directives, node-valued first, loops withheld on the root, drift warning), RemoveDirectiveBlock (offered only on a single-clause non-switch head), AddIfClause (offered only when the clause is absent), DeleteClause (both head forms AND the next-head-shares-the-close case), OnDirectiveEdited (seed and commit inverse; empty removes), AdvanceStyleEntry (reflected keys, value templates, present-keys filtered). Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:1879-1927, :1990-1995, :1957-1975, :2155-2205, :2971-3021; Lang/BuilderStyleSurface.cs:81-134.

**Godot today:** The gate greps for identifiers, and every one of these identifiers exists. `["RemoveDirectiveBlock", "func unwrap_directive"]` is green while the function is offered in four places and corrupts the file in all but one (LANG-02). `["DeleteClause", "func delete_clause"]` is green while the middle-clause case unbalances the braces (LANG-03). `["AddIfClause", "func add_if_clause"]` is green while the menu offers a second @else (LANG-06). `["OnDirectiveEdited", "RowMenuId.EDIT_HEADER"]` is green while the seed/commit pair writes `@if (@if (true))` (LANG-04). `["AdvanceStyleEntry", "RowMenuId.ADD_STYLE_ENTRY"]` is green while the menu writes a stringified Dictionary (LANG-01). `["AddWrapItems", "const WRAPS"]` is green over three entries with no collection picker and no drift guard. And there is NO entry at all for: WarnOnDirectiveDrift, NextCaseLabel, AddSwitchClause, TryClauseNestTarget/InsertIntoClause, ShowForeachWrapMenu, LoopVarFor, BuilderStyleSurface (reflection), TemplatesFor (value helpers), LoadOptionsFor (formatter options per directory). Compounding it: `builder_chrome_test.gd` contains zero references to `RowMenuId` or `_on_row_menu` — the menu the source calls "the builder's primary editing gesture" has no test — and `builder_edits_test.gd` exercises only the single-clause happy path of every directive operation.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One addition to the proposed remedy: the compile assertion is NOT sufficient on its own. `Compiler.compile` returned ok=true for BOTH LANG-01 and LANG-16, and only `GDScript.reload()` caught them — so the `load()`/`reload()` half the claim mentions second is the load-bearing half for every style-dictionary operation, and should be written first.

**To build:** Keep the checklist, but stop letting a name answer a behaviour. For each directive/style entry add a COMPILE assertion in `builder_edits_test.gd`: run the operation on a fixture that exercises the hard case (multi-clause @if, middle clause, @match head, clause row, an @if that already has an @else) and assert `Compiler.compile(after).ok` AND that the generated .gd `load()`s without a parse error — the second half is what would have caught LANG-01 and LANG-16, since the .guitkx compiler reports ok=true for both. Add a `builder_chrome_test.gd` block that calls `_on_row_context` then `_on_row_menu` for every RowMenuId against a card with all eight badge kinds, asserting each result compiles. Add the nine missing parity lines so the checklist is an honest account of the gap.

**Godot specifics:** All of this is headlessly reachable: `Graph.Card` + `Service.populate_card` + `Edits.*` are pure, and `BuilderWindow` is a `Window` that can be constructed without `EditorInterface` for the menu-dispatch half (the menus are `PopupMenu`s whose `id_pressed` handlers can be called directly). `GDScript.reload()` works headlessly and is the only check that catches a dictionary-literal defect. The gesture rig at `addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd` is not needed for any of it.

**Risk:** Six green gate lines standing over functions that corrupt the user's file, which is worse than six red ones — they are the reason nobody looked.

### `LANG-14` No capability table and no schema-drift warning: the schema already names two directives the builder cannot offer

> Also filed as `ctx-13`, `LI-08` — one defect.

**Unity does:** A static `Dictionary<string,bool>` covers all eight schema controlFlow names; only its KEY SET is read, by WarnOnDirectiveDrift, which on the first wrap-menu open after the schema loads logs one Unity warning per schema name the table does not cover: "schema controlFlow directive '<name>' has no builder support — wrap/clause menus will not offer it." §8.1: "the builder must never silently trail the language again." Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:1854-1877, :1893; Plans~/UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:762-777.

**Godot today:** ABSENT. Nothing under `builder/` calls `GuitkxSchema.control_flow()` (grepped: zero hits for control_flow / drift / ControlFlow). The schema names eight — `@if @elif @else @for @while @match @case @default` — and the builder's editing vocabulary covers @if/@for/@while/@match (wrap) and @elif/@else (clause adds). `@case` and `@default` are PROJECTED (`Graph.Badge.CASE`, `DEFAULT`, `builder_graph_service.gd:716, 723`) but can never be authored (LANG-08). That is exactly the drift the warning exists to catch, and it is live today.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The remediation's normalisation step is backwards: schema `controlFlow` entries are keyed `"directive"` and the value already CARRIES the `@` (`{ "directive": "@if", "form": ..., "description": ... }`, guitkx-schema.json:16-25), not `name` without it. Compare `str(entry["directive"])` directly against the table's keys.

**To build:** Add a `const DIRECTIVE_SUPPORT := {"@if": true, "@elif": false, "@else": false, "@for": true, "@while": true, "@match": true, "@case": false, "@default": false}` beside `Edits.WRAPS`, and a one-shot `_warn_on_directive_drift()` called at the top of the wrap-menu build that `push_warning`s for every `GuitkxSchema.control_flow()` name absent from the table. Better than Unity's runtime-only check: also assert it in `tests/builder_parity.gd`, which already reads files headlessly — a CI failure beats a console line nobody reads. Note the schema entries here are keyed `name` without the `@`, so normalise before comparing.

**Godot specifics:** `GuitkxSchema` is a `@tool` class with `static var _schema` populated by `_ensure_loaded()` — a static FUNC, so the editor DOES run it (the hazard is static VAR initialisers, per the canvas_palette rule). Reference it via a preload const from the builder, not the global `class_name`. Unlike Unity there is no LSP round-trip: the schema is a bundled JSON read synchronously, so the check never has to be deferred and can simply run in a test.

**Risk:** The builder trails the language today, silently, in exactly the way the guard was written to prevent.

### `LANG-15` `@for` never binds a real collection and never singularises its loop variable

> Also filed as `ctx-12`, `SM-13` — one defect.

**Unity does:** Picking '@foreach…' does NOT wrap — it opens a searchable menu of in-scope enumerables: typed component props (LSP-first with a 1500 ms timeout, signature-parse fallback) whose type looks enumerable, plus hook-state locals extracted by regex from every body row, each labelled `expr  —  origin`, with the warn-orange freeform as the escape hatch. LoopVarFor then singularises from the collection's last path segment ('model.Rows' → 'row', anything not ending in 's' → 'item', leading capital lowered) and collision-checks against every word in the card body, appending 'Item' on a clash. This is UB-03. Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:2235-2297, :2299-2329, :3536-3605.

**Godot today:** ABSENT. `Edits.WRAPS` seeds the literal `@for (item in range(1))` and wraps immediately. There is no collection menu, no props lookup, no body-local scan and no singularisation anywhere under `builder/` (grepped for loop_var / singular / enumerable / collection — nothing). The `range(1)` choice is itself a genuine improvement over Unity's empty-collection problem (it keeps the wrapped row on screen, and the comment says so), but it means every loop the builder authors starts by iterating a throwaway range with a variable called `item` that names nothing in scope.

**To build:** Add `_show_for_wrap_menu(row)`: gather candidate collections from (a) the card's own body rows — `builder_graph_service` already emits `card.body` hook chips and `card.island_lines`, so a regex for `^\s*var\s+(\w+)\s*[:=]` over them gives the locals with origin "setup"; (b) the component's declared params, available from `Compiler.analyzed_decls(source)["decls"][i]["params"]`, filtered by a type test (`Array`, `PackedStringArray`, `Dictionary`, `[]`, `Range`). Offer each as `expr  —  origin`, keep the SearchMenu freeform row (it already exists and is exactly Unity's escape hatch), then seed `@for (<loop_var> in <expr>)` with a `_loop_var_for(expr, taken)` helper.

**Godot specifics:** No async is needed and none should be introduced: Unity's version is `async void` waiting on an LSP, whereas `RuitkGuitkx.analyzed_decls` is a synchronous pure parse the builder already calls in five places. That makes the whole feature headlessly testable in `builder_edits_test.gd`, which Unity's cannot be. Type strings here are GDScript (`Array[Dictionary]`, `PackedStringArray`), so the enumerable test is a different substring set from Unity's — and untyped params are common, which is exactly why the freeform row has to stay.

**Risk:** Every loop the builder writes must be retyped in the source pane or the inline editor before it does anything.

### `LANG-18` All eight directive kinds render in one colour and there is no badge chip; `Graph.Line.badge` is dead data

**Unity does:** BadgeKind doubles as a colour key drawn as a pill chip: 1 @if amber (1.00,0.72,0.30), 2 @foreach green (0.51,0.78,0.52), 3 @else/@else if pink (0.94,0.38,0.57), 14 @switch blue (0.31,0.76,0.97), 15 @case/@default light blue (0.55,0.73,0.97), default mauve (0.77,0.53,0.75); the background is the same hue at alpha 0.2. Unity: Canvas/BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:380-395, :491-510; Canvas/BuilderGraphModel.cs:54-58.

**Godot today:** PARTIAL — the model is right and the view ignores it. `_directive_head` sets `badge` (all eight of `Graph.Badge.IF/ELIF/ELSE/FOR/WHILE/MATCH/CASE/DEFAULT`) and `badge_text` faithfully, and the row menu reads `badge_text`. But `CanvasMarkupRow` in `canvas_view.guitkx` picks a style by `row.kind` only and paints every DIRECTIVE row with the single `P.directive_row()` tint `Color(0.902, 0.729, 0.949)`. Grepping the whole builder for `Badge.` outside the graph model and its producer returns nothing — the field is never read by the canvas. The keyword survives only because it is the first token of `row.text`, drawn as plain monospace at the row's indent, with no chip and no background.

**To build:** Add `canvas_palette.gd: static func badge_color(badge: int) -> Color` and `badge_chip(tint) -> Dictionary` (the palette already has `kind_badge` / `kind_badge_text` to copy), then in `canvas_view.guitkx`'s `CanvasMarkupRow` emit a `PanelContainer` + `Label` chip carrying `row.badge_text` when `row.kind == DIRECTIVE`, with the rest of `row.text` beside it. Give @for and @while their own hue rather than porting Unity's missing `case 4:` — that omission is documented in the register as unexplained, not intended.

**Godot specifics:** The palette is a hand-written `@tool` script for the documented static-var reason, so `badge_color` must be a static FUNC (which the file's existing entries already are) — a `const` table of Colors is fine, a `static var` is not. `canvas_view.guitkx` is DOGFOODED and its generated `.gd` is COMMITTED and gated by `tests/builder_view_build.gd`, so the edit must be made in the `.guitkx` and the `.gd` regenerated and committed in the same change. Adding a chip changes row width, so `builder_canvas_metrics.gd` — the one place every consumer measures with — must be updated too, and `builder_canvas_test.gd`'s golden markup trees will need re-baselining.

**Risk:** At a glance an @if, an @else, a @for and a @case are the same colour, so the shape of a branching card cannot be read without reading every word.

### `LANG-20` The console reports one first-error line per failed module — never warnings, never the rest

**Unity does:** Diagnose merges T1 (parse) with T2 (analyzer), an analyzer crash never takes squiggles down, and the console prints EVERY diagnostic as `{Code} L{SourceLine}: {Message}` — deliberately not the first four: "the console scrolls, and a copy that silently dropped the tail would be worse than no copy at all". Unity: Lang/BuilderLanguage.cs:104-126; Controls/CodeField.cs:999-1036.

**Godot today:** PARTIAL. `BuilderConsole.report` adds ONE row per failed module carrying `Preview._first_error`, which returns the first diagnostic with `severity == 0` and discards every other error and every warning in that module. Warnings never appear at all except the two the console synthesises itself (skipped-dependency, budget-exhausted) and the blank-module note. Separately the source pane never calls `_editor.set_line_diagnostics(...)`, so the reused `GuitkxCodeEdit` — which owns a dedicated diagnostics gutter (guitkx_code_edit.gd:29, :511) — shows no per-line marks inside the builder, even though the .guitkx editor view feeds exactly that gutter.

**To build:** Have `Preview` return the full diagnostic list per failed module (it already has `result["diagnostics"]`) and have `BuilderConsole.report` emit one row per diagnostic with its code and line, warnings included — `add_diagnostics` already renders that shape and is only used for the blank-module note today. Then feed the focus module's diagnostics into `_source._editor.set_line_diagnostics()` on each preview round, which is the Godot-native form of Unity's squiggles.

**Godot specifics:** The deliberate divergence is the source pane reusing `guitkx_code_edit.gd` instead of porting CodeField — which is fine, but the reuse is incomplete: the control's diagnostics gutter is present, configured and never fed. Note the debounce Unity needs does not apply here, because the pane is an explicit edit/apply pane and `apply_edit` parses before handing anything over (builder_source_pane.gd:230-247) — that is a legitimate engine translation, not a gap. Severity 0 = error and 1 = warning in this pipeline (`builder_console.gd:22-23`), and `_first_error` hardcodes 0.

**Risk:** A module with four errors reports one, with no line; a module with warnings reports nothing.

### `LANG-19` "Edit header…" is offered on @else and @default, where it silently does nothing

**Unity does:** `hasHeader = BadgeText != "@else" && != "@default"` gates the "Edit {badge} header" item, so a clause with no header never offers one. Unity: BuilderWindow.cs:1935-1948.

**Godot today:** ABSENT. `_on_row_context` adds `RowMenuId.EDIT_HEADER` for every DIRECTIVE row. `Edits.set_directive_header` correctly refuses a header-less clause ("inventing a parenthesis would make it a different construct", builder_edits.gd:325-328) and returns the source unchanged — verified headless on an `@else` row: `changed? false`. `_on_inline_committed` then does nothing because `after == before`, and there is no toast. So the user opens a field over an `@else`, types, presses Enter, and nothing happens with no explanation.

**To build:** Gate the item at `chrome/builder_window.gd:1094`: `if row.badge_text != "@else" and row.badge_text != "@default"`. Cheap, and it makes the refusal in `set_directive_header` unreachable-by-UI rather than silently absorbed.

**Godot specifics:** The refusal is already right and well-commented in the pure layer; only the menu is wrong. Note `_on_inline_committed`'s `if after != before` swallows every no-op edit without a toast — worth a general `toast("Nothing changed")` there, matching what `_on_search_picked` at builder_window.gd:1435-1437 already does.

**Risk:** A menu item that opens an editor and discards what is typed into it.

### Live preview: compile pipeline, mirroring, scheduling, knobs, state panel, usage notes, failure isolation

### `PV-01` Applying a source edit produces no ledger entry, no card re-projection and NO preview round — the funnel rejects it as a no-op

**Unity does:** UB-161 trigger 1: 'an applied source edit' is one of the four enumerated triggers that must produce a compile. Unity's CodeField keeps the buffer to itself while editing; ApplySourceEdit is what hands the text to the window, which writes it into the session and calls NotifyBufferChanged() (BuilderWindow.cs:1188). The window's ApplyEdit is the first thing to see the new text, so before != after always holds and the ledger, the card and the compile all run.

**Godot today:** BROKEN. builder_source_pane.gd:103 wires TextEdit.text_changed to _on_text_changed, which at :195 calls workspace.apply_edit(_path, after) — writing EVERY KEYSTROKE straight into module.buffer_text (builder_workspace.gd:290-298 → builder_module.gd:256-264) — and then emits buffer_edited. builder_window.gd:903-906 _on_buffer_edited returns immediately while _source.is_editing(), so nothing is recorded. Then Apply fires edit_applied (builder_source_pane.gd:248), which builder_window.gd:723-724 routes into apply_edit(path, text, ...) — where builder_window.gd:883-884 reads `before := module.buffer_text`, finds it ALREADY EQUALS `after`, and returns false at :885. No ledger.begin/record/end, no _after_model_change, therefore no Service.populate_card, no preview.request_refresh(), no _refresh_status(). The typed edit is in the model and invisible to every surface: the canvas card still shows the old markup, the preview still shows the old build, the status bar still shows the old dirty count, and Ctrl+Z undoes the PREVIOUS action while the typed text stays. Cancel is asymmetric and works, because there before != after genuinely holds (builder_source_pane.gd:262 → builder_window.gd:725-726). Nothing listens to workspace.changed either (the only .changed.connect in the whole builder is builder_window.gd:731 on the ledger). tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:200-236 appears to cover this and does not: it drives the pane with `pane.editor().text = "..."`, and the pane's own comment at builder_source_pane.gd:180-184 states that assigning TextEdit.text does not emit text_changed — which is true in Godot 4 (TextEdit::set_text guards _text_changed with setting_text and emits text_set instead). So the test never writes through _on_text_changed, before != after in the window, and the test passes on a path real typing never takes.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One nuance worth keeping: the MODEL is correct throughout (Save writes the right bytes, and the card catches up the next time any structural op calls `reproject()`). What is lost is the ledger entry, the card re-projection, the preview round and the status refresh — and Ctrl+Z after typing undoes the previous action while the typed text stays.

**To build:** Stop the source pane writing the model per keystroke while an edit is open. builder_source_pane.gd:_on_text_changed should NOT call workspace.apply_edit while _editing; hold the text in the editor and let apply_edit()/cancel_edit() be the only writers, exactly as the class comment at :204-209 already claims ('the pane hands the buffer over once, on apply'). Then builder_window.gd:723-724's apply_edit sees a real before/after pair, records one ledger entry and runs _after_model_change → request_refresh. Alternative if per-keystroke model writes must stay (they are what makes refresh_from_model cheap): snapshot `before` at _set_editing time and give the window an apply path that takes the explicit before, rather than re-reading module.buffer_text. Add a WINDOW-level test that drives real input — pane.editor().insert_text_at_caret(...) as tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:650-653 already does for the non-editing case — and asserts w.ledger.entries().size() == 1 and w.preview.has_pending() after apply.

**Godot specifics:** The trap is Godot-specific: TextEdit.text_changed does not fire for programmatic assignment, so any test that seeds the editor by assignment exercises a different code path from a user typing. Use insert_text_at_caret / real InputEventKey (addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd is the rig for the latter). Note also that GuitkxEditor is a CodeEdit; its editable flag is what gates the whole path, so a fix must keep _set_editing's read-only default (builder_source_pane.gd:145-146) intact.

**Risk:** The single edit funnel — the builder's stated core invariant ('a keystroke, a canvas drop and a replayed undo all reach the model through apply_edit, so they produce the same ledger entry, preview round and re-projection', CLAUDE.md) — is bypassed by the surface users type in. Source-pane work is unundoable and invisible until an unrelated gesture happens to re-project.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderWindow.cs:1188 (ApplySourceEdit → NotifyBufferChanged), UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:2578-2600 (UB-161 trigger list); godot builder_source_pane.gd:103,185-197,248 and builder_window.gd:723-724,883-885,903-906,731

### `PV-02` The compile and the pane are anchored on the window FOCUS, not on the file being rendered — selecting a style freezes the component and the header lies about it

**Unity does:** UB-202 (FIXED, HIGH). BuilderWindow.cs:4686-4694: `string rendered = _previewPane?.ShownFile ?? _focusFile;` and the batch, the assembly and the buffer are all keyed on `rendered`. The recorded lesson is that UB-190, UB-194 and UB-198 were each real, each correctly fixed, and none of them was this — 'the pane was asked to render a component out of the STYLE's assembly with the STYLE's text. It could not, so it kept the last good render — which looks exactly like the edit did nothing.'

**Godot today:** WRONG in the same shape. builder_window.gd:920 compiles with `_focus_path`, and builder_preview_pane.gd:155 overwrites `_path` with whatever module it was handed, renderable or not — so the pane's anchor is never independent of the focus. builder_window.gd:2158-2172 select_module always calls _preview_pane.show_module(_focus_path). Consequence: click a style module (in the folder pane, the library, or a canvas card) and _path becomes the style. Every later compile_finished (builder_window.gd:737-742) calls show_module(style), builder_preview.gd:539-547 returns false because has_render() is false, and builder_preview_pane.gd:169-171 keeps the last good render. The component on the stage is now frozen: editing the style rebuilds it and its importers, and the mounted component is never re-mounted against the new build. Worse, builder_preview_pane.gd:157 has already set the header to `<S.STYLE>` over a render of `<APP>`, and :170 reports 'last good render — the current edit does not build yet' when in fact the style built fine. Recovery requires re-selecting the component by hand.

**To build:** Give the pane a `_rendered_path` separate from `_shown_path`: show_module should only move the render anchor when the module actually mounts. builder_window.gd:920 should compile against `_preview_pane.rendered_path()` falling back to `_focus_path`, and builder_window.gd:737-742 should call show_module on the rendered path, not on `_preview_pane.path()`. The non-component branch (builder_preview_pane.gd:174-178) should then render as a note ALONGSIDE the still-live component rather than replacing its identity — the header tag must name what is on the stage.

**Godot specifics:** builder_preview.gd:320-340's non-component importer seeding (the UB-190 fix) is present and correct, so once the anchor is right the closure already keeps the on-screen component in the batch. Nothing here needs Control input routing; it is pure state ownership, so it is headlessly testable against builder_preview_pane.gd with a stub graph — which is exactly what no suite currently does (see PV-06 note: there is no PreviewPane test anywhere in tests/).

**Risk:** The preview silently shows a render that is not what the code says, with copy that misattributes the cause. Editing a style is half of what a builder session is; this makes that half look broken.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderWindow.cs:4686-4694 + BuilderPreviewPane.cs:806-813 (ShownFile) + UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:3426-3440 (UB-202); godot builder_window.gd:920,737-742,2158-2172 and builder_preview_pane.gd:155,157,169-171

### `PV-03` There is no end-of-round hand-off: compile_finished fires per module MID-ROUND and the window fully remounts the preview on each one

**Unity does:** The round is a transaction. BuilderPreviewCompiler.cs:136-274 returns one BuilderCompileSummary; only skips fire CompileFinished. BuilderWindow.cs:4695-4708 then hands the pane an assembly ONCE, after the whole round, and BuilderPreviewPane.cs:888-916 tears the fiber tree down only when the component TYPE object actually changed (UB-155/UB-179).

**Godot today:** builder_preview.gd:208 and :235 emit compile_finished INSIDE the build loop, once per module decided. builder_window.gd:737-742 connects a lambda that calls _preview_pane.show_module(...) on every one of them. So a round that rebuilds a style plus three components produces FOUR full remounts in a single frame, each running builder_preview_pane.gd:158 (_build_knobs, which clears _props), then builder_preview.gd:548 unmount(), :552 _clear_scratch_comp_cache() (dropping every cached child factory, forcing a load() per child), and :556 RuitkRoot.create(). Because emissions follow topological order, the first several mounts run against the focus's PREVIOUS build — built_script() still returns the old script until the focus itself compiles at the end of the batch. It also falsifies the premise stated at builder_preview.gd:277-278 ('Nothing is mounted against these scripts at this point; the mount happens after the round') — a consumer reacting to compile_finished mounts DURING the loop, before later modules in the same batch have compiled.

**To build:** Add an explicit end-of-round signal (`round_finished(summary)`) emitted once at builder_preview.gd:248, and move the window's re-show onto it. Keep compile_finished as a per-module diagnostic feed for the console only. Then hand the pane the built script once, from the round's anchor — the Godot analogue of Unity's OnRecompiled(assembly, bufferText).

**Godot specifics:** Signal emission inside a loop is the GDScript equivalent of Unity's event-during-iteration hazard, and here the handler re-enters the pipeline (show_module → builder_preview_pane.gd:168 request_refresh on failure). RuitkRoot.create/unmount are not free: unmount runs every effect cleanup and frees every host node (reconciler.gd:1386-1397, _drain_node_pool), so N remounts per round is N full teardowns of a real Control tree inside an editor frame.

**Risk:** Multiplies every other preview cost by the batch size, guarantees at least one mount per round against a stale script, and is the mechanical cause of PV-04 (knob wipe) and PV-11 (state panel never shows anything but initial values).

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderPreviewCompiler.cs:136-274 + BuilderWindow.cs:4695-4708 + BuilderPreviewPane.cs:888-916; godot builder_preview.gd:208,235,248,277-278,548-556 and builder_window.gd:737-742

### `PV-04` Knob values are wiped on every compile round — there is no component-identity check and no carry-over

**Unity does:** BuilderPreviewPane.cs:749-767: identity is `SourceOf(type)` + `PropsSignature(type)`, explicitly 'never reference equality, which would wipe every knob the user typed on each 300 ms recompile'. When identity holds, BuildKnobs is not re-run at all; when it does not, CarryOver (BuilderPreviewPane.cs:773-786) copies every same-named, same-typed value onto the fresh props instance. The Unreal leg reached the same conclusion independently and named the field for it: `TSet<FString> AppliedSeeds; // Seeds already applied, so re-previewing on every keystroke does not undo a knob the user turned after the seed landed.`

**Godot today:** ABSENT. builder_preview_pane.gd:153-158 runs _build_knobs() unconditionally on every show_module, and :241-246 clears every child widget and calls _props.clear() before re-seeding from the usage row. Combined with PV-03 (show_module fires once per module per round), any edit anywhere in the tree resets every knob to its usage literal and destroys the LineEdit the user may be typing into (builder_preview_pane.gd:279-286), taking keyboard focus with it. There is no notion of 'the same component' at all: the pane holds no previous props and no signature.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: In practice this is currently masked by a worse defect (see MISSED-1): on this repo's own naming convention no knob rows are ever built at all, so there is nothing to wipe. Fix the seeding and this becomes live immediately. Also note the widget rebuild is `remove_child` + `queue_free()`, so the visible symptom in Godot is a focused LineEdit disappearing mid-word, not just a value reset.

**To build:** Hold `_last_props` and a component signature — the file path plus the sorted `name:type` list from Attributes.props_of_component (builder_attributes.gd:32-59, which already produces exactly that). In show_module, rebuild the knob rows only when the signature changed; otherwise reuse the existing widgets and _props. When the signature does change, carry values across by name+type before re-seeding. Track which props were seeded (Unreal's AppliedSeeds) so a re-seed never overwrites a value the user typed.

**Godot specifics:** Rebuilding the rows also means queue_free()ing the focused LineEdit, so in Godot the visible symptom is focus loss and a half-typed value vanishing, not just a reset. Reusing widgets avoids that. Note the props signature is available WITHOUT reflection here — the card's projected signature string is the source of truth — so this is cheaper than Unity's version, not harder.

**Risk:** The knobs are the only way to drive a preview rather than look at it (the pane's own doc at builder_preview_pane.gd:51-52 says so). Resetting them on every round makes them unusable for the one workflow they exist for: adjust a prop, edit the markup, see the result.

*high · feature · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderPreviewPane.cs:749-767,773-786 + ruitk-unreal RuitkUiBuilderPreview.h:135-137 (AppliedSeeds); godot builder_preview_pane.gd:153-158,241-246,279-286

### `PV-05` A prop with no literal usage gets NO knob at all — a component nothing uses yet has zero knobs

**Unity does:** BuilderPreviewPane.cs:1218-1263: every readable+writable public prop of type string/int/float/bool gets a row unconditionally. SeededLiteral only decides the STARTING VALUE — `if (seeded != null) p.SetValue(...)` — and the field is created either way from the prop's own default. Capability contract §9: 'Primitive props on the focused component appear as knobs.'

**Godot today:** builder_preview_pane.gd:259-264: `var seeded := _seeded_literal(usage, name); if seeded.is_empty(): continue`. The prop is skipped entirely. So a component that nothing in the tree imports yet — the state of every component in the first minutes of a session — gets an empty knobs block, as does a component used only as `<Card title={state[0]} />` (an expression, correctly rejected as a seed at :306-312). The function's own doc comment at :239-240 claims it 'falls back to the prop's own default when the usage passes an expression', which the code does not do. There is also no member-knob miner for non-primitive props (Unity BuilderPreviewPane.cs:1261-1263 BuildMemberKnobs).

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Understated, if anything. My probe on the canonical fixture (`components/row/row.guitkx` exporting `Row(text: String = "")`, used by app as `<Row text="one" />` — a prop that DOES have a literal usage) printed `knob rows built = 0`. The reason is MISSED-1: the seed lookup keys on the file-stem title, so the usage is never found. Both the no-seed skip AND the seed lookup are broken, and fixing only the skip still leaves every knob starting at a default that `props_of_component` discards.

**To build:** Invert the condition: always emit a row for a prop whose declared type is String/int/float/bool, and use the seed only when one exists. Seed the field's initial text from the seed, otherwise from the declared default that builder_attributes.gd:47-50 already parses out and currently throws away (`name: Type = default` → the default is stripped). Emit the row with the declared default as the starting value, and only omit rows for Callable-typed props (Unity skips delegates at BuilderPreviewPane.cs:1223).

**Godot specifics:** builder_attributes.gd:props_of_component already parses `name: Type = default` and discards the default at :47-50 — keep it and pass it through. Typed widgets should follow: SpinBox for int/float and CheckBox for bool rather than a LineEdit for everything (builder_preview_pane.gd:279), because _typed at :333-341 silently int()s garbage and hands a String to any non-primitive prop, which then errors at the Godot property assign in RuitkHost.

**Risk:** The knobs are missing exactly when they matter most — a new component, previewing at its empty defaults, which is precisely the 'picture of nothing' the usage-seeding machinery exists to avoid.

*high · feature · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderPreviewPane.cs:1218-1263 + UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:350-351; godot builder_preview_pane.gd:239-240,259-264 and builder_attributes.gd:47-50

### `PV-06` No Trace toggle for the compile pipeline: the trace signal has no listener, considered/reasons are computed and discarded, and the parity gate is green over the wrong function

**Unity does:** UB-201 (RESOLVED, HIGH), and explicitly not a fix but the thing that made the next three fixes possible: 'the pipeline's failures are INVISIBLE and identical from outside: a module missing from the batch, a module that compiled and produced no change, and a module whose compile silently failed all look the same in the preview — nothing happens.' BuilderWindow.cs:4591-4649 TogglePreviewTrace + TracePreviewCompile writes one multi-line entry per round: `preview: rendering X, focus Y`, `considered:` (comma-joined names), `rebuilt:` (name + reason per entry), `FAILED:`, `skipped:`. Three sinks feed the one toggle. It is a named capability (§11) and it paid for itself on its first run (UB-202) and again on UB-223.

**Godot today:** HOLLOW. builder_preview.gd:50 declares `signal trace(message: String)` and emits it at :195 and :245 — and NOTHING in the addon connects it. The only connection anywhere is tests/builder_preview_test.gd:437. The Summary carries `considered` (builder_preview.gd:58, filled at :179-180) and `reasons` (:60, filled at :224), and builder_console.gd:92-110 report() reads only failures, skipped and budget_exhausted — considered and reasons are computed on every round and thrown away. The toolbar 'Trace' button (builder_window.gd:614, :981-983) calls builder_console.gd:174-206, which dumps SESSION STATE — module list, dirty flags, ledger depth, mounted path — and says nothing about what the last round decided. There is no toggle and no per-round log. tests/builder_parity.gd:94 `["TogglePreviewTrace", "func trace"]` passes because the matcher is a plain substring test (tests/builder_parity.gd:147-151) and builder_console.gd:174 literally reads `func trace(`. The gate is green over a function that answers a different question.

**To build:** Connect builder_preview.gd's trace signal to the console (or to print), gated by a persisted toggle on the toolbar. Extend builder_preview.gd to emit per-module lines the way Unity does — `rebuilt: <file> (text changed)` / `(dependency rebuilt)` from summary.reasons, `considered: <names>` from summary.considered, `FAILED:` and `skipped:` — and add the equivalent of the family-binding probe for this engine: after each mount, report which V.comp path each child factory resolved to. Fix the parity entry to name an identifier that only the real behaviour can satisfy (e.g. `trace_preview_round` or the toggle's MenuId), not `func trace`.

**Godot specifics:** The Godot analogue of Unity's family-key/inlining trace is the V._comp_cache path binding — builder_preview.gd:625-628 clears scratch entries but never reports what a child resolved to, which is the one thing that would distinguish 'the child rebuilt' from 'the parent is still calling last round's factory'. RuitkDiagnostics already has a trace ladder (reconciler.gd:1318-1330 _trace_desc) that could be borrowed for naming fibers.

**Risk:** This is the diagnostic that Unity's own record says three correct-but-wrong fixes were made without. The Godot leg has PV-02 (a UB-202 reintroduction) sitting in its pipeline right now and no instrument that would show it. Meanwhile the gate reports parity.

### `PV-07` The preview mounts on the editor's SHARED scheduler with process-global budgets — there is no per-preview frame-budgeted scheduler

**Unity does:** Every pane owns a BuilderRenderScheduler: four priority queues, TickBudgetMs = 4.0, delegate dedupe, self-unhooking from EditorApplication.update, per-action try/catch, and its own BeginBatch/EndBatch state. The stated reason (VISUAL_EDITOR_PLAN §2.1, VE-10): 'EditorRenderScheduler's queues are process-global statics with no time budget, so a preview component scheduling unbounded work would starve every other editor mount', and the global BeginBatch/EndBatch are static too. Capability contract §9 names it: 'mounting the result through the real reconciler, on its own frame-budgeted scheduler'.

**Godot today:** ABSENT. builder_preview.gd:556 calls RuitkRoot.create(container, ...) → reactive_root.gd:22-25 → RuitkReconciler.new(container), and reconciler.gd:196-199/:328 enqueue onto `Scheduler.for_tree(tree)` — scheduler.gd:64-75, one RuitkScheduler per SceneTree, which in the editor is the EDITOR's SceneTree, shared with anything else the addon mounts. The slice quantum and cumulative budget come from RuitkConfig.time_slice_ms / frame_budget_ms (reconciler.gd:234-235), which are process-global statics; there is no per-root override. reactive_root.gd:22 also calls RuitkSettings.apply(), which loads the user's PROJECT settings onto those statics inside the editor process the first time a preview mounts. The port plan's C2 row (plans/BUILDER_PORT_PLAN.md:144) lists 'own frame budget' as delivered — but what was built is builder_preview.gd:85 budget_msec, a COMPILE-round budget. That is a real and good feature (see present list); it is not the render scheduler the contract clause names.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Accurate statement: the builder does not own its scheduler instance and cannot override `time_slice_ms`/`frame_budget_ms` per root — the reconciler reads the `RuitkConfig` statics directly (reconciler.gd:234-235), and `RuitkRoot.create` calls `RuitkSettings.apply()` (reactive_root.gd:22), which loads the user's PROJECT settings onto those statics inside the editor process the first time a preview mounts. That last part is the real defect worth writing up: a project that sets `time_slicing = false` or a large budget changes how the EDITOR renders. Severity medium, not high. On the plan row: BUILDER_PORT_PLAN.md:144's 'own frame budget' sits in a list of compile-pipeline items ('compile in import order, seed `_comp_cache`, scratch for value imports, own frame budget, ~0.3s debounce') and most plainly names `budget_msec`, which IS built — reading it as a claim about the render scheduler is a stretch.

**To build:** Either (a) add a `scheduler` parameter to RuitkRoot.create / RuitkReconciler so the builder can pass a budgeted instance it owns and disposes with the window, plus per-root time_slice_ms / frame_budget_ms overrides on the reconciler rather than reading the statics; or (b) accept the shared scheduler as a deliberate divergence and DOCUMENT it in CLAUDE.md alongside the other listed ones, with the honest note that a preview component with a runaway effect will stall the editor. Today it is neither — it is a contract clause silently unmet and a plan row that reads as done.

**Godot specifics:** scheduler.gd:64-75 keys by SceneTree instance id and wires pump to tree.process_frame; a builder-owned instance would need its own pump, most naturally from builder_window.gd:301 _process, which already drives tick(). The reconciler reads RuitkConfig statics directly at reconciler.gd:234-235, so per-root budgets need a field, not a global. Godot's editor runs the whole editor UI on that same SceneTree, so the starvation concern VE-10 raises applies at least as strongly here as in Unity.

**Risk:** A preview component whose render or effects schedule unbounded work competes with the editor itself under whatever budget the user's PROJECT settings happen to specify. The contract clause and the plan row both claim otherwise.

*high · engine-translation · OVERSTATED* — unity BuilderRenderScheduler.cs:10-137 + VISUAL_EDITOR_PLAN.md §2.1/VE-10 + UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:347-349; godot builder_preview.gd:556 + reactive_root.gd:22-25 + reconciler.gd:196-199,234-235,328 + scheduler.gd:64-75 + plans/BUILDER_PORT_PLAN.md:144

### `PV-08` A transient compiler-environment failure is reported as a source failure in every module, against the compiler's own documented caller contract

**Unity does:** BuilderPreviewCompiler.cs:44-83 separates 'the compiler could not initialise' from 'this module did not compile': EnsureReady LATCHES _initError and the pane says `Preview compiler unavailable: <InitError>` (BuilderWindow.cs:4679-4681) rather than blaming any file.

**Godot today:** The distinction exists in the compiler and is ignored by the preview. guitkx.gd:138-146 returns `{ ok:false, env_error:true, diagnostics:[GUITKX2507] }` when the vocabulary cannot be read, and the comment at :141-143 states the caller contract verbatim: 'callers must keep any existing sibling .gd and the previous sidecar (a transient tooling state is not a source regression); the next call self-heals once the read succeeds.' The compiler's own callers honour it — guitkx_codegen.gd:488,496,727 — and it is gated by tests/guitkx_test.gd:1747-1757. builder_preview.gd:263-264 does not: any non-ok result goes through _first_error and becomes a module failure. :231-234 then erases _compiled_from (fine) AND _built (dropping the last good script, so built_script returns null and the pane can no longer re-mount even unchanged code), marks the module a failed_root, and blocks every dependent at :200-209. Because the environment failure hits every module in the batch, one unreadable vocabulary.json turns into 'N failed, M skipped' naming the user's own files, with GUITKX2507 as the error text — and builder_window.gd:734-736 forces the console open for it. This is precisely the editor-first-scan window the compiler comment describes.

**To build:** In builder_preview.gd:_build, check `bool(result.get("env_error", false))` before treating the result as a failure. On env_error: leave _compiled_from and _built untouched (so the last good script keeps serving), do not add to failed_roots, do not append to summary.failures, and surface it once per round as a single pipeline-level message ('the .guitkx compiler is not ready — retrying') rather than per file. Add the env_error case to tests/builder_preview_test.gd, which currently has no coverage of it.

**Godot specifics:** This is a Godot-only failure mode with no Unity analogue: the vocabulary read depends on the editor's filesystem state, and the builder is by definition an editor-time consumer, so it is the caller MOST likely to hit the unready window. Also note that dropping _built here is worse in Godot than in Unity, because Godot has no _currentAssembly fallback layer (Unity's UB-157 patch) to cushion it.

**Risk:** A tooling hiccup is reported as the user's code being broken, in the user's file names, with the console forced open, and it takes the last good render's script down with it.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderPreviewCompiler.cs:44-83 + BuilderWindow.cs:4679-4681; godot guitkx.gd:138-146 (contract) + guitkx_codegen.gd:488,496,727 (honoured elsewhere) + tests/guitkx_test.gd:1747-1757 + builder_preview.gd:263-264,231-234,200-209

### `PV-09` The pane's status copy conflates three different states, the module note is unreachable, and the console it defers to is forced open and never closes

**Unity does:** Three distinct messages, chosen by three distinct tests. BuilderPreviewPane.cs:655 classifies by file name first; :674-687 distinguishes 'declares a component but no type was found' (a compile problem — 'Check the errors under the source pane; the preview appears as soon as they clear. Saving is not required.', the UB-125 rewrite) from 'this module has no visual' (NoPreviewText: signature + consumers). And a failed round names its FIRST error IN THE PANE with the file, the skip count and 220 characters of the message (BuilderWindow.cs:4709-4728, the UB-15 fix), keeping the last good render underneath.

**Godot today:** builder_preview_pane.gd:159-179 orders three outcomes by whether the stage happens to be non-empty. (1) mount succeeds → 'rendered from the real component'. (2) mount fails and _slot has children → 'last good render — the current edit does not build yet'. (3) mount fails and the stage is empty → _module_note, else _show_idle. So the module note at :131-145 (the ported ModuleInfoFor — signature plus consumers) is UNREACHABLE for the entire common case, because once anything has ever rendered the stage is never empty again; a style module always reports 'the current edit does not build yet', which is false. A component that genuinely failed to compile gets the same sentence, with no file name and no error text. The actual error only reaches builder_console.gd:96-100 via builder_window.gd:922, in a panel the user may not be looking at. And builder_window.gd:734-736 sets `_console.visible = true` on any failure while NOTHING anywhere sets it back to false (the only other writers are :367 at construction and :982/:986 for Trace and Help) — so the first typo opens the console permanently and it takes a strip off the canvas for the rest of the session, which is the exact failure builder_window.gd:362-365's own comment says the console was redesigned to avoid.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The console point is worse than stated: Trace and Help also pin it open (:982, :986) and neither is a toggle, so there is no user gesture that closes the console at all once it has been shown — the strip the comment at :362-365 says the redesign removed comes back permanently on the first Trace press, not only on the first typo.

**To build:** Split the three cases on their real predicates, not on child count: has_render(built_script) == false → module note (and keep the component on the stage, per PV-02, with the header still naming what is rendered); built_script == null and the round reported a failure for this path → name the file and show the first error, truncated; built_script == null and no failure → 'not built yet, a round is queued'. Surface the round's first failure in the pane itself from summary.failures (builder_window.gd:920-922 already has the Summary in hand). Give the console an auto-hide: clear _console.visible when a round comes back clean.

**Godot specifics:** builder_console.gd:245's _sync_visibility deliberately only sizes the ItemList and leaves on-screen-ness to the window ('Whether the console is ON SCREEN is the window's call'), so the missing half is entirely in builder_window.gd. The pane's own Label wrapping is already set up (autowrap_mode at :91) so a two-line error fits.

**Risk:** Every failure mode of the preview reads as the same sentence, and that sentence is wrong for two of the three. Combined with PV-06 there is no instrument anywhere that distinguishes them.

*high · visual · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderPreviewPane.cs:655,674-687 + BuilderWindow.cs:4709-4728 + UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md UB-15/UB-125; godot builder_preview_pane.gd:131-145,159-179 + builder_window.gd:362-367,734-736,920-922,982,986

### `PV-10` The round that select_module forces is never reported — its Summary is discarded while the console is made visible with stale rows

**Unity does:** Every CompileDirty call in Unity is immediately followed by TracePreviewCompile(summary, rendered) and the failure-surfacing block (BuilderWindow.cs:4693-4728). There is one call site, so there is one reporting path.

**Godot today:** There are two call sites and only one reports. builder_window.gd:918-923 (tick) calls compile_dirty and passes the Summary to _console.report(). builder_window.gd:2170-2171 (select_module, the UB-153 mount-asks-for-a-compile path) calls `preview.compile_dirty(_focus_path)` and throws the return value away. If that round fails, the compile_finished handler at :734-736 makes the console visible — showing whatever the PREVIOUS round left in it, or nothing at all — while the failure that just happened is reported nowhere.

**To build:** Capture the summary at builder_window.gd:2171 and pass it through the same reporting path (_console.report + the pane's failure surfacing from PV-09). Better: extract a single `_run_round(anchor)` helper that both call sites use, so a third call site cannot reintroduce this.

**Godot specifics:** Purely a wiring fix in builder_window.gd; both call sites are in the same file and the Summary type is already the console's input (builder_console.gd:92). Headlessly testable through the window harness that tests/builder_chrome_test.gd already builds (_window()).

**Risk:** Selecting a module whose compile fails opens an empty or stale console and reports nothing — the failure looks like the pane simply not updating.

*medium · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderWindow.cs:4693-4728; godot builder_window.gd:918-923 vs :2170-2171, and :734-736

### `PV-11` The state panel is inert: blank labels, whole-subtree scrape, and it never refreshes after the mount

**Unity does:** BuilderPreviewPane.cs:379-441: TickStatePanel refreshes twice a second off EditorApplication.update, bails out while the user has focus inside the panel, and RefreshStatePanel shows the slots of the SELECTED component only (FindFocusedFiber, :442-465, matching the render delegate's method and falling back to the top-most stateful fiber). Slot labels come from the SOURCE — CollectStateNames (:485-513) walks the buffer for `use*` calls against HookRegistry's slot-arity table, so a row is named after the user's own `var (count, setCount) = useState(...)` variable, and a custom hook truncates the walk with an explicit note rather than silently. Fields are editable and write back into the fiber's state store. Unreal reached the same design: FRuitkUiBuilderLiveState carries Name, Display and a Write callback.

**Godot today:** builder_preview_pane.gd:351-398 exists and is answered by tests/builder_parity.gd:90, but: (1) the label is `"%s #%d" % [str(fiber.get("type")), i]` at :393, and fiber.type is set to "" for every non-HOST fiber (reconciler.gd:617) — state lives on FUNCTION fibers, so every row reads ' #0', ' #1'. reconciler.gd:1325-1330 already has the correct fallback (_trace_desc → component.get_method()) and it is not used. (2) _collect_state at :381-398 walks the whole subtree depth-first, so a child component's internals surface indistinguishably from the previewed component's own. (3) _refresh_state is called only from the mount-success branch at :162 — never on a timer — so it shows initial values only; combined with PV-03 (remount per round) the panel can never show a value that a user interaction produced, which is the exact question the doc comment at :95-97 claims it answers ('why is it showing the empty branch' is a question about state). (4) No slot names from source, so a useMemo cell and a useState cell are indistinguishable rows. (5) Read-only — the file's comment at :346-350 calls this deliberate, but that reasoning ('calling a useState setter from outside a render would schedule a re-render of a preview the user is not interacting with, which is a different feature wearing the same label') is contradicted by both other legs, where re-rendering the preview from a state field IS the feature; and it is not in CLAUDE.md's list of agreed divergences.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Sub-claim (5) is fairer than stated: the read-only choice IS argued in the file at builder_preview_pane.gd:346-350, so it is a documented decision rather than a silent omission — it is just not in CLAUDE.md's divergence list and it is contradicted by the other two legs. Grade it as 'undecided divergence', not as missing work.

**To build:** Name rows from the component: use the fiber's component Callable method name (reconciler.gd:1325-1330's rule) or, better, port CollectStateNames — scan the buffer for `use*(` calls and take the assigned variable name, which the .guitkx setup block makes just as scannable as C#. Restrict the walk to the fibers whose component Callable matches the mounted render, with the top-most stateful fiber as fallback. Drive _refresh_state from builder_window.gd:301 _process on a ~0.5 s cadence, with the focus-inside-the-panel bail-out. Then make the rows editable: hooks.gd:117 stores `{kind:"state", value, setter}` — the setter is right there, and calling it is exactly what a Godot re-render needs.

**Godot specifics:** fiber.type being "" for FUNCTION fibers is the specific Godot trap here and is one line from reconciler.gd. Editing writes must go through the stored setter Callable, not by mutating slot.value, or the reconciler's bailout (reconciler.gd:428 can_bail on unchanged props/state) will skip the re-render — hooks.gd:314 sets has_pending_update, which is what makes the update land. Refreshing on a timer needs the panel to not steal focus: rebuild rows in place rather than queue_free()ing them (same fix shape as PV-04).

**Risk:** A named capability, green on the parity gate, that shows unlabelled initial values of the wrong fibers and never updates.

### `PV-12` No external-file-change trigger: the workspace can adopt disk text and nothing ever asks it to

**Unity does:** UB-161 trigger 4, and one of the two gaps the research found: 'Trigger 4 did not exist. An external file change refreshed the CARD and never rebuilt, so the preview silently kept showing the pre-change build.' Wired via OnUitkxImported / ReloadCleanFromDisk → NotifyBufferChanged (BuilderWindow.cs:192).

**Godot today:** builder_workspace.gd:237-249 reload_clean_from_disk exists, is correct (clean modules only, never clobbering unsaved edits) and is tested at tests/builder_model_test.gd:747-753 — and has ZERO callers in the addon. Nothing in the builder observes the filesystem: no EditorFileSystem.filesystem_changed connection, no focus-in handler, no mtime poll (grep for filesystem_changed / NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS across builder/ returns nothing). So a .guitkx edited in the Godot script editor or an external editor while the builder holds it clean is invisible to the card, the graph and the preview.

**To build:** Connect EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem().filesystem_changed (and, following the editor addon's own precedent, an editor focus-in check — the plugin already knows a .guitkx-only external edit does not reliably flip Godot's changed flag) to a handler that calls workspace.reload_clean_from_disk(paths of clean modules), then reproject() + preview.request_refresh() for whatever it returns.

**Godot specifics:** EditorInterface is not available in a headless --script run, so the observer must be optional and injectable — the same shape as builder_preview.gd:89's now_msec Callable — or the whole builder becomes untestable headlessly. The existing editor plugin already solves the 'external .guitkx edit does not flip the changed flag' problem with an mtime staleness guard (per CLAUDE.md); reuse it rather than re-deriving.

**Risk:** The preview silently shows a build from before an external edit, with no signal that it has. Rare, and wrong the same way Unity's was.
