### `PV-13` No disk fall-through: an import added in-session to a real file outside the loaded tree cannot compile in the preview

**Unity does:** BuilderModuleSource (BuilderModuleSource.cs:29-181) answers every module question from the tree FIRST and falls through to FileSystemModuleSource for paths the tree has no opinion about — with IsAccountedFor deliberately refusing to re-admit a module the tree has DELETED or MOVED AWAY. 'A fall-through is not automatically wrong — a hand-written module outside the open tree is a legitimate import target' (ISO-G).

**Godot today:** There is no fall-through, because the mirror is total: builder_preview.gd:424-450 mirrors exactly workspace.modules() and nothing else, and the compiler resolves specifiers against scratch_root_for() (:140-141) — so an import naming a file the workspace does not hold resolves into the mirror, finds nothing, and fails. builder_workspace.gd:184-201 closes the tree over imports transitively AT LOAD TIME, which covers the common case, but the tree is fixed after that: builder_workspace.gd:210-236 `open()` — the one function that would bring a single outside file in — has zero callers in the addon. So typing `import { Thing } from "../shared/thing"` at a real on-disk module outside the loaded tree compiles fine in the real build and fails in the preview, and PV-09's copy blames the user's edit for it.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The load-time closure is stronger than the claim implies and covers the common case properly: builder_workspace.gd:189-201 walks `_import_targets_of` transitively and pulls in every reachable on-disk target, so a cross-tree import that already exists when the tree opens IS in the model and IS mirrored. The gap is strictly the in-session case — an import typed (or dropped) during the session at a file outside the loaded tree. That narrows it to medium, as graded.

**To build:** When _imports_of maps a specifier to a path the workspace does not hold, and FileAccess.file_exists(that path), pull it into the workspace via the existing builder_workspace.gd:210 open() (which already re-checks disk for clean modules) so it gets mirrored like any other module — the tree-first, disk-second rule, expressed as membership rather than as a source overlay. Guard it with the IsAccountedFor rule: never re-admit a path some module's disk_path claims but the tree has deleted or moved away (builder_module.gd carries disk_path already). And count the pull-ins per round and name them, which is ISO-G's fall-through log.

**Godot specifics:** Because Godot mirrors rather than overlays, 'fall-through' means 'mirror it too', which is strictly simpler than Unity's IModuleSource. The IsAccountedFor guard matters more here, not less: deletion is ABSENCE in this leg (CLAUDE.md), so silently re-admitting a deleted module from disk would resurrect it into the mirror and keep satisfying an import that should have started failing — which builder_preview.gd:421-423's own comment identifies as the worst failure mode of a stale mirror.

**Risk:** A legitimate cross-tree import compiles for real and fails in the preview, reported as a source error against the user's file.

*medium · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderModuleSource.cs:29-181 + BUILDER_ISOLATION_PLAN.md ISO-1/ISO-G; godot builder_preview.gd:140-141,424-450 + builder_workspace.gd:161-201,210-236 (open() unreferenced)

### `PV-14` A render failure escapes the pane: no error boundary around the mount and no empty-render diagnostic

**Unity does:** Two separate diagnostics, both from UB-15/UB-154. BuilderPreviewPane.cs:936-946 wraps the synchronous render in try/catch and shows 'Render failed: <msg>\nMost often a required prop — seed it in PROPS above.' BuilderPreviewPane.cs:917-935 warns unconditionally when the render produced no elements: 'preview mounted <Type> from <Assembly> but the render produced no elements' — the diagnostic UB-205 relies on to tell 'renders nothing' from 'rendered the wrong thing'.

**Godot today:** Neither. builder_preview.gd:556 calls RuitkRoot.create with a bare V.fc(Callable(script, "render"), props) — no boundary. GDScript cannot try/catch, but this runtime's documented substitute exists and is unused: v.gd:178-179 V.error_boundary, backed by fail.gd's cooperative RuitkFail latch and reconciler.gd:_begin_error_boundary. Grep for error_boundary or RuitkFail across the whole editor addon returns nothing. So a component that calls RuitkFail.render(reason) — or dereferences a null required prop and hard-errors — produces an engine error in the Output dock and a stage that is either empty or half-built, with the pane reporting 'rendered from the real component — every edit re-renders'. And there is no empty-render check at all: builder_preview_pane.gd:159-163 reports success on a mount that produced zero children, so 'my component renders nothing' is indistinguishable from 'it rendered'.

**To build:** Wrap the mount: RuitkRoot.create(container, V.error_boundary({ "fallback": ..., "on_error": <callable that sets the pane's note> }, [V.fc(...)])). Route the boundary's error into the same status line PV-09 defines, with the 'most often a required prop — seed it in the knobs above' hint. Separately, after a successful mount check _slot.get_child_count() == 0 and say so explicitly rather than claiming a render.

**Godot specifics:** CLAUDE.md flags error boundaries as cooperative here and the knob-research memory records them as INERT in this leg — which makes the preview the single best place to prove they work, since it is the one host that mounts arbitrary user code. A hard GDScript crash still cannot be caught; the boundary covers the RuitkFail path, which is what the generated code raises. The empty-render check is trivial and headlessly testable (the existing suite already mounts into a Control at tests/builder_preview_test.gd:493-514).

**Risk:** The one place the builder runs untrusted user code has no failure containment, and its two most common silent outcomes (threw, rendered nothing) both report as success.

*medium · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderPreviewPane.cs:917-935,936-946 + UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md UB-15/UB-154; godot builder_preview.gd:556 + builder_preview_pane.gd:159-163 + v.gd:178-179 (V.error_boundary, no builder caller)

### `PV-15` Clicking a preview element selects only the mounted module, and there is no row-to-preview direction at all

**Unity does:** Capability contract §9, both directions: 'Clicking an element in the preview selects the markup row that produced it, and vice versa.' BuilderPreviewPane wires ComponentPicked to OnPreviewComponentPicked, which maps the clicked ELEMENT back to the component that owns it.

**Godot today:** Half of one direction. builder_preview_pane.gd:117-123 handles gui_input on the STAGE PanelContainer and emits component_picked(_path) — the mounted module, not the row — and the comment at :112-116 is honest that Godot nodes carry no back-reference to the .guitkx row. The row-to-preview direction does not exist anywhere. There is also a routing consequence not discussed: because the mounted component's own Controls default to mouse_filter STOP, the stage's gui_input only fires for clicks that land in gaps between them — so on a component that fills its stage, the picking gesture never fires at all.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Two refinements for the write-up. (1) The proposed fix already has a working in-repo precedent to copy — `builder_canvas_host.gd:241-245`, which forces `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE` on every non-BaseButton Control after each render — rather than the modifier-key or overlay-Control workarounds suggested. (2) The pane is honest about the missing element→row mapping at :112-116, so grade the module-level half as a knowingly partial port, not as invented behaviour.

**To build:** Give the mount a row identity to point at. The compiler already knows a row's span (RuitkGuitkxJsxScan.element_end is what builder_graph_service.gd projects rows from), so the emitter could stamp a per-element marker the host applies as node metadata (RuitkHost is the single seam that maps props to node properties). With that, a click resolves to a row and a selected row can highlight its node. Short of the emitter change: at minimum make the existing gesture reachable — set the mounted subtree's mouse_filter to PASS while a modifier is held, or put a transparent overlay Control over the stage that captures picking clicks, so the module-level pick fires on any click rather than only on gaps.

**Godot specifics:** Control.mouse_filter is the whole story for the reachability half and is entirely inside the pane. The row-identity half needs a codegen change and must not alter what the real build emits — the preview compiles through the real compiler at real paths by design (CLAUDE.md), so any marker has to be emitted for both or gated by a compile flag threaded through Compiler.compile's existing options.

**Risk:** A named contract clause with one direction absent and the other unreachable on exactly the components most worth clicking.

*medium · gesture · CONFIRMED* — unity UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:351-353 + BuilderWindow.cs OnPreviewComponentPicked; godot builder_preview_pane.gd:73,112-123 (stage-level gui_input, module-level payload)

### `PV-16` Summary.considered and Summary.reasons have no consumer — the UB-201 data is collected every round and dropped

**Unity does:** Considered exists for one stated reason: 'a module missing from the batch looks exactly like one that compiled and changed nothing — which is the failure that cost three rounds of guessing.' Reasons carries 'text changed' / 'dependency rebuilt' per module. Both are rendered by TracePreviewCompile into one console entry per round.

**Godot today:** Both are built. builder_preview.gd:58 declares considered and :179-180 fills it from the post-closure batch; :60 declares reasons and :224 fills it with exactly Unity's two strings. builder_console.gd:92-110 report() reads failures, skipped and budget_exhausted and nothing else, and no other consumer of Summary exists in the addon. So every round pays to compute the two fields that answer 'why did nothing happen' and then discards them.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: Broader than claimed: `focus_ok` and `focus_error` (builder_preview.gd:67-68, set at :236-238) are ALSO unread in production — a grep finds them only in tests/builder_preview_test.gd (lines 163, 252, 258, 275, 396, 408). That is the single field that answers 'did the module I am looking at build', and no surface reads it. Four of the Summary's seven fields are test-only.

**To build:** Render them. Either fold into PV-06's trace toggle (one line per round: `considered: a.guitkx, b.style.guitkx` / `rebuilt: a.guitkx (text changed)`), or, cheaper and always-on, extend builder_console.gd:_summarize (:110-116) to say `N built, M considered` instead of just `N module(s) rebuilt, no problems` — which at least distinguishes 'the batch was empty' from 'the batch ran and changed nothing'.

**Godot specifics:** Purely additive in builder_console.gd; the Summary is already the console's parameter type and tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:694+ already constructs Summary objects directly, so it is trivially gateable.

**Risk:** The instrument for the pipeline's one indistinguishable failure class is half-built: the data exists, nothing shows it, and the gap is invisible because the fields are populated.

### `PV-17` The whole preview PANE is untested — no suite constructs it, so every defect above sits behind a green run

**Unity does:** Not a Unity behaviour; a gate judgement. Unity's own record (UB-201, UB-202) is that this pipeline's failures are indistinguishable from outside, which is why the reference invested in a trace rather than in more tests.

**Godot today:** tests/builder_preview_test.gd (530 lines) drives builder_preview.gd thoroughly — dirty-since-built, closure, ordering, isolation, debounce, budget, scratch hygiene, teardown — and never touches builder_preview_pane.gd. tests/builder_chrome_test.gd covers the source pane, console, inline editor, folder pane and the funnel, and contains no reference to PreviewPane at all (grep for PreviewPane / _build_knobs / _refresh_state / _usage_note / _module_note across tests/ hits only tests/builder_parity.gd:86-90). So the four pane behaviours the parity gate lists are gated by a substring search over source text and by nothing else. That is why PV-04, PV-05, PV-09 and PV-11 are all live at once: each is a function that exists, is named the right thing, and does the wrong thing.

**To build:** A pane suite: construct RuitkBuilderPreviewPane with a real Preview over the existing tests/__builder_preview_tmp fixture and a projected graph, then assert (a) a knob row exists for every declared primitive prop, seeded or not; (b) a knob value survives a second show_module for the same file; (c) the state panel's row labels name the component; (d) selecting a style module does not relabel the header over a component render; (e) a component that mounts zero children reports so. All of it runs headless — the pane is a VBoxContainer and the mount already works headless (tests/builder_preview_test.gd:8-11 says so). Also fix the parity entries that a substring cannot distinguish, starting with tests/builder_parity.gd:94.

**Godot specifics:** Everything in the pane is headlessly constructible; the only editor dependency is none. The knob widgets are LineEdits, so a value change must be driven with the same care as the source pane (text_changed does not fire on assignment — set text then call the handler, or use insert_text_at_caret), or the test will pass on a path the user never takes, exactly as tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:200-236 does today.

**Risk:** Six of the gaps in this report are in one 402-line file that no test instantiates, while a 73-entry gate reports the area as answered.

### `PV-18` The module note's consumer detection uses a substring match where the sibling function uses an exact one

**Unity does:** UsageFor matches markup rows exactly: `Text.Trim('<','>')` equals the node's Title, Ordinal.

**Godot today:** Two functions in the same file disagree. builder_preview_pane.gd:227 (_usage_note) compares `str(row.name) != title` — exact, correct. builder_preview_pane.gd:141 (_module_note) uses `str(row.text).contains(card.title)` over import rows — so a module named `Row` reports itself 'used by' every module that imports `RowHeader`, and a module named `Card` matches an import of `CardList`.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: There is an irony worth putting in the write-up: on the repo's canonical fixture the LOOSE match is the one that works and the STRICT one is broken. My probe printed `module_note(row) = 'Row(text: String = "") — used by app'` (correct, by accident — the lowercase stem 'row' is a substring of the import specifier `./components/row/row`) while `usage_note(row) = 'nothing in this tree uses it yet'` (wrong — app.guitkx uses `<Row text="one" />`). Both should compare resolved paths or `card.exports`; see MISSED-1, which is the root cause.

**To build:** Resolve the import row to a path with Specifiers.map (builder_specifiers.gd:47-56, already the builder's one resolver) and compare paths, or at minimum compare against the card's exports exactly. The graph already carries resolved import edges — builder_graph_service.gd computes them — so the projection can answer this without a text match at all.

**Godot specifics:** builder_graph.gd:171 imports is Array[Line] with .text being the raw source line; the resolved target is available from the graph's edges rather than from the line text. Preload-const access only, as everywhere else here.

**Risk:** Cosmetic and rare, but it is the copy that a style/hook module shows in place of a render — and it is currently unreachable anyway (PV-09), so fixing PV-09 exposes it.

*low · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity BuilderWindow.cs UsageFor (exact Trim/equals match); godot builder_preview_pane.gd:141 vs :227

### `ub-risk.path-availability-asks-disk` is_path_available consults the disk about an in-memory tree, and the name prompt asks a different question entirely

**Unity does:** BuilderWorkspace.IsPathAvailable is ONE rule with TWO exceptions, and both exist because disk lags the model by an arbitrary amount under the save-only contract. BuilderWorkspace.cs:75-96: false if the tree already holds a module there; true if no file exists; and when a file DOES exist it is still available if (a) some module in the tree HasMoved and its DiskPath canonicalises to that path (its own vacated pre-move copy — UB-222: "moving a module BACK to where it started failed with 'already there', pointing at the module's own pre-move copy, which no amount of retrying could clear because only Save can"), or (b) the path appears in _tree.OrphanedPaths() (a saved module deleted this session — UB-172: "The name was reserved by something invisible"). UB-172's other half made it THE rule: ValidateNewName (BuilderWindow.cs:6138), the move guard (:550, :5700), the placement plan (:5700) and CreateNew (:259) all call the same function "so they cannot disagree".

**Godot today:** wrong, and split in two. builder_workspace.gd:97-105 `is_path_available` is `_tree.by_path(full) == null and not FileAccess.file_exists(full)` — NEITHER exception. Its own doc comment (:95-96) asserts the exception is unnecessary ("a deleted module is not in the tree, so its name is free the instant it goes") while the very next line still asks the filesystem, which still has the file. And builder_window.gd:1803 `_validate_name` does not call it at all — it uses `workspace.try_get(folder.path_join(name + suffix))`, a tree-only test. The two disagree exactly in the deleted-but-unsaved case: the prompt ACCEPTS the name, `create_new` (builder_workspace.gd:257-265) returns null on `is_path_available`, `_create_named` (builder_window.gd:1887-1894) returns "" — and nothing is created, with no toast, no console line, no error. `_unused_name` (:1932) is a third tree-only test on the same question.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One scoping nuance worth carrying into the plan: the has_moved exception is currently MOOT for moves, because no move route consults `is_path_available` at all (see the next gap) — it only bites `create_new` (create a module at a path a moved module vacated but Save has not yet cleared). The orphan exception bites the same single caller. So the fix is one function plus one caller, not a sweep.

**To build:** Give `is_path_available` both exceptions — walk `_tree.modules()` for `module.has_moved() and Paths.same(module.disk_path, full)`, and walk `_tree.orphaned_paths()` for `Paths.same(orphan, full)` — then make `_validate_name` call it instead of `try_get`, and have `_create_named` toast on a null return rather than swallowing it. `_unused_name` should skip a name `is_path_available` refuses, not just one `try_get` finds. All of it is pure `FileAccess`/model code and belongs in `builder_model_test.gd` beside the existing create/delete fixtures: delete a saved module, re-create it under the same name, assert a module comes back.

**Godot specifics:** Pure model layer — headlessly testable, no EditorInterface, no Control involved. Keep the preload-const discipline (`Paths`, `Module` are already preloaded in builder_workspace.gd:29-31); do not reach for the global `RuitkBuilderTree` name from here. The silent-return path is the dangerous half: GDScript has no exceptions, so `create_new` returning null is the only signal and every caller currently drops it.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/Document/BuilderWorkspace.cs:75-96 (both exceptions) and Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:6138 (ValidateNewName routes through it); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:97-105 and chrome/builder_window.gd:1803,1887,1932

### `ub-risk.move-has-no-destination-guard` No move route checks whether the destination is occupied, so two modules can claim one path and Save silently overwrites one

**Unity does:** Every move is guarded by the same availability rule before anything is mutated. MoveModuleToFolder (BuilderWindow.cs:548-554) builds the destination path and refuses with a toast — `Toast(Path.GetFileName(to) + " is already there")` — when `!_workspace.IsPathAvailable(to)`; the placement plan does the same and aborts the WHOLE plan (:5699-5707: "a collision cancels all of it rather than leaving half the tree in the new folder"). This is the same one rule as the create guard, which is UB-172's whole point.

**Godot today:** absent in three of four routes. `place_module` (builder_window.gd:1727-1748) checks only `Paths.same(module.folder, target_folder)`; `move_folder` → `_move_one` (:1750-1757) → `workspace.place_at` (builder_workspace.gd:304-308) → `_tree.move_to` (builder_tree.gd:111-139) check nothing; `_rename_to` (:1897-1917) checks nothing. Only `_place_tree_in` (:2078-2082) tests the destination. The folder pane's drop rule `_drop_target_for` (builder_folder_pane.gd:141-156) rejects only self-moves and self-subtree moves, so a plain drag of `Card.guitkx` onto a folder that already holds `Card.guitkx` is accepted. The consequence is not cosmetic: `RuitkBuilderTree._reindex` (builder_tree.gd:205-218) is last-writer-wins, so `_by_path` silently drops one module, and `save_all` (builder_workspace.gd:512-538) then iterates `_tree.modules()` and writes BOTH to the same `target` — the second overwrites the first, `set_projection` de-duplicates the path so nothing is orphaned, and one module's text is gone with no diagnostic. `RuitkBuilderTree.validate()` (:227-249) reports exactly this ("two modules claim %s") and has zero production callers.

**To build:** Put the guard where the moves are, not at each caller: refuse inside `RuitkBuilderWorkspace.move_to`/`place_at` when `_tree.by_path(destination)` is a DIFFERENT module (UB-119's lesson — the refusal lives at the write, not at the caller), returning [] as those functions already do for a refusal, and toast from `place_module`/`move_folder`/`_rename_to` on the empty return. Then call `_tree.validate()` after every structural edit in a debug build and push_error on a non-empty result. Cover it in `builder_edits_test.gd`/`builder_save_test.gd` as a before/after disk-state case: two modules of the same file name, one dragged onto the other's folder, assert the move is refused and both files survive Save.

**Godot specifics:** Entirely `FileAccess`-free until Save, so the whole path is headlessly provable. The drop itself is Godot DnD (`_get_drag_data`/`_can_drop_data`/`_drop_data` on the folder pane's Tree, builder_folder_pane.gd:89-133) — `_can_drop_data` is the natural place to ALSO refuse visually, but the model-level refusal must exist regardless, because `place_module` is reachable from the card menu and from a replayed ledger entry too.

*critical · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:548-554 and :5699-5707; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1727-1757,1897, document/builder_workspace.gd:304-322, document/builder_tree.gd:111-139,205-218,227-249

### `ub-risk.focus-outliving-its-module` There is no focus rebind at all: delete the focused module and the window still names it to the status bar, the preview and the compile anchor

**Unity does:** UB-131/162/163/171: `RebindFocusIfMissing` (BuilderWindow.cs:1680) moves the focus to any live, non-deleted session, and an empty workspace CLEARS the focus so MountCanvas shows the empty state. It is called from six sites — after a ledger replay (:1503), after a deletion (:5813), after the empty-module settle (:5813 region), after journal restore (:860), and on both save paths (:6225, :6278) — and the ORDER is the rule: every model change lands FIRST, then the focus is validated, then the views refresh exactly once. UB-163's sequel is that tolerating a null focus at the LAYER (TryGet(null) answers NOT FOUND; one FocusFull accessor returning "" so "there is no focus" reads as "this is not the focused file") is what makes the rebind safe.

**Godot today:** absent. Grepping `rebind` over addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/ returns nothing, and `_focus_path` (builder_window.gd:131) is never cleared or re-pointed except by `select_module` (:2156), which early-returns on an empty path (:2152). So after `delete_module(_focus_path)` (:2414-2438) or an undone creation replayed through `_replay_change` (:2124-2128), `_focus_path` still names a module that has left the tree. Consequences, all live: `_refresh_status` (:2458) prints the deleted file name; `tick()` (:920) calls `preview.compile_dirty(_focus_path)` and `_restrict_to_focus_closure` (builder_preview.gd:322-324) early-returns because `by_path` has no such key, so the closure restriction — UB-158's cost control — is silently off; `_create_folder`/`create_module` (:1919) place new modules in the dead module's folder; and `_preview_pane` keeps the deleted module on stage forever (see the preview-anchor gap). The tolerance half IS done: `by_path`/`try_get` answer NOT FOUND for an empty path (builder_tree.gd:60-67, builder_workspace.gd:84-86) and the source pane clears itself (builder_source_pane.gd:159-162), so this does not crash — it goes quietly wrong.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: "There is no focus rebind at all" is a shade strong: two move routes DO maintain the focus across a path change — `move_folder` (builder_window.gd:1708-1709) and `_place_tree_in` (:2066-2067) both do `if Paths.same(_focus_path, from): _focus_path = module.file_path()`. What is absent is the MISSING-module rebind (delete, undone create, abort, journal restore). Note also that `place_module` (:1727-1748) is the third move route and does NOT repoint — so it produces a dangling focus by the move path too, which strengthens the gap rather than weakening it.

**To build:** Add `_rebind_focus_if_missing()` to builder_window.gd: if `workspace.try_get(_focus_path) == null`, pick the first module by sorted path and `select_module` it, or set `_focus_path = ""` and show the empty state when the tree is empty. Call it at the end of `delete_module`, at the end of `_replay` (after `reproject()`, before the panes refresh — the order is already right at :2105-2113), after `abort()`, and after `restore_recovery()`. Add an entry to `tests/builder_parity.gd` for it — there is none today, so the checklist does not even ask the question.

**Godot specifics:** `select_module` is already re-entrancy guarded by `_choosing` (:2153,2178), so calling it from the rebind is safe. The empty-focus case has to be handled without going through `select_module` (it refuses an empty path by design) — set `_focus_path = ""` directly and call `_sync_empty_state()` (:815-818) plus `_refresh_status()`. Headlessly testable in builder_chrome_test.gd, which already builds a real window with `_window()`.

### `ub-risk.focus-is-not-the-shown-file` The compile anchor and the shown file are one variable, and a failed mount still advances the pane's path — so editing a style freezes the component with a caption that lies

**Unity does:** UB-202, found by UB-201's trace on its first run after three wrong guesses: `BuilderPreviewPane.ShownFile` (Preview/BuilderPreviewPane.cs:813) becomes the anchor, and BuilderWindow.cs:4690 reads `string rendered = _previewPane?.ShownFile ?? _focusFile;` — the compile anchor, the assembly and the buffer text are ALL keyed on what is ON SCREEN, not on what is SELECTED. Clicking a style entry to edit it moves the FOCUS onto the style module while the preview goes on showing the component, and the batch is built around the component so the style edit lands live.

**Godot today:** wrong, with a second defect layered on it. builder_window.gd carries only `_focus_path` (:131); :920 compiles `preview.compile_dirty(_focus_path)` and :2172 shows `_preview_pane.show_module(_focus_path)` — the same variable does both jobs. Then builder_preview_pane.gd:148-176 `show_module` assigns `_path` and rebuilds the knobs BEFORE attempting the mount, and `builder_preview.mount` (builder_preview.gd:546-548) returns false without unmounting when the script has no `render`. So selecting a style companion leaves the component's nodes in `_slot`, and the very next branch — `if _slot.get_child_count() > 0` (:169-171) — claims "last good render — the current edit does not build yet" and returns. The `_module_note` branch two lines below (:173-178), whose whole purpose is to say "this module has no component to render", is unreachable once anything has ever rendered, and `mount`'s own comment ("The pane shows the module's own note instead") describes behaviour that does not happen. Worse, the `compile_finished` re-show (builder_window.gd:741-742) re-calls `show_module(_preview_pane.path())` — the STYLE path — so the component on stage is never re-mounted against the rebuilt style: the pane freezes on the pre-edit render with the header reading `<MYSTYLE>` and the knobs showing the style's (empty) props. UB-202's exact symptom, "looks exactly like 'the edit did nothing'". The compiler half is correct — `_restrict_to_focus_closure` seeds the importers for a non-component focus (builder_preview.gd:333-338, UB-190) — so the component IS being rebuilt; only the pane never picks it up.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: The requested/shown split already half-exists one layer down: `RuitkBuilderPreview` tracks `_mounted_path` and exposes `mounted_path()` / `is_mounted()` (builder_preview.gd:552-560), set only on a successful mount. The pane and the window simply do not read it. That makes the fix smaller than the writeup implies — `shown_path()` can delegate to `preview.mounted_path()` rather than introducing a fourth path variable.

**To build:** Split requested from shown in builder_preview_pane.gd: keep `_path` for the request, add `_shown` set only when `preview.mount(...)` returns true, and expose `shown_path()`. Make `show_module` on a non-component NOT touch `_shown` and fall to `_module_note` (test `preview.has_render(preview.built_script(path))` before the child-count test, so the ordering defect goes away). Then anchor the round on the shown file: `preview.compile_dirty(_preview_pane.shown_path() if not empty else _focus_path)` at builder_window.gd:920, and have the `compile_finished` handler re-mount `shown_path()` rather than `path()`.

**Godot specifics:** `builder_preview_pane.gd` (402 lines) has ZERO test coverage — grepping `PreviewPane` over tests/ returns nothing — while tests/builder_parity.gd:88-92 answers UsageFor / ModuleInfoFor / BuildKnobs / state panel with identifiers that live in it. That is four green parity entries over an untested file, and this defect sits in the middle of them. The mount itself is `RuitkRoot.create(container, V.fc(...))` (builder_preview.gd:554), so the pane's nodes really are the reconciler's; clearing them means `unmount()`, which is exactly what the early `return false` skips.

*high · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:4690 and Builder/Editor/Preview/BuilderPreviewPane.cs:813; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:131,920,741-742,2172 and chrome/builder_preview_pane.gd:148-178, preview/builder_preview.gd:539-556

### `ub-risk.index-as-identity` _menu_row is a stale source SPAN carried across re-projection, and a second selection the canvas does not draw

**Unity does:** UB-170's two halves must both hold: nodes are built from a SORTED list so numbering only moves when membership does, and no callback carries a position across a render — the card menu carries the module PATH and the host resolves it when the menu opens. UB-168 is the same one layer up (`OnPick = () => RequestDeleteCard(index)` captured at menu-open time and run later). UB-170 records what was deliberately left index-based — onSelect/setSelected — precisely because their staleness is COSMETIC; the destructive paths were converted.

**Godot today:** partial: the card path is fixed, the row path is not. Card ordering is sorted by `Paths.key(file_path)` with the reason stated (builder_graph_service.gd:49-55) and `_open_card_menu(file_path, at)` resolves index→path at menu-open time (builder_window.gd:701-705, :2193). But `_menu_row` (builder_window.gd:102) stores a live `Graph.Line` object holding `at`/`end_at` CHARACTER OFFSETS, and `Edits.remove` cuts by exactly those (builder_edits.gd:175-182). `_after_model_change` (:880-893) calls `Service.populate_card`, which mints entirely new Line objects — and nothing invalidates `_menu_row`. Click a row, type in the source pane, press Delete: the cut lands on a span the buffer no longer has. Second, independent defect: `RuitkBuilderCanvasHost.select_card` clears the canvas's own row selection (builder_canvas_host.gd:135-144, "EXACTLY ONE THING IS SELECTED AT A TIME") but `_menu_row` survives, so after clicking card B the canvas draws no row selection while Delete still acts on a row in card A (`_menu_target`, set at :1016, is A). The window has two selection stores and only one of them is singular.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: "Nothing invalidates `_menu_row`" is inaccurate — three paths do: `_delete_selection` after a successful row delete (:276), `_cancel_active_edit` (:292), and the `_inline.cancelled` handler (:690-692), whose comment states the reason exactly ("leaving `_menu_row` pointing at a row after the user pressed Escape means the next Delete acts on a row they walked away from"). The seeded-wrap flow at :1595-1614 also deliberately re-resolves the Line from the FRESH projection, with the comment "the `Line` objects this function started with belong to the old projection and carry offsets the buffer no longer has" — i.e. the hazard is already understood in one place. The gap is that the same re-resolution was never applied to the two remaining routes: after `_after_model_change`, and on card selection.

**To build:** Stop storing the Line. Store `(_menu_target, section, row_index)` and re-resolve through `_row_of(card_index, section, row_index)` — which already exists (builder_window.gd:1002-1008 region) — at the moment the action runs, exactly as `_open_card_menu` does for cards. Clear the row selection wherever the canvas clears its own: hook `card_selected` (:681) and `select_card` to null `_menu_row`, or better, read the selection from `_canvas.selected_row_section`/`selected_row_index` so there is only one store. `_delete_selection` should refuse and toast when the resolved row comes back null rather than falling through to the module.

**Godot specifics:** The canvas is a `.guitkx` view (canvas_view.guitkx) rendered by this reconciler, and rows are keyed elements (`key={ str(row.at) }`, canvas_view.guitkx:186,203,222) — so a keyed PanelContainer genuinely survives a re-render while the Line behind it is replaced, which is the Godot spelling of UB-170's "a lambda living on a KEYED element". tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:1059-1060 manually sets `w._menu_row = null` before exercising the module fall-through, so the suite documents the trap as intended behaviour instead of catching it.

### `ub-risk.layout-repath-passengers-and-drivers` layout.repath is dead in practice — reproject() reloads the layout from disk and discards the re-keying, and rename/place call it not at all

**Unity does:** UB-220/UB-221. `BuilderCanvasHost.RepathLayout` (Canvas/BuilderCanvasHost.cs:940-947) re-keys the config AND WRITES IT IMMEDIATELY, and the comment says why in as many words: "the canvas remounts straight after a rename and reloads the config from disk, so an in-memory re-keying alone would be thrown away. This is UserSettings state, not project content, so it is outside the save-only contract." It is called for the folder move and the file move and for both directions of undo/redo (BuilderWindow.cs:629, :3698, :3702, :5750, :6218), and the placement pass snapshots where every module sat BEFORE the pass and reconciles afterwards so passengers and drivers are both answered (:5726-5753).

**Godot today:** wrong, and hollow. `RuitkBuilderCanvasLayout.repath` (builder_canvas_layout.gd:180-217) is correct in itself — it re-keys positions, moves the root, retires the outgrown file — and it has exactly ONE production call site, builder_window.gd:1707 inside `move_folder`. Eight lines later `reproject()` (:1714) runs, and `reproject` reassigns `layout = CanvasLayout.for_graph(graph)` (:825), which reads a fresh object off disk. The mutation is thrown away, verbatim the thing the Unity comment warns about. Nothing calls `layout.save()` between the two — `_capture_layout()` fires only on a card drag (:1033) and on Save (:1978). `_rename_to` (:1897-1917) and `place_module` (:1727-1748) call `repath` at all. So renaming the folder-owning component changes `root_path`, `_rel_key` is computed against the new `root_dir` (builder_canvas_layout.gd:229-234), every stored key misses, and every card the user placed falls to its seeded slot — UB-220's "exactly one card keeps its place and the rest sit in a column". And because `_retired` (:48) is only populated by `repath`, the outgrown layout file is never deleted, so stale layouts accumulate for the by-membership scan to keep finding — UB-185's 35-files symptom.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One mitigating detail the plan should know: `for_graph` tries `load_for_members` BEFORE `load_for_root` (builder_canvas_layout.gd:99-110), so for a move that leaves most member paths untouched the saved file is still found by membership overlap and only the moved card loses its slot. The catastrophic "every card falls to a seeded column" case is specifically the folder-owning / root rename, where every member path changes at once and overlap drops to zero — which is precisely the case `repath` is never called for. So the symptom is narrower than 'the layout is lost on any move', and the fix priority is `_rename_to` first.

**To build:** Make repath persist: either add a `repath_and_save()` that calls `save(...)` immediately (matching the Unity contract that layout is user settings, outside save-only), or stop `reproject()` from re-reading — carry the live layout forward when its `root_path` still matches. Then call it from `_rename_to` (both the folder move when `owns_folder()` and the file move), from `place_module`, from `_place_tree_in`, and from `_replay_change`'s MOVE branch in both directions. Use the UB-220 snapshot shape in the batch loops: record `module.file_path()` for EVERY module before the pass and reconcile after, so passengers get told too — the current loop at :1703-1707 reads `from` per-iteration, which is already the same string as `to` for anything a parent carried.

**Godot specifics:** The layout lives under `user://ruitk_builder/layouts` (builder_canvas_layout.gd:27), outside the project, so writing it on a rename is cheap and touches nothing Godot imports — the save-only contract genuinely does not cover it. tests/builder_canvas_test.gd:508-545 drives `Layout.repath` directly and passes, which is precisely why this is green: the unit is right and the wiring is dead. A test at the WINDOW level (rename the root component, assert `layout.positions` still resolves the other cards) is what would have caught it.

### `ub-risk.rename-is-not-in-the-ledger` A rename performs four coordinated edits and records none of them — Ctrl+Z cannot reverse it

**Unity does:** BuilderWindow.cs:3774-3788: the rename opens a ledger scope, calls MoveModule, records `_ledger.RecordMove(full, newFull)`, then records every import rewrite ReconcileImports produced, then closes the scope — one entry for what the register calls "four edits that land together or not at all: the export, the file, the folder when the module owns one, and every importer's specifier". UB-220 depends on it ("for both directions of undo and redo, so the layout follows a rename out and back").

**Godot today:** absent. builder_window.gd:1897-1917 `_rename_to` calls `workspace.move_to(...)`, throws away the returned rewrites, calls `reproject()` and `select_module(...)` — with no `ledger.begin`, no `record_move`, no `ledger.record` for the rewrites. `RuitkBuilderLedger.record_move` exists (builder_ledger.gd:219-231) and `_replay_change` handles `ChangeKind.MOVE` (builder_window.gd:2131-2133), so the machinery is complete and the rename is the one structural gesture that does not use it. The only `record_move` call site in production is `place_module` (:1741). Practical result: rename a component, then Ctrl+Z — the history walks past the rename to some earlier text edit and re-applies it against a tree whose paths have changed underneath, and the rename itself is unreachable from the history menu (`_show_history`, :154-172) because it never became an entry.

**To build:** Wrap `_rename_to` the way `place_module` is wrapped: `ledger.begin("Rename %s to %s")`, `var snapshot := workspace.capture_imports()`, `workspace.move_to(...)`, `ledger.record_move(old_path, new_path)`, record every rewrite from `workspace.reconcile_imports(snapshot)`, `ledger.end()` — noting that `move_to` already reconciles internally (builder_workspace.gd:339-345), so either record the rewrites it returns or hoist the capture/reconcile out as `place_module` does. Add a before/after case to tests/builder_edits_test.gd: rename, undo, assert both the path and every importer's specifier are back.

**Godot specifics:** `Ledger.begin`/`end` collapse nested scopes into the outermost (builder_ledger.gd:139-160), so wrapping `_rename_to` cannot double-record even though `move_to` may itself be re-entered. `_replay_change` resolves modules by IDENTITY first (`workspace.by_id(change.module_id)`, :2118-2120), which is exactly what makes a replayed rename safe — the mechanism is waiting for a caller.

### `ub-risk.journal-written-never-offered` The crash journal is captured every five seconds and never offered — the only recovery under the save-only contract has no caller, and the parity gate is green over it

**Unity does:** UB-173/the save-only contract's insurance. BuilderWindow.cs:149 hooks `UnityEditor.EditorApplication.delayCall += OfferJournalRestore` on construction; OfferJournalRestore (:6255-6275) peeks the journal, asks, and either restores or clears. Capture runs on a timer (:6244-6249). The offer is the point — the journal exists only while there is unsaved work, so "the file being there means exactly one thing and the offer needs no other evidence".

**Godot today:** half built. `_journal_tick` (builder_window.gd:933-943) writes the whole tree every 5000 ms, and `RuitkBuilderJournal` (document/builder_journal.gd) is complete and correct — `peek`, `try_restore`, `clear`, and a projection that travels with the modules so a restored delete stays deleted (:117-124). But `pending_recovery`, `restore_recovery` and `discard_recovery` (builder_window.gd:946-965) have ZERO callers anywhere in the repository; grepping all of addons/ and tests/ finds only tests/builder_parity.gd:111 naming `func pending_recovery`. plugin.gd never asks after `_open_builder` (:422-446). So the journal is written on every session, is never read back, and the recovery path has never once run outside builder_save_test.gd's direct calls to the Journal class. Meanwhile `_disable_plugin` (plugin.gd:162-164) `queue_free()`s the window — "takes the builder with it" — with no prompt and no consultation of `dirty_changed`, which also has no listener (builder_window.gd:52, emitted at :2472, subscribed nowhere).

**To build:** Call `pending_recovery()` from `_open_builder` after the window is constructed and before `open_tree`, and put up a ConfirmationDialog naming `modules` and `saved_at` — restore on accept, `discard_recovery()` on decline. It has to be deferred a frame (the window is popped up in the same call), which is Godot's analogue of Unity's `delayCall`. Separately, connect `dirty_changed` in plugin.gd so the Window title carries the unsaved marker and `close_requested` can ask before hiding. Then FIX THE PARITY ENTRY: `["OfferJournalRestore", "func pending_recovery"]` is answered by a function with no caller — change the token to something only the wiring can satisfy, or add a headless assertion that the plugin calls it.

**Godot specifics:** Godot has no domain reload, so the journal's only job is a crash, a kill, or the plugin being disabled/reloaded — all of which free the Window. `EditorInterface.get_base_control()` is the dialog's parent (plugin.gd:437 already uses it for the Window), and the offer must survive a headless run gracefully: `Journal.peek()` is pure `FileAccess` on `user://`, so the model half stays testable; only the dialog needs an editor.

### `ub-risk.empty-module-is-a-broken-file` An emptied module ALREADY ON DISK is skipped by Save with a console warning — the emptying, and any rename pending on it, are discarded

**Unity does:** UB-206/UB-112/UB-149. `ResolveEmptyModules` (BuilderWindow.cs:5771-5815) runs BEFORE anything is written and is a blocking three-way dialog naming every empty module: "Delete them" / "Cancel save" / "Save anyway". Cancel aborts the whole save (:5867 gates on its return). "Delete them" goes through the ordinary deletion path — `StripReferencesTo`, `_ledger.RecordDeletion`, `_workspace.Delete`, then `RebindFocusIfMissing` — "which is what would have prevented the second error too", the second error being the wave of unused-import diagnostics in every importer.

**Godot today:** partial, and the residual half is the destructive one. builder_workspace.gd:507-510 `if _is_blank(module): continue` — placed BEFORE the `has_moved()` branch and before `mark_projected(target)`. For a never-saved module that is right and matches Unity's intent. For a module that is ALREADY ON DISK and has just been emptied, it is wrong three ways: the old disk content stays, the emptying is silently not written, the module keeps `disk_path` so the projection loop (:539-543) still claims the path and it is never orphaned — and any PENDING RENAME on that module is skipped with it, permanently, because the move branch is downstream of the `continue`. builder_window.gd:1969-1973 logs a console WARNING and lets the save proceed; the save then reports success. The warning is transient: `Console.report` clears `_rows`/`_list` at the top of every round (builder_console.gd:99-100), so the next compile erases it. There is no cancel, no delete offer, and no reference stripping — so an importer of a never-written blank still gets an unresolved import (GUITKX2305) at the next real compile.

**To build:** Move the question in front of the write, as Unity does. In `builder_window.save()`, before `workspace.save_all()`, if `workspace.blank_modules()` is non-empty put up a ConfirmationDialog (Godot has no three-button DisplayDialogComplex — use a ConfirmationDialog with a custom third button via `add_button`) naming each file: Delete them / Cancel save / Save anyway. "Delete them" must run through `delete_module` so `referrers_to` refuses or the imports are dealt with, and must land in one ledger entry. Distinguish the two cases in the workspace: `_is_blank(module) and not module.is_on_disk()` is the harmless skip; `_is_blank(module) and module.is_on_disk()` is a user decision and must not be silently dropped.

**Godot specifics:** GUITKX0303 (a directive body cannot be empty) and the compiler's own top-level-declaration requirement are the Godot spelling of Unity's CS1029 — a blank `.guitkx` is a file the compiler rejects, so writing one really does break the sweep. The dialog needs a real `Window`, but `blank_modules()` and the on-disk/never-saved split are pure model and belong in builder_save_test.gd's disk-state matrix, which already asserts exact bytes after Save.

### `ub-risk.place-tree-undo-half-reverts` 'Place the tree' records no moves and loses the rewrites its own inner reconciles already made, so undoing it leaves modules at their new paths with the old specifiers

**Unity does:** BuilderWindow.cs:5731-5738: the placement loop records EVERY rewrite each `PlaceAt` returns into the open ledger scope — `foreach (var rewrite in rewrites) _ledger.Record(rewrite.FilePath, rewrite.Before, rewrite.After)` — so the entry holds the complete before/after set whatever order the tree hands modules back. UB-193 states the surrounding rule: when a batch re-files every module individually, the imports must be captured ONCE around the whole batch, because "reconciling per move would re-spell specifiers against a half-moved tree, each pass correct about a state nobody ever sees".

**Godot today:** wrong on both halves. builder_window.gd:2059-2072 `_place_tree_in` opens `ledger.begin("Place the tree")`, takes an outer `capture_imports()` snapshot, then calls `workspace.move_to(...)` per module — and `move_to` runs its OWN `capture_imports`/`reconcile_imports` internally (builder_workspace.gd:339-345), rewriting importer buffers mid-batch and returning rewrites the loop discards. At the end the outer `reconcile_imports(snapshot)` re-derives the final spelling; for any importer an inner pass already brought to that spelling, `_rewrite_specifiers` finds nothing to change, returns "", and the rewrite is skipped (builder_workspace.gd:412-419) — so it is never recorded. No `ledger.record_move` is emitted for any module either. The entry therefore holds a PARTIAL set of text edits and zero moves: Ctrl+Z after placing a new tree reverts the recorded importers to their provisional-root specifiers, leaves the unrecorded ones alone, and leaves every module at its real path. The tree is then internally inconsistent, dirty, and the next Save writes it.

**To build:** Record the inner rewrites — `for rewrite in workspace.move_to(...)` inside the loop, exactly as `move_folder` does at :1710-1712 — or hoist the reconcile out of `_move` for batch callers so there is only one pass. Emit `ledger.record_move(from, module.file_path())` for each placed module. And take the UB-220 snapshot (`was_at[module] = module.file_path()` before the pass) so the layout repath and the focus repoint answer for passengers too. Same treatment for `move_folder` (:1699-1716), which records the outer rewrites but no moves.

**Godot specifics:** `_replay_change` (builder_window.gd:2117-2133) already handles MOVE in both directions via `move_to_path`, and resolves by `module_id` first, so a recorded move replays correctly — the entry just has none to replay. Nothing here touches disk (the placement is model-only until Save), so the whole matrix is headlessly assertable in builder_save_test.gd alongside the existing abort/undo cases.

### `ub-risk.derived-root-as-a-persistence-key` A second root definition survives: tree_root() picks the shallowest folder by STRING LENGTH and drives create placement, while the graph's root comes from the predicate walk

**Unity does:** UB-185/189/221. The root is the module that owns the tree's ROOT FOLDER, found by the same folder walk the loader uses so it gives the same answer from any module in the tree; the walk takes a PREDICATE for its one question so the graph can answer from the MODULES while the loader answers from disk; and `LoadForMember` was REMOVED rather than left beside `LoadForMembers` — "two lookups that can disagree is how this went wrong once already" (Canvas/BuilderCanvasConfig.cs:58,101; Document/BuilderTree.cs:309).

**Godot today:** partial — the good one exists and a second one sits beside it. `RuitkBuilderTree.resolve_root_from` (builder_tree.gd:296-345) is the predicate-parameterised walk with the disk and model answers separated and the shared-`components` hazard gated on the grandparent; it feeds `graph.root_path` (builder_graph_service.gd:77) and therefore the layout key. But builder_window.gd:1816-1826 `tree_root()` is an independent heuristic: the shallowest module folder BY `folder.length()`. Two ways it disagrees. (a) `load_tree` deliberately pulls in modules whose imports LEAVE the root (builder_workspace.gd:157-166), so a shared module one folder over gives `tree_root()` a shorter string and every create from the empty canvas (`_create_folder`, :1864,:1867) is placed OUTSIDE the tree. (b) Length is not depth: `res://a/bbbbbbbbbbbb` (depth 2) loses to `res://zz/yy/xx` (depth 3). tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:1097 pins the length heuristic as the intended answer, so the gate defends the divergence.

**To build:** Delete `tree_root()` and answer from the one walk: `BuilderTree.resolve_root_from(workspace.modules(), _focus_path).get_base_dir()`, or read `graph.root_path.get_base_dir()` when a graph exists. Fix the test at builder_chrome_test.gd:1097 to assert the walk's answer, and add the fixture UB-189's test used — a tree with a member outside the root folder — so the disagreement is pinned rather than the heuristic.

**Godot specifics:** `resolve_root_from` takes a `Callable` predicate and is a static on a preloaded const — callable from the window with no class-cache exposure. Both answers are pure string/model work, so the disagreement is provable headlessly with a fixture that has an out-of-root import target.

### `ub-risk.keyboard-model-unroutable` The keyboard model needs focus the canvas can never take, and the typing guard kills Ctrl+S and Ctrl+Z along with Delete

**Unity does:** UB-74 guards Delete/Escape while a text surface holds focus. UB-82 is the sequel and the warning: "that guard was self-defeating for a while — a KeyDownEvent goes to the FOCUSED element and nothing in the canvas was focusable, so Delete could only ever fire while a TextField held focus, which is exactly when the guard suppressed it." The fix was to make the canvas focusable so the key can reach the window in a state the guard permits.

**Godot today:** the same trap, unaddressed and untested. `builder_window._gui_input` (builder_window.gd:226-253) only runs when the window Control is in the focus chain — Godot delivers a key to the focused Control and bubbles up its ancestors. `RuitkBuilderCanvasHost` sets `mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` (builder_canvas_host.gd:91) and never sets `focus_mode`, so it stays FOCUS_NONE: clicking a card consumes the press and moves key focus NOWHERE. `plugin.gd:422-446` `_open_builder` never calls `grab_focus` (only `open_builder_on` does, :455), so a builder opened from the menu has no focus owner at all and the entire keyboard model is inert until the user clicks a Button or the source editor. Worse, `_typing_focused()` (:255-260) gates the WHOLE model including the Ctrl branch — so with the caret in the source pane's CodeEdit, which is where a user spends most of their time, Ctrl+S does nothing and the only Save is the toolbar button. Unity's guard covers Delete/Escape only.

**Correction from the adversarial pass** — this supersedes the headline and the paragraph above: One factual amendment: the window Control IS already focusable — builder_window.gd:139 `focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_ALL` with the comment "Focusable, or the window never sees a key at all". So half of UB-82's fix is in; what is missing is the CANVAS being focusable, which is what makes a canvas click land focus somewhere `_gui_input` can bubble from and simultaneously makes `_typing_focused()` read false in the state Delete is meant for. Phrase the work item as 'the canvas is the unfocusable link', not 'nothing is focusable'.

**To build:** Give the canvas host `focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_ALL` and `grab_focus()` on its own mouse-press handler (builder_canvas_host.gd:379+ already accepts the event), so a canvas click puts focus somewhere the window's `_gui_input` can bubble from — and so `_typing_focused()` reads false in exactly the state Delete is meant to work in. Call `_builder.grab_focus()` from `_open_builder` too. Narrow `_typing_focused()` to the Delete/Escape branch and let Ctrl+S/Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y through unconditionally (the CodeEdit's own Ctrl+Z will win inside it because it accepts the event first, which is the correct precedence).

**Godot specifics:** This is pure Godot input routing and cannot be proved by any existing gate: tests/builder_chrome_test.gd calls `w._delete_selection()` and `editor._gui_input(escape)` DIRECTLY (:760,:923,:1054), and addons/ruitk_builder_shots/plugin.gd — whose own comment at :104 says "every headless check of these passes, because a headless check calls `_gui_input` directly" — pushes only mouse gestures (pan, wheel, card menu, chip, DnD, row click, card drag; :134-347). No keyboard gesture is driven at the real Window anywhere. The shots rig is where a Delete/Ctrl+S/Escape case belongs.

### `ub-risk.delete-by-keypress-with-a-fallthrough` UB-87's three compounding factors are all present: a never-cleared card focus, a row selection nulled after a row delete, and no confirmation on the keyboard path

**Unity does:** UB-87 (CRITICAL): `DeleteSelection` falls back to the CARD selection when no row is selected, and deleting a card deletes a FILE. Three individually harmless facts compounded — the card selection is never empty, deleting a row clears the row selection so the SECOND press escalates, and a keypress carries no confirmation where a menu click at least names the file. The first fix put the confirmation in `RequestDeleteCard`, the SHARED guard, so the menu path was covered too; UB-88 then superseded it by moving the deletion behind the save-only contract and putting the confirmation ONTO Save, "the moment it stops being reversible".

**Godot today:** the mechanism is reproduced verbatim; only UB-88's contract keeps it from being data loss. `_delete_selection` (builder_window.gd:269-279): with `_menu_row` null it runs `delete_module(_focus_path)`; line 276 nulls `_menu_row` after a row delete (factor 2); `_focus_path` is set by every `select_module` (:2156) and never cleared (factor 1); `delete_module` (:2414-2438) has no prompt on any path (factor 3). Two Delete presses remove an element and then the whole file. The mitigations are real and worth stating: the delete is a tree removal recorded with the module itself (`ledger.record_deletion(file_path, module)`, :2433) so Ctrl+Z restores it; `referrers_to` refuses while anything imports it (:2422-2429) with a naming toast; and `_confirmed_deletions` (:1989-2013) names every file at Save. What is missing relative to Unity is the shared-guard confirmation and, more importantly, the ROW selection being a second store the canvas does not draw — see the _menu_row gap, which makes the first of the two presses land in a file the user is not looking at.

**To build:** Do not re-add a per-keypress modal — UB-88 explicitly dissolved that. Do three cheaper things: toast on the module fall-through naming the file ("Deleted Card.guitkx — Ctrl+Z to put it back, applies on Save"), so a keypress is never silent; resolve the row selection from the canvas rather than from `_menu_row` so "nothing selected" is a state the user can see; and rebind the focus after `delete_module` so the second press cannot address a module that is already gone.

**Godot specifics:** tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:1059 sets `w._menu_row = null` by hand before asserting the fall-through, so the suite pins the escalation as intended rather than testing the two-press sequence. A real test is `_on_row_clicked(...)` → `_delete_selection()` → `_delete_selection()` and assert the module survives.

### `ub-risk.card-new-moves-focus-without-the-panes` _on_card_new reassigns _focus_path outside select_module, so a cancelled create leaves the focus pointing where nothing is shown

**Unity does:** UB-131/163's ordering rule: the focus is a single fact validated after every model change, and "BIRTH LOCATION FOLLOWS WHERE YOU RIGHT-CLICKED, NEVER WHAT IS FOCUSED" (capability reference §5) is achieved by passing the menu TARGET into the create, not by moving the focus onto it. Unity's `ShowCreatePrompt` takes `Target` explicitly (BuilderWindow.cs:6065, `name => ValidateNewName(kind, name, Target)`).

**Godot today:** divergent-defect. builder_window.gd:1650-1654 `_on_card_new` does `_focus_path = _menu_target` and then `prompt_create(kind)` — a direct write that bypasses `select_module` (:2150-2176) and therefore updates no pane: the source pane, folder pane, library selection and preview all still show the previous module. If the prompt is CANCELLED, that state persists: `_refresh_status` will name one file, the panes show another, and `tick()`'s `preview.compile_dirty(_focus_path)` anchors the closure on the module the user right-clicked rather than the one on screen — the same shape as the preview-anchor gap, arrived at by a different route. The comment in `_create_folder` (:1856-1862) explains precisely why placement must not follow the focus, and then `_on_card_new` moves the focus to make placement work.

**To build:** Delete the assignment. `_create_folder` already reads `_menu_target` (:1862) — it never needed `_focus_path` — so `_on_card_new` should be `if _menu_target.is_empty(): return` then `prompt_create(kind)`. Nothing else in the create path reads `_focus_path` except `create_module` (:1919), which has no callers.

**Godot specifics:** `select_module` is the single funnel for focus and is `_choosing`-guarded (:2153) — every other focus move goes through it. This is the one raw write, and it is the one that leaves the window inconsistent.

*medium · logic · CONFIRMED* — unity ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:6065 (Target passed, focus untouched); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1650-1654 vs :1856-1875 and :2150-2176

### `ub-risk.folder-ownership-by-name-alone` owns_folder() excludes only STYLE and HOOK, and the file suffix cannot tell a util or value module from a component

**Unity does:** UB-142: only a PLAIN module file can own a folder; a companion never does, and "the kind test comes before the name test". The near-miss was catastrophic precisely because UB-135 had just made a folder-owning rename really move the folder — renaming `Showcase.style.uitkx` in `Showcase/` would have taken the whole component subtree, every sub-component included.

**Godot today:** the STYLE/HOOK half is done and well reasoned; the kind system underneath cannot express the rest. `RuitkBuilderModule.owns_folder` (builder_module.gd:113-118) returns false for STYLE and HOOK first, with the reasoning restated verbatim. But `Module.kind_of` (:211-212) derives the kind from the FILE SUFFIX, and `suffix_for` (:157-164) maps UTIL, VALUE, MODULE and COMPONENT all to plain `.guitkx` (Paths.SUFFIX_PLAIN) — so a module created through `prompt_create(Kind.UTIL)` is reloaded from disk as a COMPONENT, and while it is still in memory as UTIL it can own a folder. Downstream, `can_create_at` (builder_window.gd:1838-1848) gates the create submenu on `kind == COMPONENT`, `_validate_name` (:1791-1796) demands PascalCase for COMPONENT and camelCase otherwise, and `_restrict_to_focus_closure`'s non-component importer seed (builder_preview.gd:333-338) keys on the same field — all three change answer for the same file across a save-and-reload. The path-collision guard mostly masks the folder-ownership half (a util and a component of the same name in one folder collide on `Paths.key`, which is case-folded), so the severity is low, not the mechanism's absence.

**To build:** Either give UTIL/VALUE a real file marker so `kind_of` can round-trip them, or make the in-memory kind for a plain `.guitkx` be decided by the same analysis the graph already runs (`analyzed_decls` — builder_graph_service.gd already classifies declarations for badges) rather than by the create prompt. In the meantime, restrict `owns_folder()` to `kind == Kind.COMPONENT` explicitly rather than excluding two kinds, so it means what UB-142 says it means.

**Godot specifics:** The declaration-level kinds (UTIL/VALUE/MODULE) and the file-level ones (COMPONENT/HOOK/STYLE) share one enum by deliberate design (builder_module.gd:34-48 explains why), and this is the cost of that: a value that means one thing to the suffix splitter and another to the graph. Any fix has to keep the two layers' answers reconciled or the badge and the suffix drift, which is the thing the shared enum exists to prevent.
