### `ub-risk.unwired-second-routes` create_module and dirty_changed exist, are reachable, and are wired to nothing — the class of gap the parity gate was written to catch

**Unity does:** Not a Unity defect — a Godot-side instance of the pattern tests/builder_parity.gd:9-15 names as the reason it exists: "most of it was a mechanism that already existed with nothing wired to it: a drop handler with no drag, a layout store with no way to move a card, an entry_activated nobody listened to, a provisional root the create flow never used."

**Godot today:** two more of them. `create_module(kind)` (builder_window.gd:1919-1931) is a full second creation route — it auto-names via `_unused_name`, records a creation, reprojects and selects — and has zero callers; every create in the UI goes through `prompt_create` → `_create_named`. It bypasses `_validate_name` entirely, including the whole-tree component-name rule (UB-211) that `_validate_name` implements at :1806-1809, so if anything ever wires it up it will mint duplicate component exports. `dirty_changed` (:52, emitted at :2470-2472) has no subscriber anywhere: plugin.gd:435 connects `close_requested` to a bare `hide()` and the Window title is a constant (:430), so the host has no idea whether the session holds unsaved work.

**To build:** Delete `create_module` or route it through `_validate_name`; connect `dirty_changed` in plugin.gd to stamp the Window title ("RUITK Builder •") and to gate a close prompt. Both are five-line changes; the value is that neither is left as a live second path into the model, which is the shape every entry in the parity gate's preamble has.

**Godot specifics:** `dirty_changed` is emitted from `_refresh_status`, which runs on every model change, so the wiring is free. The Window is created lazily in `_open_builder` and kept between openings (plugin.gd:419-437), which is exactly why the title matters — a hidden window holding a dirty tree is invisible until someone reopens it.

*low · risk · CONFIRMED* — unity ruitk-unity/Plans~/UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md (the recurring 'missing owner' shape, UB-136) and tests/builder_parity.gd:9-15 stating the pattern; godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:52,1919-1931,2470-2472, addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/plugin.gd:430-435

## Leads from the adversarial pass, adjudicated

The 78 gaps the skeptics noticed while trying to refute the register have now been through refutation themselves: **72 confirmed, 4 overstated, 2 refuted**. The refuted ones are listed too, so nobody re-finds them.

A separate critic found that at least fifteen of these restate a gap already in the register above. They are not re-deduplicated here — check the gap list before adding one to a backlog.

- **Lead 13 (batch position 13): "Opening the builder on another file DESTROYS the open session's unsaved work, with no veto, no prompt and no toast — the one guard Unity wrote a paragraph about"** *(critical · CONFIRMED)* — No guard exists on the reachable path. `open_tree` (chrome/builder_window.gd:749-774) calls `workspace.load_tree(focus_path)` at :764 unconditionally and `ledger.clear()` at :766, with no check for an already-loaded file and no `has_unsaved_changes()` test anywhere in it. A repo-wide grep for `has_unsaved_changes` under builder/ returns only four sites — the 5s journal tick (chrome/builder_window.gd:937), the status line (:2447), `Journal.capture`'s own early-out (document/builder_journal.gd:41) and the definition (document/builder_workspace.gd:94) — none of them a load guard. The bypass is real and is the advertised route: `_open_builder` protects itself with `if _builder.focus_path().is_empty()` (plugin.gd:444), but `open_builder_on` (plugin.gd:451-455) calls `_open_builder()` and then `_builder.open_tree(file_path)` unconditionally, and it is wired straight to the FileSystem dock context item at plugin.gd:88-92 via `_builder_context.open_requested.connect(open_builder_on)`. So 'Open in RUITK Builder' on any .guitkx replaces the whole in-memory tree and clears the history that could walk it back. (chrome/builder_window.gd:764 `workspace.load_tree(focus_path)` and :766 `ledger.clear()` with no preceding guard; plugin.gd:451-455 `func open_builder_on(...): _open_builder(); if _builder != null and not file_path.is_empty(): _builder.open_tree(file_path)`; plugin.gd:91 `_builder_context.open_requested.connect(open_builder_on)`.)
- **Lead 69 (batch position 69): "One editor for every module means ONE undo stack: Ctrl+Z in the source pane after switching modules overwrites the focused module's buffer with a DIFFERENT module's whole text"** *(critical · CONFIRMED)* — Every mechanical precondition is in the code, and the addon's own sibling surface shows the fix it was missing. The pane holds a single `_editor: GuitkxEditor` built once in `_init` (chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:34, 101-118); `show_module` swaps modules by assigning `_editor.text = module.buffer_text` (:151) and NEVER calls `clear_undo_history()`. A grep for `clear_undo_history` across the whole editor addon returns exactly two hits, both in the OTHER surface — editor/guitkx_editor_view.gd:426 (`_reload_editor`) and :578 (`_load_text`) — and that surface also keeps one editor PER PATH via `_ensure_editor(path)`. So the main-screen view solves this two ways and the builder pane does neither. Godot's `TextEdit.set_text` records a complex undo operation while undo is enabled (nothing here disables it — no `undo_enabled` write exists anywhere in the addon), so the swap itself is an undoable step and one Ctrl+Z restores the previous module's whole text. The write-through then lands unguarded: `_on_text_changed` (:172-185) calls `workspace.apply_edit(_path, after)`, `Workspace.apply_edit` only looks the module up and delegates (document/builder_workspace.gd:290-298), and `Module.apply_edit` checks only `read_only` and CR normalization before `buffer_text = new_text_lf` (document/builder_module.gd:256-264). The parse gate the lead says is absent really is absent from this path — `Compiler.compile` is called only in the pane's explicit `apply_edit()` button handler (chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:214-216), which `_on_text_changed` never reaches. Note this is NOT the documented CodeField.cs divergence: reusing `guitkx_code_edit.gd` is the agreed decision, but failing to clear its undo history on a module swap is a wiring defect in that reuse, and the same file's sibling consumer already does it right. (chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:151 `_editor.text = module.buffer_text` in `show_module` with no `clear_undo_history()`; editor/guitkx_editor_view.gd:425-426 `ed.text = text` / `ed.clear_undo_history()` and :577-578 the same pair; document/builder_module.gd:256-264 `apply_edit` — read_only and CR checks only, then `buffer_text = new_text_lf`.)
- **A folder drag that lands on a component-owned folder bypasses the ledger entirely -- the move is NOT undoable, and read-only does not stop it** *(critical · CONFIRMED)* — `move_folder`'s owner-delegation branch is `for module in workspace.modules(): if module.owns_folder() and Paths.same(module.folder, source): return _move_one(module, target_folder, leaf)` (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1681-1683), and `_move_one` (:1751-1757) is only `workspace.place_at` + `reproject()` + `toast()` — no `ledger.begin`, no `ledger.record_move`, no `capture_imports`/`reconcile_imports`, no `layout.repath`, no `preview.request_refresh()`, no `_source.refresh_from_model()`. The non-owner branch immediately below does all of it (`ledger.begin` :1698, `capture_imports` :1699, `layout.repath` :1706, `reconcile_imports`→`ledger.record` :1710-1712, `ledger.end` :1713, `preview.request_refresh` :1715). All four sub-claims hold: (a) `Workspace.place_at` (document/builder_workspace.gd:308-312) guards only `module == null` and tree membership, while `move_to` (:321-325) has `if module == null or module.read_only: return []` — and the owner branch runs BEFORE `move_folder`'s own read-only loop (:1686-1694), so a read-only owner is re-filed silently; (b) `layout.repath` is genuinely absent from `_move_one`; (c) `workspace.changed` has no subscriber anywhere under builder/ (only `ledger.changed` is connected, builder_window.gd:731), so nothing else nudges the preview. The Unity reference makes the divergence explicit: `MoveFolderToFolder` delegates to `MoveModuleToFolder` (BuilderWindow.cs:599), and that method is the FULL operation — read-only refusal at :530-534, occupied-path refusal at :550-553, `_ledger.Begin` at :555, `_ledger.RecordMove` at :562, `_ledger.End` at :563, then `RefreshHistoryPanel/RefreshChrome/MountCanvas/_folderPane.Rebuild` at :564-567. (builder_window.gd:1681-1683 (`return _move_one(module, target_folder, leaf)`) and :1751-1757 (`_move_one` = place_at + reproject + toast) against the correct non-owner path at :1698-1715; builder_workspace.gd:308-312 (place_at, no read_only guard) vs :321-325 (move_to, has one); ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:525-568 and :594-599.)
- **A component that owns its folder is FLATTENED when re-filed: the folder level is destroyed, companions collide in the destination, and owns_folder() flips to false (adversarial-pass lead #14)** *(critical · CONFIRMED)* — Reproduced headlessly against the real model layer. `place_at` (builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:309-312) passes the target folder straight through to `_move` (:342-347) -> `BuilderTree.move_to` (builder/document/builder_tree.gd:111-139), which sets `module.folder = canon(new_folder)` with no reference to `owns_folder()` and then re-roots everything that was in the old folder onto that same target. Empirically: a component at `<sbx>/card/card.guitkx` with `<sbx>/card/card.style.guitkx` beside it and `owns_folder() == true`, after `ws.place_at(card, "<sbx>/widgets")`, lands at `<sbx>/widgets/card.guitkx` and `<sbx>/widgets/card.style.guitkx`, and `owns_folder()` is now false — exactly as the lead states. Both reachable callers throw the correct answer away: `place_module` (builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1725-1748) never consults `owns_folder()` at all, and `move_folder`'s owner fast-path computes `destination := target_folder.path_join(leaf)` at :1676 and then calls `_move_one(module, target_folder, leaf)` (:1684), which forwards `target_folder` — not `destination` — to `place_at` (:1751-1756). The window's own docstring at :1724 asserts the opposite ("A module that owns its folder carries it, which `place_at` handles"). Worse than the lead states: the undo is asymmetric. Replaying the move back (`move_to_path` to `<sbx>/card/card.guitkx`) returns the component but leaves the companion at `<sbx>/widgets/card.style.guitkx`, because `owns` is recomputed as false at that point — verified in the same run. Test coverage is exactly as the lead claims: tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:945-967 is the only `place_module` case and it uses `app.style.guitkx`, a companion, the one kind for which the current code is right. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:309-312, :342-347; builder/document/builder_tree.gd:111-139; builder/document/builder_module.gd:113-120; builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1676-1684, :1725-1748, :1751-1756; tests/builder_chrome_test.gd:945-967)
- **Abort destroys the entire session on one unguarded toolbar click — no confirmation, no toast, and it erases the crash journal on the way out (lead #74)** *(critical · CONFIRMED)* — `run_command` routes `MenuId.ABORT` straight to `abort()` (builder_window.gd:992-993), and `abort()` (:2076-2084) is six statements with no dialog and no toast: `workspace.abort_all()`, `ledger.clear()`, `Journal.clear()`, `reproject()`, `_source.refresh_from_model()`, return. `abort_all` (builder_workspace.gd:554-572) is documented 'Abort IS load re-run' and re-reads every buffer from disk. All three recovery routes are cut in that one call, exactly as the lead says: the ledger is cleared so Ctrl+Z has nothing, the journal is cleared so a restore offer would find nothing, and disk has already been re-read. The asymmetry is in the same file: SAVE raises a hand-built ConfirmationDialog naming every file it would delete (`_confirmed_deletions`, :1989-2013), and the Abort button sits immediately to its right on the toolbar (:618, one line after the Save button at :617). The builder's own help text names the destructiveness — builder_console.gd:221, 'Abort throws the whole session away' — so it is understood and simply unguarded. `abort()` also returns a `reverted` count that `run_command` discards, so even the after-the-fact 'N changes dropped' toast the return value was clearly written for is never shown. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:992-993 (the route), :2076-2084 (abort(), no dialog/toast, return value dropped by the caller), :1989-2013 (_confirmed_deletions — the ConfirmationDialog Save does raise), :617-618 (Save and Abort adjacent on the toolbar); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:554-572 (abort_all re-reads disk); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_console.gd:221 (the help line that names the danger).)
- **BODY hit-test has no horizontal resolution: `rows` is a wrapped-LINE count that `_row_of` uses as a chip INDEX, so most hook chips are unreachable and the reachable ones are the wrong ones** *(critical · CONFIRMED)* — builder_canvas_metrics.gd:240-242 records BODY as _section_row(Section.BODY, top, SECTION_OVERHEAD_H, chips, CHIP_ROW_H) where chips = _chip_rows(...) (:280-297) counts WRAPPED LINES, not chips. row_hit (:503-535) derives index purely from y (`var index := int(into / row_height)` at :526) and returns it as the section's row index, and every consumer then treats it as a position in card.body: builder_window.gd:1537-1538 _row_of returns card.body[index]; builder_canvas_host.gd:152-162 _track_hover reads graph.cards[index].body[row_index] for the hover-usages feature; builder_window.gd:1630-1644 _body_row_rect positions the inline editor at lead + row_index * row_height. Nothing supplies an x-aware alternative — the chips are drawn in an HFlowContainer whose PanelContainers and Labels are all mouse_filter=Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE (canvas_view.guitkx:199-212), so every hit-test necessarily goes through the geometric row_hit. With inner = 340 - 24 = 316px and chip width = min(310, 25 + len * 6.9), two chips routinely share a line, so rows < card.body.size() and the high indices are unreachable. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_canvas_metrics.gd:225-242, 278-297, 503-535 (index at :526), consts at :50,66,68,69,74; .../builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1530-1548, 1630-1644; .../builder/canvas/builder_canvas_host.gd:152-162, 538-545; .../builder/canvas/canvas_view.guitkx:196-215)
- **The whole "Add attribute…" menu writes stringified Dictionaries — the same defect as LANG-01, on the builder's most-used menu item** *(critical · CONFIRMED)* — builder_attributes.gd:69-74 is verbatim what the lead describes. Schema.godot_properties returns an Array of DICTIONARIES ({name, type} built at lsp/guitkx_schema.gd:106) and Schema.events_for_class returns {name, signal} dicts (:142), yet props_of_host does `var name := str(prop)` at :70 and `"name": str(event)` at :74 — stringifying the containers. All four consequences hold: the bogus name makes Schema.property_info return {} (guitkx_schema.gd:112-122), so type collapses to "Variant" and Attributes.default_value falls to its `_:` arm and seeds null (:103); _append's present-key filter compares real attr names against stringified dicts (:136-141) so it never suppresses an attribute already on the row; and the picked payload's name is written straight into the buffer by builder_window.gd:1382-1388 (`name = str(payload["name"])` -> Edits.set_attribute). The LSP's own consumer reads it correctly (lsp/guitkx_completion.gd), which proves this is a builder-local slip, and the parity gate entry ["ShowAttributeMenu", "func menu_for"] (tests/builder_parity.gd:55) is satisfied by a function that is broken for every host tag. **Correction:** The lead's one-line fix is not sufficient. Schema.property_info returns `"type": int(p.get("type", TYPE_NIL))` — a Variant.Type ENUM, not a name (guitkx_schema.gd:118) — so `str(info.get("type", "Variant"))` would yield "4" / "1" even after the name is read correctly, and default_value would still fall to its `_:` null arm for every host property. The type must come from godot_properties' own already-correct `type_string(...)` value (guitkx_schema.gd:106), i.e. read both fields off `prop` and drop the property_info round trip entirely. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_attributes.gd:64-75 (str(prop) at :70, str(event) at :74), :78-103 (default_value), :136-146 (_append); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/lsp/guitkx_schema.gd:93-107, 112-122, 134-143; .../builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1177, 1378-1389; tests/builder_parity.gd:55)
- **Lead 5 (batch position 5): "A util, value or module card never draws its EXPORTS section at any zoom — the only content those cards have"** *(high · CONFIRMED)* — The model/view divergence is exactly as described, and I found nothing that draws exports for a non-STYLE card. `_fill_export_detail` (canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:897-921) is called from :214 for EVERY card that did not project markup — that is every non-COMPONENT kind, plus any component whose markup will not parse — and it appends a `Badge.UTIL_BODY` header row per declaration. `section_stack` reserves an EXPORTS section purely on `not card.export_detail.is_empty()` (canvas/builder_canvas_metrics.gd:247-250), with no kind test. But the ONLY EXPORTS renderer in the view is gated `@if (draws_exports and card.kind == 2)` (canvas/canvas_view.guitkx:231, generated canvas/canvas_view.gd:153), and `Module.Kind` is COMPONENT=0, HOOK=1, STYLE=2 (document/builder_module.gd:40-48) — so kind 2 is STYLE only. The second half of the lead also holds: `row_hit` gates sections on `draws_section(section, lod)` (canvas/builder_canvas_metrics.gd:513-516), and `draws_section` is LOD-based only — `EXPORTS` returns `shows_detail(lod)` with no kind test (:141-146) — so it happily reports EXPORTS row indices inside blank card space, and `_row_of` answers `Section.EXPORTS` with `card.export_detail` (chrome/builder_window.gd:1542-1543), opening a row menu for a row nothing drew. - **Read mode is not read-only — the reused control's own keyboard verbs (Ctrl+/, Ctrl+Shift+D, Ctrl+Shift+K, Alt+Up/Down) mutate the buffer and write straight to the model, bypassing the snapshot AND the parse gate (adversarial-pass lead #70)** *(high · CONFIRMED)* — Reproduced headlessly end to end. `GuitkxCodeEdit._gui_input` (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/editor/guitkx_code_edit.gd:219-262) dispatches Alt+Up/Down -> `move_lines_up/down`, Ctrl+/ -> `toggle_comment`, Ctrl+Shift+D -> `duplicate_lines`, Ctrl+Shift+K -> `delete_lines` with no `editable` test anywhere, and `toggle_comment` (:348-376) mutates via `set_line`, which TextEdit does not gate on `editable` either. The source pane's write-back, `_on_text_changed` (builder/chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:185-201), guards on workspace/path/read-only/no-op but NOT on `_editing` or `editable`, so it calls `workspace.apply_edit` directly. In a real SceneTree with `editable == false` and `is_editing() == false`, one synthetic Ctrl+/ turned line 2 into `\t# return ( <Label text="AAA" /> )` and the workspace buffer took it with one `buffer_edited` emission; a following Ctrl+Shift+D put a fourth line in both the editor and the model. Both bypass `_set_editing`'s snapshot (:207-225) and `apply_edit`'s `Compiler.compile` gate (:230-244). **Correction:** This sits next to, but is not, the agreed divergence "the source pane reuses guitkx_code_edit.gd rather than porting Unity's CodeField.cs". The reuse decision and its stated reason are intact; what has drifted is that the reused control's mutating keyboard verbs were never gated behind the pane's own read/edit toggle, and `_on_text_changed` has no `_editing` guard to catch them. The fix is a guard in the pane (and/or an `editable` test in the code edit's verbs), not a reversal of the divergence. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/editor/guitkx_code_edit.gd:219-262, :348-376; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:102, :146, :185-201, :207-225, :230-244; reproduced under Godot 4.7 headless: model buffer commented and duplicated with editable=false, is_editing=false, 2 buffer_edited emissions)
- **The three outer capture_imports/reconcile_imports pairs in the window are dead code, and they are the ONLY thing three ledger scopes record (lead #2)** *(high · CONFIRMED)* — Verified by code AND by running the real window headless. `Workspace._move` (builder_workspace.gd:342-347) already does capture_imports() -> _tree.move_to() -> reconcile_imports(), so any caller that wraps a move in its own capture/reconcile pair reconciles an already-reconciled tree and gets [] back. `move_folder` (builder_window.gd:1668) and `_place_tree_in` (:2042) use that return value as the scope's ONLY content, and `_commit` drops an empty scope (builder_ledger.gd:322-325 `if entry == null or entry.changes.is_empty(): return`). Measured, not inferred: I built a two-module tree where app.guitkx imports `./shared/thing`, called `move_folder(app/shared -> app/components)`; the specifier demonstrably changed to `~/tests/.../components/shared/thing`, and the ledger went from 0 entries to 0 entries with `can_undo=false`. Same run for `_place_tree_in`: both modules relocated out of UNSAVED_ROOT, 0 ledger entries, `can_undo=false`. `place_module` (:1725) survives only because it also calls `ledger.record_move` at :1741. No test covers move_folder's ledger output (tests/builder_chrome_test.gd only exercises place_module at :949 and _place_tree_in's success flag at :454). **Correction:** One refinement to the lead's arithmetic: it says 'Two of those three use the return value as the entry's only content'. That is exactly right (move_folder and _place_tree_in). The fix it proposes — record a `record_move` per module, or have `_move` hand the rewrites to the caller — is the correct shape. (builder_workspace.gd:342-347 (_move does its own capture/reconcile and returns the rewrites); builder_window.gd:1698-1712 (move_folder: begin -> capture -> loop of move_to -> reconcile -> record -> end); builder_window.gd:2059-2071 (_place_tree_in, same shape); builder_ledger.gd:322-325 (_commit drops an empty scope). Headless measurement: move_folder rewrote the importer's specifier and produced 0 ledger entries / can_undo=false; _place_tree_in moved 2 modules and produced 0 entries / can_undo=false.)
- **Every window-level move DISCARDS the import rewrites the workspace returns, and records an empty second reconcile instead (lead #18)** *(high · CONFIRMED)* — Same root cause as lead #2 and verified the same way. `_move_one` (builder_window.gd:1751-1756) calls `workspace.place_at`, which returns the rewrites, and then uses them ONLY as a boolean: `var moved := workspace.place_at(...)` / `if moved.is_empty(): return false`. The rewrites are never recorded. The three call sites then take a second, redundant snapshot and reconcile again over text the inner reconcile has already fixed, so `_rewrite_specifiers` hits its `str(imp["spec"]) == str(w["wanted"])` skip (builder_workspace.gd:437-438), returns "", and the outer pass records nothing — measured as 0 ledger entries for move_folder and _place_tree_in. **Correction:** Two accuracy notes. (1) `place_module` DOES produce a ledger entry — `ledger.record_move` at :1741 — so it is not 'missing the entry', only the rewrite text; and because MOVE replay goes back through `workspace.move_to_path` -> `_move` (builder_window.gd:2134-2136), which reconciles internally, the specifiers self-heal on undo. The real, measured damage is concentrated in move_folder and _place_tree_in, where the whole entry is empty and dropped. (2) The lead understates the is-it-empty-flag half. I measured a worse consequence than a missing record: re-filing a module whose move has NO import consequence is silently REFUSED. `place_module(app.style.guitkx -> app/styles)` returned false on a tree where nothing imported the style module, and returned true on an otherwise identical tree where app.guitkx imported it. `_move_one` is reading 'no specifier needed rewriting' as 'the move failed', and the module stays put with no toast and no explanation. (builder_window.gd:1751-1756 (_move_one: rewrites used as an is-it-empty flag and thrown away); builder_window.gd:1735-1743 (place_module's own redundant snapshot/reconcile); builder_workspace.gd:309-312 and :340-346 (place_at/_move already reconcile and return the rewrites); builder_workspace.gd:433-440 (the skip that makes the second pass a no-op).)

(builder_window.gd:556-586 (_on_library_activated, two-way dispatch) vs :2242-2274 (drop_library_entry, three-way dispatch); builder_library_pane.gd:135-144 (all six sections); builder_window.gd:1226-1236 (_with_component_import matches COMPONENT cards only). The builder does own the right primitive — `Specifiers.map` (document/builder_specifiers.gd:49-56, documented as 'The ONE place in the builder that turns an import into a path') — and a grep shows every OTHER consumer uses it (canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:122, document/builder_workspace.gd:377 and :711, preview/builder_preview.gd:413); `referrers_to` is the one place that does not. Its only caller is the delete refusal at chrome/builder_window.gd:2421. Accuracy note for the record: `graph` is assigned only in `reproject()` (chrome/builder_window.gd:824) and is never reset to null, so the graph-null half is latent (reachable only before the first projection) while the specifier-text half is live on every delete. - **BATCH 1 / pos 49 — RuitkBuilderPreviewPane.clear() has no caller, and open_tree tears down neither the mount nor the preview's per-module caches** *(medium · CONFIRMED)* — The headline is exactly right. `clear()` (chrome/builder_preview_pane.gd:183-188) documents itself as "Called when the tree closes, so a preview never outlives the tree it came from" and has no caller — the window's references to `_preview_pane` are builder_window.gd:46, 121, 376, 377, 378, 727, 741, 742, 844, 845, 2165, 2172, none of them `clear`. `open_tree` (builder_window.gd:749-774) calls the STATIC `Preview.clear_scratch()` (:759) but never `preview.teardown()` and never `preview.unmount()`; `teardown()` — the one thing that empties `_compiled_from` / `_mirrored` / `_built` (preview/builder_preview.gd:590-596) — runs only from `_exit_tree` (builder_window.gd:146), and per CLAUDE.md the window is hidden rather than freed on close, so between sessions it never runs at all. The observable failure is real but arrives by a slightly different route than the lead argues, so I have narrowed it in `correction`. **Correction:** The dead `clear()` and the missing teardown in `open_tree` are exactly as stated. The stale-`built_script` consequence is weaker than claimed: `select_module` (builder_window.gd:2165-2172) compiles the new focus before showing it (`if preview.built_script(_focus_path) == null: preview.compile_dirty(...)`), and `_sync_scratch` re-writes any mirror file that `clear_scratch()` removed because it re-checks `FileAccess.file_exists(mirrored)` (builder_preview.gd:430-431) — and a cache hit requires the same path AND the same buffer text, which compiles to the same script. The live consequence is the MOUNT: `show_module` deliberately keeps the last good render when `preview.mount(...)` fails (builder_preview_pane.gd:167-172), so opening a second tree focused on a hook/util/style module — or on a component that does not build — leaves the PREVIOUS tree's component on the stage under the new tree's `_tag` header, captioned "last good render — the current edit does not build yet". The caches also simply grow across trees, since nothing prunes them between sessions.
- **The same missing row-kind gate exists on the library DROP path, with only half a guard** *(medium · OVERSTATED)* — The structural claim is right but one of its two worked examples is already refused. Correct: `Edits.can_place` (edits/builder_edits.gd:55-69) tests only null-ness, placement, `row.depth == 0` and whether the PARENT is a DIRECTIVE — never the row's own `kind`; and `drop_library_entry` refuses exactly one kind, `if row == null or row.kind == Graph.LineKind.IMPORT: return false` (chrome/builder_window.gd:2257). A middle-band drop resolves to `Placement.INSIDE` (edits/builder_drag.gd:152-153) which `can_place` waves through unconditionally (:58-59), so dropping `<Label>` on a hook chip runs `Edits.insert` against a `LineKind.HOOK` GDScript line (chips are built as `row.kind = Graph.LineKind.HOOK`, builder_graph_service.gd:451-459) — the hole is live. EXPORTS rows are a second live case the lead does not mention: a HOST/COMPONENT entry dropped there yields `row.kind == EXPORT`, which is not IMPORT and so passes. Wrong: the 'setup-island line' example. `Drag.resolve` does not use the window's `_row_of` — it uses its own (edits/builder_drag.gd:165-178), whose match handles only IMPORTS/BODY/MARKUP/EXPORTS and whose default arm `_: return null` covers `Section.ISLAND` and `Section.SIGNATURE`. So an island drop arrives with `row == null` and is refused by the very guard the lead calls half a guard. **Correction:** The gate is genuinely missing from `can_place`/`insert`/`set_attribute` and `drop_library_entry` refuses only `LineKind.IMPORT` — so the argument for putting the refusal in the operations rather than in the menu builder stands. But the live drop targets are BODY hook chips (kind HOOK) and EXPORTS entry rows (kind EXPORT), NOT setup-island lines: `Drag._row_of` (builder_drag.gd:176-177) has no `Section.ISLAND` arm, so an island drop resolves to a null row and is already refused. (builder_edits.gd:55-69 (`can_place` — no `row.kind` test); builder_window.gd:2257 (`if row == null or row.kind == Graph.LineKind.IMPORT: return false`); builder_drag.gd:165-178 (`_row_of` default arm returns null for ISLAND/SIGNATURE) and :143-153 (`_placement_of`, middle band → INSIDE); builder_graph_service.gd:451-459 (body chips are LineKind.HOOK).)
- **`record_typing` and its whole coalescing window are unreachable in real use — dead code standing in for the feature they were ported to provide** *(medium · CONFIRMED)* — The chain is exactly as described and I could find no second door into it. `record_typing` (document/builder_ledger.gd:170-194) has precisely one caller in the whole repo — `ledger.record_typing(file_path, before, after)` at chrome/builder_window.gd:907, inside `_on_buffer_edited`, whose first two statements are `if _source != null and _source.is_editing(): return` (:904-905). The only emitter of `buffer_edited` is `_on_text_changed` (chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:185-197, emit at :197), which needs a real `text_changed`; `_editor.editable` is set true in exactly one place, `_set_editing`'s `_editor.editable = on` (:218), which runs in lockstep with `_editing = on` (:217), and `is_editing()` returns `_editing` (:225-226) — every other assignment (:102, :146, :244, :257) sets it false. So the intended edit-mode gesture can never reach `record_typing`, and the TYPING_WINDOW_MSEC merge at :180-187 never runs for it. The lead's stated exception is also real: `guitkx_code_edit.gd`'s own `_gui_input` (editor/guitkx_code_edit.gd:219-262) dispatches `move_lines_up/down`, `toggle_comment`, `duplicate_lines` and `delete_lines` with no `editable` check at all, so those mutate the buffer in read mode, `_editing` is false, and `_on_buffer_edited` falls through to `record_typing` — which is to say the only live path into it is the side door. (builder_ledger.gd:170-194 (`record_typing`, the TYPING_WINDOW_MSEC merge at :180-187); its sole caller builder_window.gd:907, gated at :904-905; builder_source_pane.gd:185-197 (`_on_text_changed` → `buffer_edited.emit`), :216-218 (`_editing = on` / `_editor.editable = on`), :225-226; guitkx_code_edit.gd:219-262 (Alt+Up/Down, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+Shift+D, Ctrl+Shift+K — no editable check).)
- **After the unsaved tree is placed, the source pane still points at the vacated provisional path, and the next edit blanks it** *(medium · CONFIRMED)* — Batch 8, lead #16. `_place_tree_in` (builder_window.gd:2042-2074) repoints only `_focus_path` (:2066-2067, inside the move loop) and then calls `reproject()`; it never calls `select_module`. `reproject()` (:821-851) refreshes the canvas, folder pane, library and status but never touches `_source`, `_preview_pane.show_module` or `_library.select_component`. `save()` (:1951-1981) does not either. `BuilderSourcePane._path` (builder_source_pane.gd:37, written only in `show_module` at :139) therefore still holds the `res://__ruitk_builder_unsaved__~/...` path, and `refresh_from_model` (:152-162) does `workspace.try_get(_path)` → null → `clear()`. The proposed one-line fix is also correct: `show_module`'s early-out is `Paths.key(file_path) == Paths.key(_path)` at builder_source_pane.gd:133, and the paths genuinely differ after placement, so `select_module(_focus_path)` would repoint source pane, folder pane, library and preview pane in one call. I also checked the one plausible refutation — that the folder pane's rebuild re-announces the selection — and it does not: `rebuild()` re-selects `previously_selected` (the dead provisional path), `select_path` finds no row in `_rows` and calls `deselect_all()` without emitting (builder_folder_pane.gd:285-296). **Correction:** The trigger is narrower than "any keystroke, any canvas gesture". A keystroke in the source pane does NOT reach `refresh_from_model`: `_on_text_changed` (builder_source_pane.gd:180-192) bails at `module == null` and never emits `buffer_edited`, so pane keystrokes on the dead path are silently swallowed instead — arguably worse, since the user types into a live-looking editor and nothing is recorded. The blanking happens on the first change that comes from elsewhere (a canvas gesture, a row-menu edit, an undo), all of which route through `_after_model_change` → `_source.refresh_from_model()` (builder_window.gd:882-894). (chrome/builder_window.gd:2042-2074 (_place_tree_in, no select_module), :821-851 (reproject, no _source/_preview refresh), :1951-1981 (save); chrome/builder_source_pane.gd:37, :133, :139, :152-162, :173-176; chrome/builder_folder_pane.gd:285-296)
- **Nothing refuses a drop into a read-only location -- Save then writes into res://addons/** *(medium · CONFIRMED)* — Batch 8, lead #24. `Paths.is_writable_location` (document/builder_paths.gd:77-81) has exactly two callers in the entire addon — `Workspace.is_read_only_location` (:116-117), used only at LOAD to stamp `Module.read_only` (:181, :199, :225). Nothing re-derives it after a move, and `save_all` filters on `module.read_only or is_unlocated(...)` (:503), i.e. on the flag, not on where the module now lives. Every read-only guard in the window is on the DRAGGED module: `place_module` :1729, `move_folder` :1691, row menu :1072, card menu :2198-2200, `delete_module` :2418 — `grep -n is_writable_location chrome/builder_window.gd` returns nothing. The folder pane offers the destination with no policy check: `_folder_item`/`_ensure_folder` (builder_folder_pane.gd:228-252) build a row for whatever `module.folder` says, and `_drop_target_for` (:141-156) rejects only self-drops, subtree-drops and no-op drops. So an `res://addons/...` folder pulled in by the import closure is a fully legal drop target, and a writable component dropped there is written to `res://addons/` at Save. The claim that this is a family gap also checks out against the reference: BuilderWorkspace.cs:140 captures `IsReadOnlyLocation(full)` at load and :600 filters on `module.IsReadOnly`. **Correction:** Real defect, but not a parity gap — the Unity leg has the identical hole, so nothing has drifted from the agreed port. File it as a family bug (destination policy), not as a Godot regression. Fix is a `Paths.is_writable_location(destination)` refusal with a toast, in `place_module` (builder_window.gd:1729) and `move_folder` (:1673), plus dropping the row as a target in `_drop_target_for`. (document/builder_paths.gd:77-81; document/builder_workspace.gd:116-117, :181, :503; chrome/builder_window.gd:1729 (place_module guards only the dragged module), :1691; chrome/builder_folder_pane.gd:141-156, :240-252; reference: ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/Document/BuilderWorkspace.cs:140, :600)
- **Abort reverts every buffer and never asks for a preview round — the stage keeps rendering the work that was just thrown away** *(medium · CONFIRMED)* — Batch 8, lead #48. `abort()` is five statements — `workspace.abort_all()`, `ledger.clear()`, `Journal.clear()`, `reproject()`, `_source.refresh_from_model()` (builder_window.gd:2076-2084) — with no `preview.request_refresh()` and no `_preview_pane.show_module(...)`. Its two siblings both have it: `_replay` at :2111-2113 and `restore_recovery` at :958-960 each end with `reproject()` / `_source.refresh_from_model()` / `preview.request_refresh()`. `reproject()` itself (:821-851) never requests a round. The consequence chain holds: `tick()` returns early unless `preview.is_due()` (:918), and `is_due()` is `_pending and elapsed >= debounce_msec` where `_pending` is set only by `request_refresh` (preview/builder_preview.gd:113-121). I checked the one other candidate route — the ABORT command — and `run_command`'s `MenuId.ABORT` branch is a bare `abort()` (:992-993), so nothing downstream compensates. `workspace.abort_all()` emits `changed` (document/builder_workspace.gd:569) but the window never connects that signal (`grep -n changed.connect` finds only `_canvas.camera_changed` and `ledger.changed`). (chrome/builder_window.gd:2076-2084 (abort), :2105-2113 (_replay, has it), :955-961 (restore_recovery, has it), :918 (tick gate), :992-993 (the ABORT command); preview/builder_preview.gd:113-121)
- **Wheel zoom and Reset view never repaint the host, so the background and dot grid stay at the previous camera and zoom (adversarial-pass lead #6)** *(medium · CONFIRMED)* — There are exactly two `queue_redraw()` calls in the whole builder canvas host — `set_camera` (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_canvas_host.gd:126) and the middle-button pan branch of `_handle_motion` (:510) — plus one on the edge overlay (builder_canvas_edges.gd:75). The wheel-zoom branch (builder_canvas_host.gd:387-401) mutates `camera`/`zoom`, calls `_render()` and emits `camera_changed`; `fit_to_view` (:211-218, what Reset view / MenuId.FIT_VIEW at builder_window.gd:999 and `_fit_when_sized` at :808 call) does the same. `_render()` (:254-277) only re-roots the reconciler tree and calls `_edges.refresh` — it never repaints the host. The host's own `_draw` (:353-368) is what paints the ground colour and the dot grid, whose spacing and offset are both functions of `zoom` and `camera`. Neither `camera_changed` listener repaints either: `_on_camera_changed` (builder_window.gd:2187-2191) only writes into `layout`, and the second listener (:700) calls `_sync_layer_selector` (:646-655), which touches only the dropdown. `_process` (:293-307) runs `_fit_cards`/`_pass_mouse_through` and never redraws. So after a scroll-wheel zoom the cards and the Bezier edges move while the grid stays at the previous pitch and offset until an unrelated `set_camera` or pan happens to fire. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_canvas_host.gd:126, :387-401, :211-218, :254-277, :353-368, :510; builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:646-655, :699-700, :999, :2187-2191)
- **The camera and zoom are discarded on every reprojection, so creating or renaming a module snaps the canvas back to Layer 2, centred (adversarial-pass lead #30)** *(medium · CONFIRMED)* — `_on_camera_changed` (builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:2187-2191) writes `layout.camera`/`layout.zoom` and returns — it never sets `has_saved_view` and never saves. `reproject()` then replaces the whole object: `layout = CanvasLayout.for_graph(graph)` (:825), and `for_graph` (builder/canvas/builder_canvas_layout.gd:100-111) re-reads from disk via `load_for_members`/`load_for_root` or returns a fresh `Self.new()`, so everything `_on_camera_changed` recorded is gone. `has_saved_view` is set in only two places: `capture_from` (:156-163) and `_read` (:267-279, i.e. a layout that came off disk). With no layout file, :837-843 sets `_canvas.zoom = Metrics.DEFAULT_ZOOM` and calls `_centre_when_sized()` — the described snap-back. `reproject()` has 13 call sites (create, rename, delete, move, undo, …), so the symptom is on every structural gesture. **Correction:** One detail of the lead's framing is imprecise: after the first card drag or Save, the snap is not to Layer 2 but to the last CAPTURED camera — `reproject` takes the `has_saved_view` branch at :828-830 and assigns `_canvas.camera`/`_canvas.zoom` from the layout it just re-read off disk. The underlying claim (the live camera is discarded on every reprojection) holds in both branches; only the visible destination differs. - **The inline editor is never closed or repositioned when the camera moves or the graph re-projects (adversarial-pass lead #62)** *(medium · CONFIRMED)* — `open_at` (builder/chrome/builder_inline_editor.gd:63-77) assigns `position` and `size` once and nothing revisits them. - **`builder_workspace.rescan` — the injected callable whose own docstring says the plugin wires it — is never assigned in production, so a Save never asks the editor to rescan (lead #34)** *(medium · CONFIRMED)* — A repo-wide grep for any assignment to `rescan` finds none. The builder also makes no editor-filesystem call of its own: grep for `EditorInterface` / `get_resource_filesystem` under builder/ returns only `canvas_palette.gd:32` (theme lookup) and a comment in `builder_folder_pane.gd:35`. - **Every keystroke in a knob does a full unmount/remount of the reconciler tree, with no debounce (lead #50)** *(medium · CONFIRMED)* — Exactly as described. `_knob_row` connects the LineEdit's per-keystroke `text_changed` straight through: builder_preview_pane.gd:282-285 is `field.text_changed.connect(func(text): _props[name] = _typed(...); if preview != null: preview.mount(_slot, _path, _props))`. `mount` (builder_preview.gd:536-558) runs `unmount()` (which frees the host tree and runs every effect cleanup), then `_clear_scratch_comp_cache()` — whose own comment at :552-555 notes it 'costs one `load` per child' — then `RuitkRoot.create()`. There is no timer, no `set_deferred`, no dirty flag on this path. The compile path next door does have one: `debounce_msec := 300` (builder_preview.gd:81), read at :121. So the knob path does strictly more work per event than a debounced compile round does, five times over for a five-character word. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_preview_pane.gd:282-285 (text_changed -> mount, undebounced); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/preview/builder_preview.gd:536-558 (mount = unmount + cache clear + RuitkRoot.create), :81 and :121 (the 300 ms debounce the compile path does have).)

That strengthens the lead's own point about tokens needing to be distinctive identifiers. (tests/builder_parity.gd:33 and :36; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:2353-2374 (drop_module), :2299 (drop_module_export, also matched by the token), :1725-1748 (place_module, the real answer); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:101-105 vs :309-312 / :321-325 / :342-347)
- **Lead 45 (batch position 45): "`row.set_meta(\"entry_name\", name)` is written twice, and the duplicate is what hides the LIB-03 toggle-order bug"** *(low · CONFIRMED)* — Verbatim correct, including the line numbers. `chrome/builder_library_pane.gd:311` and `:315` are the identical statement `row.set_meta("entry_name", name)`, with the three-line selection block at :312-314 (`if kind == ENTRY_COMPONENT and name == _selected_component:` / `row.button_pressed = true` / `row.toggle_mode = true`) sandwiched between them. "") -> BuilderWorkspace.cs:256-267 -> BuilderModule.Fresh -> BuilderModule.cs:142 Id = NewId(). Unity does NOT carry the module on Change.Removed for a creation the way the lead proposes; Removed is deletion-only there too (BuilderWindow.cs:1360-1373). So the identity churn on redo is the reference's own behaviour. **Correction:** The id-churn is not a Godot-only defect — Unity's redo re-mints an id identically, so this lead as written should not be actioned. There IS a real Godot-only divergence on the very same two lines that the lead missed: Unity's UNDO arm captures the pending buffer into the change before deleting (BuilderWindow.cs:1381-1384, `if (pending != null) change.After = pending.BufferText;`) and its redo replays `change.After`, so the text survives the round trip. Godot's undo arm (builder_window.gd:2127) just calls workspace.delete(path) and its redo hard-codes an EMPTY buffer, while _create_named (builder_window.gd:1886) seeds Edits.template_for(kind, name). So undo+redo of a create silently replaces the seeded template with a blank module — which builder_workspace.gd:508 then refuses to write at Save as a blank module. That is the entry worth keeping, not the id. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:2116-2133 (_replay_change); .../builder/document/builder_workspace.gd:256-265 (create_new); .../builder/document/builder_module.gd:236-247 (fresh, id = new_id()); .../builder/document/builder_ledger.gd:254-262 (record_creation stores no module); ../ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:1375-1390; .../Document/BuilderWorkspace.cs:256-267; .../Document/BuilderModule.cs:105,142)

So the library's name prompt lands over the canvas at whatever row the user last right-clicked. The reference does the opposite deliberately: Unity's library '+ new' button calls BuilderSearchMenu.RememberPointer(evt.position, focusedWindow) on its OWN PointerDownEvent immediately before onNewFile() (BuilderLibraryPane.cs:194-200), overwriting the remembered pointer so the prompt opens at the button. **Correction:** One detail to tighten: _menu_at is set only by a ROW right-click (_on_row_context), not by a card or empty-canvas right-click — the card menu (_on_card_new -> prompt_create) inherits the same stale value. So the accurate statement is 'the last right-click that landed on a card ROW', and the fix belongs on both _on_library_create and any other prompt_create caller that is not the row menu, matching Unity's per-invoker RememberPointer. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_preview_pane.gd:201-206; .../builder/canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:1105-1112; .../builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:2166-2172; ../ruitk-unity/Builder/Editor/BuilderWindow.cs:1112-1113)
- **_confirmed_deletions leaks its ConfirmationDialog on every agreed save** *(low · CONFIRMED)* — builder_window.gd:1999-2013 builds a ConfirmationDialog, add_child()s it, and the only queue_free is on dialog.close_requested (:2011). The confirmed handler (:2007-2010) sets _deletions_agreed, calls save() and clears the flag — it never frees. Godot's AcceptDialog hides itself and emits `confirmed` on OK and emits `canceled` on Escape; `close_requested` is a Window signal raised by the window-manager close, not by a programmatic hide — so both the accepted AND the escaped paths leave a hidden dialog parented to the builder, one per save that had orphans. The builder Window is hidden rather than freed on close (plugin.gd), so they accumulate for the whole editor session. The adjacent function in the same file does it right on every exit path — _ask_where_the_tree_lives frees its EditorFileDialog in both the dir_selected and canceled lambdas (:2027, :2031) — which is the in-file precedent this one missed. **Correction:** Slightly understated rather than overstated: the Escape/cancel path leaks too, because AcceptDialog raises `canceled`, not `close_requested`, on Escape. The fix should free on confirmed AND canceled (or connect queue_free to visibility_changed when hidden), not only add it to the confirmed lambda. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1989-2014 (queue_free only at :2011), 2022-2035 (the correctly-freed neighbour))
- **The state column is 72px wide with clipping left at its default, and its widest value is 13 characters** *(low · CONFIRMED)* — The lead asked to be measured rather than assumed, so I measured it on the project's own Godot 4.7 binary. The code is as described: builder_folder_pane.gd:70-73 sets `set_column_expand(0, true)`, `set_column_clip_content(0, false)`, `set_column_expand(1, false)`, `set_column_custom_minimum_width(1, 72)`, and `set_column_clip_content(1, ...)` is never called (the only other column call in the file is `set_column_title`). `_state_of` (builder_folder_pane.gd:212-224) can return "moved, edited". The only tooltip in the pane is on column 0 (:196). Headless probe results: a non-expanding column's drawn width equals its custom minimum regardless of content and regardless of the clip flag (72 with a 13-char value, 72 with a 48-char value, 10 when the minimum is 10 and the value is 13 chars — clip on or off), and TreeItem cells default to `text_overrun_behavior == 3` (OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS). "moved, edited" measures 111px at font size 16 and roughly 97px at the editor's default 14. The column is genuinely too narrow for its widest value, with no tooltip to recover it. **Correction:** The mechanism named in the lead is wrong, which matters because it points at the wrong fix. `clip_content` defaults to FALSE (probe: `is_column_clipping_content(1)` on a fresh Tree returns false), i.e. the default is identical to the value column 0 sets explicitly at :71 — that call is a restatement of the default, not a treatment column 1 was denied, and setting the flag on column 1 would change nothing (or, set to true, clip harder). The truncation comes from the TreeItem cell's default OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS against a 72px column, and content does NOT widen a non-expanding column in Godot 4.7. The fix is the width (or a column-1 tooltip / a shorter word than "moved, edited"), never the clip flag. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_folder_pane.gd:70-73, :196 (tooltip on column 0 only), :212-224 (_state_of); measured with Godot_v4.7-stable headless: fresh_col1_clip=false, col1 width 72 for both a 13-char and a 48-char value, overrun behavior 3, "moved, edited" = 111px @16)
- **'Add entry...' is offered on every EXPORTS row, including rows where it can only be a no-op** *(low · OVERSTATED)* — The unconditional offer is real: builder_window.gd:1083-1091 adds `Add entry...` for ANY row where `section == Metrics.Section.EXPORTS`, and `_style_key_items` (builder_window.gd:1242-1249) takes `var owner := str(row.name)` and hands it to `Edits.insert_style_entry` (builder_edits.gd:550-573), which matches on `str(dm["name"]) != export_name or str(dm["kind"]) != "value"` and otherwise returns the source unchanged — producing the `after == before` toast at builder_window.gd:1432-1434. The fallback-to-export_detail for an unparseable component (builder_graph_service.gd:208-214) is also real, and its declarations are funcs, so `kind != "value"` and the entry can never apply there. But the lead's enumeration of the three row shapes is wrong on one of them, and it is the one the user is most likely to click. **Correction:** Two of the three EXPORTS row shapes work correctly, not one. The declaration header carries the declaration name (builder_graph_service.gd:906) — the lead grants this. The `+ entry` badge row does NOT have its name unset: builder_graph_service.gd:920 is `add.name = str(dm["name"])`, the same declaration name the header carries, so picking a key from the `+ entry` row applies correctly. Only the per-entry rows misfire, because builder_graph_service.gd:913 sets `erow.name = str(entry["key"])` (e.g. "bg_color") — plus the non-`value` declarations in the unparseable-component fallback. So the accurate statement is: 'Add entry…' is offered unconditionally on the EXPORTS section and no-ops on a style entry row and on any non-`value` declaration, and it fails loudly via an explicit toast rather than corrupting anything. The suggested gate would also be wrong as written — gating on `row.badge == Graph.Badge.STYLE_HEADER` would remove the item from the `+ entry` row (badge ADD_ENTRY), which currently works. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_graph_service.gd:920 (add.name = decl name — refutes 'name unset') vs :913 (erow.name = entry key — the real defect) and :906 (header); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:1083-1091, :1242-1249, :1432-1434; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_edits.gd:552-553)
- **Library rows carry no kind tint — the one surface that lists all six kinds together is the one surface that does not colour-code them** *(low · CONFIRMED)* — `_entry_row` (builder_library_pane.gd:295-321) builds a plain `Button` — flat=false, left alignment, text, tooltip, two metas, a `pressed` connection and a double-click handler — with no `add_theme_color_override`, no `modulate`, and no stylebox. `_add_section` (builder_library_pane.gd:208-238) builds the section header the same way, also untinted. The whole file has exactly ONE colour override, `Parts.ACCENT_COLOR` on the drag ghost at :278, and it never imports the palette at all (no `Palette` const, no `canvas_palette` preload). Meanwhile the vocabulary the lead says is taught elsewhere does exist: `Palette.kind_tint` (canvas/canvas_palette.gd:133-148) returns a distinct colour for all six kinds plus unknown, and the window's own legend uses it (builder_window.gd:628-631). The pane does list all six kinds in one column (builder_library_pane.gd:135-144: NATIVE ELEMENTS, CUSTOM COMPONENTS, HOOKS, STYLE MODULES, UTIL MODULES, HOOK MODULES) and distinguishes them only by the section heading text and the `<...>` angle brackets on the two tag kinds (:307-308). **Correction:** Purely cosmetic, and the kinds are not unlabelled — each section carries a text heading naming its kind, so nothing is ambiguous, only inconsistent with the canvas. I would rate it low rather than medium. The suggested fix is sound and is not blocked by the recorded divergence: canvas_palette.gd is a hand-written @tool script (canvas/canvas_palette.gd) and `kind_tint` is a static func, so editor code can call it. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_library_pane.gd:295-321 (_entry_row, no tint), :208-238 (_add_section, no tint), :278 (the file's only colour override); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/canvas_palette.gd:133-148 (kind_tint); addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:628-631 (legend uses it))
- **The preview stage has no scroll and no clip, so a component taller than the pane pushes the captions and the state panel out of the split with no way to reach them** *(low · CONFIRMED)* — Every structural claim holds. `RuitkBuilderPreviewPane extends VBoxContainer` (builder_preview_pane.gd:3). `_stage` is a `PanelContainer` with `custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, 120)` and `size_flags_vertical = SIZE_SHRINK_BEGIN` (builder_preview_pane.gd:60-62), and the mount target `_slot` is a `MarginContainer` added straight into it (:76-79), so the mounted component's minimum size propagates up through MarginContainer -> PanelContainer -> the pane's own minimum, unbounded. `grep -rn clip_contents` over builder/ returns three hits and none of them is this pane — builder_canvas_host.gd:91 and the two canvas_view card hits — so `_stage` has no clip. There is no `ScrollContainer` anywhere under builder/chrome: the pane is added as a direct child of a `VSplitContainer` (builder_window.gd:373-378), with the source pane as its sibling. The three controls that get pushed are exactly the ones named, and they come after `_stage` in the VBox: `_origin` (:81-86), `_note` (:88-93), `_state_panel` (:98-100). There is no zoom-to-fit and no size cap on the stage anywhere in the file. (addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_preview_pane.gd:3, :60-62, :76-79, :81-86, :88-93, :98-100; addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:373-378 (pane is a bare VSplitContainer child, no ScrollContainer))

**Refuted — do not act on these:**

- ~~Unity's loop-wrap root guard is NOT a gap here, and a plan that ports it would be wrong (lead #58)~~ — This lead is a do-not-do note rather than a gap, and I verified both halves of it. Code: `Edits.WRAPS` (builder_edits.gd:675-681) is a flat three-entry list with no root predicate, and the wrap menu that consumes it (builder_window.gd:1156-1164) builds its items straight from WRAPS plus @match with no `isRoot` filter — so there is nothing to remove and nothing missing. Language: I compiled the two cases through the real compiler (RuitkGuitkxCodegen.compile_file on Godot 4.7). `@for (item in range(1))` wrapping a component's return root compiled ok=true with only GUITKX0106 (the missing-`key` warning), and `@while (false)` on the root likewise compiled ok=true with only GUITKX0106. There is no root-directive gate anywhere in the compiler. The Godot leg's ungated behaviour is correct and Unity's UITKX0025 constraint is engine-specific — porting `isRoot` into WRAPS would introduce a refusal the language does not have.
- ~~`row_clicked` fires on PRESS, so beginning a row drag also navigates and re-points Delete~~ — The Godot behaviour matches the reference exactly; the lead's Unity citation is misread. Unity's markup-row onPointerDown (CanvasView.uitkx:1080-1098) arms the drag via BuilderDragService.Begin and then, on the SAME press and unconditionally, calls setSelected/setSelRowNode/setSelRowIdx, onRowSelect and onRowClick before e.StopPropagation(). Its own comment at :1077-1079 says so: 'The service captures the pointer; a release under the travel threshold stays a plain click (the select below already ran).' Unity's onRowClick handler (BuilderWindow.cs:1744-1753 OnCanvasRowClicked) does exactly what the Godot _on_row_clicked does — OpenFileFromCanvas, _codeField.FocusLine(sourceLine), SyncLibrarySelection. So in Unity too, beginning a row drag selects the row, focuses the file and scrolls the source pane. The StopPropagation the lead cites is what stops the ROOT canvas handler (pan / canvas context menu) from also seeing the press — and the Godot leg does the analogous thing with accept_event() at builder_canvas_host.gd:430.

## Deliberate divergences, re-confirmed

Differences from Unity the research examined and judged sound, so nobody re-litigates them.

**Action ledger: undo/redo, coalescing, history jump, what is recorded and what is not**

- **The ledger is not persisted** — Correct translation. The Godot leg keeps the tree across a crash via document/builder_journal.gd instead of a reload journal, and the ledger lives only as long as the window. (unity BuilderActionLedger.cs:18-21 (NonSerialized, domain reload drops it); godot builder_ledger.gd:16-18 ("Godot has no domain reload to survive").)
- **Clear() and the Changed event** — BETTER THAN UNITY on both counts. Unity's Abort never clears the ledger, leaving a history that replays against a tree that no longer matches; Godot's abort() clears it. The `changed` signal has a real subscriber. (The subscriber's own toolbar loop is inert — see gap L-01 — but the status label does refresh.) (unity BuilderActionLedger.cs:104,:342-349 with zero consumers; godot builder_ledger.gd:294-299 consumed at builder_window.gd:766 (open_tree) and :2080 (abort), signal wired at :731.)

**Canvas drawing: LOD bands, card geometry, section stack, edges, anchors, palette, grid, framing**

- **One edge per import row PLUS one per markup row that instantiates a module** — Both legs draw import edges and usage edges. Godot only emits a usage edge for a tag the card actually IMPORTED, where Unity matches any component card by title. That is a correct language translation, not a gap: cross-file resolution in .guitkx is STRICT (GUITKX2305), so an unimported usage is a compile error and an edge to it would draw a relationship that cannot exist. (unity BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:861-888 + IndexOfTitle:1044-1053 (matches ANY component card by Title); godot builder_graph_service.gd:130-147 (usage edges, gated on `target_of_name`))
- **Screen-space Bezier with a 40px pull floor and a terminal dot** — Godot samples the cubic in SCREEN space from screen endpoints with zoom=1.0, so the 40px floor, the 2px stroke and the 3.5px dot are literally constant pixels instead of world units divided by zoom — the same result by a simpler route, and it is why the whole overlay is screen-space (edges.gd:4-9). The added divergence — pulling along the DOMINANT axis (metrics.gd:465-474) — is required by Godot's row-major seeded layout, where children sit below rather than right; Unity's always-horizontal pull would double every curve back through itself. (unity BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:1060-1085 (StrokeEdge: dx = max(40/zoom, |dx|*0.45), lineWidth 2/zoom, terminal dot r=4/zoom at full alpha); godot builder_canvas_edges.gd:156-166 + builder_canvas_metrics.gd:464-485)

**Canvas input and gestures: pan, zoom, hit-testing, selection, card drag, row drag, drop bands**

- **Three LOD bands driven by zoom** — The listed divergence is honoured and correctly chose LodOf's numbers, which are the ones the capability contract documents. Two further, undocumented deviations: CARD_WIDTH_FULL is 360 not Unity's 430 (justified in-file at :51-52), and a FOURTH implicit band exists -- ATTRIBUTE_ZOOM 1.2 (:116-120) gates the attribute run, so at 0.80<=zoom<1.2 the toolbar reads 'Layer 3 - Edit' while attributes are still hidden. Self-consistent (row heights and widths do not change with it) but it is a band no dropdown can name and it is not in plans/UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md. (unity CanvasView.uitkx:108 (0.45/1.05) vs BuilderCanvasHost.cs:769 (0.32/0.80) | godot builder_canvas_metrics.gd:37-38, :84-87 (ONE lod_of at 0.32/0.80), :49-53 (widths 300/340/360))
- **Toolbar layer dropdown** — Better than the reference: the preset zooms ABOUT THE CANVAS CENTRE rather than resetting the camera to a hard-coded corner, so picking a layer does not lose the user's place -- Unity's source offers no rationale for the 60/30 slam. The selector also follows the zoom back, matching ZoomChanged->SetActiveMode. Not synced on layout restore, though: see GAP-07. (unity BuilderWindow.cs:29-33, BuilderCanvasHost.cs:339-350 (camera slammed to 60,30) | godot builder_canvas_metrics.gd:41 (LAYER_PRESETS 0.30/0.75/1.25), chrome/builder_window.gd:61-65 (LAYERS), :636-642 (_on_layer_chosen), :645-655 (_sync_layer_selector))
- **Programmatic camera/selection pushes** — UB-104's hazard (a hook setter called during render) cannot arise: the host lives OUTSIDE the reconciler and pushes camera/selection as plain props, then calls _render(). It does hit the other half of the same problem -- the graph is repopulated in place so props compare equal and the bailout skips -- and answers it with a monotonic `revision` prop threaded to every level (canvas_view.guitkx:1-8, :57). That is the correct GDScript answer. (unity CanvasView.uitkx:65-105 + UB-104 | godot builder_canvas_host.gd:111-120 (_revision), :123-132 (set_camera), :254-276 (_render))
- **The cross-pane drag machine** — The best-argued divergence in this subsystem. Unity's whole defect cluster comes from CapturePointer on a row the reconciler owns; Godot uses the engine's DnD (mouse_focus based, no widget capture) and re-resolves both ends by position against the live graph. Verified on Godot 4.7: _get_drag_data is handed the PRESS position (mpos - drag_accum), not the current one, so the row picked up is the row pressed even after 10 px of travel. The drop lands (probe: DROP at=... data={source:row,...}). The ghost is set_drag_preview, a faithful stand-in for BuilderDragService.ShowGhost. (unity BuilderDragService.cs:18-27, :31-161 + UB-30/31/32 + BUILDER_PORT_GUIDE.md 8.3 | godot edits/builder_drag.gd:1-18 (class note), :100-132 (resolve by POSITION against the current graph), :192-209 (source_row by offset then index), builder_canvas_host.gd:457-487 (Godot's own DnD protocol))
- **The library pane as a drag source** — Drag source and the UB-80 double-click-to-frame are both present and correct. Godot deliberately ADDS click-to-insert, which Unity deliberately does NOT have and gives a reason for. Defensible here (it inserts AFTER the selected row and is one undoable ledger entry, chrome/builder_window.gd:575-581) but it reverses a stated Unity decision; worth recording in CLAUDE.md's divergence list rather than leaving it as an unremarked difference. (unity BuilderLibraryPane.cs:697-729 ('draggable ONLY -- no click handler, so a misjudged click never mutates the buffer') | godot chrome/builder_library_pane.gd:267-280 (_get_drag_data on the pane, one implementation for all rows), :311-321 (double-click frames a workspace entry), chrome/builder_window.gd:715-718 (entry_activated -> insert))
- **Ctrl+wheel over a scrolling card section** — Genuinely not needed: no card section is a scroll view here, so nothing consumes the plain wheel and Ctrl carries no meaning. Correct engine translation -- but only because the section CAPS that create those scrollers are also absent (GAP-12). (unity BuilderCanvasHost.cs:313-334, :704-757 | godot canvas_view.guitkx (no ScrollContainer anywhere in a card), builder_canvas_host.gd:388-401 (the plain wheel always zooms))

**Create / rename / delete / move flows, save, abort, unsaved-tree placement, journal recovery**

- **A component OWNS the folder named after it; a companion never does** — Godot folds case where Unity is ordinal. The Unity inventory itself records that nothing justifies the ordinal choice while family matching is case-insensitive, so Godot's is the better-argued rule, not a defect. UB-142's actual point — a Style/Hook companion never owns — is honoured (builder_module.gd:114-115). (unity BuilderModule.cs:88-96 (Ordinal compare); godot builder_module.gd:113-118 uses to_lower() on both sides.)

**Document model: workspace, tree, module, specifiers, dirtiness, projection, orphans, read-only, import reconciliation**

- **Map and Relative correct only as a pair** — An improvement, not a gap: the builder writes exactly the specifier the compiler would, '~/' included, so a builder-authored import is indistinguishable from a hand-written one and cannot drift as the language moves. (unity Document/BuilderSpecifiers.cs:6-63 (own path arithmetic, '~/' broken); godot builder_specifiers.gd:39-79 delegates to RuitkGuitkx.import_specifier and RuitkGuitkxResolve.resolve_specifier, with root_for() asked of the FILE)

**Folder pane: tree rendering, state column, selection, re-filing by drag, folding**

- **Row icons** — Correct and well-argued: the editor theme is unavailable under --headless, and tests/builder_chrome_test.gd builds the real pane. Godot also sidesteps Unity's uncached-FolderIcon-per-row and never-caches-a-miss ModuleIcon defects for free. (unity BuilderFolderPane.cs:374-405; godot builder_folder_pane.gd:34-35 ("Text, not editor icons: the pane is built headlessly in the suites, where `EditorInterface` has no theme to ask"))
- **Row shape and indentation** — Godot uses the engine's own Tree, which supplies indentation, hit-testing, scrolling and keyboard navigation. The whole class of 'the label stole the pointer' bug Unity had to guard against (commit 83a8c4c4) cannot exist here. Legitimate engine translation. (unity BuilderFolderPane.cs:185-232 (hand-built rows, 6 + depth*16 padding, both children pickingMode Ignore); godot builder_folder_pane.gd:3 (`extends Tree`), :62-81)
- **Click vs drag arbitration** — Godot's Viewport arbitrates press-vs-drag itself; re-implementing a 4px threshold on top would fight it. Correct translation. Consequence: the pane inherits the editor-wide drag feel rather than Unity's pane-local 4px (which itself disagrees with BuilderDragService's 5f). (unity BuilderFolderPane.cs:37, :246-277 (4px euclidean travel, manual pointer capture); godot builder_folder_pane.gd:89-109 (`_get_drag_data`) -- the engine's own drag threshold and capture)
- **Double-click a file opens it** — The port implements BOTH the contract (single click focuses) and the implementation (double-click frames the card) -- the deliberate resolution of the spec/source contradiction. `module_activated` also selects the card on the canvas, honouring Unity's 'every route into a file moves the gold ring' invariant. (unity BuilderFolderPane.cs:250-255, BuilderWindow.cs:4504-4512, UI_BUILDER_CAPABILITIES.md:90-91; godot builder_folder_pane.gd:299-308 (`item_selected` -> `module_selected`, `item_activated` -> `module_activated`), builder_window.gd:667, :675-677)
- **Selection in the pane** — Matches the capabilities contract and the Unreal leg (SRuitkUiBuilderFolderPane.cpp:154-168). The loop guard the inventory says a port must budget for exists on BOTH ends. Verified empirically on Godot 4.7: `select_path` on an unselected row announces nothing, and `rebuild()`'s selection restore announces nothing, across two frames -- so the echo cannot fire. (unity BuilderFolderPane.cs:39-50, :337-349 (no selection state exists at all); godot builder_folder_pane.gd:80 (`select_mode = Tree.SELECT_ROW`), :275-296 (`selected_path()` / `select_path()` with the echo guard), builder_window.gd:2151-2175 (`select_module` with `_choosing`))
- **Per-module state column** — An addition with no Unity counterpart, and it earns its place: it is the one surface that makes the save-only contract visible per file, and Unity's own consequence (a read-only module looks identical until a drop toasts a refusal) is exactly what it fixes. Derived every call, never stored. Covered by builder_chrome_test.gd:538-552 and :1199-1202. (unity BuilderFolderPane.cs:172-232 (no read of IsDirty/HasMoved/IsOnDisk/IsReadOnly anywhere), BuilderWindow.cs:6289-6298 (aggregate in the status label only); godot builder_folder_pane.gd:70-77 (second, non-expanding 72px column), :211-224 (`_state_of` derives read-only / new / moved / moved, edited / edited))
- **Right-click menu and keyboard** — An addition. It reuses the card menu rather than inventing a second one, so it cannot drift. Folder rows are non-selectable so `item_mouse_selected` never fires for them -- folders have no context menu, matching Unity. Keyboard navigation comes free from Tree; Unity has none. **Graph projection: cards, rows, sections, imports, hook chips, markup walk, edges**

- **One edge per markup row that instantiates another module** — Two deliberate differences, both improvements: matching by import binding rather than card title fixes Unity's own noted hole (`import { Card as Tile }` used as `<Tile>` draws no usage edge there, and does here), and storing the edge means the seeded layout can see usages. `is_usage` is set but not read by the painter, so a usage edge and an import edge to the same target are drawn identically — Unity draws usage edges in a fixed usage tint. (unity: BuilderCanvasDrawing.cs:820-880, :1033-1051 (IndexOfTitle, ordinal title match, derived at paint time) | godot: builder_graph_service.gd:131-149 (stored as `Edge` with `is_usage`, matched against the names the card actually IMPORTED via `target_of_name`))
- **Declared export names read from the source** — An intentional improvement over the reference: Unity's documented staleness cannot happen here because `clear_detail()` empties `exports` first and the fill is unconditional. (unity: BuilderGraphService.cs:565-585 (early-returns when Exports is non-empty, so a renamed export stays stale until a full LoadTree) | godot: builder_graph_service.gd:184-188 — filled from `analyzed_decls` on EVERY `populate_card`, with no early return; consumed by chrome/builder_window.gd:1027-1029)
- **Default layout seeded from the root** — Three reasoned divergences, all documented in place: top-down instead of left-to-right ("a parent over its children is the shape the graph actually has"), unreachable modules get a column past the deepest instead of joining the root's, and a style companion is pulled onto its owner's row. The empty-tree guard Unity crashed on is present (`if graph.cards.is_empty(): return`). Godot needs no `X==0 && Y==0` guard because the seed always runs before the saved layout is applied on top. (unity: BuilderGraphService.cs:1354-1405 (BFS depth COLUMNS at x = 60 + d*560, per-column Y accumulation, `X==0 && Y==0` guard) | godot: builder_graph_service.gd:990-1055 (BFS LEVELS as ROWS, centred, row pitch = the tallest measured card + 48); gated by tests/builder_graph_test.gd:563-596)

**Language intelligence: completion, diagnostics plumbing, schema cache, element/hook classification**

- **The whole out-of-process LSP transport has no analogue and needs none** — Listed as deliberate in CLAUDE.md and tests/builder_parity.gd:119. The divergence deletes ten whole failure classes (orphaned dotnet processes, torn headers, BOM on stdin, unanswered server requests, ThreadAbort console spam). The one thing it does NOT delete is what those ten carried — see gaps LI-04/LI-06/LI-16. (unity Builder/Editor/Lsp/RuitkDotnetLocator.cs:19-199 + Lsp/BuilderLspClient.cs:28-405 (four-rung dotnet probe, three DLL layouts, hidden spawn with roll-forward, session PID list, once-per-domain stale sweep, handshake, shutdown ladder, Content-Length framing, reader thread, three-way dispatch); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/lsp/ contains only pure GDScript modules (guitkx_schema.gd, guitkx_completion.gd, guitkx_context.gd, guitkx_hover.gd, guitkx_workspace.gd, guitkx_analyzer_bridge.gd) — no process, no socket, no framing anywhere)
- **No document-version protocol, so none of the four staleness bugs can exist** — Strictly better: no versions, no _lspOpened set that is never cleared, no DidClose with zero call sites, no synthesized-buffer resync. The expensive half still debounces — builder/preview/builder_preview.gd:81,120-121 (300 ms). - **Schema is a bundled JSON read directly, with a dev fallback** — No double-serialize, no casing ambiguity, no async. Verified live: 54 hostElements, 45 styleKeys, 3 structuralAttributes, 7 commonAttributes, 8 controlFlow, 3 preambleDirectives, 5 declarations. (unity Builder/Editor/Lsp/BuilderLspClient.cs:505 + Library/BuilderLibraryPane.cs:305-307 (ruitk/schema returns an object whose `json`/`Json` field is the document as a STRING, parsed a second time, both casings accepted); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/lsp/guitkx_schema.gd:12-13,28-40 (_BUNDLED_SCHEMA then _DEV_SCHEMA, FileAccess.get_file_as_string, JSON.parse_string))
- **Directive descriptions are accurate here, so UB-04's never-display rule does not transfer** — Correct not to port the prohibition. Note none of this reaches the builder at all — the wrap menu shows the header text only (builder_window.gd:1157-1164). (unity Builder/Editor/Lsp/BuilderSchemaCache.cs:71-79 + Plans~/UI_BUILDER_BUGS.md:240-267 (UB-04: the schema claims @if generates a ternary and @foreach a .Select().ToArray() while the emitter generates IIFEs, so descriptions must NEVER be displayed); godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/lsp/guitkx_schema.gd:172-183 hover_for_directive DOES display them, and the bundled descriptions were verified correct for this compiler (@if/@elif/@else/@for/@while/@match/@case/@default, all eight accurate))

**Language surface: directive vocabulary, style key surface with value helpers, text/labels, element classification**

- **Adding a clause rewrites the construct's final '}' into '} @elif … {' with a fresh '}'** — The shared-head rewrite is exact, including the refusal when the close line is not a lone `}` (Unity toasts; Godot returns the source unchanged — a silent refusal, minor). Both listed divergences are correctly implemented and correctly justified: `@elif` not `@else if` (`@else if` would be two directives with no body between them, GUITKX0303), and the new clause gets a `<Control />` body because a directive body cannot be empty here. The comment at :610-613 states both reasons accurately. (unity BuilderWindow.cs:2088-2114 | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/edits/builder_edits.gd:588-630)
- **Directive spellings are painted as keywords in the source pane** — A legitimate engine translation and a better one. The tokenizer emits a `directive` token for ANY `@ident`, so the vocabulary cannot drift out of the highlighter, and Unity's ordering trap (the alternation must list '@else if' before '@else' or only '@else' colours) simply does not exist — `@elif` is one word here anyway. The GDScript keyword set is separate and complete. This is the source pane reuse working as the divergence intended. (unity Controls/CodeField.cs:1109-1126, :1343-1349 | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/editor/guitkx_tokenizer.gd:132-138, :78)
- **Repeated parses of the same buffer are not repeated** — No memo exists, and the motivation for one is largely engineered away: an edit re-projects only the card that changed rather than the whole tree, and the source pane is an explicit edit/apply pane so a keystroke does not trigger a parse at all. Recorded as a deliberate translation rather than a gap — but note there IS no memo, so a full `reproject()` (open, undo, save-with-format) does re-analyze every module, and the four analysis entry points (`analyzed_decls`, `decl_structure`, `scan_imports`, `_split_body`) are each called fresh. If tree-wide re-projection ever gets hotter, a path-keyed memo is the answer Unity already validated. (unity Lang/BuilderLanguage.cs:30-66 | godot addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/chrome/builder_window.gd:877-894 (_after_model_change re-populates ONE card), addons/reactive_ui_toolkit_editor/builder/canvas/builder_graph_service.gd (no memo))

- **HOOKS: curated leads merged with the runtime's real hook registry** — Better than the reference and by the listed divergence (language intelligence comes from the compiler/editor LSP layer, not a builder-owned client). Godot reads the hooks synchronously from the compiler's vocabulary, so `library.lsp-failure` — Unity's "Palette unavailable: <message>" degradation, and UB-09's knock-on of an empty schema cache — has no analogue and needs none. **Live preview: compile pipeline, mirroring, scheduling, knobs, state panel, usage notes, failure isolation**

- **Compiles happen on action boundaries, not on keystrokes** — Godot's edit/apply gate is stricter than Unity's: keystrokes cannot reach the funnel at all. Side effect worth knowing: builder_ledger.gd:170-194 record_typing is consequently unreachable — its only caller is builder_window.gd:909, which returns before it. Dead feature, but a chrome/history concern, not preview. - **A style/hook/util module never attempts to render** — Godot's single mechanism subsumes both of Unity's: asking the built script's method list catches style, hooks AND util in one test. The comment at :517-519 correctly notes has_method() does not report a GDScript's statics on the script object. Gated by tests/builder_preview_test.gd:493-514.
